Secondary causes include immune complex deposition, systemic vasculitis, dehydration, and concurrent bacterial superinfection that exacerbates viral-induced renal injury.
treatment: No specific antiviral therapy is curative; supportive care includes aggressive IV fluid therapy (balanced polyionic solutions) to maintain renal perfusion, NSAIDs (flunixin meglumine 1.1 mg/kg IV) for inflammation control, and corticosteroids if immune-mediated glomerulonephritis is confirmed. Antiviral agents such as valacyclovir (30 mg/kg PO q8h) may be considered for EHV cases. Monitor renal values and electrolytes closely.
treatment_ja: 特異的な抗ウイルス治療は確立されていないため、支持療法が中心となる。腎灌流維持のための積極的な静脈内輸液（バランス電解質液）、フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg IV）による抗炎症療法、免疫介在性糸球体腎炎が確認された場合はコルチコステロイドを投与する。EHV症例にはバラシクロビル（30 mg/kg PO q8h）を考慮する。腎機能値および電解質を継続的にモニタリングする。

name: Renal Bacterial Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Bacterial infection of the renal parenchyma (pyelonephritis) typically occurs via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract, or less commonly through hematogenous spread. Bacteria colonize the renal pelvis and parenchyma, causing inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of nephrons, potentially leading to renal insufficiency or failure. Common causative organisms include Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Staphylococcus spp., Corynebacterium spp., and Actinobacillus equuli.
pathophysiology_ja: 腎臓の細菌感染（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路からの上行性感染、またはまれに血行性播種によって生じます。細菌が腎盂および腎実質に定着し、炎症、膿瘍形成、ネフロンの進行性破壊を引き起こし、腎機能不全や腎不全に至る可能性があります。一般的な起因菌には大腸菌、レンサ球菌、ブドウ球菌、コリネバクテリウム属、アクチノバチルス・エクーリなどが含まれます。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infection from the lower urinary tract (cystitis, urethritis), urolithiasis causing urinary stasis, and hematogenous spread from distant infection sites. Secondary or predisposing factors include immunosuppression, urinary tract obstruction, catheterization, bladder paralysis, and conditions that impair normal urine flow such as nephrolithiasis or ureteral strictures.
treatment: Initiate aggressive, prolonged antibiotic therapy (4-6 weeks minimum) based on urine culture and sensitivity; commonly trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, enrofloxacin, or penicillin/gentamicin combinations. Provide IV fluid therapy to maintain hydration and renal perfusion. Address predisposing factors such as urolithiasis or urinary obstruction surgically if needed.
treatment_ja: 尿培養および感受性試験に基づき、トリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾール、エンロフロキサシン、またはペニシリン・ゲンタマイシン併用などの長期抗菌薬療法（最低4〜6週間）を開始する。静脈内輸液療法により水分補給と腎灌流を維持する。尿路結石や尿路閉塞などの素因がある場合は、必要に応じて外科的に対処する。

name: Renal Fungal Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Fungal organisms (commonly Aspergillus spp., Candida spp., or Mucor spp.) colonize the renal parenchyma, leading to granulomatous or necrotizing inflammation. Hyphae may invade renal vasculature causing thrombosis and infarction, resulting in progressive destruction of renal tissue. In severe cases, fungal masses (fungal balls) can obstruct the renal pelvis or ureters, leading to hydronephrosis and renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 真菌（主にAspergillus属、Candida属、Mucor属など）が腎実質に定着し、肉芽腫性または壊死性炎症を引き起こす。菌糸が腎血管に侵入して血栓症や梗塞を引き起こし、腎組織の進行性破壊をもたらす。重症例では真菌塊（ファンガスボール）が腎盂や尿管を閉塞し、水腎症や腎不全に至ることがある。
causes: Primary causes include opportunistic fungal infections (Aspergillus spp., Candida spp., Cryptococcus spp.) that gain access via hematogenous spread or ascending urinary tract infection. Predisposing factors include prolonged antibiotic therapy, immunosuppression (corticosteroid use, concurrent illness), indwelling urinary catheters, and debilitated general condition. Secondary causes include disseminated systemic mycosis originating from respiratory or gastrointestinal sources.
treatment: Administer systemic antifungal therapy with fluconazole (5 mg/kg PO q24h) or amphotericin B (0.3–0.5 mg/kg IV slowly, with careful renal monitoring). Discontinue predisposing antibiotics and immunosuppressive agents. Provide IV fluid therapy to support renal perfusion; consider nephrectomy if unilateral disease with severe parenchymal destruction.
treatment_ja: フルコナゾール（5 mg/kg 経口 1日1回）またはアムホテリシンB（0.3〜0.5 mg/kg 緩徐静注、腎機能を慎重にモニタリング）による全身性抗真菌療法を実施する。誘因となる抗菌薬や免疫抑制剤を中止し、輸液療法で腎灌流を維持する。片側性で腎実質の重度破壊がある場合は腎摘出術を検討する。

name: Renal Infection (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infection (pyelonephritis) in horses typically results from ascending bacterial infection via the ureters from the lower urinary tract, or less commonly from hematogenous spread. Bacteria colonize the renal pelvis and parenchyma, causing inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue. Chronic infection can lead to fibrosis, hydronephrosis, and ultimately renal failure if bilateral or if the contralateral kidney is compromised.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路から尿管を経由した上行性細菌感染、またはまれに血行性播種によって生じます。細菌が腎盂および腎実質に定着し、炎症、膿瘍形成、腎組織の進行性破壊を引き起こします。慢性感染は線維化、水腎症を引き起こし、両側性の場合や対側腎が障害されている場合は最終的に腎不全に至ることがあります。
causes: The most common causative organisms include Escherichia coli, Proteus spp., Streptococcus spp., Corynebacterium renale, and Actinobacillus equuli. Predisposing factors include urolithiasis, urinary tract obstruction, bladder paralysis, catheterization, immunosuppression, and anatomical abnormalities. Mares may be more susceptible due to their shorter urethra facilitating ascending infections.
treatment: Initiate prolonged systemic antibiotic therapy (4-6 weeks) based on urine culture and sensitivity, commonly trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (30 mg/kg PO BID) or enrofloxacin (5 mg/kg IV/PO SID). Provide IV fluid therapy to maintain hydration and promote diuresis. Address underlying predisposing factors such as urolithiasis or urinary obstruction surgically if indicated.
treatment_ja: 尿培養および感受性試験に基づき、トリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾール（30 mg/kg 経口 BID）またはエンロフロキサシン（5 mg/kg 静注/経口 SID）などの全身性抗菌薬を4〜6週間投与する。静脈内輸液療法で水分補給と利尿を促進する。尿路結石や尿路閉塞などの基礎疾患がある場合は、外科的処置を含め適切に対処する。

name: Renal Inflammation (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal inflammation (nephritis) in horses involves immune-mediated or infectious damage to the glomeruli, tubules, or interstitium of the kidneys, leading to impaired filtration, proteinuria, and azotemia. Inflammatory cell infiltration and edema disrupt normal nephron function, potentially progressing to fibrosis and chronic renal insufficiency if left untreated. Glomerulonephritis may result from immune complex deposition, while tubulointerstitial nephritis often follows toxic or infectious insults.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎炎は、免疫介在性または感染性の障害により糸球体、尿細管、または間質に炎症が生じ、濾過機能の低下、蛋白尿、高窒素血症を引き起こす。炎症細胞の浸潤と浮腫がネフロン機能を障害し、未治療の場合は線維化や慢性腎不全に進行する可能性がある。糸球体腎炎は免疫複合体の沈着、尿細管間質性腎炎は毒性物質や感染性因子による障害に起因することが多い。
causes: Primary causes include bacterial infections (e.g., Leptospira, Streptococcus equi), viral infections (e.g., equine infectious anemia), and nephrotoxic agents such as NSAIDs, aminoglycosides, and heavy metals. Secondary causes include immune complex deposition from systemic diseases (e.g., purpura hemorrhagica), septicemia, endotoxemia, and hemodynamic compromise leading to ischemic renal injury. Ingestion of toxic plants (e.g., oak, red maple) can also contribute to renal inflammation.
treatment: Discontinue nephrotoxic agents (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides) immediately. Administer aggressive IV fluid therapy (polyionic isotonic crystalloids) to restore renal perfusion and correct azotemia. Treat underlying infections with appropriate antibiotics (e.g., penicillin for Streptococcus equi, oxytetracycline for Leptospira). Corticosteroids (dexamethasone 0.05–0.1 mg/kg IV) may be used for immune-mediated nephritis. Monitor electrolytes, urine output, and serum creatinine closely.
treatment_ja: 腎毒性薬剤（NSAIDs、アミノグリコシド系）を直ちに中止する。積極的な静脈内輸液療法（等張晶質液）を実施し、腎灌流を回復させアゾテミアを是正する。基礎感染症には適切な抗菌薬（Streptococcus equiにはペニシリン、レプトスピラにはオキシテトラサイクリン）を投与する。免疫介在性腎炎にはデキサメタゾン（0.05〜0.1 mg/kg IV）を使用する。電解質、尿量、血清クレアチニンを継続的にモニタリングする。

name: Renal Neoplasia (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal neoplasia in horses involves abnormal, uncontrolled cellular proliferation within the kidney parenchyma or renal pelvis. The most commonly reported types include renal cell carcinoma, nephroblastoma, and lymphoma, which can cause progressive destruction of normal renal tissue, obstruction of urine flow, and potential metastasis to lungs, liver, and lymph nodes. As the tumor enlarges, it compromises renal function, may invade surrounding structures, and can lead to paraneoplastic syndromes including weight loss and anemia.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎腫瘍は、腎実質または腎盂における異常で制御不能な細胞増殖を伴う。最も一般的に報告される種類には腎細胞癌、腎芽腫、リンパ腫があり、正常な腎組織の進行性破壊、尿流の閉塞、肺・肝臓・リンパ節への転移を引き起こしうる。腫瘍が増大すると腎機能が低下し、周囲組織への浸潤や、体重減少・貧血などの傍腫瘍症候群を引き起こすことがある。
causes: The exact etiology of renal neoplasia in horses is largely unknown, with no consistently identified predisposing factors. Primary renal tumors such as renal cell carcinoma and nephroblastoma arise from malignant transformation of renal epithelial or embryonal cells, possibly due to spontaneous genetic mutations. Secondary renal involvement may occur through metastasis from other primary tumors or as part of multicentric lymphoma.
treatment: Unilateral nephrectomy is the primary treatment for localized renal tumors when the contralateral kidney is functional. For renal lymphoma, systemic chemotherapy (e.g., corticosteroids, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin) may be attempted. Supportive care includes IV fluid therapy, analgesics (flunixin meglumine), and monitoring renal function via serial bloodwork.
treatment_ja: 対側腎の機能が正常である場合、限局性腎腫瘍に対しては患側の腎摘出術が第一選択となる。腎リンパ腫にはコルチコステロイド、シクロホスファミド、ドキソルビシン等による全身化学療法を検討する。補助療法として輸液療法、鎮痛薬（フルニキシンメグルミン）の投与、および血液検査による腎機能の継続的モニタリングを行う。

name: Renal Metabolic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal metabolic disease in horses involves impaired kidney function leading to disrupted electrolyte balance, acid-base homeostasis, and waste product excretion. The kidneys fail to adequately regulate calcium, phosphorus, and other mineral metabolism, potentially resulting in hypercalcemia, hyperphosphatemia, or metabolic acidosis. Chronic dysfunction can lead to renal secondary hyperparathyroidism, soft tissue mineralization, and progressive nephron loss.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎代謝疾患は、腎機能障害により電解質バランス、酸塩基平衡、および老廃物排泄が障害される疾患である。腎臓がカルシウム、リン、その他のミネラル代謝を適切に調節できなくなり、高カルシウム血症、高リン血症、または代謝性アシドーシスを引き起こす可能性がある。慢性的な機能障害は腎性二次性上皮小体機能亢進症、軟部組織の石灰化、および進行性のネフロン喪失につながる。
causes: Primary causes include chronic kidney disease, nephrotoxin exposure (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals, vitamin D toxicosis), and nephrolithiasis. Secondary causes include dehydration, hemodynamic compromise, systemic infections, and excessive dietary calcium or oxalate-containing plants that place metabolic stress on the kidneys.
treatment: Initiate aggressive IV fluid therapy (balanced polyionic solutions) to restore renal perfusion and correct dehydration. Discontinue nephrotoxic agents (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides) immediately. Address electrolyte imbalances with dietary phosphorus restriction, aluminum hydroxide as a phosphate binder, and sodium bicarbonate for metabolic acidosis. Manage hypercalcemia with saline diuresis and furosemide (1 mg/kg IV).
treatment_ja: 積極的な静脈内輸液療法（バランス電解質液）を開始し、腎灌流の回復と脱水の補正を行う。腎毒性薬剤（NSAIDs、アミノグリコシド系）は直ちに中止する。電解質異常にはリン制限食、水酸化アルミニウム（リン吸着剤）、代謝性アシドーシスに対し重炭酸ナトリウムを投与する。高カルシウム血症には生理食塩水による利尿とフロセミド（1 mg/kg 静注）で対応する。

name: Renal Nutritional Deficiency (Horse)
pathophysiology: Nutritional deficiencies, particularly of vitamins (such as vitamin A, D, or E) and minerals (such as calcium, phosphorus, or magnesium), can impair normal renal tubular function and glomerular integrity in horses. Imbalances in the calcium-phosphorus ratio or excessive dietary oxalates can lead to nephrocalcinosis, tubular degeneration, and progressive renal insufficiency. Chronic deficiency states may result in dystrophic mineralization of renal parenchyma and impaired electrolyte homeostasis.
pathophysiology_ja: ビタミン（A、D、Eなど）やミネラル（カルシウム、リン、マグネシウムなど）の栄養欠乏は、馬の腎尿細管機能および糸球体の健全性を損なう可能性があります。カルシウム・リン比の不均衡や過剰なシュウ酸塩の摂取は、腎石灰化症、尿細管変性、進行性腎不全を引き起こします。慢性的な欠乏状態は腎実質の異栄養性石灰化および電解質恒常性の障害をもたらすことがあります。
causes: Primary causes include dietary imbalances in calcium and phosphorus (especially inverse Ca:P ratios), excessive oxalate-containing plants (e.g., tropical grasses such as Setaria or Panicum), and deficiencies in vitamin A or vitamin D. Secondary causes include chronic poor-quality forage, inadequate mineral supplementation, and prolonged grazing on nutrient-depleted pastures.
treatment: Correct dietary imbalances by adjusting the calcium-to-phosphorus ratio to approximately 2:1, removing oxalate-rich forages, and supplementing with calcium carbonate, vitamin A, and vitamin D3 as needed. Provide IV calcium borogluconate for acute hypocalcemia and administer IV fluids (lactated Ringer's solution) to support renal perfusion. Monitor serum electrolytes, BUN, and creatinine regularly to guide ongoing nutritional and supportive therapy.
treatment_ja: カルシウムとリンの比率を約2:1に調整し、シュウ酸塩を多く含む飼料を除去し、必要に応じて�ite�ite calcium carbonate（炭酸カルシウム）、ビタミンA、ビタミンD3を補給して食餌性不均衡を是正する。急性低カルシウム血症にはボログルコン酸カルシウムを静脈内投与し、乳酸リンゲル液による輸液療法で腎灌流を維持する。血清電解質、BUN、クレアチニンを定期的にモニタリングし、継続的な栄養管理と支持療法を調整する。

name: Renal Genetic Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal genetic disorders in horses involve inherited mutations affecting renal tubular or glomerular structure and function, leading to progressive nephron loss, impaired filtration, and electrolyte imbalances. Examples include renal tubular dysplasia and polycystic kidney disease, where abnormal development or cyst formation disrupts normal renal architecture. Progressive fibrosis and inflammation ultimately result in chronic renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎遺伝性疾患は、腎尿細管または糸球体の構造と機能に影響を及ぼす遺伝子変異が関与し、進行性のネフロン喪失、濾過障害、電解質異常を引き起こします。腎尿細管異形成や多発性嚢胞腎などが含まれ、異常な発達や嚢胞形成が正常な腎構造を破壊します。進行性の線維化と炎症が最終的に慢性腎不全につながります。
causes: The primary cause is inherited genetic mutations, often autosomal recessive, affecting genes responsible for normal renal development and function. Specific conditions include renal tubular dysplasia (reported in certain breeds) and polycystic kidney disease. Environmental factors and secondary infections may accelerate disease progression but are not the primary cause.
causes_ja: 主な原因は、正常な腎発達と機能に関与する遺伝子の遺伝性変異であり、多くの場合常染色体劣性遺伝です。特定の疾患には腎尿細管異形成（特定の品種で報告）や多発性嚢胞腎が含まれます。環境要因や二次感染は疾患の進行を促進する可能性がありますが、主要な原因ではありません。
treatment: No curative treatment exists for renal genetic disorders in horses; management is supportive. Intravenous fluid therapy (balanced polyionic solutions) corrects dehydration and electrolyte imbalances. ACE inhibitors (e.g., benazepril 0.5 mg/kg PO q24h) may slow proteinuria progression. Dietary phosphorus restriction, oral phosphate binders (aluminum hydroxide), and monitoring of BUN/creatinine are essential for managing chronic kidney disease progression.
treatment_ja: 馬の腎遺伝性疾患に根治療法は存在せず、治療は対症療法が中心となる。静脈内輸液療法（バランス電解質液）により脱水および電解質異常を補正する。ACE阻害薬（例：ベナゼプリル0.5 mg/kg 経口 1日1回）は蛋白尿の進行を抑制しうる。食事中のリン制限、経口リン吸着剤（水酸化アルミニウム）の投与、およびBUN・クレアチニンの定期的モニタリングが慢性腎臓病の進行管理に不可欠である。

name: Renal Autoimmune Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: The immune system produces autoantibodies or autoreactive T-cells directed against renal antigens, leading to immune complex deposition within glomeruli and/or tubulointerstitial tissue. This triggers complement activation, inflammatory cell infiltration, and progressive damage to the glomerular basement membrane and tubular structures. The resulting chronic inflammation leads to glomerulonephritis, tubular necrosis, fibrosis, and progressive loss of renal function.
pathophysiology_ja: 免疫系が腎臓の自己抗原に対する自己抗体または自己反応性T細胞を産生し、糸球体や尿細管間質組織に免疫複合体が沈着します。これにより補体活性化、炎症細胞の浸潤、糸球体基底膜および尿細管構造の進行性障害が引き起こされます。結果として慢性炎症が糸球体腎炎、尿細管壊死、線維化、および進行性の腎機能低下をもたらします。
causes: The primary cause is immune dysregulation leading to loss of self-tolerance against renal antigens, potentially triggered by preceding infectious diseases (e.g., Streptococcus equi, equine infectious anemia), chronic antigenic stimulation, or drug reactions. Secondary factors include immune complex deposition from systemic autoimmune conditions, genetic predisposition, and chronic inflammatory states that promote molecular mimicry or epitope spreading.
treatment: Immunosuppressive therapy with corticosteroids (dexamethasone 0.05-0.1 mg/kg IV/IM initially, then oral prednisolone tapering) is the cornerstone. Azathioprine (3 mg/kg PO q24h) may be added for steroid-sparing effect. Supportive care includes IV fluid therapy, ACE inhibitors (benazepril 0.5 mg/kg PO) to reduce proteinuria, and monitoring renal parameters closely.
treatment_ja: 免疫抑制療法が治療の基本であり、デキサメタゾン（0.05〜0.1 mg/kg IV/IM）を初期投与後、経口プレドニゾロンへ漸減移行する。ステロイド減量目的でアザチオプリン（3 mg/kg PO q24h）を併用する場合がある。補助療法として輸液療法、蛋白尿軽減のためのACE阻害薬（ベナゼプリル0.5 mg/kg PO）投与、および腎機能パラメータの継続的モニタリングを実施する。

name: Renal Degenerative Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal degenerative disease in horses involves progressive deterioration of nephrons, including tubular degeneration, interstitial fibrosis, and glomerulosclerosis, leading to impaired renal filtration, concentration ability, and waste excretion. Chronic insult results in irreversible loss of functional renal tissue, culminating in azotemia, electrolyte imbalances, and eventual renal failure. The compensatory hypertrophy of remaining nephrons may temporarily maintain function until a critical mass of tissue is lost.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎変性疾患は、尿細管変性、間質線維化、糸球体硬化症を含むネフロンの進行性劣化を伴い、腎濾過機能、濃縮能力、老廃物排泄の障害を引き起こす。慢性的な障害により機能的腎組織の不可逆的喪失が生じ、高窒素血症、電解質異常、最終的に腎不全に至る。残存ネフロンの代償性肥大により、組織の臨界量が失われるまで一時的に機能が維持されることがある。
causes: Primary causes include chronic exposure to nephrotoxins (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals, vitamin D toxicosis), oxalate-containing plants, and pigment nephropathy from rhabdomyolysis or hemolysis. Secondary causes include chronic ischemia, recurrent pyelonephritis, nephrolithiasis, immune-mediated glomerulonephritis, and age-related senile nephrosclerosis. Idiopathic renal degeneration is also recognized, particularly in older horses.
treatment: Treatment is primarily supportive: IV fluid therapy (polyionic isotonic fluids) to correct dehydration and maintain renal perfusion, dietary modification with reduced protein and calcium, and discontinuation of all nephrotoxic agents (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides). ACE inhibitors (enalapril) may reduce proteinuria. Manage electrolyte imbalances (calcium, phosphorus) and provide gastroprotectants (omeprazole) for secondary uremic gastritis.
treatment_ja: 治療は主に支持療法が中心となる。等張電解質輸液による脱水補正と腎灌流維持、低タンパク・低カルシウム食への変更、腎毒性薬剤（NSAIDs、アミノグリコシド系）の即時中止が重要である。ACE阻害薬（エナラプリル）によるタンパク尿軽減、電解質（カルシウム・リン）異常の補正、尿毒症性胃炎に対するオメプラゾール投与などの対症療法を実施する。

name: Renal Traumatic Injury (Horse)
pathophysiology: Blunt or penetrating trauma to the kidney results in parenchymal disruption, subcapsular or perirenal hemorrhage, and potential urine leakage into the retroperitoneal space. The injury may range from minor contusions with microhemorrhage to complete renal fracture or vascular pedicle avulsion, leading to significant hemorrhage, uroperitoneum, and secondary inflammation or infection. Compensatory mechanisms by the contralateral kidney may maintain renal function if the injury is unilateral.
pathophysiology_ja: 鈍的外傷または穿通性外傷により腎実質の損傷が生じ、被膜下出血や腎周囲出血、さらに後腹膜腔への尿漏出が起こり得る。損傷は軽度の挫傷から腎の完全破裂や血管茎の断裂まで多岐にわたり、重篤な出血、尿腹症、二次的な炎症や感染を引き起こす可能性がある。一側性損傷の場合、対側腎の代償機能により腎機能は維持されることがある。
causes: Primary causes include blunt abdominal trauma from kicks by other horses, falls, collision with fixed objects, or vehicular accidents. Secondary causes may include penetrating injuries from sharp objects, fractured ribs lacerating the kidney, or iatrogenic injury during percutaneous renal biopsy or surgical procedures.
causes_ja: 主な原因は他馬からの蹴り、転倒、固定物への衝突、交通事故などによる腹部への鈍的外傷である。二次的原因として、鋭利な物体による穿通性損傷、肋骨骨折による腎臓の裂傷、経皮的腎生検や外科手術中の医原性損傷が挙げられる。
treatment: Stabilize with IV crystalloid fluids (e.g., lactated Ringer's solution) and blood transfusion if severe hemorrhage occurs. Administer flunixin meglumine (1.1 mg/kg IV q12h) for pain and inflammation control, plus broad-spectrum antibiotics (e.g., gentamicin and penicillin) to prevent secondary infection. Minor contusions are managed conservatively with stall rest and monitoring; severe renal fracture or vascular pedicle avulsion may require nephrectomy.
treatment_ja: 重度の出血がある場合は乳酸リンゲル液の静脈内投与および輸血で循環を安定させる。フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg IV 12時間毎）で疼痛・炎症を管理し、ゲンタマイシンおよびペニシリン等の広域抗菌薬で二次感染を予防する。軽度の挫傷は馬房安静と経過観察で保存的に管理するが、重度の腎破裂や血管茎断裂の場合は腎摘出術が必要となることがある。

name: Renal Behavioral Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal behavioral disorder in horses involves abnormal behaviors (such as frequent posturing to urinate, flank watching, or irritability) arising from chronic renal pain or discomfort due to underlying kidney pathology such as nephrolithiasis, nephritis, or renal neoplasia. Afferent pain signals from the renal capsule or parenchyma lead to visceral pain responses manifesting as behavioral changes. Chronic irritation of the renal system may also cause referred pain to the flank and lumbar regions, further altering the horse's demeanor and performance.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎行動障害は、腎結石症、腎炎、腎腫瘍などの基礎的な腎臓病変による慢性的な腎臓の痛みや不快感から生じる異常行動（頻繁な排尿姿勢、脇腹を気にする行動、易刺激性など）を伴います。腎被膜や実質からの求心性疼痛信号が内臓痛反応を引き起こし、行動変化として現れます。慢性的な腎系の刺激は脇腹や腰部への関連痛を引き起こし、馬の気性やパフォーマンスをさらに変化させます。
causes: Primary causes include nephrolithiasis, chronic nephritis, renal cysts, renal neoplasia, and pyelonephritis causing persistent renal discomfort. Secondary causes may involve ureterolithiasis, hydronephrosis, renal toxicity from NSAIDs or aminoglycosides, and chronic urinary tract infections that contribute to ongoing renal pain and associated behavioral changes.
treatment: Address the underlying renal pathology: surgical removal of nephroliths or neoplasia if feasible, antibiotics (trimethoprim-sulfonamide or enrofloxacin) for pyelonephritis. Manage pain with flunixin meglumine (1.1 mg/kg IV) or butorphanol (0.02-0.04 mg/kg IV). Provide IV fluid therapy for renal support and discontinue nephrotoxic agents.
treatment_ja: 原因となる腎疾患の治療として、腎結石や腫瘍の外科的除去、腎盂腎炎にはトリメトプリム・スルホンアミドまたはエンロフロキサシンを投与する。疼痛管理にはフルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg IV）またはブトルファノール（0.02-0.04 mg/kg IV）を使用する。腎機能維持のため輸液療法を実施し、腎毒性薬剤の投与を中止する。

name: Renal Infectious Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infectious disease in horses involves bacterial colonization of the renal parenchyma, typically via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract or hematogenous spread. Bacterial invasion triggers an inflammatory response leading to nephritis or pyelonephritis, causing tubular damage, interstitial inflammation, and potentially abscess formation. Progressive infection can impair glomerular filtration and tubular function, leading to azotemia and renal insufficiency if untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症は、下部尿路からの上行性感染または血行性伝播により細菌が腎実質に定着することで発生します。細菌の侵入により炎症反応が誘発され、腎炎や腎盂腎炎を引き起こし、尿細管の損傷、間質性炎症、さらには膿瘍形成に至ることがあります。感染が進行すると糸球体濾過および尿細管機能が障害され、未治療の場合は高窒素血症や腎不全に至る可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infections (commonly Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Actinobacillus equuli, and Corynebacterium spp.) from the lower urinary tract, as well as hematogenous spread from distant infection sites. Secondary contributing factors include urolithiasis, urinary tract obstruction, immunosuppression, catheterization, and concurrent systemic infections such as strangles or neonatal septicemia.
treatment: Initiate aggressive parenteral antibiotic therapy based on urine culture and sensitivity, commonly trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (30 mg/kg PO BID) or enrofloxacin (5 mg/kg IV SID) for 2-4 weeks. Provide IV fluid therapy (balanced polyionic solutions) to maintain hydration and promote renal perfusion. Address underlying causes such as urolithiasis surgically if present, and monitor renal function via serial serum creatinine and urinalysis.
treatment_ja: 尿培養および感受性試験に基づき、トリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾール（30 mg/kg 経口 BID）またはエンロフロキサシン（5 mg/kg 静注 SID）などの抗菌薬を2～4週間積極的に投与する。等張電解質輸液による静脈内輸液療法で水分補給と腎灌流を維持する。尿路結石などの基礎疾患が存在する場合は外科的に対処し、血清クレアチニンおよび尿検査の定期的モニタリングで腎機能を評価する。

name: Renal Parasitic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal parasitic disease in horses occurs when parasitic organisms such as Halicephalobus gingivalis (formerly Halicephalobus deletrix), Strongylus vulgaris larvae, or Dioctophyme renale migrate to or lodge within the renal parenchyma, renal pelvis, or perirenal tissues. The parasites cause direct mechanical damage to nephrons, provoke granulomatous or eosinophilic inflammatory responses, and may lead to progressive renal fibrosis, obstruction of urine flow, and impaired renal function. Vascular damage from migrating larvae (particularly S. vulgaris) can also cause renal infarction and hemorrhage.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎寄生虫症は、Halicephalobus gingivalis、普通円虫（Strongylus vulgaris）の幼虫、または腎虫（Dioctophyme renale）などの寄生虫が腎実質、腎盂、または腎周囲組織に移行・寄生することで発症する。寄生虫はネフロンへの直接的な機械的損傷を引き起こし、肉芽腫性または好酸球性炎症反応を誘発し、進行性の腎線維化、尿流閉塞、腎機能障害をもたらす。特にS. vulgarisの移行幼虫による血管障害は腎梗塞や出血を引き起こすことがある。
causes: Primary causes include aberrant migration of Strongylus vulgaris larvae through mesenteric and renal vasculature, infection with Halicephalobus gingivalis (a saprophytic nematode capable of invading the kidneys), and rarely Dioctophyme renale (giant kidney worm). Secondary causes include immunosuppression, heavy parasite burdens due to inadequate deworming programs, and contaminated environments that increase exposure to infective larval stages.
treatment: Administer high-dose anthelmintics such as fenbendazole (10 mg/kg PO daily for 5 days) or ivermectin (0.2 mg/kg PO); for Halicephalobus gingivalis, prolonged courses of fenbendazole or moxidectin may be attempted though prognosis is guarded. Nephrectomy of the affected kidney is considered when unilateral involvement is confirmed. Supportive care includes NSAIDs for inflammation, IV fluids for renal support, and broad-spectrum antibiotics to manage secondary infections.
treatment_ja: フェンベンダゾール（10 mg/kg 経口、5日間連続投与）やイベルメクチン（0.2 mg/kg 経口）などの駆虫薬を高用量で投与する。Halicephalobus gingivalis感染ではフェンベンダゾールまたはモキシデクチンの長期投与を試みるが、予後は慎重である。片側性の腎病変が確認された場合は患側腎の腎摘出術を検討する。補助療法として、NSAIDsによる抗炎症治療、輸液による腎機能サポート、および二次感染予防のための広域スペクトル抗菌薬投与を行う。

name: Renal Viral Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Viral agents such as equine herpesvirus (EHV) or equine arteritis virus (EAV) can target renal vasculature and tubular epithelium, causing immune-mediated glomerulonephritis, tubular necrosis, and interstitial nephritis. Viral replication within endothelial cells leads to vasculitis, impaired renal perfusion, and progressive loss of glomerular filtration. Immune complex deposition further exacerbates renal parenchymal damage and inflammation.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬ヘルペスウイルス（EHV）や馬動脈炎ウイルス（EAV）などのウイルスが腎血管や尿細管上皮を標的とし、免疫介在性糸球体腎炎、尿細管壊死、間質性腎炎を引き起こす。内皮細胞内でのウイルス増殖が血管炎を引き起こし、腎灌流障害と糸球体濾過率の低下をもたらす。免疫複合体の沈着がさらに腎実質の障害と炎症を悪化させる。
causes: Primary causes include equine herpesvirus (EHV-1), equine arteritis virus (EAV), and other nephrotrophic viruses that directly infect renal tissue. Secondary causes include immune complex deposition, systemic vasculitis, and concurrent bacterial infections that compound viral-induced renal injury. Stress, immunosuppression, and co-infections may predispose horses to renal involvement.
treatment: No specific antiviral cure exists; treatment is primarily supportive. Administer IV balanced crystalloid fluids (e.g., lactated Ringer's) to maintain renal perfusion, use flunixin meglumine (1.1 mg/kg IV) for anti-inflammatory and analgesic effects, and consider valacyclovir (30 mg/kg PO BID) for EHV-1 cases. Manage secondary infections with broad-spectrum antibiotics and monitor renal values (BUN, creatinine) closely.
treatment_ja: 特異的な抗ウイルス治療法は存在せず、主に支持療法が中心となる。乳酸リンゲル液などの等張晶質液を静脈内投与し腎灌流を維持し、フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg IV）を抗炎症・鎮痛目的で使用する。EHV-1症例にはバラシクロビル（30 mg/kg 経口 BID）を検討する。二次感染には広域スペクトル抗菌薬を投与し、BUN・クレアチニン等の腎機能指標を継続的にモニタリングする。

name: Renal Bacterial Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Bacterial infection of the kidneys (pyelonephritis) in horses typically occurs via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract, or less commonly through hematogenous spread. Bacteria colonize the renal pelvis and parenchyma, causing inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue. Common causative organisms include Escherichia coli, Actinobaculum suis, Corynebacterium spp., Streptococcus spp., and other gram-negative enteric bacteria, leading to impaired renal function if left untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎臓細菌感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路からの上行性感染により発生し、まれに血行性に波及することもある。細菌が腎盂および腎実質に定着し、炎症、膿瘍形成、腎組織の進行性破壊を引き起こす。主な起因菌には大腸菌、Actinobaculum suis、Corynebacterium属、Streptococcus属などのグラム陰性腸内細菌が含まれ、未治療の場合は腎機能障害に至る。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infection from the lower urinary tract, often associated with urolithiasis, urethral obstruction, or catheterization. Secondary causes include hematogenous spread from distant infection sites, immunosuppression, urinary stasis, and structural abnormalities of the urinary tract that predispose to bacterial colonization.
treatment: Initiate prolonged antimicrobial therapy (4-6 weeks minimum) based on urine culture and sensitivity, commonly using trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole or enrofloxacin. Provide IV fluid therapy to promote diuresis and correct dehydration. Address underlying causes such as urolithiasis surgically if present, and monitor renal function via serial bloodwork and urinalysis.
treatment_ja: 尿培養および感受性試験に基づき、トリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾールまたはエンロフロキサシン等の抗菌薬を最低4〜6週間投与する。静脈内輸液療法により利尿を促進し脱水を補正する。尿路結石などの基礎疾患がある場合は外科的に対処し、血液検査および尿検査により腎機能を継続的にモニタリングする。

name: Renal Fungal Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Fungal organisms, most commonly Aspergillus spp. or Candida spp., colonize the renal parenchyma and/or renal pelvis, leading to granulomatous or necrotizing inflammation. This results in progressive destruction of renal tissue, impaired renal function, and potentially formation of fungal masses (fungal balls) that can obstruct urine outflow. Hematogenous dissemination from a primary site or ascending infection from the lower urinary tract may contribute to renal involvement.
pathophysiology_ja: 主にAspergillus属やCandida属などの真菌が腎実質や腎盂に定着し、肉芽腫性または壊死性の炎症を引き起こす。これにより腎組織の進行性破壊、腎機能障害が生じ、真菌塊（ファンガスボール）が形成されて尿路閉塞を引き起こすことがある。原発巣からの血行性播種や下部尿路からの上行性感染が腎への波及経路となる。
causes: Primary causes include opportunistic fungal infections by Aspergillus spp., Candida spp., or other environmental fungi. Secondary causes and predisposing factors include prolonged antibiotic therapy, immunosuppression (e.g., corticosteroid use), indwelling urinary catheters, and debilitation from chronic illness. Pre-existing renal damage or urinary stasis may also facilitate fungal colonization.
treatment: Systemic antifungal therapy with amphotericin B (0.3–0.5 mg/kg IV slowly every 48 hrs) combined with fluconazole (5 mg/kg PO q24h) for prolonged courses (weeks to months). Discontinue predisposing antibiotics or immunosuppressants. Nephrectomy may be indicated for unilateral fungal granulomas unresponsive to medical therapy. Provide IV fluid support to maintain renal perfusion and monitor renal values closely.
treatment_ja: アムホテリシンB（0.3〜0.5 mg/kg IV、48時間ごと緩徐投与）とフルコナゾール（5 mg/kg PO、1日1回）の全身性抗真菌療法を数週間〜数か月間実施する。誘因となる抗菌薬や免疫抑制剤は中止する。片側性の真菌性肉芽腫で内科治療に反応しない場合は腎摘出術を検討する。輸液療法で腎灌流を維持し、腎機能値を頻回にモニタリングする。

name: Renal Infection (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infection (pyelonephritis) in horses typically occurs via ascending bacterial infection from the lower urinary tract through the ureters to the renal pelvis and parenchyma. Bacteria colonize the renal medulla, triggering an inflammatory response that leads to tissue destruction, abscess formation, and impaired renal function. Chronic infection can result in progressive nephron loss, fibrosis, and potentially renal failure if bilateral involvement occurs.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路から尿管を経由して腎盂および腎実質へ細菌が上行性に感染することで発生します。細菌が腎髄質に定着し、炎症反応を引き起こして組織破壊、膿瘍形成、腎機能障害をもたらします。慢性感染は進行性のネフロン喪失や線維化を引き起こし、両側性の場合は腎不全に至る可能性があります。
causes: The primary cause is ascending bacterial infection, most commonly by Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Corynebacterium renale, or Actinobacillus equuli. Predisposing factors include urolithiasis, urinary stasis, bladder paralysis, catheterization, immunosuppression, and anatomical abnormalities. Hematogenous spread from distant infection sites is a less common secondary cause.
treatment: Initiate prolonged systemic antibiotic therapy (4-6 weeks) based on urine culture and sensitivity, commonly trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole or enrofloxacin for gram-negative pathogens. Provide IV fluid therapy to maintain renal perfusion and promote diuresis. Address underlying predisposing factors such as urolithiasis or bladder dysfunction, and consider nephrectomy if unilateral infection is refractory to medical management.
treatment_ja: 尿培養・感受性試験に基づき、トリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾールやエンロフロキサシンなどの全身性抗菌薬を4〜6週間長期投与する。静脈内輸液療法で腎灌流を維持し利尿を促進する。尿路結石や膀胱機能障害などの素因を是正し、片側性感染で内科的治療に抵抗性の場合は腎摘出術を検討する。

name: Renal Inflammation (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal inflammation (nephritis) in horses involves immune-mediated or infectious damage to the glomeruli, tubules, or interstitium of the kidneys, leading to impaired filtration, proteinuria, and azotemia. Inflammatory cell infiltration and edema disrupt normal nephron function, potentially progressing to fibrosis and chronic renal insufficiency. Glomerulonephritis may result from immune complex deposition, while tubulointerstitial nephritis often follows toxic or infectious insults.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎炎（腎臓の炎症）は、免疫介在性または感染性の障害により糸球体、尿細管、または間質が損傷を受け、濾過機能の低下、蛋白尿、高窒素血症を引き起こす。炎症細胞の浸潤と浮腫がネフロン機能を障害し、線維化や慢性腎不全に進行する可能性がある。糸球体腎炎は免疫複合体の沈着により、尿細管間質性腎炎は中毒性または感染性の障害に続いて生じることが多い。
causes: Primary causes include bacterial infections (e.g., leptospirosis, streptococcal infections), viral infections (e.g., equine infectious anemia), and nephrotoxic agents such as NSAIDs, aminoglycosides, and heavy metals. Secondary causes include immune-mediated diseases, systemic infections leading to immune complex deposition, dehydration, and hemodynamic compromise from endotoxemia or severe colic.
treatment: Discontinue nephrotoxic agents (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides) immediately. Administer IV fluid therapy (lactated Ringer's or 0.9% NaCl) to correct dehydration and support renal perfusion. Treat underlying infections with renal-safe antibiotics (e.g., penicillin, trimethoprim-sulfa); consider corticosteroids (dexamethasone 0.05-0.1 mg/kg IV) for immune-mediated nephritis, and provide electrolyte monitoring with supportive care.
treatment_ja: 腎毒性薬剤（NSAIDs、アミノグリコシド系）を直ちに中止する。乳酸リンゲル液または生理食塩水による静脈内輸液療法を実施し、脱水の補正と腎灌流の維持を図る。基礎感染症には腎安全性の高い抗菌薬（ペニシリン、トリメトプリム・スルファ剤）を投与し、免疫介在性腎炎にはデキサメタゾン（0.05〜0.1 mg/kg IV）を検討する。電解質モニタリングと対症療法を継続する。

name: Renal Neoplasia (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal neoplasia in horses involves the uncontrolled proliferation of cells within the kidney parenchyma or renal pelvis. The most commonly reported types include renal cell carcinoma, nephroblastoma, and lymphoma, which can disrupt normal renal architecture, impair kidney function, and potentially metastasize to lungs, liver, and other organs. Tumor growth may cause progressive renal insufficiency, hematuria, and space-occupying effects leading to abdominal discomfort.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎腫瘍は、腎実質または腎盂内の細胞が制御不能に増殖することで発生します。最も一般的に報告される種類には腎細胞癌、腎芽腫、リンパ腫があり、正常な腎構造を破壊し、腎機能を障害し、肺や肝臓などへ転移する可能性があります。腫瘍の増大により進行性の腎不全、血尿、腹部不快感を引き起こすことがあります。
causes: The exact etiology of renal neoplasia in horses is largely unknown. Potential contributing factors include genetic predisposition, chronic renal inflammation or irritation, and age-related cellular mutations. Nephroblastoma tends to occur in younger horses, suggesting possible congenital or developmental origins, while renal cell carcinoma is more common in older horses.
treatment: Primary treatment is unilateral nephrectomy when the tumor is confined to one kidney and no metastasis is detected. Supportive care includes IV fluid therapy, NSAIDs (flunixin meglumine 1.1 mg/kg IV) for pain management, and broad-spectrum antibiotics perioperatively. Chemotherapy options are limited in horses and prognosis is guarded if metastasis is present.
treatment_ja: 腫瘍が片側の腎臓に限局し転移がない場合、片側腎摘出術が第一選択治療となる。術前後の支持療法として輸液療法、疼痛管理にフルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg 静脈内投与）、および広域スペクトル抗菌薬の投与を行う。馬における化学療法の選択肢は限られており、転移が認められる場合の予後は慎重である。

name: Renal Metabolic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal metabolic disease in horses involves impaired kidney function leading to disrupted electrolyte balance, acid-base homeostasis, and waste product excretion. The kidneys fail to adequately regulate calcium, phosphorus, and other mineral metabolism, potentially resulting in hypercalcemia or hyperphosphatemia, metabolic acidosis, and azotemia. Chronic dysfunction can lead to renal secondary hyperparathyroidism, soft tissue mineralization, and progressive nephron loss.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎代謝疾患は、腎機能の障害により電解質バランス、酸塩基平衡、および老廃物の排泄が乱れる疾患である。腎臓がカルシウム、リン、その他のミネラル代謝を適切に調節できなくなり、高カルシウム血症や高リン血症、代謝性アシドーシス、高窒素血症を引き起こす。慢性的な機能障害は腎性二次性副甲状腺機能亢進症、軟部組織の石灰化、進行性のネフロン喪失につながる可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include chronic kidney disease (CKD), nephrolithiasis, nephrotoxin exposure (such as aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals, or oxalate-containing plants), and chronic dehydration. Secondary causes include systemic conditions such as leptospirosis, pyelonephritis, hemodynamic compromise, and age-related nephron degeneration. Excessive dietary calcium or imbalanced calcium-to-phosphorus ratios may also contribute to renal metabolic dysfunction.
treatment: Administer IV fluid therapy (balanced polyionic solutions) to correct dehydration and promote diuresis. Address electrolyte imbalances with calcium gluconate or phosphate binders as needed. Discontinue nephrotoxic agents (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides), provide dietary management with low-protein, low-calcium feed, and treat underlying infections with appropriate antimicrobials such as trimethoprim-sulfadiazine.
treatment_ja: 脱水補正と利尿促進のため、バランス電解質輸液（ポリイオン液）の静脈内投与を行う。必要に応じてグルコン酸カルシウムやリン吸着剤で電解質異常を是正する。腎毒性薬剤（NSAIDs、アミノグリコシド系）を中止し、低タンパク質・低カルシウム飼料による食事管理を実施し、基礎感染症にはトリメトプリム・スルファジアジン等の適切な抗菌薬で治療する。

name: Renal Nutritional Deficiency (Horse)
pathophysiology: Nutritional deficiencies, particularly of vitamin A, vitamin D, calcium, phosphorus, or oxalate-rich diets, can lead to renal damage through nephrocalcinosis, tubular degeneration, and impaired renal function. Imbalanced calcium-phosphorus ratios or excessive oxalate intake causes mineral deposition in renal tubules and parenchyma, leading to progressive nephropathy. Chronic deficiency or toxicity disrupts normal renal filtration and concentrating ability, potentially resulting in renal fibrosis and failure.
pathophysiology_ja: ビタミンA、ビタミンD、カルシウム、リンなどの栄養欠乏やシュウ酸塩を多く含む飼料の摂取により、腎石灰化症、尿細管変性、腎機能障害が生じる。カルシウム・リン比の不均衡やシュウ酸塩の過剰摂取は腎尿細管および実質にミネラル沈着を引き起こし、進行性腎症をもたらす。慢性的な栄養欠乏または過剰は正常な腎濾過・濃縮機能を障害し、腎線維化および腎不全に至る可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include dietary deficiencies of vitamin A, vitamin D, or imbalanced calcium-phosphorus ratios, as well as excessive intake of oxalate-containing plants (such as sorrel, rhubarb, or tropical grasses). Secondary causes include chronic ingestion of nephrotoxic plants, prolonged poor-quality forage, and inadequate mineral supplementation leading to metabolic disturbances affecting renal function.
treatment: Correct dietary imbalances by adjusting calcium-phosphorus ratios (ideally 2:1), supplementing vitamin A (50,000-100,000 IU/day) and vitamin D as needed, and eliminating oxalate-rich plants from the diet. Provide IV fluid therapy (balanced polyionic solutions) to support renal perfusion and promote diuresis. Administer supportive care including electrolyte correction and gradual dietary transition to high-quality forage.
treatment_ja: カルシウム・リン比（理想的には2:1）の是正、ビタミンA（50,000～100,000 IU/日）およびビタミンDの必要に応じた補給、シュウ酸含有植物の飼料からの除去により食餌バランスを改善する。腎灌流維持と利尿促進のためバランス電解質輸液を静脈内投与する。電解質補正および良質な乾草への段階的な飼料転換を含む支持療法を実施する。

name: Renal Genetic Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal genetic disorders in horses involve inherited mutations affecting renal tubular or glomerular structure and function, leading to progressive nephron loss, impaired filtration, and disrupted electrolyte and fluid homeostasis. Examples include renal dysplasia and polycystic kidney disease, where abnormal renal development or cyst formation results in progressive renal insufficiency. Over time, compensatory mechanisms fail, leading to azotemia, uremia, and multi-organ consequences of chronic kidney disease.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎臓遺伝性疾患は、腎尿細管や糸球体の構造と機能に影響を与える遺伝子変異に起因し、進行性のネフロン喪失、濾過障害、電解質・水分バランスの異常を引き起こします。腎異形成や多発性嚢胞腎などが含まれ、腎臓の異常発達や嚢胞形成により進行性の腎機能不全に至ります。代償機構が破綻すると、高窒素血症や尿毒症、多臓器への影響が生じます。
causes: The primary cause is inherited genetic mutations that disrupt normal renal development or function, often following autosomal recessive or dominant inheritance patterns depending on the specific disorder. Specific mutations may affect genes involved in renal tubular differentiation, basement membrane formation, or ciliary function. Secondary factors such as concurrent infections, dehydration, or nephrotoxic exposure may accelerate disease progression in genetically predisposed individuals.
treatment: No curative treatment exists for renal genetic disorders in horses; management is supportive. Intravenous fluid therapy corrects dehydration and electrolyte imbalances. ACE inhibitors (e.g., enalapril 0.5 mg/kg PO q24h) may slow proteinuria progression. Dietary phosphorus restriction, oral phosphate binders, and monitoring of BUN/creatinine guide ongoing renal support. Severely affected foals may require humane euthanasia.
treatment_ja: 馬の腎遺伝性疾患に根治療法は存在せず、治療は対症療法が中心です。静脈輸液療法により脱水および電解質異常を補正します。ACE阻害薬（例：エナラプリル0.5 mg/kg 経口 1日1回）で蛋白尿の進行を抑制します。食餌中のリン制限、経口リン吸着剤の投与、BUN・クレアチニンの定期モニタリングにより腎機能を管理します。重症の仔馬には安楽死の検討が必要となる場合があります。

name: Renal Autoimmune Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: The immune system produces autoantibodies or autoreactive lymphocytes directed against renal antigens, including glomerular basement membrane components and tubular epithelial cells. Immune complex deposition or direct antibody-mediated injury leads to glomerulonephritis, tubulointerstitial nephritis, and progressive destruction of renal parenchyma. Complement activation and inflammatory cell infiltration further exacerbate tissue damage, resulting in impaired renal function and potential progression to chronic kidney disease.
pathophysiology_ja: 免疫系が糸球体基底膜成分や尿細管上皮細胞などの腎抗原に対する自己抗体または自己反応性リンパ球を産生する。免疫複合体の沈着や抗体介在性の直接的な障害により、糸球体腎炎、尿細管間質性腎炎、および腎実質の進行性破壊が生じる。補体の活性化と炎症細胞の浸潤がさらに組織損傷を悪化させ、腎機能障害および慢性腎臓病への進行を引き起こす。
causes: The primary cause is immune dysregulation leading to loss of self-tolerance against renal antigens, potentially triggered by genetic predisposition. Secondary causes include preceding infections (e.g., Streptococcus equi, equine infectious anemia), drug reactions, systemic autoimmune conditions such as systemic lupus erythematosus-like syndrome, and chronic antigenic stimulation from persistent infections that result in molecular mimicry or bystander activation.
treatment: Immunosuppressive therapy with corticosteroids (dexamethasone 0.05-0.1 mg/kg IV/IM daily, tapering over weeks) is first-line. Azathioprine (3 mg/kg PO daily) may be added for steroid-sparing effect. Supportive care includes IV fluid therapy for renal perfusion, ACE inhibitors (benazepril 0.5 mg/kg PO) to reduce proteinuria, and monitoring renal parameters closely.
treatment_ja: 免疫抑制療法として副腎皮質ステロイド（デキサメタゾン0.05〜0.1 mg/kg IV/IM、漸減投与）を第一選択とする。アザチオプリン（3 mg/kg PO）をステロイド節減目的で併用可能。支持療法として腎灌流維持のための輸液、蛋白尿軽減のためACE阻害薬（ベナゼプリル0.5 mg/kg PO）を投与し、腎機能パラメータを綿密にモニタリングする。

name: Renal Degenerative Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal degenerative disease in horses involves progressive deterioration of renal parenchyma, including tubular degeneration, interstitial fibrosis, and glomerulosclerosis, leading to impaired filtration, concentration, and excretion functions. Chronic nephron loss results in azotemia, electrolyte imbalances, and eventual renal failure. The remaining nephrons undergo compensatory hypertrophy but ultimately fail to maintain adequate renal function.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎変性疾患は、尿細管変性、間質線維化、糸球体硬化症を含む腎実質の進行性劣化を伴い、濾過・濃縮・排泄機能の障害をもたらす。慢性的なネフロンの喪失により高窒素血症、電解質異常、最終的には腎不全に至る。残存ネフロンは代償性肥大を起こすが、最終的に十分な腎機能を維持できなくなる。
causes: Primary causes include chronic exposure to nephrotoxins (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals, vitamin D toxicosis), oxalate-containing plants, and age-related degenerative changes. Secondary causes include chronic renal ischemia, recurrent pyelonephritis, nephrolithiasis, and systemic diseases such as equine infectious anemia or immune-mediated glomerulonephritis. Idiopathic cases with no identifiable underlying cause are also commonly reported.
treatment: Treatment is primarily supportive: IV fluid therapy (polyionic isotonic fluids) to correct dehydration and electrolyte imbalances, discontinuation of all nephrotoxic agents (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides), and dietary management with reduced protein and calcium. ACE inhibitors (enalapril 0.5 mg/kg PO q24h) may help manage proteinuria. Phosphate binders (aluminum hydroxide 30-90 mg/kg PO) address hyperphosphatemia, and sodium bicarbonate corrects metabolic acidosis.
treatment_ja: 治療は主に対症療法で、脱水・電解質異常の補正に等張性輸液を静脈内投与し、腎毒性薬剤（NSAIDs、アミノグリコシド系）を直ちに中止する。低タンパク・低カルシウム食による食事管理を行う。蛋白尿にはACE阻害薬（エナラプリル0.5 mg/kg 経口 1日1回）を使用し、高リン血症には水酸化アルミニウム（30-90 mg/kg 経口）、代謝性アシドーシスには重炭酸ナトリウムを投与する。

name: Renal Traumatic Injury (Horse)
pathophysiology: Blunt or penetrating trauma to the lumbar region causes direct parenchymal damage to the kidney, leading to hemorrhage, disruption of the renal capsule, and potential urine leakage into the retroperitoneal space. Subsequent inflammation, hematoma formation, and possible ischemia of renal tissue may result in progressive nephron loss. In severe cases, vascular pedicle injury can cause life-threatening hemorrhage or renal infarction.
pathophysiology_ja: 腰部への鈍的または穿通性外傷により腎実質が直接損傷を受け、出血、腎被膜の破裂、および後腹膜腔への尿漏出が生じる。続発する炎症、血腫形成、および腎組織の虚血によりネフロンの進行性喪失が起こりうる。重症例では腎血管茎の損傷により致命的な出血や腎梗塞を引き起こす可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include blunt abdominal or lumbar trauma from falls, kicks from other horses, collisions with fixed objects, or accidents during transport. Secondary causes may include iatrogenic injury during percutaneous renal biopsy or surgical procedures, and rarely penetrating wounds from foreign bodies or sharp objects. Violent exertion or severe casting injuries during anesthetic recovery can also contribute.
causes_ja: 主な原因は、落馬、他馬からの蹴り、固定物への衝突、輸送中の事故などによる腹部・腰部への鈍的外傷である。二次的原因として、経皮的腎生検や外科手術中の医原性損傷、まれに異物や鋭利な物体による穿通創がある。激しい運動や麻酔覚醒時の転倒による損傷も原因となりうる。
treatment: Stabilize with IV crystalloid fluids (LRS or 0.9% NaCl) for hemorrhagic shock; administer flunixin meglumine (1.1 mg/kg IV q12h) for pain and inflammation, and broad-spectrum antibiotics (e.g., penicillin-gentamicin). Monitor hematocrit and renal values closely. Surgical intervention (nephrectomy) is indicated for uncontrolled hemorrhage or severe capsular disruption.
treatment_ja: 出血性ショックに対し乳酸リンゲル液または生理食塩水の静脈内輸液で循環を安定させ、フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg IV 12時間毎）で鎮痛・抗炎症を図り、ペニシリン・ゲンタマイシン等の広域抗菌薬を投与する。ヘマトクリット値および腎機能を頻回にモニタリングし、制御不能な出血や腎被膜の高度損傷がある場合は腎摘出術を検討する。

name: Renal Behavioral Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal behavioral disorder in horses involves abnormal behaviors (such as frequent posturing to urinate, excessive flank watching, or stretching) associated with renal pain or dysfunction. Chronic or acute renal inflammation, calculi, or nephritis can stimulate visceral pain pathways, leading to characteristic postural and behavioral changes. The discomfort originating from the kidneys or upper urinary tract manifests as stereotypic pain-related behaviors rather than overt systemic illness in early stages.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎行動障害は、腎臓の痛みや機能障害に関連した異常行動（頻繁な排尿姿勢、過度の脇腹注視、伸展姿勢など）を伴います。慢性または急性の腎炎症、結石、腎炎が内臓痛経路を刺激し、特徴的な姿勢および行動変化を引き起こします。腎臓や上部尿路に由来する不快感が、初期段階では全身性の明らかな疾患ではなく、疼痛関連の常同行動として現れます。
causes: Primary causes include renal calculi (nephrolithiasis), pyelonephritis, renal neoplasia, and chronic interstitial nephritis causing persistent renal pain. Secondary causes may involve ureterolithiasis, renal cysts, perirenal abscess, or referred pain from adjacent structures. Toxic nephropathies from plants (e.g., oak, red maple) or medications (e.g., NSAIDs) can also contribute to renal discomfort manifesting as behavioral changes.
treatment: Administer analgesics such as flunixin meglumine (1.1 mg/kg IV q12h) or butorphanol (0.01-0.04 mg/kg IV) for visceral pain control. Treat underlying causes: antibiotics (trimethoprim-sulfonamide 30 mg/kg PO BID) for pyelonephritis, surgical removal of renal calculi if indicated, and IV fluid therapy to support renal perfusion and diuresis.
treatment_ja: 内臓痛の管理としてフルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg IV 12時間毎）やブトルファノール（0.01-0.04 mg/kg IV）を投与する。原因疾患に応じ、腎盂腎炎にはトリメトプリム・スルホンアミド（30 mg/kg PO BID）を使用し、腎結石が確認された場合は外科的除去を検討する。腎灌流と利尿促進のため静脈内輸液療法を併用し、腎機能の維持を図る。

name: Renal Infectious Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infectious disease in horses involves bacterial invasion of the renal parenchyma, typically via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract or hematogenous spread. Bacteria such as Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., or Actinobacillus equuli colonize the renal pelvis and parenchyma, leading to inflammation (pyelonephritis), abscess formation, and progressive destruction of nephrons. This results in impaired renal function, azotemia, and potential systemic sepsis if untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症は、下部尿路からの上行感染または血行性播種により細菌が腎実質に侵入することで発生します。大腸菌、レンサ球菌、アクチノバチルス・エクーリなどの細菌が腎盂および腎実質に定着し、炎症（腎盂腎炎）、膿瘍形成、およびネフロンの進行性破壊を引き起こします。これにより腎機能障害、高窒素血症、未治療の場合は全身性敗血症に至る可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infections (most commonly E. coli, Streptococcus spp., Corynebacterium spp.) from the lower urinary tract, and hematogenous spread from distant infection sites. Secondary causes and predisposing factors include urolithiasis, urinary tract obstruction, immunosuppression, catheterization, bladder paralysis, and chronic lower urinary tract infections.
treatment: Initiate broad-spectrum antimicrobial therapy based on culture and sensitivity, commonly trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (30 mg/kg PO BID) or enrofloxacin (5 mg/kg IV/PO SID) for 2-4 weeks. Provide aggressive IV fluid therapy (crystalloids) to maintain renal perfusion and urine flow. Address underlying causes such as urolithiasis or obstruction surgically if needed, and administer NSAIDs (flunixin meglumine 1.1 mg/kg IV) for pain and inflammation control.
treatment_ja: 培養・感受性試験に基づき広域スペクトル抗菌薬を開始する。一般的にトリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾール（30 mg/kg 経口 1日2回）またはエンロフロキサシン（5 mg/kg 静注/経口 1日1回）を2〜4週間投与する。積極的な輸液療法（晶質液の静脈内投与）により腎灌流と尿流量を維持する。尿石症や尿路閉塞などの基礎疾患がある場合は外科的に対処し、疼痛・炎症管理としてフルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg 静注）を投与する。

name: Renal Parasitic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal parasitic disease in horses involves migration and colonization of parasites such as Halicephalobus gingivalis (formerly Halicephalobus deletrix), Strongylus vulgaris larvae, or Dioctophyme renale within the renal parenchyma and vasculature. Parasitic invasion causes granulomatous inflammation, tubular destruction, and interstitial nephritis, leading to progressive renal dysfunction. Larval migration through renal arteries may also cause thrombosis and ischemic damage to the kidney.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎寄生虫疾患は、Halicephalobus gingivalis、普通円虫（Strongylus vulgaris）の幼虫、または腎虫（Dioctophyme renale）などの寄生虫が腎実質や血管系に移行・定着することで発症する。寄生虫の侵入は肉芽腫性炎症、尿細管破壊、間質性腎炎を引き起こし、進行性の腎機能障害をもたらす。幼虫の腎動脈内移行は血栓症や腎臓の虚血性障害を引き起こすこともある。
causes: Primary causes include aberrant migration of Strongylus vulgaris larvae through mesenteric and renal vasculature, infection with Halicephalobus gingivalis (a free-living nematode capable of opportunistic tissue invasion), and rarely Dioctophyme renale (giant kidney worm). Secondary causes include immunosuppression or heavy parasite burden facilitating aberrant larval migration to the kidneys.
treatment: Administer high-dose fenbendazole (10 mg/kg PO daily for 5 days) or ivermectin (0.2 mg/kg PO) to target migrating larvae; for Halicephalobus gingivalis, prolonged courses of fenbendazole or moxidectin may be attempted though prognosis is guarded. Supportive care includes IV fluid therapy, NSAIDs (flunixin meglumine 1.1 mg/kg IV) for inflammation, and nephrectomy of the affected kidney in unilateral cases with severe parenchymal destruction.
treatment_ja: フェンベンダゾール高用量投与（10 mg/kg 経口、5日間連続）またはイベルメクチン（0.2 mg/kg 経口）で移行幼虫を標的とする。Halicephalobus gingivalis感染にはフェンベンダゾールまたはモキシデクチンの長期投与を試みるが予後は慎重である。支持療法として輸液療法、フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg 静注）による抗炎症治療を実施し、片側性で腎実質の重度破壊がある場合は患側腎の腎摘出術を検討する。

name: Renal Viral Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Viral agents such as equine herpesvirus (EHV) or equine arteritis virus (EAV) can cause vasculitis and immune-mediated damage to renal glomeruli and tubular epithelium, leading to impaired renal filtration and tubular necrosis. Immune complex deposition in renal vasculature contributes to glomerulonephritis, progressive renal insufficiency, and potentially acute kidney injury. Secondary inflammation and edema further compromise renal blood flow and parenchymal function.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬ヘルペスウイルス（EHV）や馬動脈炎ウイルス（EAV）などのウイルスが血管炎や免疫介在性の糸球体および尿細管上皮障害を引き起こし、腎濾過機能の低下や尿細管壊死をもたらす。腎血管への免疫複合体の沈着が糸球体腎炎や進行性腎不全、急性腎障害の原因となる。二次的な炎症や浮腫がさらに腎血流と実質機能を障害する。
causes: Primary causes include viral infections such as equine herpesvirus (EHV-1, EHV-4), equine arteritis virus (EAV), and occasionally equine infectious anemia virus (EIAV) that target or secondarily affect renal tissue. Secondary causes include immune complex deposition, systemic vasculitis, dehydration, and concurrent bacterial infections that exacerbate renal damage.
treatment: No specific antiviral cure exists; treatment is supportive. Administer IV balanced polyionic fluids (e.g., lactated Ringer's solution) to maintain renal perfusion and correct electrolyte imbalances. Use flunixin meglumine (1.1 mg/kg IV q12-24h) for anti-inflammatory and anti-endotoxic effects. Consider corticosteroids cautiously for immune-mediated glomerulonephritis. Monitor renal parameters (BUN, creatinine) closely and manage secondary bacterial infections with nephro-safe antibiotics such as penicillin.
treatment_ja: 特異的な抗ウイルス療法は存在せず、治療は対症療法が中心となる。腎灌流の維持と電解質補正のため、乳酸リンゲル液などの等張輸液を静脈内投与する。フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg IV 12-24時間毎）を抗炎症・抗エンドトキシン目的で使用する。免疫介在性糸球体腎炎にはコルチコステロイドの慎重な投与を検討する。BUN・クレアチニン等の腎機能指標を継続的にモニタリングし、二次的細菌感染にはペニシリン等の腎毒性の低い抗菌薬を選択する。

name: Renal Bacterial Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Bacterial pathogens, commonly Escherichia coli, Actinobacillus spp., Streptococcus spp., or Corynebacterium spp., ascend via the lower urinary tract or spread hematogenously to the renal parenchyma. This leads to inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tubules and interstitium (pyelonephritis), potentially impairing glomerular filtration and concentrating ability. Chronic infection may result in fibrosis, nephrolithiasis, and eventual renal insufficiency or failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 大腸菌、アクチノバチルス属、レンサ球菌属、コリネバクテリウム属などの細菌が下部尿路からの上行感染または血行性に腎実質に到達し、炎症・膿瘍形成を引き起こします。これにより腎尿細管および間質の進行性破壊（腎盂腎炎）が生じ、糸球体濾過率や濃縮能が障害されます。慢性感染では線維化、腎結石、最終的に腎不全に至る可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infection from the lower urinary tract (most common), often associated with E. coli, Streptococcus spp., Actinobacillus spp., and Corynebacterium renale. Secondary causes and predisposing factors include urolithiasis, urinary tract obstruction, bladder paralysis, catheterization, immunosuppression, and hematogenous spread from distant infectious foci such as endocarditis or abscesses.
treatment: Administer prolonged systemic antibiotics (4-6 weeks minimum) based on urine culture and sensitivity, commonly trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole or enrofloxacin for gram-negative pathogens, or penicillin for Streptococcus spp. Provide IV fluid therapy to maintain renal perfusion and correct azotemia. Address predisposing factors such as urolithiasis or urinary obstruction surgically if indicated; consider nephrectomy for unilateral renal abscessation unresponsive to medical therapy.
treatment_ja: 尿培養・感受性試験に基づき、長期間（最低4〜6週間）の全身性抗菌薬投与を行う。グラム陰性菌にはトリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾールまたはエンロフロキサシン、Streptococcus属にはペニシリンを選択する。腎灌流維持および高窒素血症の是正のため輸液療法を実施する。尿路結石や尿路閉塞などの素因がある場合は外科的に対処し、片側性腎膿瘍が内科療法に反応しない場合は腎摘出術を検討する。

name: Renal Fungal Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Fungal organisms, most commonly Aspergillus spp. or Candida spp., colonize the renal parenchyma and/or renal pelvis, causing granulomatous or necrotizing inflammation. The infection may result in progressive destruction of renal tissue, obstruction of the collecting system by fungal masses (fungal balls), and potential hematogenous dissemination. Immunosuppression, prolonged antibiotic therapy, or indwelling urinary catheters predispose to fungal colonization and ascending or hematogenous renal infection.
pathophysiology_ja: 主にAspergillus属やCandida属などの真菌が腎実質や腎盂に定着し、肉芽腫性または壊死性の炎症を引き起こします。感染は腎組織の進行性破壊、真菌塊（ファンガスボール）による集合系の閉塞、および血行性播種を引き起こす可能性があります。免疫抑制、長期抗菌薬投与、または留置尿道カテーテルが真菌の定着および上行性・血行性腎感染の素因となります。
causes: Primary causes include infection by opportunistic fungi such as Aspergillus spp., Candida spp., or less commonly Cryptococcus or Mucor spp., typically via hematogenous spread or ascending urinary tract infection. Secondary contributing factors include prolonged broad-spectrum antibiotic therapy, immunosuppression (from corticosteroid use, concurrent illness, or stress), and urinary tract instrumentation or catheterization.
treatment: Systemic antifungal therapy with fluconazole (5 mg/kg PO q24h) or amphotericin B (0.3-0.5 mg/kg IV slowly in dextrose) for Aspergillus or Candida infections. Discontinue broad-spectrum antibiotics and correct underlying immunosuppression. Nephrectomy may be considered for unilateral disease with extensive parenchymal destruction or obstructive fungal masses unresponsive to medical therapy.
treatment_ja: フルコナゾール（5 mg/kg 経口 1日1回）またはアムホテリシンB（0.3〜0.5 mg/kg ブドウ糖液で緩徐に静注）による全身性抗真菌療法を実施する。広域抗菌薬の投与を中止し、基礎にある免疫抑制状態を是正する。片側性で腎実質の広範な破壊や閉塞性真菌塊が内科治療に反応しない場合は、腎摘出術を検討する。

name: Renal Infection (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infection (pyelonephritis) in horses typically occurs via ascending bacterial infection from the lower urinary tract through the ureters to the renal pelvis and parenchyma. Bacteria such as Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., and Corynebacterium renale colonize the renal tissue, causing inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal parenchyma. If bilateral or left untreated, it can lead to chronic renal failure due to irreversible nephron loss and fibrosis.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路から尿管を経由して腎盂および腎実質へ細菌が上行性に感染することで発生します。大腸菌、レンサ球菌、コリネバクテリウム・レナーレなどの細菌が腎組織に定着し、炎症、膿瘍形成、腎実質の進行性破壊を引き起こします。両側性または未治療の場合、ネフロンの不可逆的喪失と線維化により慢性腎不全に至ることがあります。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infections from cystitis or urethritis, commonly involving E. coli, Streptococcus spp., Actinobacillus spp., and Corynebacterium renale. Secondary causes include urolithiasis causing urinary stasis, urinary tract obstruction, immunosuppression, and catheterization-related contamination. Nephrolithiasis and anatomical abnormalities predisposing to urine stagnation can also contribute.
treatment: Initiate aggressive systemic antibiotic therapy based on urine culture and sensitivity, commonly trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (30 mg/kg PO BID) or enrofloxacin (5 mg/kg IV/PO SID) for 2-4 weeks. Provide IV fluid therapy to maintain hydration and promote diuresis. Address underlying causes such as urolithiasis or obstruction surgically if needed, and monitor renal function via serial bloodwork and urinalysis.
treatment_ja: 尿培養・感受性試験に基づき、トリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾール（30 mg/kg PO BID）またはエンロフロキサシン（5 mg/kg IV/PO SID）などの全身性抗菌薬を2〜4週間投与する。静脈内輸液療法で水分補給と利尿を促進する。尿路結石や閉塞などの基礎疾患がある場合は外科的に対処し、血液検査および尿検査で腎機能を継続的にモニタリングする。

name: Renal Inflammation (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal inflammation (nephritis) in horses involves immune-mediated or infectious damage to the glomeruli, tubules, or interstitium of the kidneys, leading to impaired filtration, protein loss, electrolyte imbalances, and accumulation of metabolic waste products. Inflammatory cell infiltration and edema disrupt normal renal architecture, potentially progressing to fibrosis and chronic renal insufficiency if untreated. Glomerulonephritis often results from immune complex deposition, while tubulointerstitial nephritis may follow toxic or infectious insults.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎炎は、免疫介在性または感染性の障害により糸球体、尿細管、または間質が損傷を受け、濾過機能の低下、タンパク質喪失、電解質異常、代謝老廃物の蓄積を引き起こす。炎症細胞浸潤と浮腫が正常な腎構造を破壊し、未治療の場合は線維化や慢性腎不全に進行する可能性がある。糸球体腎炎は免疫複合体沈着により、尿細管間質性腎炎は毒性物質や感染症に続発することが多い。
causes: Primary causes include bacterial infections (e.g., Leptospira, Streptococcus equi), viral infections (e.g., equine infectious anemia), and nephrotoxic agents such as NSAIDs, aminoglycosides, heavy metals, and certain plants. Secondary causes include immune complex deposition from chronic infections or systemic diseases, septicemia, endotoxemia, and hemodynamic compromise leading to ischemic renal injury. Equine proliferative nephritis associated with Klossiella equi parasites is also recognized.
treatment: Discontinue all nephrotoxic agents (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides). Administer aggressive IV fluid therapy (balanced polyionic solutions) to restore renal perfusion and correct electrolyte imbalances. Treat underlying infections with renal-safe antimicrobials (e.g., penicillin for Streptococcus, oxytetracycline for Leptospira). Corticosteroids (dexamethasone) may be used for immune-mediated nephritis. Monitor serum creatinine, BUN, and urine output closely.
treatment_ja: すべての腎毒性薬剤（NSAIDs、アミノグリコシド系）を直ちに中止する。積極的な静脈内輸液療法（バランス電解質液）により腎灌流を回復し、電解質異常を補正する。基礎感染症には腎安全性の高い抗菌薬（レンサ球菌にはペニシリン、レプトスピラにはオキシテトラサイクリン）を投与する。免疫介在性腎炎にはデキサメタゾンの使用を検討する。血清クレアチニン、BUN、尿量を継続的にモニタリングする。

name: Renal Neoplasia (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal neoplasia in horses involves uncontrolled proliferation of renal parenchymal or mesenchymal cells, leading to progressive destruction of normal kidney architecture and impaired renal function. The most commonly reported types include renal cell carcinoma, nephroblastoma, and lymphoma. Tumor growth may cause local tissue invasion, obstruction of urine flow, hematuria, and in malignant cases, metastasis to lungs, liver, and other organs.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎腫瘍は、腎実質または間葉系細胞の制御されない増殖を伴い、正常な腎臓構造の進行性破壊と腎機能の低下を引き起こす。最も一般的に報告される腫瘍には腎細胞癌、腎芽腫（ネフロブラストーマ）、およびリンパ腫がある。腫瘍の成長は局所組織への浸潤、尿流の閉塞、血尿を引き起こし、悪性の場合は肺、肝臓などへの転移が生じる。
causes: The exact etiology of renal neoplasia in horses is largely unknown, though genetic predisposition, chronic irritation, and environmental carcinogens may play a role. Renal cell carcinoma is the most common primary renal tumor in adult horses, while nephroblastoma is more frequently seen in younger horses. Renal lymphoma may occur as part of multicentric lymphoma.
treatment: Unilateral nephrectomy is the primary treatment for localized renal tumors such as renal cell carcinoma or nephroblastoma, provided the contralateral kidney is functional. Supportive care includes IV fluid therapy, NSAIDs (flunixin meglumine 1.1 mg/kg IV) for pain management, and monitoring renal parameters. Prognosis is guarded to poor, especially with metastatic disease; chemotherapy options remain limited in equine oncology.
treatment_ja: 腎細胞癌や腎芽腫などの限局性腎腫瘍に対しては、対側腎の機能が正常であれば片側腎摘出術が第一選択となる。支持療法として輸液療法、疼痛管理にフルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg 静脈内投与）などのNSAIDsを使用し、腎機能パラメータを継続的にモニタリングする。転移性疾患では予後は慎重～不良であり、馬における化学療法の選択肢は依然として限られている。

name: Renal Metabolic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal metabolic disease in horses involves disruption of normal kidney function affecting electrolyte balance, acid-base homeostasis, and waste product excretion. Impaired renal tubular function leads to abnormal handling of calcium, phosphorus, and bicarbonate, resulting in metabolic acidosis or alkalosis and mineral imbalances. Progressive nephron damage can lead to azotemia, uremia, and secondary metabolic derangements including renal secondary hyperparathyroidism and osteodystrophy.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎代謝疾患は、電解質バランス、酸塩基平衡、老廃物排泄に影響を及ぼす腎機能の障害を伴う。腎尿細管機能の低下により、カルシウム、リン、重炭酸の処理が異常となり、代謝性アシドーシスまたはアルカローシスやミネラル不均衡が生じる。進行性のネフロン障害は高窒素血症、尿毒症、および腎性二次性副甲状腺機能亢進症や骨異栄養症などの二次的代謝異常を引き起こす。
causes: Primary causes include chronic kidney disease, nephrotoxin exposure (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals, vitamin D toxicosis), and nephrolithiasis. Secondary causes include dehydration, sepsis, hemodynamic compromise, high-oxalate plant ingestion, and hypercalcemia from various etiologies. Nutritional imbalances with excessive phosphorus or calcium intake can also contribute to renal metabolic dysfunction.
treatment: Aggressive IV fluid therapy (polyionic isotonic crystalloids) to restore hydration and renal perfusion. Correct electrolyte imbalances (calcium, phosphorus) and acid-base disturbances with sodium bicarbonate if metabolic acidosis is present. Discontinue nephrotoxic agents (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides), manage dietary calcium/phosphorus ratios, and provide supportive care including gastroprotectants (omeprazole 4 mg/kg PO SID) and nutritional support.
treatment_ja: 積極的な静脈内輸液療法（等張性ポリイオン晶質液）により水和状態と腎灌流を回復させる。電解質異常（カルシウム、リン）を補正し、代謝性アシドーシスには重炭酸ナトリウムを投与する。腎毒性薬剤（NSAIDs、アミノグリコシド系）を中止し、食事中のカルシウム・リン比を管理し、胃粘膜保護剤（オメプラゾール4 mg/kg 経口1日1回）および栄養補助を含む支持療法を実施する。

name: Renal Nutritional Deficiency (Horse)
pathophysiology: Nutritional deficiencies, particularly of vitamin A, vitamin D, calcium, phosphorus, or oxalate-containing plant ingestion, can impair renal tubular function and lead to nephrocalcinosis or tubular degeneration in horses. Imbalanced calcium-phosphorus ratios (especially excess phosphorus) promote calcium deposition in renal tissue, causing progressive nephropathy. Chronic oxalate ingestion from tropical grasses can bind calcium, leading to hypocalcemia and secondary renal calcium oxalate crystal deposition with resultant tubular damage.
pathophysiology_ja: ビタミンA、ビタミンD、カルシウム、リンなどの栄養素の欠乏やシュウ酸含有植物の摂取により、腎尿細管機能障害や腎石灰化症、尿細管変性が引き起こされる。カルシウムとリンの比率の不均衡（特にリン過剰）は腎組織へのカルシウム沈着を促進し、進行性腎症を引き起こす。熱帯牧草からの慢性的なシュウ酸摂取はカルシウムと結合し、低カルシウム血症および二次的な腎シュウ酸カルシウム結晶沈着を生じ尿細管障害をもたらす。
causes: Primary causes include dietary calcium-phosphorus imbalance (excess phosphorus or deficient calcium), chronic ingestion of oxalate-rich plants (e.g., Setaria, Cenchrus, Panicum species), and deficiencies in vitamin A or vitamin D. Secondary causes include prolonged grazing on tropical grasses with high oxalate content, inadequate mineral supplementation, and poor-quality forage leading to chronic nutritional imbalances.
treatment: Correct dietary calcium-phosphorus ratio to approximately 2:1 by supplementing limestone (calcium carbonate) at 30-60 g/day and reducing high-phosphorus feeds such as bran. Remove access to oxalate-rich grasses. Administer parenteral vitamin A (100,000-250,000 IU IM) and vitamin D supplementation as needed, along with IV fluid therapy to support renal perfusion in acute cases.
treatment_ja: 飼料中のカルシウム・リン比を約2:1に矯正するため、�iteite calcium（炭酸カルシウム）を1日30〜60g補給し、フスマ等の高リン飼料を制限する。シュウ酸含有牧草への放牧を中止する。必要に応じてビタミンA（100,000〜250,000 IU筋注）およびビタミンDを投与し、急性期には腎灌流維持のため輸液療法を実施する。

name: Renal Genetic Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal genetic disorders in horses involve inherited mutations affecting renal tubular or glomerular structure and function, leading to progressive nephron loss, impaired filtration, and eventual chronic renal failure. Examples include renal dysplasia and polycystic kidney disease, where abnormal development or cyst formation disrupts normal renal architecture. Progressive fibrosis and loss of functional nephrons result in azotemia, electrolyte imbalances, and uremia.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎臓遺伝性疾患は、腎尿細管や糸球体の構造・機能に影響を与える遺伝子変異に起因し、進行性のネフロン喪失、濾過機能障害、最終的に慢性腎不全に至ります。腎形成異常や多発性嚢胞腎などが含まれ、異常な発育や嚢胞形成により正常な腎構造が破壊されます。進行性の線維化と機能的ネフロンの喪失により、高窒素血症、電解質異常、尿毒症が生じます。
causes: The primary cause is inherited genetic mutations, which may follow autosomal recessive or dominant inheritance patterns depending on the specific disorder. Certain breeds may be predisposed, and consanguineous breeding increases the risk of homozygous expression of deleterious alleles. Secondary factors such as concurrent infections or nephrotoxic insults may accelerate progression in genetically affected individuals.
treatment: No curative treatment exists for renal genetic disorders in horses; management is supportive. Intravenous fluid therapy (balanced polyionic solutions) corrects dehydration and electrolyte imbalances. ACE inhibitors (e.g., benazepril) may slow proteinuria progression. Dietary modification with reduced protein and phosphorus, phosphate binders (aluminum hydroxide), and monitoring of azotemia are essential for managing chronic renal failure.
treatment_ja: 馬の腎遺伝性疾患に根治療法はなく、治療は対症療法が中心となる。輸液療法（バランス電解質液）により脱水や電解質異常を補正する。ACE阻害薬（ベナゼプリル等）は蛋白尿の進行抑制に有用である。低タンパク・低リン食への食事管理、リン吸着剤（水酸化アルミニウム）の投与、および高窒素血症のモニタリングが慢性腎不全の管理に不可欠である。

name: Renal Autoimmune Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: The immune system produces autoantibodies or autoreactive lymphocytes directed against renal antigens, leading to immune complex deposition in glomeruli and/or tubulointerstitial inflammation. This results in progressive glomerulonephritis, tubular damage, and loss of nephron function. Complement activation and inflammatory cell infiltration further exacerbate renal tissue destruction, potentially leading to chronic kidney disease.
pathophysiology_ja: 免疫系が腎臓の抗原に対する自己抗体または自己反応性リンパ球を産生し、糸球体への免疫複合体沈着および/または尿細管間質性炎症を引き起こします。これにより進行性の糸球体腎炎、尿細管障害、ネフロン機能の喪失が生じます。補体活性化と炎症細胞浸潤が腎組織の破壊をさらに悪化させ、慢性腎臓病に至る可能性があります。
causes: The primary cause is immune dysregulation leading to loss of self-tolerance against renal antigens, potentially triggered by chronic infections (e.g., equine infectious anemia, streptococcal infections), drug reactions, or systemic autoimmune conditions. Secondary causes include persistent antigen-antibody complex formation from other diseases and genetic predisposition. Environmental factors and concurrent inflammatory conditions may also contribute to disease initiation.
treatment: Immunosuppressive therapy with corticosteroids (dexamethasone 0.05-0.1 mg/kg IV initially, then oral prednisolone tapering) combined with azathioprine (3 mg/kg PO q24h) to suppress autoantibody production. Supportive care includes IV fluid therapy, ACE inhibitors (benazepril 0.5 mg/kg PO q24h) for renal protection, and monitoring of renal parameters and proteinuria.
treatment_ja: 副腎皮質ステロイド（デキサメタゾン0.05-0.1 mg/kg IV、その後経口プレドニゾロンを漸減）とアザチオプリン（3 mg/kg PO q24h）による免疫抑制療法で自己抗体産生を抑制する。補助療法として輸液療法、ACE阻害薬（ベナゼプリル0.5 mg/kg PO q24h）による腎保護を行い、腎機能パラメータおよび蛋白尿を定期的にモニタリングする。

name: Renal Degenerative Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal degenerative disease in horses involves progressive deterioration of renal parenchyma, including tubular necrosis, interstitial fibrosis, and glomerulosclerosis, leading to impaired glomerular filtration and tubular function. Chronic degeneration results in loss of functional nephrons, azotemia, electrolyte imbalances, and eventual renal failure. The disease may be compounded by reduced renal blood flow, accumulation of uremic toxins, and secondary metabolic derangements.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎変性疾患は、尿細管壊死、間質線維化、糸球体硬化症を含む腎実質の進行性変性を伴い、糸球体濾過および尿細管機能の障害を引き起こす。慢性変性により機能的ネフロンが喪失し、高窒素血症、電解質異常、最終的には腎不全に至る。腎血流量の低下、尿毒症性毒素の蓄積、二次的な代謝異常により病態が悪化する場合がある。
causes: Primary causes include chronic nephrotoxin exposure (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals, vitamin D toxicosis), ischemic injury, and age-related degenerative changes. Secondary causes include chronic dehydration, systemic infections, immune-mediated glomerulonephritis, nephrolithiasis, and prolonged hemodynamic compromise such as from endotoxemia or severe colic.
treatment: Discontinue all nephrotoxic agents (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides). Provide aggressive IV fluid therapy (polyionic isotonic crystalloids) to correct azotemia and maintain hydration. Supportive care includes dietary protein restriction, phosphate binders (aluminum hydroxide 30-90 mg/kg PO BID), and ACE inhibitors (benazepril 0.5 mg/kg PO SID) to reduce proteinuria and slow progression.
treatment_ja: すべての腎毒性薬剤（NSAIDs、アミノグリコシド系）を直ちに中止する。積極的な静脈内輸液療法（等張性ポリイオン晶質液）で高窒素血症の是正と水分補給を維持する。支持療法として食事中のタンパク質制限、リン吸着剤（水酸化アルミニウム30〜90 mg/kg 経口BID）、およびACE阻害薬（ベナゼプリル0.5 mg/kg 経口SID）を投与し、蛋白尿軽減と進行抑制を図る。

name: Renal Traumatic Injury (Horse)
pathophysiology: Blunt or penetrating trauma to the lumbar region disrupts the renal parenchyma, capsule, or vascular pedicle, leading to hemorrhage, hematoma formation, and potential urine leakage into the retroperitoneal space. Subsequent inflammation, ischemia, and possible secondary infection can further compromise renal function. In severe cases, vascular disruption may cause life-threatening hemorrhage or eventual renal infarction and fibrosis.
pathophysiology_ja: 腰部への鈍的または穿通性外傷により腎実質、腎被膜、または腎血管茎が損傷し、出血、血腫形成、および後腹膜腔への尿漏出が生じる。続発する炎症、虚血、二次感染が腎機能をさらに障害する可能性がある。重症例では血管損傷により致命的な出血や腎梗塞・線維化に至ることがある。
causes: Primary causes include blunt abdominal or lumbar trauma from kicks by other horses, falls, collisions with fixed objects, or accidents during transportation. Secondary causes include penetrating injuries from external objects, iatrogenic damage during percutaneous renal biopsy, and rarely, rib fractures with fragment displacement into the kidney.
causes_ja: 主な原因は、他馬からの蹴り、転倒、固定物への衝突、輸送中の事故などによる腹部・腰部への鈍的外傷である。二次的原因には外部物体による穿通性損傷、経皮的腎生検時の医原性損傷、まれに肋骨骨折片の腎への刺入が含まれる。
treatment: Stabilize with IV crystalloid fluids (LRS or 0.9% NaCl) and control hemorrhage; administer flunixin meglumine (1.1 mg/kg IV q12h) for pain and anti-inflammatory effect, plus broad-spectrum antibiotics (gentamicin 6.6 mg/kg IV q24h and penicillin 22,000 IU/kg IV q6h). Monitor with serial ultrasound; nephrectomy is indicated for severe vascular pedicle avulsion or uncontrolled hemorrhage.
treatment_ja: 乳酸リンゲル液または生理食塩水の静脈内投与で循環を安定させ、出血をコントロールする。フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg IV 12時間毎）で鎮痛・抗炎症を図り、ゲンタマイシン（6.6 mg/kg IV 24時間毎）およびペニシリン（22,000 IU/kg IV 6時間毎）で広域抗菌療法を行う。超音波検査で経過観察し、腎血管茎断裂や止血不能な場合は腎摘出術を実施する。

name: Renal Behavioral Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal behavioral disorder in horses involves abnormal behaviors associated with underlying renal pain or dysfunction, such as chronic nephritis, nephrolithiasis, or renal neoplasia. Pain originating from the kidneys or ureters triggers visceral nociceptive pathways, leading to altered posture, reluctance to move, flank guarding, and changes in urination patterns. Chronic renal discomfort may also manifest as performance decline, irritability, and behavioral changes that mimic musculoskeletal or gastrointestinal disorders.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎行動障害は、慢性腎炎、腎結石症、腎腫瘍などの腎臓の疼痛や機能障害に関連した異常行動を伴います。腎臓や尿管に由来する痛みが内臓侵害受容経路を刺激し、姿勢の変化、運動の拒否、側腹部の防御反応、排尿パターンの変化を引き起こします。慢性的な腎臓の不快感は、パフォーマンスの低下、易刺激性、筋骨格系や消化器系疾患に類似した行動変化として現れることがあります。
causes: Primary causes include nephrolithiasis, pyelonephritis, renal cysts, renal neoplasia, and chronic interstitial nephritis causing persistent renal pain. Secondary causes may involve ureterolithiasis, renal vascular compromise, toxic nephropathy from NSAIDs or aminoglycosides, and referred pain from adjacent structures. Idiopathic renal discomfort without identifiable structural lesions has also been reported.
treatment: Address underlying renal pathology: nephroliths may require surgical removal (nephrolithotomy) or lithotripsy; pyelonephritis is treated with prolonged antimicrobials (trimethoprim-sulfonamide or enrofloxacin based on culture). Provide analgesia with flunixin meglumine (1.1 mg/kg IV) or butorphanol (0.01-0.04 mg/kg IV) for visceral pain. Supportive care includes IV fluid therapy to maintain renal perfusion and correction of electrolyte imbalances.
treatment_ja: 基礎疾患の治療を行う：腎結石には外科的除去（腎切石術）または砕石術を検討し、腎盂腎炎には培養結果に基づきトリメトプリム・スルホンアミドまたはエンロフロキサシンによる長期抗菌薬療法を実施する。内臓痛にはフルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg IV）またはブトルファノール（0.01〜0.04 mg/kg IV）で鎮痛を行う。補液療法による腎灌流維持と電解質補正を含む支持療法を併用する。

name: Renal Infectious Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infectious disease in horses involves bacterial invasion of the renal parenchyma, typically via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract or hematogenous spread. Pathogens such as Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Actinobacillus equuli, and Leptospira spp. colonize renal tissue, causing inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive nephritis. This leads to impaired glomerular filtration, tubular dysfunction, and potentially acute or chronic renal failure if left untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症は、下部尿路からの上行性感染または血行性播種により細菌が腎実質に侵入することで発生する。大腸菌、レンサ球菌、Actinobacillus equuli、レプトスピラなどの病原体が腎組織に定着し、炎症、膿瘍形成、進行性の腎炎を引き起こす。これにより糸球体濾過機能および尿細管機能が障害され、未治療の場合は急性または慢性腎不全に至る可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infections (commonly E. coli, Streptococcus spp., Corynebacterium spp.) from the lower urinary tract, and hematogenous spread from distant infection sites. Secondary causes include urolithiasis causing urinary stasis, immunosuppression, leptospirosis, and predisposing factors such as dehydration, concurrent systemic illness, or nephrotoxic drug administration.
treatment: Initiate broad-spectrum antibiotics such as trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (30 mg/kg PO BID) or enrofloxacin (5 mg/kg IV/PO SID), adjusting based on urine culture and sensitivity results. Provide aggressive IV fluid therapy (balanced polyionic solutions) to maintain renal perfusion and promote diuresis. Address underlying causes such as urolithiasis surgically if indicated, and administer NSAIDs (flunixin meglumine 1.1 mg/kg IV) for pain and inflammation control.
treatment_ja: トリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾール（30 mg/kg 経口 1日2回）またはエンロフロキサシン（5 mg/kg 静注/経口 1日1回）などの広域抗菌薬を開始し、尿培養・感受性試験の結果に基づき調整する。積極的な静脈内輸液療法（バランス電解質液）で腎灌流を維持し利尿を促進する。尿路結石などの基礎疾患には必要に応じ外科的処置を行い、フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg 静注）で疼痛・炎症を管理する。

name: Renal Parasitic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal parasitic disease in horses occurs when parasitic organisms such as Halicephalobus gingivalis (Halicephalobus deletrix), Strongylus vulgaris larvae, or Dioctophyme renale migrate to or invade the kidneys, causing granulomatous nephritis, tubular destruction, and interstitial inflammation. Larval migration through renal vasculature can lead to thrombosis, infarction, and progressive renal parenchymal damage. Chronic infection may result in fibrosis, impaired renal function, and secondary hydronephrosis.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎寄生虫症は、Halicephalobus gingivalis、Strongylus vulgarisの幼虫、またはDioctophyme renaleなどの寄生虫が腎臓に移行・侵入し、肉芽腫性腎炎、尿細管破壊、間質性炎症を引き起こすことで発症する。幼虫の腎血管系への移行は血栓症、梗塞、進行性の腎実質障害を引き起こす可能性がある。慢性感染は線維化、腎機能障害、続発性水腎症につながることがある。
causes: Primary causes include migration of parasitic larvae such as Strongylus vulgaris (aberrant larval migration), Halicephalobus gingivalis (opportunistic nematode), and rarely Dioctophyme renale (giant kidney worm). Infection typically occurs through ingestion of infective larvae from contaminated pasture or soil, with subsequent hematogenous or direct migration to the kidneys. Secondary causes include immunosuppression and heavy parasite burden facilitating aberrant migration.
treatment: Administer broad-spectrum anthelmintics such as fenbendazole (10 mg/kg PO daily for 5 days) or ivermectin (0.2 mg/kg PO). For Halicephalobus gingivalis, prognosis is grave and treatment is often unrewarding; high-dose fenbendazole or moxidectin may be attempted. Supportive care includes IV fluids for renal support, NSAIDs (flunixin meglumine 1.1 mg/kg IV) for inflammation, and nephrectomy may be considered for unilateral severe cases.
treatment_ja: フェンベンダゾール（10 mg/kg 経口、5日間連続投与）やイベルメクチン（0.2 mg/kg 経口）などの広域駆虫薬を投与する。Halicephalobus gingivalis感染では予後が極めて不良であり、高用量フェンベンダゾールまたはモキシデクチンの投与を試みる。腎機能維持のための輸液療法、フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg 静注）による抗炎症治療、片側性の重症例では腎摘出術も検討する。

name: Renal Viral Disease (Horse)
