pathophysiology: Viral agents such as equine herpesvirus (EHV) or equine arteritis virus (EAV) can target renal vasculature and tubular epithelium, causing immune-mediated glomerulonephritis, tubular necrosis, and interstitial nephritis. Viral-induced vasculitis may compromise renal blood flow, leading to ischemic injury and progressive renal dysfunction. Immune complex deposition in glomeruli further exacerbates inflammation and impairs filtration capacity.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬ヘルペスウイルス（EHV）や馬動脈炎ウイルス（EAV）などのウイルスが腎血管や尿細管上皮を標的とし、免疫介在性糸球体腎炎、尿細管壊死、間質性腎炎を引き起こす。ウイルス性血管炎により腎血流が障害され、虚血性損傷や進行性腎機能不全に至る。糸球体への免疫複合体の沈着が炎症をさらに悪化させ、濾過能力を低下させる。
causes: Primary causes include equine herpesvirus (EHV-1, EHV-4), equine arteritis virus (EAV), and potentially other nephrotrophic viruses that directly infect renal tissue. Secondary causes include immune complex deposition, systemic vasculitis, dehydration, and concurrent bacterial infections that compound viral-induced renal damage.
treatment: No specific antiviral therapy is proven; supportive care includes aggressive IV fluid therapy (balanced polyionic solutions) to maintain renal perfusion, NSAIDs (flunixin meglumine 1.1 mg/kg IV BID) for inflammation control, and corticosteroids if immune-mediated glomerulonephritis is confirmed. Acyclovir or valacyclovir may be considered for EHV cases. Monitor electrolytes, BUN, and creatinine closely.
treatment_ja: 確立された特異的抗ウイルス療法はなく、支持療法が中心となる。腎灌流維持のための積極的な輸液療法（バランス電解質液の静脈内投与）、フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg IV BID）による抗炎症治療、免疫介在性糸球体腎炎が確認された場合はコルチコステロイドを使用する。EHV症例にはアシクロビルまたはバラシクロビルを検討する。電解質、BUN、クレアチニンを継続的にモニタリングする。

name: Renal Bacterial Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Bacterial pathogens, most commonly Escherichia coli, Actinobacillus spp., Streptococcus spp., or Corynebacterium spp., ascend via the lower urinary tract or reach the kidneys hematogenously, causing inflammation of the renal parenchyma and/or pelvis (pyelonephritis). The resulting infection leads to progressive destruction of renal tissue, impaired tubular and glomerular function, and potentially abscess formation or septicemia if untreated. Chronic infection may result in renal fibrosis, nephrolithiasis, and ultimately renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 大腸菌、Actinobacillus属、Streptococcus属、Corynebacterium属などの細菌が下部尿路からの上行感染または血行性に腎臓に到達し、腎実質や腎盂に炎症（腎盂腎炎）を引き起こす。感染により腎組織の進行性破壊、尿細管および糸球体機能の障害が生じ、未治療では膿瘍形成や敗血症に至ることがある。慢性感染は腎線維化、腎結石、最終的には腎不全につながる可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include ascending urinary tract infections (most common), hematogenous spread from distant infection sites, and direct extension from adjacent structures. Predisposing factors include urolithiasis, urinary tract obstruction, bladder paralysis, catheterization, immunosuppression, and congenital urinary tract anomalies. Common causative organisms include E. coli, Actinobacillus spp., Streptococcus spp., Proteus spp., Klebsiella spp., and Corynebacterium renale.
treatment: Initiate aggressive systemic antibiotic therapy based on urine culture and sensitivity; trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (30 mg/kg PO BID) or enrofloxacin (5 mg/kg IV/PO SID) are common first-line choices. Provide IV fluid therapy to maintain renal perfusion and urine flow. Address predisposing factors such as urolithiasis or obstruction, and monitor renal values and urine sediment serially.
treatment_ja: 尿培養・感受性試験に基づき、トリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾール（30 mg/kg PO BID）またはエンロフロキサシン（5 mg/kg IV/PO SID）などの全身性抗菌薬を積極的に投与する。腎灌流と尿流量を維持するために静脈内輸液療法を実施する。尿路結石や閉塞などの素因を是正し、腎機能指標および尿沈渣を定期的にモニタリングする。

name: Renal Fungal Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Fungal organisms, most commonly Aspergillus spp. or Candida spp., colonize the renal parenchyma and/or renal pelvis, leading to granulomatous or necrotizing inflammation. The infection disrupts normal renal architecture, potentially causing obstruction, abscess formation, and progressive loss of renal function. Hematogenous spread or ascending infection from the lower urinary tract can lead to fungal nephritis and pyelonephritis.
pathophysiology_ja: 主にAspergillus属やCandida属などの真菌が腎実質や腎盂に定着し、肉芽腫性または壊死性の炎症を引き起こす。感染は正常な腎構造を破壊し、閉塞、膿瘍形成、および進行性の腎機能低下をもたらす可能性がある。血行性播種または下部尿路からの上行性感染により真菌性腎炎および腎盂腎炎が生じる。
causes: Primary causes include opportunistic fungal infections by Aspergillus spp., Candida spp., or other environmental fungi that invade the kidneys via hematogenous spread or ascending urinary tract infection. Predisposing factors include prolonged antibiotic therapy, immunosuppression, indwelling urinary catheters, and concurrent systemic illness that compromises immune function. Secondary bacterial infections may complicate the condition.
treatment: Systemic antifungal therapy with fluconazole (5 mg/kg PO q24h) or itraconazole; amphotericin B (0.3-0.6 mg/kg IV slowly) reserved for refractory cases with careful nephrotoxicity monitoring. Discontinue predisposing antibiotics and immunosuppressants. Nephrectomy may be indicated for unilateral abscessation or obstruction unresponsive to medical management.
treatment_ja: フルコナゾール（5 mg/kg 経口 1日1回）またはイトラコナゾールによる全身性抗真菌療法を実施し、難治性症例にはアムホテリシンB（0.3〜0.6 mg/kg 緩徐静注）を腎毒性を慎重にモニタリングしながら使用する。誘因となる抗菌薬や免疫抑制剤は中止する。片側性の膿瘍形成や閉塞で内科的治療に反応しない場合は腎摘出術を検討する。

name: Renal Infection (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infection (pyelonephritis) in horses typically results from ascending bacterial infection via the ureters from the lower urinary tract, or less commonly via hematogenous spread. Bacteria colonize the renal pelvis and parenchyma, causing inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of nephrons. Chronic infection can lead to fibrosis, hydronephrosis, and ultimately renal failure if bilateral or if the contralateral kidney is compromised.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路から尿管を経由した上行性細菌感染、またはまれに血行性播種によって発生します。細菌が腎盂および腎実質に定着し、炎症、膿瘍形成、およびネフロンの進行性破壊を引き起こします。慢性感染は線維化、水腎症を引き起こし、両側性または対側腎が障害されている場合は最終的に腎不全に至ることがあります。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infections, most commonly by Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Corynebacterium renale, and Actinobaculum suis. Predisposing factors include urolithiasis, urinary stasis, bladder paralysis, catheterization, immunosuppression, and anatomical abnormalities. Mares may be more susceptible due to their shorter urethra facilitating bacterial ascent.
treatment: Initiate prolonged systemic antibiotic therapy (4-6 weeks) based on urine culture and sensitivity, commonly trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, enrofloxacin, or penicillin/gentamicin combinations. Provide IV fluid therapy to maintain hydration and promote renal perfusion. Address predisposing factors such as urolithiasis or urinary obstruction surgically if indicated, and monitor renal function via serial bloodwork and urinalysis.
treatment_ja: 尿培養・感受性試験に基づき、トリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾール、エンロフロキサシン、またはペニシリン/ゲンタマイシン併用などの全身性抗菌薬を4〜6週間投与する。静脈内輸液療法で水分補給と腎灌流を維持する。尿路結石や尿路閉塞などの素因がある場合は外科的に対処し、血液検査および尿検査で腎機能を継続的にモニタリングする。

name: Renal Inflammation (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal inflammation (nephritis) in horses involves immune-mediated or infectious injury to the glomeruli, tubules, or interstitium, leading to impaired filtration, protein loss, and progressive renal dysfunction. Inflammatory cell infiltration and edema compromise renal blood flow and tubular function, resulting in azotemia, electrolyte imbalances, and potentially acute or chronic renal failure. Prolonged inflammation can lead to fibrosis and irreversible loss of nephron function.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎炎は、糸球体・尿細管・間質への免疫介在性または感染性の障害により、濾過機能の低下、蛋白漏出、進行性の腎機能不全を引き起こす。炎症細胞の浸潤や浮腫が腎血流と尿細管機能を障害し、高窒素血症や電解質異常、急性または慢性腎不全を招く。慢性的な炎症は線維化を引き起こし、ネフロンの不可逆的な喪失に至る。
causes: Primary causes include bacterial infections (e.g., leptospirosis, streptococcal infections), viral infections (e.g., equine infectious anemia), and immune-mediated glomerulonephritis. Secondary causes include nephrotoxic drugs (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides), heavy metals, systemic diseases, dehydration, and septicemia that result in secondary renal damage.
treatment: Discontinue nephrotoxic agents (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides) immediately. Initiate aggressive IV fluid therapy (lactated Ringer's or 0.9% NaCl) to restore renal perfusion. Treat underlying infections with appropriate antibiotics (e.g., penicillin for streptococcal or leptospiral infections), administer corticosteroids (dexamethasone 0.05-0.1 mg/kg IV) for immune-mediated cases, and provide supportive care including electrolyte correction and dietary protein restriction.
treatment_ja: 腎毒性薬剤（NSAIDs、アミノグリコシド系）を直ちに中止する。積極的な静脈内輸液療法（乳酸リンゲル液または生理食塩水）を開始し、腎灌流を回復させる。基礎感染症には適切な抗菌薬（レプトスピラやレンサ球菌感染にはペニシリン系）を投与し、免疫介在性の場合はコルチコステロイド（デキサメタゾン0.05〜0.1 mg/kg静注）を使用する。電解質補正および食事中のタンパク質制限を含む支持療法を併せて行う。

name: Renal Neoplasia (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal neoplasia in horses involves the abnormal proliferation of cells within the kidney parenchyma, collecting ducts, or surrounding tissues. The most commonly reported primary renal tumors include renal cell carcinoma, nephroblastoma, and lymphoma, which can disrupt normal renal architecture, impair filtration and excretory function, and potentially metastasize to regional lymph nodes, lungs, and other organs. Tumor growth may cause progressive renal insufficiency, hematuria, and space-occupying effects within the retroperitoneal space.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎腫瘍は、腎実質、集合管、または周囲組織における細胞の異常増殖を伴います。最も一般的に報告される原発性腎腫瘍には腎細胞癌、腎芽腫（ネフロブラストーマ）、およびリンパ腫があり、正常な腎構造を破壊し、濾過・排泄機能を障害し、所属リンパ節や肺などへ転移する可能性があります。腫瘍の増大により進行性の腎機能不全、血尿、後腹膜腔内の占拠性病変を引き起こします。
causes: The exact etiology of renal neoplasia in horses is largely unknown. Potential contributing factors include genetic predisposition, chronic renal inflammation, and exposure to environmental carcinogens, although no specific causative agent has been definitively identified. Nephroblastoma is more frequently seen in younger horses, suggesting a possible congenital or developmental origin.
treatment: Unilateral nephrectomy is the primary treatment for localized renal tumors when the contralateral kidney is functional. For lymphoma, systemic chemotherapy with corticosteroids (dexamethasone) and cyclophosphamide may be considered. Supportive care includes IV fluid therapy, analgesics (flunixin meglumine), and monitoring renal function post-operatively.
treatment_ja: 対側腎の機能が正常であれば、限局性腎腫瘍に対しては片側腎摘出術が第一選択となる。リンパ腫の場合、デキサメタゾンやシクロホスファミドによる全身化学療法が検討される。術後は輸液療法、鎮痛剤（フルニキシンメグルミン）の投与、および腎機能モニタリングを含む支持療法を行う。

name: Renal Metabolic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal metabolic disease in horses involves impaired kidney function leading to disruption of electrolyte balance, acid-base homeostasis, and waste product excretion. The kidneys fail to adequately regulate calcium, phosphorus, and other mineral metabolism, potentially resulting in hypercalcemia or hyperphosphatemia, azotemia, and metabolic acidosis. Chronic dysfunction can lead to renal tubular acidosis, nephrocalcinosis, and secondary nutritite imbalances affecting multiple organ systems.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎代謝性疾患は、腎機能の障害により電解質バランス、酸塩基平衡、老廃物の排泄が乱れる疾患である。腎臓がカルシウム、リン、その他のミネラル代謝を適切に調節できなくなり、高カルシウム血症や高リン血症、高窒素血症、代謝性アシドーシスを引き起こす。慢性的な機能障害は腎尿細管性アシドーシス、腎石灰化症、および多臓器に影響する二次的な栄養不均衡をもたらす可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include excessive dietary calcium or oxalate-containing plants (e.g., tropical grasses high in oxalates), chronic kidney disease, and inherited or acquired renal tubular defects. Secondary causes include dehydration, nephrotoxic drug exposure (e.g., NSAIDs, aminoglycosides), systemic infections, and prolonged electrolyte imbalances due to inappropriate diet or supplementation. Hypervitaminosis D and heavy metal toxicity can also contribute to renal metabolic dysfunction.
treatment: Correct underlying cause by removing nephrotoxic agents and oxalate-rich plants from the diet. Provide IV fluid therapy (balanced polyionic solutions) to restore hydration and promote diuresis. Manage electrolyte imbalances with calcium/phosphorus dietary adjustment, administer activated charcoal if toxin exposure is recent, and use phosphate binders (aluminum hydroxide) for hyperphosphatemia. Monitor renal values (BUN, creatinine) and adjust NSAID use.
treatment_ja: 腎毒性薬剤やシュウ酸含有植物の除去など原因の是正を行う。静脈内輸液療法（バランス電解質液）により脱水を補正し利尿を促進する。カルシウム・リンの食事調整で電解質異常を管理し、毒素曝露が疑われる場合は活性炭を投与する。高リン血症にはリン吸着剤（水酸化アルミニウム）を使用し、BUN・クレアチニンを定期的にモニタリングしながらNSAIDsの使用を見直す。

name: Renal Nutritional Deficiency (Horse)
pathophysiology: Nutritional deficiencies, particularly of vitamin D, calcium, or phosphorus imbalances, lead to impaired renal tubular function and mineral metabolism in horses. Chronic deficiency or excess of these nutrients causes nephrocalcinosis, tubular degeneration, and progressive renal insufficiency. Secondary hyperparathyroidism may develop, further contributing to renal calcium deposition and fibrosis.
pathophysiology_ja: ビタミンD、カルシウム、リンなどの栄養素の不均衡により、馬の腎尿細管機能およびミネラル代謝が障害されます。これらの栄養素の慢性的な欠乏または過剰は、腎石灰化症、尿細管変性、進行性腎不全を引き起こします。二次性副甲状腺機能亢進症が発症し、腎臓へのカルシウム沈着および線維化をさらに悪化させることがあります。
causes: Primary causes include dietary imbalances of calcium and phosphorus (particularly inverted Ca:P ratios), vitamin D deficiency or excess, and oxalate-rich plant ingestion (e.g., tropical grasses high in oxalates). Secondary causes include chronic feeding of high-grain diets without adequate mineral supplementation, and prolonged grazing on nutrient-depleted pastures.
causes_ja: 主な原因は、カルシウムとリンの食事性不均衡（特にCa:P比の逆転）、ビタミンDの欠乏または過剰、シュウ酸を多く含む植物の摂取（例：熱帯性牧草）です。二次的原因には、適切なミネラル補給なしに高穀物飼料を長期間給与すること、栄養素が枯渇した牧草地での長期放牧が含まれます。
treatment: Correct dietary Ca:P ratio to approximately 2:1, supplement vitamin D (if deficient) at 6,600 IU/kg feed, and provide IV fluid therapy with balanced electrolytes for renal support. Remove oxalate-rich forages from the diet. Administer calcium gluconate IV cautiously in hypocalcemic cases, and provide phosphorus binders if hyperphosphatemia is present.
treatment_ja: 飼料中のCa:P比を約2:1に是正し、ビタミンD欠乏時には6,600 IU/kg飼料の補給を行い、腎機能支持のためバランス電解質を含む輸液療法を実施する。シュウ酸含有量の高い牧草を除去する。低カルシウム血症にはグルコン酸カルシウムの慎重な静脈内投与を行い、高リン血症にはリン吸着剤を投与する。

name: Renal Genetic Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal genetic disorders in horses involve inherited mutations affecting renal tubular or glomerular structure and function, leading to progressive nephron loss, impaired filtration, and disrupted electrolyte and fluid homeostasis. Examples include renal dysplasia and polycystic kidney disease, where abnormal renal development or cyst formation replaces functional parenchyma, ultimately resulting in chronic renal failure. The progressive nature leads to azotemia, proteinuria, and eventual end-stage kidney disease.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎遺伝性疾患は、腎尿細管や糸球体の構造・機能に影響を与える遺伝子変異によって引き起こされ、ネフロンの進行性喪失、濾過機能の低下、電解質・水分バランスの障害を招きます。腎異形成や多発性嚢胞腎などでは、異常な腎発達や嚢胞形成により機能的な実質が置換され、最終的に慢性腎不全に至ります。進行性の経過により高窒素血症、蛋白尿、末期腎疾患へと進展します。
causes: The primary cause is inherited genetic mutations, which may follow autosomal recessive, autosomal dominant, or other inheritance patterns depending on the specific disorder. Specific conditions include renal dysplasia and polycystic kidney disease, where defective genes disrupt normal renal organogenesis or tubular cell proliferation. Inbreeding within certain horse breeds may increase the prevalence of these recessive alleles.
treatment: No curative treatment exists for renal genetic disorders in horses. Management is supportive: IV fluid therapy to maintain hydration and electrolyte balance, ACE inhibitors (e.g., benazepril) to reduce glomerular hypertension, dietary protein restriction, phosphate binders for hyperphosphatemia, and monitoring of renal values. Nephrectomy may be considered for unilateral polycystic disease if the contralateral kidney is functional.
treatment_ja: 馬の腎臓遺伝性疾患に根治的治療法は存在しません。治療は対症療法が中心で、輸液療法による水分・電解質バランスの維持、ACE阻害薬（例：ベナゼプリル）による糸球体内圧の軽減、食事中のタンパク質制限、高リン血症に対するリン吸着剤の投与、および腎機能の定期的モニタリングを行います。片側性多発性嚢胞腎で対側腎が正常に機能している場合は、腎摘出術が検討されることがあります。

name: Renal Autoimmune Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: The immune system produces autoantibodies or autoreactive lymphocytes directed against renal antigens, leading to immune complex deposition in glomeruli and/or tubulointerstitial inflammation. This results in progressive glomerulonephritis, tubular damage, and loss of nephron function. Complement activation and inflammatory cell infiltration further exacerbate renal tissue destruction, potentially leading to chronic kidney disease.
pathophysiology_ja: 免疫系が腎臓の自己抗原に対する自己抗体または自己反応性リンパ球を産生し、糸球体への免疫複合体沈着や尿細管間質性炎症を引き起こす。これにより進行性の糸球体腎炎、尿細管障害、およびネフロン機能の喪失が生じる。補体活性化と炎症細胞浸潤が腎組織の破壊をさらに悪化させ、慢性腎臓病に至る可能性がある。
causes: The primary cause is immune dysregulation leading to loss of self-tolerance against renal antigens, potentially triggered by chronic infections (e.g., Streptococcus equi), viral infections, or drug reactions. Secondary causes include immune complex formation associated with equine infectious anemia, Leptospira infection, or other systemic immune-mediated conditions. Genetic predisposition and environmental factors may also contribute to disease development.
treatment: Immunosuppressive therapy with corticosteroids (dexamethasone 0.05-0.1 mg/kg IV daily, tapering over weeks) combined with azathioprine (3 mg/kg PO daily) to suppress autoantibody production and reduce immune complex deposition. Supportive care includes IV fluid therapy to maintain renal perfusion, ACE inhibitors (benazepril 0.5 mg/kg PO daily) to reduce proteinuria, and treatment of underlying infections such as Streptococcus equi.
treatment_ja: 免疫抑制療法として副腎皮質ステロイド（デキサメタゾン0.05〜0.1 mg/kg IV、漸減投与）およびアザチオプリン（3 mg/kg PO 1日1回）を併用し、自己抗体産生と免疫複合体沈着を抑制する。支持療法として腎灌流維持のための輸液療法、蛋白尿軽減のためACE阻害薬（ベナゼプリル0.5 mg/kg PO 1日1回）を投与し、Streptococcus equiなどの基礎感染症の治療も並行して行う。

name: Renal Degenerative Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal degenerative disease in horses involves progressive deterioration of nephron structure and function, including tubular degeneration, interstitial fibrosis, and glomerulosclerosis. This leads to impaired filtration, concentrating ability, and electrolyte regulation, ultimately resulting in chronic renal failure. Accumulation of uremic toxins and disruption of acid-base and fluid balance contribute to systemic clinical signs.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎変性疾患は、尿細管変性、間質の線維化、糸球体硬化症を含むネフロン構造と機能の進行性悪化を伴います。これにより濾過能力、濃縮能力、電解質調節が障害され、最終的に慢性腎不全に至ります。尿毒症性毒素の蓄積および酸塩基・体液バランスの破綻が全身性の臨床症状に寄与します。
causes: Primary causes include chronic nephrotoxin exposure (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals, vitamin D toxicosis), chronic pyelonephritis, and nephrolithiasis. Secondary causes include prolonged hemodynamic compromise, systemic diseases such as leptospirosis, immune-mediated glomerulonephritis, and age-related degenerative changes. Oxalate-containing plant ingestion and prolonged dehydration may also contribute.
treatment: No cure exists; treatment is supportive. Discontinue nephrotoxins immediately. Provide IV fluid therapy (balanced polyionic solutions) to correct dehydration and electrolyte imbalances. Manage uremia with dietary protein restriction, phosphate binders (aluminum hydroxide 30-90 mg/kg PO BID), and gastric protectants (omeprazole 4 mg/kg PO SID). Monitor renal values and manage hypertension if present.
treatment_ja: 根治療法は存在せず、支持療法が主体となる。腎毒性物質の投与を直ちに中止する。等張電解質輸液による脱水・電解質異常の補正を行う。尿毒症管理として食事中タンパク質制限、リン吸着剤（水酸化アルミニウム30～90 mg/kg 経口BID）、胃粘膜保護剤（オメプラゾール4 mg/kg 経口SID）を投与する。腎数値を定期的にモニタリングし、高血圧があれば管理を行う。

name: Renal Traumatic Injury (Horse)
pathophysiology: Blunt or penetrating trauma to the lumbar region causes disruption of the renal parenchyma, capsule, or vascular pedicle, leading to hemorrhage, urine leakage, and inflammation. The resulting hematoma or uroperitoneum can cause secondary complications including peritonitis, hypovolemic shock, and progressive renal dysfunction. The right kidney in horses is more protected by the ribs, while the left kidney is more mobile and potentially more susceptible to displacement-related injury.
pathophysiology_ja: 腰部への鈍的または穿通性外傷により、腎実質、被膜、または血管茎の損傷が生じ、出血、尿漏出、および炎症を引き起こす。結果として生じる血腫や尿腹症は、腹膜炎、循環血液量減少性ショック、進行性腎機能障害などの二次的合併症を引き起こす可能性がある。馬では右腎は肋骨により比較的保護されているが、左腎はより可動性が高く変位による損傷を受けやすい。
causes: Primary causes include blunt abdominal or lumbar trauma from kicks by other horses, falls, collisions with fixed objects, or vehicular accidents. Secondary causes include penetrating wounds from sharp objects or fractures of adjacent ribs or vertebral transverse processes. Iatrogenic injury during percutaneous renal biopsy or surgical procedures is also possible.
treatment: Stabilize with aggressive IV crystalloid fluid therapy (LRS or 0.9% NaCl, 20-40 mL/kg/hr initially) and control hemorrhage. Administer flunixin meglumine (1.1 mg/kg IV q12h) for pain and anti-endotoxic effects, broad-spectrum antibiotics (gentamicin 6.6 mg/kg IV q24h plus penicillin 22,000 IU/kg IV q6h). Mild cases managed conservatively with stall rest and monitoring; severe parenchymal disruption or vascular pedicle injury may require nephrectomy.
treatment_ja: 積極的な晶質液輸液（乳酸リンゲル液または生理食塩水、初期20-40 mL/kg/hr）で循環を安定化し、出血を制御する。フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg IV 12時間毎）で鎮痛・抗エンドトキシン作用を図り、広域抗菌薬（ゲンタマイシン6.6 mg/kg IV 24時間毎＋ペニシリン22,000 IU/kg IV 6時間毎）を投与する。軽度例は馬房安静と経過観察で保存的に管理し、重度の実質損傷や血管茎損傷には腎摘出術を検討する。

name: Renal Behavioral Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal behavioral disorder in horses involves chronic renal pain or discomfort arising from kidney pathology (such as nephrolithiasis, pyelonephritis, or chronic renal failure) that manifests as abnormal behavioral signs. The persistent nociceptive input from the affected kidney(s) leads to altered posture, reluctance to move, flank sensitivity, and changes in urination patterns. Systemic accumulation of uremic toxins may also contribute to central nervous system effects, further altering behavior and temperament.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎行動障害は、腎結石症、腎盂腎炎、慢性腎不全などの腎臓病変に起因する慢性的な腎臓の痛みや不快感が異常な行動徴候として発現するものです。患腎からの持続的な侵害受容刺激により、姿勢の変化、運動嫌悪、側腹部の過敏性、排尿パターンの変化が生じます。尿毒症性毒素の全身蓄積も中枢神経系に影響を及ぼし、行動や気質のさらなる変化を引き起こす可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include nephrolithiasis, chronic renal failure, pyelonephritis, renal neoplasia, and renal cysts that produce persistent pain or discomfort. Secondary causes may involve ureterolithiasis, urinary tract obstruction, toxic nephropathy (from NSAIDs, aminoglycosides, or heavy metals), and systemic diseases such as leptospirosis. Dehydration, electrolyte imbalances, and concurrent metabolic disorders can exacerbate renal dysfunction and associated behavioral changes.
treatment: Address the primary renal pathology: surgical removal of nephroliths or ureteroliths if present, antimicrobial therapy (trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole or enrofloxacin) for pyelonephritis, and IV fluid therapy for renal support. Manage pain with flunixin meglumine (1.1 mg/kg IV q12h) or butorphanol (0.01-0.04 mg/kg IV), tapering NSAIDs to minimize nephrotoxicity. Provide dietary modification with reduced protein and calcium, along with behavioral enrichment to reduce stress.
treatment_ja: 原発性腎疾患への対応として、腎結石・尿管結石の外科的除去、腎盂腎炎にはトリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾールまたはエンロフロキサシンによる抗菌療法、腎機能維持のための輸液療法を実施する。疼痛管理にはフルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg IV 12時間毎）またはブトルファノール（0.01-0.04 mg/kg IV）を使用し、腎毒性軽減のためNSAIDsは漸減する。低タンパク・低カルシウム食への食事変更およびストレス軽減のための環境改善を行う。

name: Renal Infectious Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infectious disease in horses involves bacterial colonization of the renal parenchyma, typically ascending from the lower urinary tract or via hematogenous spread. Bacterial infection triggers an inflammatory response leading to pyelonephritis, abscess formation, or interstitial nephritis, which progressively impairs glomerular filtration and tubular function. Chronic infection can result in fibrosis, renal insufficiency, and potentially septicemia if left untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症は、下部尿路からの上行性感染または血行性播種により腎実質に細菌が定着することで発症する。細菌感染により炎症反応が惹起され、腎盂腎炎、膿瘍形成、間質性腎炎を引き起こし、糸球体濾過機能および尿細管機能が進行性に障害される。慢性感染は線維化、腎不全を招き、未治療の場合は敗血症に至る可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infections (commonly Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Corynebacterium spp., and Actinobacillus equuli) from the lower urinary tract, as well as hematogenous spread from distant infection sites. Secondary causes include urolithiasis causing urinary stasis, immunosuppression, catheterization-related contamination, and pre-existing renal or urinary tract abnormalities that predispose to bacterial colonization.
treatment: Initiate broad-spectrum antibiotic therapy based on urine culture and sensitivity, commonly trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (30 mg/kg PO BID) or enrofloxacin (5 mg/kg IV/PO SID). Provide IV fluid therapy to maintain renal perfusion and correct dehydration. Address underlying causes such as urolithiasis surgically if present, and administer NSAIDs (flunixin meglumine 1.1 mg/kg IV) for pain and inflammation control.
treatment_ja: 尿培養・感受性試験に基づき、トリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾール（30 mg/kg 経口 BID）またはエンロフロキサシン（5 mg/kg 静注/経口 SID）などの広域抗菌薬療法を開始する。腎灌流維持および脱水補正のため静脈内輸液療法を実施する。尿路結石などの基礎疾患が存在する場合は外科的に対処し、フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg 静注）を用いて疼痛および炎症を管理する。

name: Renal Parasitic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal parasitic disease in horses involves migration and colonization of parasites such as Halicephalobus gingivalis (Halicephalobus deletrix), Strongylus vulgaris larvae, or Dioctophyme renale within the renal parenchyma or vasculature. Parasite migration causes direct tissue destruction, granulomatous inflammation, and fibrosis of the kidney, leading to progressive impairment of renal function. Vascular damage from migrating larvae (particularly S. vulgaris) can result in thrombosis and infarction of renal tissue.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎寄生虫疾患は、Halicephalobus gingivalis、Strongylus vulgarisの幼虫、またはDioctophyme renaleなどの寄生虫が腎実質や血管系に移行・定着することで発生します。寄生虫の移行により直接的な組織破壊、肉芽腫性炎症、腎臓の線維化が引き起こされ、腎機能が進行性に障害されます。特にS. vulgarisの幼虫移行による血管損傷は、腎組織の血栓症や梗塞を引き起こす可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include parasitic infection by Halicephalobus gingivalis (a free-living nematode with opportunistic pathogenicity), larval migration of Strongylus vulgaris through mesenteric and renal vasculature, and rarely Dioctophyme renale (giant kidney worm). Secondary causes include immunosuppression or heavy parasitic burden facilitating aberrant larval migration to the kidneys.
treatment: Administer high-dose fenbendazole (10 mg/kg PO daily for 5 days) or ivermectin (0.2 mg/kg PO) targeting migrating larvae; add corticosteroids (dexamethasone 0.05-0.1 mg/kg IV) to reduce granulomatous inflammation. Nephrectomy may be indicated for unilateral severe parenchymal destruction by Dioctophyme renale. Supportive care includes IV fluid therapy, NSAIDs for pain, and monitoring renal function via serial blood chemistry.
treatment_ja: 移行性幼虫を標的にフェンベンダゾール（10 mg/kg 経口、5日間連続投与）またはイベルメクチン（0.2 mg/kg 経口）を投与し、肉芽腫性炎症の軽減にデキサメタゾン（0.05〜0.1 mg/kg 静注）を併用する。巨大腎虫（Dioctophyme renale）による片側性の重度腎実質破壊には腎摘出術が適応となる。補助療法として輸液療法、NSAIDsによる疼痛管理、血液化学検査による腎機能の定期的モニタリングを実施する。

name: Renal Viral Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Viral agents such as equine herpesvirus (EHV) or equine arteritis virus (EAV) can cause direct cytopathic damage to renal tubular epithelial cells and glomerular endothelium, leading to immune-complex deposition, interstitial nephritis, and impaired renal function. Vasculitis induced by viral infection may compromise renal blood flow, resulting in ischemic injury and progressive renal insufficiency. Secondary inflammatory responses and fibrin deposition further exacerbate tubular necrosis and glomerulonephritis.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬ヘルペスウイルス（EHV）や馬動脈炎ウイルス（EAV）などのウイルスが腎尿細管上皮細胞や糸球体内皮に直接的な細胞障害を引き起こし、免疫複合体の沈着、間質性腎炎、腎機能障害をもたらす。ウイルス感染による血管炎が腎血流を障害し、虚血性損傷と進行性の腎不全を引き起こす。二次的な炎症反応とフィブリン沈着が尿細管壊死および糸球体腎炎をさらに悪化させる。
causes: Primary causes include infection with equine herpesvirus (particularly EHV-1), equine arteritis virus (EAV), or other nephrotrophic viruses that target renal tissue. Secondary causes include immune-mediated glomerulonephritis from viral antigen-antibody complex deposition, systemic vasculitis, and concurrent dehydration or nephrotoxic insults that worsen virus-induced renal damage.
treatment: No specific antiviral cure exists; treatment is primarily supportive. Administer IV fluid therapy (balanced polyionic solutions) to maintain hydration and renal perfusion. Use flunixin meglumine (1.1 mg/kg IV) for anti-inflammatory and analgesic effects, broad-spectrum antimicrobials to prevent secondary bacterial infection, and ACE inhibitors if proteinuria is significant. Monitor renal values (BUN, creatinine) closely.
treatment_ja: 特異的な抗ウイルス療法は存在せず、治療は主に支持療法となる。等張性電解質輸液の静脈内投与により水和と腎灌流を維持する。フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg 静注）を抗炎症・鎮痛目的で投与し、二次細菌感染予防のため広域抗菌薬を併用する。蛋白尿が顕著な場合はACE阻害薬を検討し、BUN・クレアチニン等の腎機能指標を継続的にモニタリングする。

name: Renal Bacterial Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Bacterial pathogens, commonly Escherichia coli, Actinobacillus spp., Corynebacterium spp., or Streptococcus spp., ascend via the lower urinary tract or spread hematogenously to the renal parenchyma. This leads to inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue (pyelonephritis), impairing glomerular filtration and tubular function. Chronic infection can result in fibrosis, nephrolith formation, and eventual renal failure if left untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 大腸菌、アクチノバチルス属、コリネバクテリウム属、連鎖球菌属などの細菌が下部尿路からの上行性感染または血行性に腎実質へ到達します。これにより炎症、膿瘍形成、腎組織の進行性破壊（腎盂腎炎）が生じ、糸球体濾過および尿細管機能が障害されます。慢性感染は線維化、腎結石形成、最終的には腎不全に至る可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infection from the lower urinary tract (cystitis, urethritis), often by E. coli, Streptococcus spp., Corynebacterium renale, or Actinobacillus spp. Secondary causes include urolithiasis causing urinary stasis, immunosuppression, catheterization-related contamination, and hematogenous spread from distant infection sites. Predisposing factors include anatomical abnormalities, nephrolithiasis, and conditions that impair urine flow.
treatment: Initiate aggressive systemic antibiotic therapy based on urine culture and sensitivity, commonly trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (30 mg/kg PO BID) or enrofloxacin (5 mg/kg IV/PO SID). Provide IV fluid therapy to maintain renal perfusion and correct dehydration. Address underlying causes such as urolithiasis surgically if indicated, and monitor renal function via serial bloodwork and urinalysis.
treatment_ja: 尿培養・感受性試験に基づき、トリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾール（30 mg/kg 経口 BID）またはエンロフロキサシン（5 mg/kg 静注/経口 SID）などの全身性抗菌薬療法を積極的に開始する。腎灌流維持と脱水補正のため静脈内輸液を実施する。尿路結石など基礎疾患がある場合は外科的処置を検討し、血液検査および尿検査で腎機能を継続的にモニタリングする。

name: Renal Fungal Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Fungal organisms, most commonly Aspergillus spp. or Candida spp., colonize the renal parenchyma and/or renal pelvis, leading to granulomatous or necrotizing inflammation. This results in progressive destruction of renal tissue, impaired renal function, and potential formation of fungal masses (fungal balls) that may obstruct the urinary tract. Hematogenous dissemination or ascending infection from the lower urinary tract can spread the infection to one or both kidneys.
pathophysiology_ja: 主にAspergillus属やCandida属などの真菌が腎実質および/または腎盂に定着し、肉芽腫性または壊死性炎症を引き起こします。これにより腎組織の進行性破壊、腎機能障害、さらには尿路を閉塞する真菌塊（ファンガスボール）の形成が生じます。血行性播種または下部尿路からの上行性感染により片側または両側の腎臓に感染が広がる可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include opportunistic fungal infections by Aspergillus spp., Candida spp., or other fungi, often secondary to immunosuppression from prolonged antibiotic therapy, corticosteroid use, or debilitating systemic disease. Predisposing factors include urinary tract obstruction, indwelling urinary catheters, and disruption of normal mucosal barriers. In rare cases, environmental exposure to high fungal spore loads may contribute to primary infection.
treatment: Administer systemic antifungal therapy with fluconazole (5 mg/kg PO q24h) or amphotericin B (0.3–0.5 mg/kg IV slowly in dextrose, every 48h) while monitoring renal values closely. Discontinue predisposing factors such as corticosteroids or unnecessary antibiotics. In cases of unilateral fungal mass or severe parenchymal destruction, nephrectomy of the affected kidney should be considered alongside supportive IV fluid therapy.
treatment_ja: フルコナゾール（5 mg/kg 経口 1日1回）またはアムホテリシンB（0.3〜0.5 mg/kg ブドウ糖液で緩徐に静注、48時間ごと）による全身性抗真菌療法を実施し、腎機能を厳密にモニタリングする。コルチコステロイドや不要な抗菌薬など誘因となる薬剤は中止する。片側性の真菌塊形成や重度の腎実質破壊がある場合は、患側腎の腎摘出術を検討し、輸液による支持療法を併用する。

name: Renal Infection (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infection (pyelonephritis) in horses typically occurs via ascending bacterial infection from the lower urinary tract through the ureters to the renal pelvis and parenchyma. Bacteria colonize the renal tissue, causing inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal parenchyma. Common causative organisms include Escherichia coli, Corynebacterium renale, Streptococcus spp., and Actinobacillus equuli, which induce neutrophilic infiltration, tubular necrosis, and fibrosis.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路から尿管を経由して腎盂および腎実質へ細菌が上行性に感染することで発生します。細菌が腎組織に定着し、炎症、膿瘍形成、腎実質の進行性破壊を引き起こします。大腸菌、コリネバクテリウム・レナーレ、連鎖球菌、アクチノバチルス・エクーリなどが主な原因菌で、好中球浸潤、尿細管壊死、線維化を誘発します。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infection from cystitis or urethritis, often associated with Escherichia coli, Corynebacterium renale, or Streptococcus spp. Secondary causes include nephrolithiasis causing urinary stasis, urinary tract obstruction, immunosuppression, catheterization, and hematogenous spread from systemic infections. Predisposing factors include anatomical abnormalities, pregnancy, and chronic lower urinary tract disease.
treatment: Initiate aggressive systemic antibiotic therapy based on urine culture and sensitivity, commonly trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (30 mg/kg PO BID) or enrofloxacin (5 mg/kg IV/PO SID) for 4-6 weeks. Provide IV fluid therapy to maintain hydration and renal perfusion. Address underlying causes such as nephrolithiasis or urinary obstruction surgically if indicated, and monitor renal function via serial bloodwork and urinalysis.
treatment_ja: 尿培養および感受性試験に基づき、トリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾール（30 mg/kg 経口 1日2回）またはエンロフロキサシン（5 mg/kg 静注/経口 1日1回）を4〜6週間にわたり積極的に全身投与する。静脈内輸液療法で水分補給と腎灌流を維持する。腎結石や尿路閉塞などの基礎原因がある場合は外科的に対処し、定期的な血液検査および尿検査により腎機能をモニタリングする。

name: Renal Inflammation (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal inflammation (nephritis) in horses involves immune-mediated or infectious insult to the glomeruli, tubules, or interstitium, leading to impaired filtration, proteinuria, and progressive loss of renal function. Inflammatory cell infiltration and edema damage the nephron architecture, potentially resulting in fibrosis and chronic renal insufficiency if left untreated. Secondary effects include electrolyte imbalances, azotemia, and disruption of acid-base homeostasis.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎炎は、糸球体・尿細管・間質に対する免疫介在性または感染性の障害により、濾過機能の低下、蛋白尿、腎機能の進行性喪失を引き起こします。炎症細胞の浸潤と浮腫がネフロン構造を損傷し、未治療の場合は線維化や慢性腎不全に至る可能性があります。二次的に電解質異常、高窒素血症、酸塩基平衡の乱れが生じます。
causes: Primary causes include bacterial infections (e.g., Leptospira, Streptococcus), viral infections (e.g., equine infectious anemia), and immune-mediated glomerulonephritis. Secondary causes include nephrotoxic drugs (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides), systemic sepsis, heavy metal toxicity, and prolonged dehydration or hemodynamic compromise leading to ischemic injury.
treatment: Aggressive IV fluid therapy (polyionic isotonic crystalloids) to restore renal perfusion and correct electrolyte imbalances. Discontinue all nephrotoxic agents (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides). Administer antimicrobials (penicillin or oxytetracycline) if infectious etiology such as Leptospira is confirmed. Corticosteroids (dexamethasone 0.05-0.1 mg/kg IV) may be used for immune-mediated nephritis. Monitor urine output, serum creatinine, and BUN closely.
treatment_ja: 腎灌流の回復と電解質異常の是正のため、多価イオン等張晶質液による積極的な静脈内輸液療法を実施する。NSAIDsやアミノグリコシド系など全ての腎毒性薬剤を直ちに中止する。レプトスピラ等の感染性病因が確認された場合はペニシリンまたはオキシテトラサイクリンを投与する。免疫介在性腎炎にはデキサメタゾン（0.05〜0.1 mg/kg IV）を使用する。尿量、血清クレアチニン、BUNを継続的にモニタリングする。

name: Renal Neoplasia (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal neoplasia in horses involves the uncontrolled proliferation of cells within the kidney, most commonly renal cell carcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma, or lymphoma. Tumor growth disrupts normal renal architecture, impairing filtration and excretory functions, and may metastasize to regional lymph nodes, lungs, and other organs. Progressive tumor expansion can cause compression of adjacent structures, hematuria, and eventually systemic paraneoplastic effects including weight loss and anemia.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎腫瘍は腎臓内の細胞が無制御に増殖するもので、腎細胞癌、扁平上皮癌、リンパ腫が最も一般的です。腫瘍の成長は正常な腎構造を破壊し、濾過・排泄機能を障害し、所属リンパ節や肺などに転移する可能性があります。進行性の腫瘍拡大により隣接構造の圧迫、血尿が生じ、最終的には体重減少や貧血などの全身性腫瘍随伴症候群を引き起こします。
causes: The exact etiology of renal neoplasia in horses is largely unknown, though age-related cellular mutations and genetic predisposition may play a role. Renal cell carcinoma is the most commonly reported primary renal tumor, while lymphoma may affect the kidney as part of multicentric disease. Chronic inflammation, environmental carcinogens, and viral factors have been hypothesized but not definitively confirmed in equines.
treatment: Unilateral nephrectomy is the primary treatment for localized renal tumors when the contralateral kidney is functional. For lymphoma, systemic chemotherapy with corticosteroids (dexamethasone) and cyclophosphamide may be attempted. Supportive care includes IV fluid therapy, NSAIDs for pain management, and monitoring renal values.
treatment_ja: 対側腎が正常に機能している場合、限局性腎腫瘍に対しては患側の腎摘出術が第一選択となる。リンパ腫の場合、デキサメタゾンやシクロホスファミドによる全身化学療法が試みられることがある。支持療法として輸液療法、NSAIDsによる疼痛管理、および腎機能値のモニタリングを行う。

name: Renal Metabolic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal metabolic disease in horses involves impaired kidney function leading to disrupted electrolyte balance, acid-base homeostasis, and waste product excretion. The kidneys fail to adequately regulate calcium, phosphorus, and other mineral metabolism, potentially resulting in hypercalcemia or hyperphosphatemia, metabolic acidosis, and azotemia. Chronic cases may lead to renal secondary hyperparathyroidism, soft tissue mineralization, and progressive nephron loss.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎代謝疾患は、腎機能の低下により電解質バランス、酸塩基平衡、老廃物の排泄が障害される疾患である。腎臓がカルシウム、リン、その他のミネラル代謝を適切に調節できなくなり、高カルシウム血症や高リン血症、代謝性アシドーシス、高窒素血症を引き起こす。慢性例では腎性二次性上皮小体機能亢進症、軟部組織の石灰化、進行性のネフロン喪失につながる可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include chronic kidney disease from nephrotoxic agents (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals), nephrolithiasis, and pyelonephritis. Secondary causes include dehydration, systemic diseases such as leptospirosis, excessive dietary calcium or oxalate-containing plants, and age-related renal degeneration. Hemodynamic insults from colic, endotoxemia, or prolonged hypotension can also precipitate renal metabolic dysfunction.
treatment: Administer IV fluid therapy (balanced polyionic solutions) to correct dehydration and promote renal perfusion. Discontinue nephrotoxic agents (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs). Manage electrolyte imbalances with dietary phosphorus restriction and aluminum hydroxide as a phosphate binder. Treat underlying infections (pyelonephritis) with appropriate antibiotics such as trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole.
treatment_ja: 脱水補正と腎灌流促進のため、バランス電解質輸液を静脈内投与する。腎毒性薬剤（アミノグリコシド系、NSAIDs）を直ちに中止する。食事中のリン制限および水酸化アルミニウムをリン吸着剤として使用し、電解質異常を管理する。腎盂腎炎などの基礎感染症にはトリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾールなどの適切な抗菌薬で治療する。

name: Renal Nutritional Deficiency (Horse)
pathophysiology: Nutritional deficiencies, particularly of vitamin A, vitamin D, calcium, or phosphorus, can impair normal renal tubular function and structural integrity in horses. Prolonged imbalances, especially excessive phosphorus or oxalate-rich diets, lead to calcium depletion, nephrocalcinosis, or tubular degeneration. This results in impaired renal concentrating ability, electrolyte wasting, and progressive renal insufficiency.
pathophysiology_ja: ビタミンA、ビタミンD、カルシウム、リンなどの栄養素の欠乏や不均衡が、馬の腎尿細管機能および構造的健全性を損なう。特にリンの過剰摂取やシュウ酸塩を多く含む飼料の長期摂取は、カルシウム枯渇、腎石灰化症、尿細管変性を引き起こす。その結果、腎濃縮能の低下、電解質喪失、進行性腎不全に至る。
causes: Primary causes include dietary deficiencies of calcium, vitamin A, or vitamin D, as well as excessive dietary phosphorus or consumption of oxalate-rich plants (e.g., tropical grasses, sorrel). Secondary causes include chronic imbalanced mineral supplementation, poor-quality forage, and prolonged grazing on oxalate-accumulating pastures leading to secondary nutritional hyperparathyroidism and renal damage.
treatment: Correct dietary imbalances by providing adequate calcium supplementation (calcium carbonate 50-100 g/day orally), balanced Ca:P ratio (2:1), and vitamin A (40,000-60,000 IU/day) and vitamin D (6,000-10,000 IU/day) supplementation. Remove oxalate-rich forages and replace with quality grass or legume hay. Provide IV fluid therapy with balanced electrolytes for horses with azotemia, and monitor renal values serially.
treatment_ja: 炭酸カルシウム（50〜100g/日経口投与）によるカルシウム補給、Ca:P比を2:1に調整し、ビタミンA（40,000〜60,000 IU/日）およびビタミンD（6,000〜10,000 IU/日）を補充して食餌性不均衡を是正する。シュウ酸含有量の高い飼料を除去し、良質なイネ科またはマメ科乾草に切り替える。高窒素血症を伴う馬にはバランス電解質輸液を実施し、腎機能値を継続的にモニタリングする。

name: Renal Genetic Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal genetic disorders in horses involve inherited mutations affecting renal tubular or glomerular structure and function, leading to progressive nephron loss, impaired filtration, and concentrating ability. Examples include renal dysplasia and polycystic kidney disease, where abnormal embryological development or cyst formation disrupts normal renal architecture. Progressive fibrosis and chronic renal failure ensue as functional nephrons are gradually destroyed.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎遺伝性疾患は、腎尿細管や糸球体の構造・機能に影響を及ぼす遺伝子変異に起因し、進行性のネフロン喪失、濾過能力および濃縮能力の低下を引き起こします。腎異形成や多発性嚢胞腎などでは、胚発生の異常や嚢胞形成により正常な腎構造が破壊されます。機能的ネフロンの漸進的破壊に伴い、進行性の線維化と慢性腎不全が生じます。
causes: The primary cause is inherited genetic mutations, which may follow autosomal recessive or dominant inheritance patterns depending on the specific disorder. Breed predispositions have been reported, and consanguinity (inbreeding) increases the risk of expression. Secondary factors such as dehydration, nephrotoxin exposure, or concurrent infection may accelerate the progression of underlying genetic renal disease.
causes_ja: 主な原因は遺伝子変異であり、特定の疾患により常染色体劣性または優性の遺伝形式をとります。品種による素因が報告されており、近親交配はリスクを高めます。脱水、腎毒性物質への曝露、併発感染などの二次的要因が、基礎にある遺伝性腎疾患の進行を加速させることがあります。
treatment: No curative treatment exists for renal genetic disorders in horses. Management focuses on supportive care: IV fluid therapy to maintain hydration, dietary modification with reduced protein and phosphorus, ACE inhibitors (e.g., enalapril 0.5 mg/kg PO q24h) to reduce glomerular hypertension, phosphate binders, and monitoring of renal values. End-stage cases may require humane euthanasia.
treatment_ja: 馬の腎遺伝性疾患に対する根治的治療法は存在しません。管理は対症療法が中心となり、輸液療法による水和維持、低タンパク質・低リン食への食事変更、ACE阻害薬（例：エナラプリル0.5 mg/kg 経口 1日1回）による糸球体内圧の軽減、リン吸着剤の投与、および腎機能値の定期的モニタリングを行います。末期症例では安楽死の検討が必要となる場合があります。

name: Renal Autoimmune Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: The immune system produces autoantibodies or autoreactive lymphocytes directed against renal antigens, leading to immune complex deposition in the glomeruli and/or tubulointerstitial tissues. This triggers complement activation, inflammatory cell infiltration, and progressive glomerulonephritis or tubulointerstitial nephritis, resulting in impaired renal function. Chronic immune-mediated injury leads to fibrosis, nephron loss, and eventual renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 免疫系が腎臓の抗原に対する自己抗体または自己反応性リンパ球を産生し、糸球体や尿細管間質組織に免疫複合体が沈着します。これにより補体活性化、炎症細胞浸潤、進行性の糸球体腎炎または尿細管間質性腎炎が引き起こされ、腎機能が障害されます。慢性的な免疫介在性損傷は線維化、ネフロンの喪失、最終的に腎不全に至ります。
causes: Primary causes include dysregulation of immune tolerance leading to autoantibody production against glomerular basement membrane or tubular antigens. Secondary causes may involve chronic infections (e.g., Streptococcus equi, equine infectious anemia), drug reactions, or systemic autoimmune conditions that trigger immune complex-mediated renal injury. Genetic predisposition and environmental factors may also contribute to immune dysregulation.
treatment: Immunosuppressive therapy with corticosteroids (dexamethasone 0.05-0.1 mg/kg IV/IM tapering over weeks) is first-line, combined with azathioprine (3 mg/kg PO daily) for steroid-sparing effect. Supportive care includes IV fluid therapy to maintain renal perfusion, ACE inhibitors (benazepril 0.5 mg/kg PO) to reduce proteinuria, and treatment of underlying infections such as Streptococcus equi.
treatment_ja: 免疫抑制療法として副腎皮質ステロイド（デキサメタゾン0.05〜0.1 mg/kg IV/IM、数週間かけて漸減）を第一選択とし、ステロイド節約効果を目的にアザチオプリン（3 mg/kg PO 1日1回）を併用する。支持療法として腎灌流維持のための輸液療法、蛋白尿軽減のためACE阻害薬（ベナゼプリル0.5 mg/kg PO）を投与し、腺疫菌などの基礎感染症があれば適切に治療を行う。

name: Renal Degenerative Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal degenerative disease in horses involves progressive deterioration of renal parenchyma, including tubular degeneration, interstitial fibrosis, and glomerulosclerosis, leading to impaired filtration, concentration, and excretion functions. Chronic nephron loss results in azotemia, electrolyte imbalances, and eventual renal failure. The disease may be associated with toxic insults, chronic ischemia, or age-related changes that cause irreversible structural damage to the kidneys.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎変性疾患は、尿細管変性、間質線維化、糸球体硬化症を含む腎実質の進行性劣化を伴い、濾過・濃縮・排泄機能の障害を引き起こします。慢性的なネフロン喪失により高窒素血症、電解質異常、最終的には腎不全に至ります。毒性物質への曝露、慢性虚血、または加齢性変化が腎臓に不可逆的な構造的損傷を引き起こすことが関与しています。
causes: Primary causes include exposure to nephrotoxins such as aminoglycoside antibiotics, NSAIDs, heavy metals, and toxic plants (e.g., oak, red maple, pigweed). Secondary causes include chronic dehydration, hemodynamic compromise, systemic infections, immune-mediated glomerulonephritis, and age-related degenerative changes. Vitamin D toxicosis and oxalate-containing plants can also contribute to renal degeneration.
treatment: Discontinue all nephrotoxic agents (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs). Provide aggressive IV fluid therapy with balanced crystalloids (e.g., lactated Ringer's solution) to correct dehydration and support renal perfusion. Manage electrolyte imbalances (calcium, phosphorus) and azotemia with dietary protein restriction; administer gastroprotectants (omeprazole, sucralfate) for secondary uremic gastritis.
treatment_ja: 腎毒性薬剤（アミノグリコシド系抗菌薬、NSAIDs）を直ちに中止する。乳酸リンゲル液などの等張晶質液による積極的な輸液療法を実施し、脱水の補正と腎灌流の維持を図る。電解質異常（カルシウム、リン）の是正および食事中タンパク質の制限により高窒素血症を管理し、尿毒症性胃炎に対してはオメプラゾールやスクラルファートなどの胃粘膜保護薬を投与する。

name: Renal Traumatic Injury (Horse)
pathophysiology: Blunt or penetrating trauma to the flank or lumbar region results in damage to the renal parenchyma, capsule, or vasculature. This can lead to hemorrhage (subcapsular or perirenal hematoma), urine leakage (uroperitoneum or retroperitoneal urine accumulation), inflammation, and potential ischemic necrosis of renal tissue. Secondary complications include infection, abscess formation, adhesions, and in severe cases, acute renal failure if bilateral damage or significant loss of functional renal mass occurs.
pathophysiology_ja: 腰部や側腹部への鈍的または穿通性外傷により、腎実質、腎被膜、または腎血管系が損傷を受ける。これにより出血（被膜下または腎周囲血腫）、尿漏出（尿腹症や後腹膜尿貯留）、炎症、および腎組織の虚血性壊死が生じうる。二次的合併症として感染、膿瘍形成、癒着が起こり、重症例では両側損傷や機能的腎組織の大幅な喪失により急性腎不全に至る可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include blunt trauma from kicks by other horses, falls, collisions with fixed objects, or crush injuries during transport. Penetrating injuries from sharp objects, stake wounds, or fracture fragments of lumbar transverse processes can also damage the kidneys. Less commonly, iatrogenic injury during percutaneous renal biopsy or surgical procedures may occur.
treatment: Stabilize with IV crystalloid fluids and blood transfusion if hemorrhage is severe. Administer NSAIDs (flunixin meglumine 1.1 mg/kg IV BID) for analgesia, broad-spectrum antibiotics (gentamicin/penicillin) to prevent secondary infection, and monitor with serial ultrasound. Nephrectomy is indicated for uncontrolled hemorrhage or severely fragmented kidney.
treatment_ja: 重度の出血には輸液療法（等張晶質液）および必要に応じ輸血で循環を安定させる。鎮痛にはフルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg IV BID）を投与し、二次感染予防に広域抗菌薬（ゲンタマイシン・ペニシリン）を併用する。連続的な超音波検査でモニタリングを行い、制御不能な出血や腎の高度損傷がある場合は腎摘出術を実施する。

name: Renal Behavioral Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal behavioral disorder in horses involves abnormal behaviors (such as stretching, posturing to urinate frequently, or flank-watching) that are associated with renal pain or dysfunction. Chronic renal inflammation, nephrolithiasis, or subclinical renal disease can stimulate visceral pain pathways, leading to altered behavior patterns. The discomfort originating from the kidneys or ureters manifests as repetitive postural changes and signs of colic-like discomfort.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎行動障害は、腎臓の痛みや機能不全に関連する異常行動（頻繁な排尿姿勢、体を伸ばす動作、脇腹を気にする行動など）を伴います。慢性腎炎、腎結石、または無症候性の腎疾患が内臓痛経路を刺激し、行動パターンの変化を引き起こします。腎臓や尿管からの不快感が反復的な姿勢変化や疝痛様の症状として現れます。
causes: Primary causes include nephrolithiasis, renal cysts, pyelonephritis, and chronic interstitial nephritis causing visceral pain. Secondary causes may involve ureterolithiasis, renal neoplasia, or referred pain from adjacent structures. Dietary imbalances (excess calcium or oxalates) and chronic dehydration may predispose horses to renal conditions that trigger behavioral changes.
treatment: Address underlying cause: nephroliths may require surgical removal (nephrotomy) or lithotripsy; pyelonephritis is treated with prolonged antimicrobials (trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 30 mg/kg PO BID or enrofloxacin 5 mg/kg IV SID). Manage visceral pain with flunixin meglumine (1.1 mg/kg IV BID) or buscopan (0.3 mg/kg IV). Correct dehydration with IV fluid therapy and adjust diet to reduce calcium/oxalate intake.
treatment_ja: 原因疾患の治療を行う：腎結石には外科的除去（腎切開術）または砕石術を検討し、腎盂腎炎にはトリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾール（30 mg/kg 経口 BID）またはエンロフロキサシン（5 mg/kg 静注 SID）の長期抗菌薬投与を実施する。内臓痛にはフルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg 静注 BID）やブスコパン（0.3 mg/kg 静注）で疼痛管理を行う。輸液療法で脱水を補正し、カルシウム・シュウ酸塩の摂取を制限する食事管理を行う。

name: Renal Infectious Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infectious disease in horses involves bacterial colonization of the kidney parenchyma, typically via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract or hematogenous spread. Bacteria such as Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., and Actinobacillus equuli cause inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue, leading to impaired glomerular filtration and tubular function. Chronic infection may result in pyelonephritis, fibrosis, and eventual renal insufficiency if left untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症は、下部尿路からの上行性感染または血行性播種により細菌が腎実質に定着することで発生する。大腸菌、レンサ球菌、Actinobacillus equuliなどの細菌が炎症、膿瘍形成、腎組織の進行性破壊を引き起こし、糸球体濾過および尿細管機能の障害をもたらす。慢性感染は腎盂腎炎、線維化、最終的には腎不全に進行する可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infections (most commonly E. coli, Streptococcus spp., Corynebacterium spp.) from the lower urinary tract, and hematogenous spread from distant infection sites. Secondary causes include urolithiasis causing urinary stasis, immunosuppression, urinary catheterization, anatomical abnormalities, and pre-existing bladder dysfunction that predispose to bacterial colonization of the kidneys.
treatment: Initiate aggressive parenteral antibiotic therapy based on urine culture and sensitivity, commonly trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (30 mg/kg PO BID) or enrofloxacin (5 mg/kg IV/PO SID) for 2-4 weeks. Provide IV fluid therapy to maintain renal perfusion and correct electrolyte imbalances. Address underlying causes such as urolithiasis surgically if needed, and provide NSAIDs (flunixin meglumine 1.1 mg/kg IV) for pain and inflammation control.
treatment_ja: 尿培養・感受性試験に基づき、トリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾール（30 mg/kg 経口 BID）またはエンロフロキサシン（5 mg/kg 静注/経口 SID）を2〜4週間投与する積極的な抗菌療法を開始する。腎灌流の維持と電解質補正のために静脈内輸液療法を実施する。尿路結石などの基礎疾患がある場合は外科的に対処し、フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg 静注）により疼痛・炎症管理を行う。

name: Renal Parasitic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal parasitic disease in horses involves migration and colonization of parasites such as Halicephalobus gingivalis (Halicephalobus deletrix), Strongylus vulgaris larvae, or Dioctophyme renale within the renal parenchyma or vasculature. Parasitic invasion causes granulomatous inflammation, tissue destruction, fibrosis, and progressive impairment of renal function. Larval migration through renal arteries can also lead to thrombosis, infarction, and secondary bacterial infection of the kidneys.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎寄生虫症は、Halicephalobus gingivalis、大型円虫（Strongylus vulgaris）の幼虫、または腎虫（Dioctophyme renale）などの寄生虫が腎実質や血管系に移行・定着することで発症する。寄生虫の侵入により肉芽腫性炎症、組織破壊、線維化が起こり、腎機能が進行性に障害される。腎動脈を介した幼虫移行は血栓症、梗塞、および二次的な細菌感染を引き起こすこともある。
causes: Primary causes include parasitic infections by Halicephalobus gingivalis (a free-living nematode with opportunistic pathogenicity), migrating larvae of Strongylus vulgaris through the mesenteric and renal vasculature, and rarely Dioctophyme renale (giant kidney worm). Secondary causes include immunosuppression, poor hygiene, and exposure to contaminated soil or water facilitating parasitic entry.
treatment: Treatment is often limited due to late diagnosis. High-dose anthelmintics such as fenbendazole (10 mg/kg PO daily for 5 days) or ivermectin (0.2 mg/kg PO) may be attempted, though efficacy against Halicephalobus gingivalis is poor. Nephrectomy of the affected kidney may be considered if disease is unilateral. Supportive care includes NSAIDs for inflammation, fluid therapy, and antimicrobials for secondary infections.
treatment_ja: 診断が遅れることが多く、治療は限定的である。フェンベンダゾール（10 mg/kg 経口 1日1回 5日間）やイベルメクチン（0.2 mg/kg 経口）などの高用量駆虫薬が試みられるが、Halicephalobus gingivalisに対する有効性は低い。片側性の場合は患側腎の腎摘出術が検討される。補助療法としてNSAIDsによる抗炎症療法、輸液療法、二次感染に対する抗菌薬投与を行う。

name: Renal Viral Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Viral agents such as equine herpesvirus (EHV) or equine arteritis virus (EAV) can cause vasculitis and immune-mediated damage to the renal vasculature and glomeruli, leading to impaired glomerular filtration and tubular dysfunction. Immune complex deposition in the kidneys results in glomerulonephritis, interstitial nephritis, and progressive renal insufficiency. In severe cases, viral-induced endothelial damage leads to thrombosis and ischemic injury to renal parenchyma.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬ヘルペスウイルス（EHV）や馬動脈炎ウイルス（EAV）などのウイルスが腎血管や糸球体に血管炎および免疫介在性障害を引き起こし、糸球体濾過と尿細管機能の低下をもたらす。免疫複合体の腎臓への沈着により糸球体腎炎、間質性腎炎、進行性腎不全が生じる。重症例ではウイルスによる内皮障害が血栓形成と腎実質の虚血性障害を引き起こす。
causes: Primary causes include equine herpesvirus (EHV-1, EHV-4), equine arteritis virus (EAV), and potentially other systemic viral infections that target renal vasculature. Secondary causes include immune complex-mediated glomerulonephritis triggered by chronic viral antigenemia, as well as concurrent dehydration, nephrotoxic drug administration, or bacterial superinfection exacerbating renal damage.
treatment: No specific antiviral cure exists; treatment is primarily supportive. Administer IV balanced crystalloid fluids (e.g., lactated Ringer's solution) to maintain renal perfusion and correct electrolyte imbalances. Use flunixin meglumine (1.1 mg/kg IV) for anti-inflammatory effects, ACE inhibitors such as benazepril for glomerular proteinuria management, and broad-spectrum antibiotics if secondary bacterial infection is suspected. Monitor renal values closely and consider plasma transfusion if hypoproteinemia develops.
treatment_ja: 特異的な抗ウイルス治療法は存在せず、主に支持療法が中心となる。乳酸リンゲル液などの等張晶質液を静脈内投与し、腎灌流の維持と電解質補正を行う。フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg IV）を抗炎症目的で投与し、糸球体性蛋白尿の管理にはベナゼプリル等のACE阻害薬を使用する。二次的細菌感染が疑われる場合は広域スペクトル抗菌薬を併用し、腎数値を厳密にモニタリングする。低蛋白血症が進行した場合は血漿輸血を検討する。

name: Renal Bacterial Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Bacterial infection of the kidneys (pyelonephritis) in horses typically occurs via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract or, less commonly, through hematogenous spread. Bacteria colonize the renal pelvis and parenchyma, causing inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue. Chronic infection can lead to fibrosis, impaired renal function, and potentially renal failure if bilateral involvement occurs.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎臓における細菌感染（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路からの上行性感染、またはまれに血行性播種によって発生します。細菌が腎盂および腎実質に定着し、炎症、膿瘍形成、および腎組織の進行性破壊を引き起こします。慢性感染は線維化や腎機能障害を招き、両側性の場合は腎不全に至る可能性があります。
causes: Common causative organisms include Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Staphylococcus spp., Corynebacterium spp., and Actinobacillus equuli. Predisposing factors include urolithiasis, urinary tract obstruction, bladder paralysis, catheterization, immunosuppression, and pre-existing lower urinary tract infections. Mares may be more susceptible due to their shorter urethra facilitating ascending infection.
treatment: Initiate broad-spectrum antimicrobial therapy based on urine culture and sensitivity, commonly trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (30 mg/kg PO BID) or enrofloxacin (5 mg/kg IV/PO SID) for 4-6 weeks minimum. Provide IV fluid therapy to maintain renal perfusion and correct dehydration. Address underlying predisposing factors such as urolithiasis or urinary obstruction surgically if indicated.
treatment_ja: 尿培養・感受性試験に基づき、トリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾール（30 mg/kg PO BID）またはエンロフロキサシン（5 mg/kg IV/PO SID）を最低4〜6週間投与する。輸液療法により腎灌流を維持し脱水を補正する。尿路結石や尿路閉塞などの素因がある場合は、必要に応じて外科的に対処する。

name: Renal Fungal Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Fungal organisms, most commonly Aspergillus spp. or Candida spp., colonize the renal parenchyma and/or renal pelvis, leading to granulomatous or necrotizing inflammation. The infection disrupts normal renal architecture, potentially causing tubular necrosis, obstruction of urine flow by fungal masses (fungal balls), and progressive loss of renal function. Hematogenous dissemination or ascending infection from the lower urinary tract can facilitate fungal colonization of the kidneys.
pathophysiology_ja: Aspergillus属やCandida属などの真菌が腎実質や腎盂に定着し、肉芽腫性または壊死性炎症を引き起こす。感染により正常な腎構造が破壊され、尿細管壊死、真菌塊（ファンガスボール）による尿路閉塞、腎機能の進行性低下が生じる。血行性播種または下部尿路からの上行性感染により腎臓への真菌定着が促進される。
causes: Primary causes include opportunistic fungal infections by Aspergillus spp., Candida spp., or other environmental fungi, often following prolonged antibiotic therapy, immunosuppression, or debilitation. Secondary causes include indwelling urinary catheters, concurrent systemic illness, corticosteroid use, or pre-existing renal damage that predisposes to fungal colonization. Prolonged hospitalization and disruption of normal mucosal barriers may also contribute.
treatment: Systemic antifungal therapy with fluconazole (5 mg/kg PO q24h) or itraconazole is first-line; amphotericin B (0.3-0.6 mg/kg IV slowly) may be used in severe cases with careful renal monitoring. Discontinue unnecessary antibiotics and corticosteroids. Supportive care includes IV fluid therapy to maintain renal perfusion and surgical intervention (nephrectomy) if unilateral obstruction or fungal mass is present.
treatment_ja: 全身性抗真菌療法としてフルコナゾール（5 mg/kg PO q24h）またはイトラコナゾールを第一選択とし、重症例ではアムホテリシンB（0.3〜0.6 mg/kg IV緩徐投与）を腎機能を慎重にモニタリングしながら使用する。不要な抗菌薬やコルチコステロイドは中止する。補液療法による腎灌流の維持、片側性の閉塞や真菌塊が認められる場合は腎摘出術などの外科的介入を行う。

name: Renal Infection (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infection (pyelonephritis) in horses typically occurs via ascending bacterial infection from the lower urinary tract through the ureters to the renal pelvis and parenchyma. Bacterial colonization triggers an inflammatory response, leading to neutrophilic infiltration, tubular damage, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue. If left untreated, chronic infection can result in renal fibrosis, impaired glomerular filtration, and potentially renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路から尿管を経て腎盂および腎実質への上行性細菌感染により発生します。細菌の定着は炎症反応を引き起こし、好中球浸潤、尿細管障害、膿瘍形成、および腎組織の進行性破壊をもたらします。未治療の場合、慢性感染は腎線維化、糸球体濾過率の低下、さらには腎不全に至る可能性があります。
causes: The primary cause is ascending bacterial infection, most commonly by organisms such as Escherichia coli, Corynebacterium renale, Streptococcus spp., and Actinobacillus equuli. Predisposing factors include urolithiasis, urinary stasis, bladder paralysis (e.g., from equine herpesvirus-1 myeloencephalopathy), catheterization, immunosuppression, and structural abnormalities of the urinary tract. Hematogenous spread from distant infection sites is a less common secondary cause.
treatment: Initiate prolonged systemic antibiotic therapy (4-6 weeks) based on urine culture and sensitivity, commonly trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole or enrofloxacin for gram-negative infections. Provide IV fluid therapy to promote diuresis and correct electrolyte imbalances. Address predisposing factors such as urolithiasis or bladder dysfunction, and monitor renal function via serial bloodwork and urinalysis.
treatment_ja: 尿培養・感受性試験に基づき、トリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾールやエンロフロキサシンなどの全身性抗菌薬を4〜6週間投与する。輸液療法により利尿を促進し電解質異常を補正する。尿石症や膀胱機能障害などの素因を治療し、血液検査および尿検査で腎機能を継続的にモニタリングする。

name: Renal Inflammation (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal inflammation (nephritis) in horses involves immune-mediated or infectious damage to the glomeruli, tubules, or interstitium of the kidneys, leading to impaired filtration, reabsorption, and secretion functions. Inflammatory cell infiltration and edema compromise renal blood flow and nephron integrity, resulting in azotemia, electrolyte imbalances, and potentially progressive renal failure. Chronic inflammation can lead to fibrosis, tubular atrophy, and irreversible loss of functional renal tissue.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎炎は、免疫介在性または感染性の障害により糸球体、尿細管、または間質に炎症が生じ、濾過・再吸収・分泌機能が障害される病態である。炎症細胞の浸潤や浮腫により腎血流とネフロンの機能が低下し、高窒素血症や電解質異常、進行性の腎不全を引き起こす。慢性的な炎症は線維化や尿細管萎縮を招き、不可逆的な腎機能喪失につながる。
causes: Primary causes include bacterial infections (e.g., Leptospira spp., Streptococcus equi), viral infections (e.g., equine infectious anemia), and immune-mediated glomerulonephritis. Secondary causes include nephrotoxic drugs (e.g., NSAIDs, aminoglycosides), toxin exposure (e.g., heavy metals, oak or red maple ingestion), systemic sepsis, and chronic dehydration or hemodynamic compromise.
treatment: Discontinue nephrotoxic agents (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides) immediately. Administer aggressive IV fluid therapy (lactated Ringer's or 0.9% NaCl) to restore renal perfusion. Treat underlying infections with renal-safe antibiotics (e.g., penicillin for Streptococcus, oxytetracycline for Leptospira). Corticosteroids (dexamethasone 0.05-0.1 mg/kg IV) may be used for immune-mediated nephritis. Monitor electrolytes, BUN, and creatinine closely.
treatment_ja: 腎毒性薬剤（NSAIDs、アミノグリコシド系）を直ちに中止する。積極的な静脈内輸液療法（乳酸リンゲル液または生理食塩水）を実施し、腎灌流を回復させる。基礎感染症には腎安全性の高い抗菌薬（レンサ球菌にはペニシリン、レプトスピラにはオキシテトラサイクリン）を投与する。免疫介在性腎炎にはデキサメタゾン（0.05〜0.1 mg/kg IV）を使用する。電解質、BUN、クレアチニンを厳密にモニタリングする。

name: Renal Neoplasia (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal neoplasia in horses involves the uncontrolled proliferation of neoplastic cells within the kidney parenchyma or renal pelvis. The most common primary renal tumors in horses include renal cell carcinoma, nephroblastoma, and lymphoma, which can disrupt normal renal architecture, impair filtration and excretory functions, and potentially metastasize to regional lymph nodes, lungs, and other organs. Progressive tumor growth may lead to renal insufficiency, obstruction of the urinary tract, and paraneoplastic syndromes.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎腫瘍は、腎実質または腎盂における腫瘍細胞の無制御な増殖を伴う。馬で最も一般的な原発性腎腫瘍には腎細胞癌、腎芽腫（ネフロブラストーマ）、リンパ腫があり、正常な腎構造を破壊し、濾過・排泄機能を障害し、所属リンパ節や肺などへ転移する可能性がある。腫瘍の進行により腎不全、尿路閉塞、および腫瘍随伴症候群が生じることがある。
causes: The exact etiology of renal neoplasia in horses is largely unknown, with no consistent genetic, infectious, or environmental risk factors clearly identified. Renal cell carcinoma is the most commonly reported primary renal tumor, while lymphoma may involve the kidneys as part of multicentric disease. Age-related cellular mutations and possible chronic renal inflammation may contribute to tumor development.
treatment: Unilateral nephrectomy is the primary treatment for localized renal tumors such as renal cell carcinoma or nephroblastoma. For renal lymphoma, systemic chemotherapy (e.g., corticosteroids, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin) may be attempted. Supportive care includes NSAIDs for pain management, fluid therapy, and monitoring remaining kidney function.
treatment_ja: 腎細胞癌や腎芽腫などの限局性腎腫瘍には片側腎摘出術が第一選択となる。腎リンパ腫に対しては、全身化学療法（コルチコステロイド、シクロホスファミド、ドキソルビシンなど）が試みられることがある。支持療法として、NSAIDsによる疼痛管理、輸液療法、および残存腎機能のモニタリングを行う。

name: Renal Metabolic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal metabolic disease in horses involves impaired kidney function affecting electrolyte balance, acid-base homeostasis, and waste product elimination. The kidneys fail to adequately regulate calcium, phosphorus, and other minerals, leading to metabolic derangements such as hypercalcemia, hyperphosphatemia, or metabolic acidosis. Chronic dysfunction may result in renal secondary hyperparathyroidism, soft tissue mineralization, and progressive nephron loss.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎代謝疾患は、電解質バランス、酸塩基平衡、および老廃物排泄に影響を与える腎機能障害を伴います。腎臓がカルシウム、リン、その他のミネラルを適切に調節できなくなり、高カルシウム血症、高リン血症、代謝性アシドーシスなどの代謝異常を引き起こします。慢性的な機能障害は、腎性二次性上皮小体機能亢進症、軟部組織の石灰化、および進行性のネフロン喪失につながる可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include chronic kidney disease, nephrolithiasis, and toxic nephropathy from ingestion of nephrotoxic plants (e.g., oak, red maple) or drugs (e.g., NSAIDs, aminoglycosides). Secondary causes include dehydration, systemic infections, hemodynamic compromise, and dietary imbalances with excessive calcium or oxalate intake. Age-related degenerative changes and obstructive urolithiasis may also contribute.
treatment: Aggressive IV fluid therapy (balanced polyionic solutions) to restore renal perfusion and correct dehydration. Discontinue nephrotoxic agents (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides). Correct electrolyte imbalances with calcium gluconate or phosphate binders as needed. Manage acidosis with sodium bicarbonate, and provide dietary modification with reduced protein and calcium intake to decrease renal workload.
treatment_ja: 積極的な静脈内輸液療法（バランス電解質液）で腎灌流を回復し脱水を是正する。NSAIDsやアミノグリコシド系薬剤など腎毒性物質を中止する。グルコン酸カルシウムやリン吸着剤で電解質異常を補正し、重炭酸ナトリウムでアシドーシスを管理する。腎臓への負担軽減のため低タンパク・低カルシウム食への食事変更を行う。

name: Renal Nutritional Deficiency (Horse)
pathophysiology: Nutritional deficiencies, particularly of vitamin A, vitamin D, calcium, phosphorus, or oxalate-rich diets, can impair renal tubular function and lead to nephrocalcinosis or renal tubular degeneration in horses. Imbalanced calcium-phosphorus ratios or excessive oxalate intake can cause calcium oxalate crystal deposition in renal tissue, resulting in progressive nephropathy. Chronic deficiency states may also impair renal concentrating ability and lead to secondary renal fibrosis.
pathophysiology_ja: ビタミンA、ビタミンD、カルシウム、リンなどの栄養素の欠乏やシュウ酸塩の過剰摂取は、腎尿細管機能を障害し、腎石灰沈着症や腎尿細管変性を引き起こします。カルシウム・リン比の不均衡やシュウ酸塩の過剰摂取はシュウ酸カルシウム結晶の腎組織への沈着を引き起こし、進行性腎症に至ります。慢性的な欠乏状態は腎濃縮能を低下させ、二次性腎線維症を引き起こすことがあります。
causes: Primary causes include prolonged dietary imbalances such as calcium-phosphorus ratio inversion (high grain/low forage diets), vitamin A or D deficiency, and ingestion of oxalate-rich plants (e.g., Oxalis, Setaria, Halogeton). Secondary causes include chronic malabsorption, parasitism, or poor-quality forage leading to cumulative nutritional deficits affecting renal function.
treatment: Correct dietary imbalances by restoring proper calcium-phosphorus ratio (2:1) with balanced forage-based feeding and removing oxalate-rich plants. Supplement vitamin A (40,000-60,000 IU/day) and vitamin D (3,000-6,000 IU/day) as needed. Provide IV fluid therapy with balanced electrolytes to support renal perfusion and tubular recovery; administer activated charcoal if acute oxalate ingestion is suspected.
treatment_ja: カルシウム・リン比（2:1）を適正化するため、良質な粗飼料中心の飼料に切り替え、シュウ酸含有植物を除去する。必要に応じてビタミンA（40,000〜60,000 IU/日）およびビタミンD（3,000〜6,000 IU/日）を補給する。バランス電解質を含む輸液療法で腎灌流と尿細管回復を支援し、急性シュウ酸摂取が疑われる場合は活性炭を経口投与する。

name: Renal Genetic Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal genetic disorders in horses involve inherited mutations affecting renal tubular or glomerular structure and function, leading to progressive nephron loss, impaired filtration, and disrupted electrolyte and fluid homeostasis. Examples include renal dysplasia and polycystic kidney disease, where abnormal kidney development or cyst formation progressively replaces functional renal parenchyma. This results in chronic renal failure with azotemia, proteinuria, and eventual end-stage kidney disease.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎遺伝性疾患は、腎尿細管や糸球体の構造・機能に影響を及ぼす遺伝子変異により、ネフロンの進行性喪失、濾過機能障害、電解質・水分バランスの乱れを引き起こします。腎異形成や多発性嚢胞腎などが含まれ、腎臓の異常発達や嚢胞形成により機能的な腎実質が進行的に置換されます。その結果、高窒素血症や蛋白尿を伴う慢性腎不全へと進行します。
causes: The primary cause is inherited genetic mutations affecting kidney development or function, such as autosomal recessive or dominant mutations leading to renal dysplasia or polycystic kidney disease. Specific breed predispositions have been identified, and consanguineous breeding increases the risk. Secondary factors such as dehydration, concurrent infections, or nephrotoxin exposure may accelerate the progression of underlying genetic renal disease.
treatment: No curative treatment exists for renal genetic disorders in horses. Management is supportive: IV fluid therapy to maintain hydration and electrolyte balance, ACE inhibitors (e.g., enalapril 0.5 mg/kg PO q24h) to reduce glomerular hypertension, dietary protein restriction, phosphate binders for hyperphosphatemia, and monitoring renal values. Breeding management to eliminate affected lines is essential.
treatment_ja: 馬の腎遺伝性疾患に根治療法は存在しません。治療は対症療法が中心で、輸液療法による水分・電解質バランスの維持、ACE阻害薬（エナラプリル0.5 mg/kg 経口 1日1回）による糸球体内高血圧の軽減、食事中のタンパク質制限、高リン血症に対するリン吸着剤の投与、および腎機能値の定期的モニタリングを行います。罹患系統を排除するための繁殖管理も不可欠です。

name: Renal Autoimmune Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: The immune system produces autoantibodies or autoreactive T cells directed against renal antigens, leading to immune complex deposition in glomeruli and/or tubulointerstitial inflammation. This results in progressive glomerulonephritis or interstitial nephritis with complement activation, inflammatory cell infiltration, and subsequent damage to the nephron architecture. Over time, chronic inflammation leads to fibrosis, loss of functional nephrons, and progressive renal insufficiency.
pathophysiology_ja: 免疫系が腎臓の抗原に対する自己抗体または自己反応性T細胞を産生し、糸球体への免疫複合体の沈着や尿細管間質の炎症を引き起こします。補体の活性化、炎症細胞の浸潤、およびネフロン構造の障害が生じます。慢性炎症により線維化が進行し、機能的ネフロンの喪失と進行性の腎不全に至ります。
causes: The primary cause is immune dysregulation leading to loss of self-tolerance against renal antigens, potentially triggered by prior infections (e.g., Streptococcus equi), drug reactions, or systemic autoimmune conditions such as equine systemic lupus-like syndrome. Secondary causes include chronic immune complex diseases, persistent viral infections, and exposure to certain toxins or medications that alter renal antigen presentation. Genetic predisposition may also play a role in susceptibility.
treatment: Immunosuppressive therapy with corticosteroids (dexamethasone 0.05-0.1 mg/kg IV initially, then oral prednisolone tapering) combined with azathioprine (3 mg/kg PO q24h) to suppress autoantibody production. Supportive care includes IV fluid therapy, ACE inhibitors (benazepril 0.5 mg/kg PO q24h) to reduce proteinuria, and monitoring renal parameters closely.
treatment_ja: 免疫抑制療法としてデキサメタゾン（0.05〜0.1 mg/kg IV、その後経口プレドニゾロンを漸減）とアザチオプリン（3 mg/kg PO 1日1回）を併用し、自己抗体産生を抑制する。補助療法として輸液療法、ACE阻害薬（ベナゼプリル0.5 mg/kg PO 1日1回）による蛋白尿軽減を行い、腎機能パラメータを継続的にモニタリングする。

name: Renal Degenerative Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal degenerative disease in horses involves progressive deterioration of nephron structure and function, including tubular degeneration, interstitial fibrosis, and glomerulosclerosis. This leads to impaired filtration, concentration ability, and electrolyte balance, ultimately resulting in chronic kidney failure. Accumulation of uremic toxins and loss of renal endocrine functions (erythropoietin, vitamin D activation) further contribute to systemic decline.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎変性疾患は、尿細管変性、間質線維化、糸球体硬化症を含むネフロン構造と機能の進行性劣化を伴います。これにより、濾過機能、濃縮能力、電解質バランスが障害され、最終的に慢性腎不全に至ります。尿毒症性毒素の蓄積と腎内分泌機能（エリスロポエチン、ビタミンD活性化）の喪失がさらに全身状態の悪化に寄与します。
causes: Primary causes include chronic nephrotoxin exposure (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals, vitamin D toxicosis), chronic ischemia, and idiopathic progressive nephropathy. Secondary causes include chronic pyelonephritis, nephrolithiasis, systemic diseases (e.g., equine infectious anemia, leptospirosis), and age-related degenerative changes. Ingestion of toxic plants such as oak (acorns) and red maple leaves can also contribute.
treatment: Remove nephrotoxic agents immediately. Provide IV fluid therapy (polyionic isotonic crystalloids) to correct dehydration and electrolyte imbalances. Manage azotemia with dietary protein restriction; treat hypertension with ACE inhibitors (benazepril 0.5 mg/kg PO q24h). Address metabolic acidosis with sodium bicarbonate supplementation and manage secondary complications such as gastric ulceration with omeprazole (4 mg/kg PO q24h).
treatment_ja: 腎毒性物質を直ちに除去する。脱水および電解質異常の是正のため等張晶質液による静脈内輸液療法を実施する。高窒素血症には食事中のタンパク質制限で管理し、高血圧にはACE阻害薬（ベナゼプリル0.5 mg/kg PO 1日1回）を投与する。代謝性アシドーシスには重炭酸ナトリウムを補充し、胃潰瘍などの二次的合併症にはオメプラゾール（4 mg/kg PO 1日1回）で対処する。

name: Renal Traumatic Injury (Horse)
pathophysiology: Blunt or penetrating trauma to the lumbar region causes direct damage to renal parenchyma, capsule, or vascular pedicle, leading to hemorrhage, hematoma formation, and potentially urine leakage into the retroperitoneal space. The resulting inflammation, ischemia, and possible secondary infection can lead to progressive renal dysfunction. In severe cases, disruption of the renal vasculature may cause life-threatening hemorrhage or subsequent renal infarction.
pathophysiology_ja: 腰部への鈍的または穿通性外傷により、腎実質、腎被膜、または血管茎に直接的な損傷が生じ、出血、血腫形成、および後腹膜腔への尿漏出が起こる。その結果生じる炎症、虚血、および二次感染により腎機能が進行性に低下する可能性がある。重症例では腎血管の断裂により致命的な出血や腎梗塞を引き起こすことがある。
causes: Primary causes include blunt trauma from kicks by other horses, falls, collisions with fixed objects, or vehicular accidents. Secondary causes include penetrating injuries from broken fence posts, sharp objects, or iatrogenic damage during rectal examination or surgical procedures. Severe exercise-related trauma or crushing injuries during casting for surgery may also contribute.
causes_ja: 主な原因は、他の馬からの蹴り、転倒、固定物への衝突、または交通事故による鈍的外傷である。二次的原因には、破損した柵の杭や鋭利な物体による穿通性外傷、直腸検査や外科手術中の医原性損傷が含まれる。激しい運動に伴う外傷や手術時の保定による圧挫損傷も原因となりうる。
treatment: Stabilize with IV crystalloid fluids (LRS or 0.9% NaCl) and control hemorrhage. Administer flunixin meglumine (1.1 mg/kg IV q12h) for analgesia and anti-inflammatory effect, broad-spectrum antibiotics (gentamicin 6.6 mg/kg IV q24h plus penicillin 22,000 IU/kg IV q6h) to prevent secondary infection. Strict stall rest with serial ultrasound monitoring; surgical nephrectomy is indicated for severe vascular pedicle avulsion or uncontrolled hemorrhage.
treatment_ja: 乳酸リンゲル液または生理食塩水による積極的な輸液療法で循環を安定させ、出血を管理する。フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg IV 12時間毎）で鎮痛・抗炎症を図り、ゲンタマイシン（6.6 mg/kg IV 24時間毎）およびペニシリン（22,000 IU/kg IV 6時間毎）の広域抗菌薬で二次感染を予防する。厳格な馬房安静と超音波検査による経時的モニタリングを実施し、腎血管茎の断裂や制御不能な出血がある場合は腎摘出術を検討する。

name: Renal Behavioral Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal behavioral disorder in horses involves abnormal behaviors (such as frequent posturing to urinate, stretching, flank watching, or irritability) that are attributed to renal pain or dysfunction. Chronic renal inflammation, nephrolithiasis, or subclinical renal disease can cause visceral pain that manifests as behavioral changes rather than overt clinical signs. Altered nociceptive signaling from the kidneys and ureters may lead to persistent discomfort-related behaviors that mimic colic or musculoskeletal pain.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎行動障害は、腎臓の疼痛や機能不全に起因する異常行動（頻繁な排尿姿勢、体の伸展、脇腹を気にする行動、易刺激性など）を伴います。慢性腎炎症、腎結石症、または潜在的な腎疾患が内臓痛を引き起こし、明らかな臨床症状ではなく行動変化として現れます。腎臓および尿管からの異常な侵害受容シグナルが、疝痛や筋骨格系の痛みに類似した持続的な不快感関連行動を引き起こします。
causes: Primary causes include nephrolithiasis, renal calculi, chronic nephritis, pyelonephritis, and renal cysts that produce intermittent or chronic renal pain. Secondary causes may involve ureterolithiasis, renal neoplasia, perirenal adhesions, or referred pain from adjacent structures. Subclinical urinary tract infections and idiopathic renal pain syndrome may also contribute to behavioral manifestations.
treatment: Treat underlying cause: nephrolithotomy or lithotripsy for renal calculi; antimicrobials (trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 30 mg/kg PO BID) for pyelonephritis. Manage renal pain with flunixin meglumine (1.1 mg/kg IV BID) or phenylbutazone (2.2-4.4 mg/kg PO BID). Provide IV fluid therapy for renal support and correct electrolyte imbalances.
treatment_ja: 原因疾患の治療として、腎結石には腎切石術または砕石術を実施し、腎盂腎炎にはトリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾール（30 mg/kg PO BID）を投与する。腎性疼痛にはフルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg IV BID）またはフェニルブタゾン（2.2～4.4 mg/kg PO BID）で管理する。輸液療法により腎機能を支持し、電解質異常を補正する。

name: Renal Infectious Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infectious disease in horses involves bacterial invasion of the renal parenchyma, typically ascending from the lower urinary tract or via hematogenous spread. Infection leads to inflammation (pyelonephritis), abscess formation, and progressive damage to the renal tubules, interstitium, and potentially the glomeruli. If untreated, chronic infection can result in renal fibrosis, impaired glomerular filtration, and eventual renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症は、下部尿路からの上行性感染または血行性播種により細菌が腎実質に侵入することで発症します。感染により腎盂腎炎、膿瘍形成が生じ、腎尿細管、間質、さらには糸球体に進行性の損傷をもたらします。未治療の場合、慢性感染は腎線維化、糸球体濾過率の低下、最終的に腎不全に至る可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infections (commonly Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Corynebacterium spp., and Actinobacillus equuli) from the lower urinary tract, as well as hematogenous spread from distant infection sites. Secondary contributing factors include urolithiasis, urinary tract obstruction, immunosuppression, indwelling urinary catheters, and pre-existing renal or bladder conditions that promote bacterial colonization.
treatment: Initiate aggressive parenteral antibiotic therapy based on urine culture and sensitivity, commonly trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (30 mg/kg PO BID) or enrofloxacin (5 mg/kg IV/PO SID) for 4-6 weeks. Provide IV fluid therapy to maintain hydration and renal perfusion. Address underlying causes such as urolithiasis surgically if present, and monitor renal function via serial bloodwork and urinalysis.
treatment_ja: 尿培養・感受性試験に基づき、トリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾール（30 mg/kg 経口 BID）またはエンロフロキサシン（5 mg/kg 静注/経口 SID）を4〜6週間投与する積極的な抗菌薬治療を開始する。静脈内輸液により水分補給と腎灌流を維持する。尿路結石などの基礎疾患がある場合は外科的に対処し、血液検査および尿検査で腎機能を継続的にモニタリングする。

name: Renal Parasitic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal parasitic disease in horses occurs when parasites such as Halicephalobus gingivalis (formerly Halicephalobus deletrix), Strongylus vulgaris larvae, or Dioctophyme renale migrate to or directly invade the renal parenchyma. The parasitic invasion causes granulomatous inflammation, tissue destruction, and progressive nephritis, potentially leading to renal insufficiency. Larval migration through renal vasculature can also cause thrombosis, ischemia, and infarction of renal tissue.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎寄生虫疾患は、Halicephalobus gingivalis、普通円虫（Strongylus vulgaris）の幼虫、または腎虫（Dioctophyme renale）などの寄生虫が腎実質に移行・侵入することで発生する。寄生虫の侵入により肉芽腫性炎症、組織破壊、進行性腎炎が引き起こされ、腎不全に至る可能性がある。幼虫の腎血管内移行は血栓症、虚血、腎組織の梗塞を引き起こすこともある。
causes: Primary causes include migration of parasitic larvae such as Strongylus vulgaris through the mesenteric and renal vasculature, direct renal invasion by Halicephalobus gingivalis (a free-living nematode with opportunistic parasitic behavior), and rarely Dioctophyme renale infection. Secondary causes include immunosuppression, heavy parasite burden due to inadequate deworming, and environmental exposure to contaminated soil or water sources harboring the parasites.
treatment: Administer broad-spectrum anthelmintics such as fenbendazole (10 mg/kg PO daily for 5 days) or ivermectin (0.2 mg/kg PO); however, efficacy against Halicephalobus gingivalis is often limited. Supportive care includes NSAIDs (flunixin meglumine 1.1 mg/kg IV) for inflammation and IV fluid therapy for renal support. Nephrectomy of the affected kidney may be considered in unilateral severe cases.
treatment_ja: フェンベンダゾール（10 mg/kg 経口、5日間連投）やイベルメクチン（0.2 mg/kg 経口）などの広域駆虫薬を投与するが、Halicephalobus gingivalisに対しては効果が限定的な場合が多い。フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg 静注）による抗炎症療法や輸液療法で腎機能を補助する。片側性の重度症例では罹患腎の腎摘出術を検討する。

name: Renal Viral Disease (Horse)
