Secondary causes include immunosuppression, heavy parasite burden due to inadequate deworming, and environmental exposure to contaminated soil or water.
treatment: Administer high-dose anthelmintics such as fenbendazole (10 mg/kg PO daily for 5 days) or ivermectin (0.2 mg/kg PO); however, efficacy against Halicephalobus gingivalis is often poor. Provide supportive care including NSAIDs (flunixin meglumine 1.1 mg/kg IV) for inflammation, fluid therapy for renal support, and corticosteroids to manage granulomatous response. Unilateral nephrectomy may be considered if damage is localized to one kidney.
treatment_ja: フェンベンダゾール（10 mg/kg 経口、5日間連続投与）やイベルメクチン（0.2 mg/kg 経口）などの高用量駆虫薬を投与するが、Halicephalobus gingivalisに対する有効性は限定的である。フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg 静注）による抗炎症療法、輸液による腎機能補助、肉芽腫性反応抑制のための副腎皮質ステロイド投与など支持療法を行う。病変が片側腎に限局している場合は片側腎摘出術を検討する。

name: Renal Viral Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Viral agents such as equine herpesvirus (EHV) or equine arteritis virus (EAV) can cause direct cytopathic damage to renal tubular epithelial cells and glomeruli, leading to immune-complex deposition, vasculitis, interstitial nephritis, and impaired renal function. Viral-induced endothelial injury in renal vasculature results in ischemia, inflammation, and progressive nephron loss. Secondary immune-mediated mechanisms may further exacerbate glomerulonephritis and tubular necrosis.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬ヘルペスウイルス（EHV）や馬動脈炎ウイルス（EAV）などのウイルスが腎尿細管上皮細胞や糸球体に直接的な細胞障害を引き起こし、免疫複合体の沈着、血管炎、間質性腎炎、腎機能障害をもたらす。腎血管内皮の障害により虚血、炎症、ネフロンの進行性喪失が生じる。二次的な免疫介在性機序が糸球体腎炎や尿細管壊死をさらに悪化させることがある。
causes: Primary causes include viral infections such as equine herpesvirus type 1 (EHV-1), equine arteritis virus (EAV), and potentially other nephrotrophic viruses that target renal tissue. Secondary causes include immune-complex deposition from systemic viral infections, concurrent bacterial superinfection, dehydration, and nephrotoxic drug administration during viral illness.
treatment: No specific antiviral therapy exists; treatment is primarily supportive. Administer IV fluid therapy (balanced polyionic solutions) to maintain renal perfusion and correct electrolyte imbalances. Use NSAIDs (flunixin meglumine 1.1 mg/kg IV) cautiously for inflammation, broad-spectrum antibiotics for bacterial superinfection, and valacyclovir (30 mg/kg PO BID) if EHV-1 is confirmed.
treatment_ja: 特異的な抗ウイルス療法は存在せず、治療は主に支持療法となる。静脈内輸液（バランス電解質液）を投与し、腎灌流の維持と電解質異常の補正を行う。抗炎症目的でフルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg IV）を慎重に使用し、細菌二次感染には広域抗菌薬を投与する。EHV-1確定例ではバラシクロビル（30 mg/kg 経口 BID）の投与を検討する。

name: Renal Bacterial Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Bacterial pathogens, most commonly Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Staphylococcus spp., or Actinobacillus spp., ascend the urinary tract or spread hematogenously to the renal parenchyma, causing inflammation, abscessation, and impaired renal function. The infection triggers neutrophilic infiltration, tubular damage, and potentially pyelonephritis, leading to progressive nephron destruction and compromised urine concentrating ability. Chronic cases may result in fibrosis, renal scarring, and eventual renal insufficiency or failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 大腸菌、レンサ球菌、ブドウ球菌、アクチノバチルス属などの細菌が尿路上行性感染または血行性に腎実質に到達し、炎症、膿瘍形成、腎機能障害を引き起こす。感染により好中球浸潤、尿細管障害、腎盂腎炎が生じ、ネフロンの進行性破壊と尿濃縮能の低下をもたらす。慢性例では線維化、腎瘢痕化が進行し、最終的に腎不全に至ることがある。
causes: Primary causes include ascending urinary tract infections from the lower urinary tract (cystitis, urethritis), hematogenous spread from distant infection sites (e.g., endocarditis, pneumonia, abscesses), and contamination during urinary catheterization. Secondary contributing factors include urolithiasis causing urinary obstruction and stasis, immunosuppression, anatomical abnormalities, and chronic debilitating conditions that predispose to bacterial colonization of the kidneys.
treatment: Initiate aggressive systemic antibiotic therapy based on urine culture and sensitivity; commonly trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (30 mg/kg PO BID) or enrofloxacin (5 mg/kg IV/PO SID). Provide IV fluid therapy to maintain renal perfusion and correct electrolyte imbalances. Address underlying causes such as urolithiasis or catheter-related infection and provide anti-inflammatory support with flunixin meglumine (1.1 mg/kg IV).
treatment_ja: 尿培養・感受性試験に基づき、トリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾール（30 mg/kg 経口 BID）またはエンロフロキサシン（5 mg/kg 静注/経口 SID）などの全身性抗菌薬療法を積極的に開始する。静脈内輸液療法により腎灌流を維持し電解質異常を補正する。尿路結石やカテーテル関連感染などの基礎疾患に対処し、フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg 静注）による抗炎症療法を併用する。

name: Renal Fungal Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Fungal organisms, most commonly Aspergillus spp. or Candida spp., colonize the renal parenchyma and/or renal pelvis, leading to granulomatous or necrotizing inflammation. The infection disrupts normal renal architecture, potentially causing tubular necrosis, obstruction of urine flow by fungal masses (fungal balls), and progressive loss of renal function. Hematogenous dissemination or ascending infection from the lower urinary tract can lead to unilateral or bilateral renal involvement.
pathophysiology_ja: Aspergillus属やCandida属などの真菌が腎実質および/または腎盂に定着し、肉芽腫性または壊死性の炎症を引き起こす。感染により正常な腎構造が破壊され、尿細管壊死、真菌塊（ファンガスボール）による尿路閉塞、および進行性の腎機能低下が生じる。血行性播種または下部尿路からの上行感染により片側性または両側性の腎障害が起こりうる。
causes: Primary causes include opportunistic fungal infections by Aspergillus spp., Candida spp., or other environmental fungi that gain access to the renal system. Secondary contributing factors include prolonged antibiotic therapy, immunosuppression, indwelling urinary catheters, debilitation, and concurrent systemic illness that compromises immune defenses.
causes_ja: 主な原因はAspergillus属、Candida属、その他の環境真菌による日和見感染である。二次的要因として、長期間の抗生物質投与、免疫抑制状態、留置尿道カテーテル、衰弱、および免疫防御を低下させる併発全身疾患が挙げられる。
treatment: Systemic antifungal therapy with fluconazole (5 mg/kg PO q24h) or amphotericin B (0.3-0.5 mg/kg IV slowly, with careful renal monitoring) is the primary approach. Correct underlying immunosuppression and discontinue unnecessary antibiotics. Nephrectomy may be indicated for unilateral, severely affected kidneys unresponsive to medical therapy.
treatment_ja: フルコナゾール（5 mg/kg 経口 1日1回）またはアムホテリシンB（0.3〜0.5 mg/kg 緩徐静注、腎機能を慎重にモニタリング）による全身性抗真菌療法が基本治療となる。基礎にある免疫抑制状態の改善および不要な抗菌薬の中止を行う。内科療法に反応しない片側性の重度罹患腎に対しては腎摘出術が適応となる場合がある。

name: Renal Infection (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infection (pyelonephritis) in horses typically occurs via ascending bacterial infection from the lower urinary tract through the ureters to the renal pelvis and parenchyma. Bacterial colonization triggers an inflammatory response, leading to neutrophilic infiltration, tubular damage, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue. If untreated, chronic infection can result in fibrosis, renal insufficiency, and potentially septicemia.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路から尿管を経由して腎盂および腎実質へ細菌が上行性に感染することで発生します。細菌の定着により炎症反応が引き起こされ、好中球浸潤、尿細管障害、膿瘍形成、および腎組織の進行性破壊が生じます。未治療の場合、慢性感染は線維化、腎不全、さらには敗血症に至る可能性があります。
causes: The most common causative agents include Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Staphylococcus spp., Corynebacterium renale, and Actinobacillus equuli, typically ascending from the lower urinary tract. Predisposing factors include urolithiasis, bladder paralysis, urethral obstruction, catheterization, immunosuppression, and conditions causing urinary stasis. Hematogenous spread from distant infection sites is a less common but recognized route.
treatment: Initiate aggressive systemic antibiotic therapy based on urine culture and sensitivity, commonly trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (30 mg/kg PO BID) or enrofloxacin (5 mg/kg IV/PO SID) for 4-6 weeks. Provide IV fluid therapy to maintain hydration and promote diuresis. Address predisposing factors such as urolithiasis or urethral obstruction surgically if indicated.
treatment_ja: 尿培養および感受性試験に基づき、トリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾール（30 mg/kg 経口 BID）またはエンロフロキサシン（5 mg/kg 静注/経口 SID）などの全身性抗菌薬を4〜6週間投与する。静脈輸液療法により水分補給と利尿を促進する。尿路結石や尿道閉塞などの素因がある場合は外科的処置を検討する。

name: Renal Inflammation (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal inflammation (nephritis) in horses involves immune-mediated or infectious injury to the glomeruli, tubules, or interstitium of the kidneys, leading to impaired filtration, proteinuria, and progressive loss of renal function. Inflammatory cell infiltration and edema disrupt normal nephron architecture, resulting in azotemia, electrolyte imbalances, and potentially acute or chronic renal failure. Immune complex deposition, direct bacterial invasion, or toxin-mediated damage can trigger the inflammatory cascade.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎炎（腎臓の炎症）は、免疫介在性または感染性の損傷が糸球体、尿細管、または間質に及ぶことで、濾過機能の障害、蛋白尿、腎機能の進行性低下を引き起こす。炎症細胞の浸潤と浮腫がネフロン構造を破壊し、高窒素血症や電解質異常、急性または慢性腎不全に至る可能性がある。免疫複合体の沈着、細菌の直接侵入、または毒素による損傷が炎症カスケードを惹起する。
causes: Primary causes include bacterial infections (e.g., Leptospira spp., Streptococcus equi), viral infections (e.g., equine infectious anemia), and nephrotoxic agents such as NSAIDs, aminoglycosides, heavy metals, and certain plants. Secondary causes include immune-complex deposition from systemic diseases, septicemia, endotoxemia, dehydration, and hemodynamic compromise leading to ischemic renal injury.
treatment: Discontinue all nephrotoxic agents (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides). Administer aggressive IV fluid therapy (balanced crystalloids) to maintain renal perfusion. Treat underlying infections with renal-safe antibiotics (e.g., penicillin for Streptococcus, oxytetracycline for Leptospira). Corticosteroids (dexamethasone 0.05-0.1 mg/kg IV) may be used for immune-mediated nephritis. Monitor electrolytes, creatinine, and urine output closely.
treatment_ja: すべての腎毒性薬剤（NSAIDs、アミノグリコシド系）を直ちに中止する。腎灌流を維持するため積極的な静脈内輸液療法（バランス晶質液）を実施する。基礎感染症には腎安全性の高い抗菌薬（連鎖球菌にはペニシリン、レプトスピラにはオキシテトラサイクリン）で治療する。免疫介在性腎炎にはデキサメタゾン（0.05〜0.1 mg/kg IV）を使用する。電解質、クレアチニン、尿量を綿密にモニタリングする。

name: Renal Neoplasia (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal neoplasia in horses involves the uncontrolled proliferation of cells within the kidney, most commonly renal cell carcinoma, lymphoma, or nephroblastoma. The tumor mass progressively replaces normal renal parenchyma, impairing renal function, and may invade local structures including the renal vein and caudal vena cava. Metastasis can occur via hematogenous or lymphatic routes to the lungs, liver, and other organs, leading to systemic disease.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎臓腫瘍は、腎細胞癌、リンパ腫、腎芽腫などが最も一般的であり、腎臓内の細胞が制御不能に増殖する疾患である。腫瘍塊は正常な腎実質を進行性に置換し、腎機能を障害し、腎静脈や後大静脈などの局所構造に浸潤することがある。血行性またはリンパ行性に肺、肝臓、その他の臓器に転移し、全身性疾患を引き起こす可能性がある。
causes: The exact etiology of renal neoplasia in horses is largely unknown, with no well-established predisposing factors identified. Renal cell carcinoma is the most frequently reported primary renal tumor, while lymphoma may affect the kidney as part of multicentric disease. Genetic mutations, chronic inflammation, and exposure to environmental carcinogens have been hypothesized but not confirmed in equines.
treatment: Unilateral nephrectomy is the primary treatment for localized renal tumors such as renal cell carcinoma or nephroblastoma, provided the contralateral kidney is functional. For renal lymphoma, systemic chemotherapy with corticosteroids (dexamethasone) and cyclophosphamide may be attempted. Supportive care includes IV fluid therapy, NSAIDs for pain management, and monitoring renal function via serial bloodwork.
treatment_ja: 腎細胞癌や腎芽腫など限局性腎腫瘍に対しては、対側腎の機能が正常であれば患側腎の摘出術（片側腎摘出術）が第一選択となる。腎リンパ腫の場合は、デキサメタゾンやシクロホスファミドを用いた全身化学療法が試みられる。支持療法として静脈内輸液、NSAIDsによる疼痛管理、および血液検査による腎機能の継続的モニタリングを実施する。

name: Renal Metabolic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal metabolic disease in horses involves disruption of normal kidney function affecting electrolyte balance, acid-base homeostasis, and waste product excretion. Impaired renal tubular function leads to abnormal handling of calcium, phosphorus, and bicarbonate, resulting in metabolic acidosis or alkalosis and mineral imbalances. Progressive nephron loss reduces glomerular filtration rate, causing azotemia and accumulation of uremic toxins.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎代謝疾患は、電解質バランス、酸塩基平衡、および老廃物排泄に影響を与える腎機能の障害を伴う。腎尿細管機能の障害により、カルシウム、リン、重炭酸塩の処理が異常となり、代謝性アシドーシスまたはアルカローシスおよびミネラル不均衡が生じる。進行性のネフロン喪失により糸球体濾過率が低下し、高窒素血症および尿毒症性毒素の蓄積を引き起こす。
causes: Primary causes include chronic kidney disease, renal tubular acidosis, nephrocalcinosis, and hypercalcemia secondary to excessive calcium intake or vitamin D toxicosis. Secondary causes include dehydration, nephrotoxic drugs (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides), heavy metal exposure, and systemic diseases such as leptospirosis or piroplasmosis that affect renal function. Dietary imbalances in calcium-phosphorus ratio and oxalate-containing plant ingestion can also contribute.
treatment: Administer IV balanced crystalloid fluids (lactated Ringer's or 0.9% NaCl) to correct dehydration and support renal perfusion. Correct electrolyte imbalances with calcium gluconate, phosphate binders (aluminum hydroxide), and sodium bicarbonate for metabolic acidosis. Discontinue nephrotoxic drugs (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides), provide dietary calcium/phosphorus adjustment, and monitor urine output and serum chemistry closely.
treatment_ja: 脱水補正と腎灌流維持のため乳酸リンゲル液または生理食塩水の静脈内輸液を実施する。電解質異常にはグルコン酸カルシウム、リン吸着剤（水酸化アルミニウム）、代謝性アシドーシスには炭酸水素ナトリウムを投与する。腎毒性薬剤（NSAIDs、アミノグリコシド系）を中止し、飼料中のカルシウム・リン比を調整し、尿量および血液生化学検査を継続的にモニタリングする。

name: Renal Nutritional Deficiency (Horse)
pathophysiology: Nutritional deficiencies, particularly of vitamin A, vitamin D, calcium, phosphorus, or oxalate-rich diets, can impair renal tubular function, promote nephrocalcinosis, or lead to calcium/phosphorus imbalances that cause renal mineralization and progressive nephron damage. Excessive dietary oxalates (e.g., from certain plants) bind calcium and deposit as calcium oxalate crystals in renal tubules, causing tubular necrosis and interstitial fibrosis. Chronic imbalances in the calcium-to-phosphorus ratio can lead to soft tissue mineralization including renal calcification, resulting in progressive loss of renal function.
pathophysiology_ja: ビタミンA、ビタミンD、カルシウム、リンなどの栄養素の欠乏やシュウ酸塩を多く含む飼料の摂取により、腎尿細管機能の障害、腎石灰化、またはカルシウム・リンの不均衡が生じ、ネフロンの進行性障害を引き起こす。過剰なシュウ酸塩はカルシウムと結合してシュウ酸カルシウム結晶として腎尿細管に沈着し、尿細管壊死や間質線維化を引き起こす。慢性的なカルシウム・リン比の不均衡は腎臓を含む軟部組織の石灰化を引き起こし、腎機能が進行的に低下する。
treatment: Correct dietary imbalances by removing oxalate-rich plants and providing balanced calcium-phosphorus ratios (Ca:P ~2:1). Supplement vitamin A (50,000-100,000 IU/day) and vitamin D as indicated. Administer IV fluids (lactated Ringer's solution) for renal support, and provide phosphate binders if hyperphosphatemia is present. Monitor renal values (BUN, creatinine) and adjust diet long-term.
treatment_ja: シュウ酸塩を多く含む植物を除去し、カルシウム・リン比（Ca:P約2:1）を適正化して食餌の不均衡を是正する。必要に応じてビタミンA（50,000～100,000 IU/日）およびビタミンDを補給する。腎支持療法として乳酸リンゲル液の静脈内輸液を行い、高リン血症にはリン吸着剤を投与する。BUN・クレアチニンを定期的にモニタリングし、長期的な食餌管理を継続する。

name: Renal Genetic Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal genetic disorders in horses involve inherited mutations affecting renal tubular or glomerular structure and function, leading to progressive nephron loss, impaired filtration, and inability to maintain fluid and electrolyte homeostasis. Specific conditions such as renal dysplasia or polycystic kidney disease result from aberrant renal development or cyst formation that progressively replaces functional renal parenchyma. This leads to chronic renal failure with azotemia, electrolyte imbalances, and eventual end-stage kidney disease.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎臓遺伝性疾患は、腎尿細管や糸球体の構造・機能に影響を及ぼす遺伝子変異に起因し、進行性のネフロン喪失、濾過機能障害、体液・電解質恒常性の維持不全を引き起こします。腎異形成や多発性嚢胞腎などの特定疾患では、腎臓の発生異常や嚢胞形成により機能的な腎実質が徐々に置換されます。これにより慢性腎不全、高窒素血症、電解質異常、最終的には末期腎疾患に至ります。
causes: The primary cause is inherited genetic mutations that affect renal development or function, often transmitted in an autosomal recessive or dominant pattern depending on the specific disorder. Examples include renal dysplasia and polycystic kidney disease, which have been identified in certain horse breeds. Secondary factors such as dehydration, nephrotoxic agents, or concurrent infections may accelerate the progression of underlying genetic renal disease.
treatment: No curative treatment exists for renal genetic disorders in horses. Management is supportive: IV fluid therapy (balanced polyionic solutions) to maintain hydration, dietary protein and phosphorus restriction, ACE inhibitors (benazepril 0.5 mg/kg PO q24h) for proteinuria and renal hypertension, and correction of electrolyte imbalances. Monitoring BUN, creatinine, and urinalysis is essential to guide ongoing therapy.
treatment_ja: 馬の腎臓遺伝性疾患に根治的治療法は存在しません。管理は対症療法が中心で、等張輸液（バランス電解質液）による水分補給、食餌中のタンパク質およびリン制限、蛋白尿・腎性高血圧に対するACE阻害薬（ベナゼプリル0.5 mg/kg 経口 1日1回）の投与、電解質異常の補正を行います。BUN、クレアチニン、尿検査を定期的にモニタリングし、治療方針を調整することが重要です。

name: Renal Autoimmune Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: The immune system produces autoantibodies or autoreactive lymphocytes directed against renal antigens, leading to immune complex deposition in the glomeruli and/or tubulointerstitial tissue. This triggers complement activation, inflammatory cell infiltration, and progressive destruction of renal parenchyma, resulting in glomerulonephritis or tubulointerstitial nephritis. Over time, chronic inflammation leads to fibrosis, nephron loss, and progressive renal insufficiency.
pathophysiology_ja: 免疫系が腎抗原に対する自己抗体または自己反応性リンパ球を産生し、糸球体および/または尿細管間質組織に免疫複合体が沈着します。これにより補体の活性化、炎症細胞の浸潤、腎実質の進行性破壊が引き起こされ、糸球体腎炎または尿細管間質性腎炎が生じます。慢性炎症により線維化、ネフロンの喪失、進行性腎不全に至ります。
causes: Primary causes include dysregulation of immune tolerance leading to production of autoantibodies against glomerular basement membrane or other renal antigens. Secondary causes may include chronic infections (e.g., Streptococcus equi, equine infectious anemia), systemic autoimmune conditions, neoplasia, or chronic drug exposure that triggers immune-mediated renal injury through molecular mimicry or immune complex formation.
treatment: Immunosuppressive therapy with corticosteroids (dexamethasone 0.05-0.1 mg/kg IV/IM daily, tapering over weeks) is the mainstay. Azathioprine (3 mg/kg PO daily) may be added for steroid-sparing effect. Supportive care includes IV fluid therapy to maintain renal perfusion, ACE inhibitors (benazepril 0.5 mg/kg PO) to reduce proteinuria, and treatment of underlying infections such as Streptococcus equi.
treatment_ja: 副腎皮質ステロイド（デキサメタゾン0.05〜0.1 mg/kg IV/IM、漸減投与）による免疫抑制療法が治療の主軸となる。アザチオプリン（3 mg/kg PO）をステロイド減量目的で併用することがある。支持療法として腎灌流維持のための輸液療法、蛋白尿軽減のためのACE阻害薬（ベナゼプリル0.5 mg/kg PO）、およびStreptococcus equiなどの基礎感染症の治療を実施する。

name: Renal Degenerative Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal degenerative disease in horses involves progressive deterioration of renal parenchyma, including tubular degeneration, interstitial fibrosis, and glomerulosclerosis, leading to impaired filtration, reabsorption, and concentrating ability. Chronic injury results in nephron loss, azotemia, electrolyte imbalances, and eventual renal failure. The disease may be unilateral or bilateral, with bilateral involvement carrying more severe systemic consequences.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎変性疾患は、尿細管変性、間質線維化、糸球体硬化を含む腎実質の進行性劣化を伴い、濾過・再吸収・濃縮能の障害を引き起こす。慢性的な障害はネフロンの喪失、高窒素血症、電解質異常、最終的には腎不全につながる。病変は片側性または両側性であり、両側性の場合はより重篤な全身症状を示す。
causes: Primary causes include chronic nephrotoxin exposure (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals, vitamin D toxicosis), chronic ischemia, and age-related degeneration. Secondary causes include chronic pyelonephritis, nephrolithiasis, systemic diseases (e.g., leptospirosis, equine infectious anemia), and prolonged hemodynamic compromise such as dehydration or hypotension.
treatment: Treatment is primarily supportive: IV fluid therapy (balanced polyionic solutions) to correct dehydration and electrolyte imbalances, discontinuation of all nephrotoxic agents (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides). Manage azotemia with dietary protein restriction and phosphate binders (aluminum hydroxide 30-90 g PO BID). ACE inhibitors (benazepril) may slow progression. Treat underlying infections with renal-safe antimicrobials. Monitor BUN, creatinine, and electrolytes serially.
treatment_ja: 治療は主に対症療法であり、脱水・電解質異常の補正のための輸液療法（バランス電解質液の静脈内投与）、および全ての腎毒性薬剤（NSAIDs、アミノグリコシド系）の中止が重要である。高窒素血症には食餌中のタンパク質制限とリン吸着剤（水酸化アルミニウム30〜90g 1日2回経口投与）で管理する。ACE阻害薬（ベナゼプリル）は進行抑制に有用な場合がある。基礎感染症には腎安全性の高い抗菌薬を使用し、BUN・クレアチニン・電解質を定期的にモニタリングする。

name: Renal Traumatic Injury (Horse)
pathophysiology: Blunt or penetrating trauma to the flank or lumbar region causes direct damage to the renal parenchyma, capsule, or vasculature, leading to hemorrhage, hematoma formation, and potential urine leakage into the retroperitoneal space. The resulting inflammation, ischemia, and possible secondary infection can compromise renal function. In severe cases, vascular disruption may lead to life-threatening hemorrhage or renal infarction.
pathophysiology_ja: 腰部や側腹部への鈍的または穿通性外傷により、腎実質、腎被膜、または腎血管が直接損傷を受け、出血、血腫形成、および後腹膜腔への尿漏出が生じる。続発する炎症、虚血、二次感染により腎機能が障害される可能性がある。重症例では血管損傷により致命的な出血や腎梗塞を引き起こすことがある。
causes: Primary causes include blunt abdominal trauma from kicks by other horses, falls during exercise or competition, collisions with fixed objects, and vehicular accidents. Secondary causes include penetrating wounds from sharp objects or fractures of adjacent ribs or lumbar vertebrae that lacerate the kidney. Pre-existing renal enlargement due to hydronephrosis or neoplasia may predispose the kidney to traumatic injury.
causes_ja: 主な原因は他馬からの蹴り、運動中や競技中の転倒、固定物への衝突、交通事故などによる腹部への鈍的外傷である。二次的原因として鋭利物による穿通創、隣接する肋骨や腰椎の骨折による腎臓の裂傷がある。水腎症や腫瘍による既存の腎腫大は外傷性損傷の素因となりうる。
treatment: Initial stabilization includes IV fluid resuscitation (lactated Ringer's solution, 10-20 mL/kg/hr) and analgesics (flunixin meglumine 1.1 mg/kg IV BID). Conservative management with stall rest, serial ultrasound monitoring, and broad-spectrum antibiotics (gentamicin 6.6 mg/kg IV SID plus penicillin 22,000 IU/kg IV QID) is preferred for minor injuries. Severe lacerations with uncontrollable hemorrhage or urine leakage may require nephrectomy.
treatment_ja: 初期安定化として輸液療法（乳酸リンゲル液10-20 mL/kg/hr IV）および鎮痛剤（フルニキシンメグルミン1.1 mg/kg IV BID）を投与する。軽度の損傷には馬房安静、連続超音波モニタリング、広域抗菌薬（ゲンタマイシン6.6 mg/kg IV SIDおよびペニシリン22,000 IU/kg IV QID）による保存的管理を行う。制御不能な出血や尿漏出を伴う重度の裂傷には腎摘出術が必要となる場合がある。

name: Renal Behavioral Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal behavioral disorder in horses involves abnormal behaviors associated with underlying renal pain or dysfunction, such as nephrolithiasis, pyelonephritis, or chronic renal disease. Pain originating from the kidneys or ureters triggers visceral nociceptive pathways, leading to behavioral manifestations including flank guarding, stretching postures mimicking colic, and frequent posturing to urinate. Chronic renal irritation may also cause referred pain to the back and hindquarters, resulting in reluctance to work, altered gait, or behavioral changes under saddle.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎行動障害は、腎結石症、腎盂腎炎、慢性腎疾患などの基礎的な腎臓の疼痛や機能障害に関連した異常行動を伴います。腎臓や尿管からの痛みが内臓侵害受容経路を刺激し、側腹部の防御、疝痛様の伸展姿勢、頻繁な排尿姿勢などの行動症状を引き起こします。慢性的な腎刺激は背部や後躯への関連痛を生じ、運動拒否や歩様異常、騎乗時の行動変化をもたらすことがあります。
causes: Primary causes include nephrolithiasis, ureteral obstruction, pyelonephritis, renal neoplasia, and chronic renal failure causing visceral pain. Secondary causes may involve ischemic nephropathy from non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug toxicity, renal cysts, or perirenal abscessation. Behavioral changes may also be exacerbated by concurrent metabolic derangements such as uremia and electrolyte imbalances.
treatment: Address the underlying renal pathology: administer analgesics such as flunixin meglumine (1.1 mg/kg IV) or butorphanol (0.01-0.04 mg/kg IV) for visceral pain control. Treat pyelonephritis with prolonged antimicrobials (trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole or enrofloxacin). Surgical intervention (nephrectomy or lithotripsy) may be required for nephrolithiasis or ureteral obstruction. Provide IV fluid therapy to support renal perfusion.
treatment_ja: 基礎的な腎疾患の治療を行う。内臓痛の管理にはフルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg IV）やブトルファノール（0.01-0.04 mg/kg IV）などの鎮痛薬を投与する。腎盂腎炎にはトリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾールやエンロフロキサシンによる長期抗菌薬療法を実施する。腎結石や尿管閉塞には腎摘出術や砕石術などの外科的介入を検討し、腎灌流維持のために輸液療法を行う。

name: Renal Infectious Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infectious disease in horses involves bacterial invasion of the renal parenchyma, typically via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract or hematogenous spread. Pathogens such as Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., and Actinobacillus equuli colonize the renal pelvis and parenchyma, causing inflammation (pyelonephritis), abscess formation, and progressive nephron destruction. This leads to impaired renal function, potentially resulting in azotemia, electrolyte imbalances, and if bilateral, renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症は、下部尿路からの上行性感染または血行性播種により細菌が腎実質に侵入することで発生する。大腸菌、連鎖球菌、Actinobacillus equuliなどの病原体が腎盂および腎実質に定着し、炎症（腎盂腎炎）、膿瘍形成、進行性のネフロン破壊を引き起こす。これにより腎機能が障害され、高窒素血症や電解質異常を生じ、両側性の場合は腎不全に至る可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infections (most commonly E. coli, Streptococcus spp., Corynebacterium spp.) from the lower urinary tract, and hematogenous spread from systemic infections. Secondary contributing factors include urolithiasis, urinary tract obstruction, immunosuppression, bladder dysfunction (e.g., from cauda equina syndrome), and indwelling urinary catheter use that predisposes to bacterial colonization.
treatment: Initiate broad-spectrum antimicrobial therapy based on culture and sensitivity, such as trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (30 mg/kg PO BID) or enrofloxacin (5 mg/kg IV/PO SID), for a minimum of 2-4 weeks. Provide IV fluid therapy to maintain hydration and renal perfusion. Address underlying causes such as urolithiasis or obstruction surgically if indicated, and administer NSAIDs (flunixin meglumine 1.1 mg/kg IV) for pain and inflammation control.
treatment_ja: 培養・感受性試験に基づき、トリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾール（30 mg/kg 経口 1日2回）またはエンロフロキサシン（5 mg/kg 静脈内/経口 1日1回）などの広域抗菌薬を最低2〜4週間投与する。静脈内輸液療法により水分補給と腎灌流を維持する。尿路結石や閉塞などの基礎疾患がある場合は外科的に対処し、フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg 静脈内投与）等のNSAIDsで疼痛・炎症を管理する。

name: Renal Parasitic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal parasitic disease in horses occurs when parasitic organisms such as Halicephalobus gingivalis (formerly Halicephalobus deletrix), Strongylus vulgaris larvae, or Dioctophyme renale migrate to and colonize the kidneys. The parasites cause direct mechanical damage to renal parenchyma, provoke granulomatous inflammation, and can lead to progressive nephritis, fibrosis, and impaired renal function. Larval migration through renal vasculature may also cause thrombosis, infarction, and secondary bacterial infection.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎寄生虫症は、Halicephalobus gingivalis、Strongylus vulgarisの幼虫、またはDioctophyme renaleなどの寄生虫が腎臓に移行・寄生することで発症する。寄生虫は腎実質に直接的な機械的損傷を与え、肉芽腫性炎症を引き起こし、進行性の腎炎、線維化、腎機能障害をもたらす。幼虫の腎血管内移行により血栓症、梗塞、二次的な細菌感染も生じうる。
causes: Primary causes include migration of parasites such as Halicephalobus gingivalis (a free-living nematode with opportunistic parasitic behavior), larval stages of Strongylus vulgaris through aberrant migration, and rarely Dioctophyme renale (giant kidney worm). Secondary causes include immunosuppression or concurrent illness that may predispose horses to opportunistic parasitic infections, as well as environmental exposure to contaminated soil or water sources.
treatment: Administer broad-spectrum anthelmintics such as fenbendazole (10 mg/kg PO daily for 5 days) or ivermectin (0.2 mg/kg PO); however, efficacy against Halicephalobus gingivalis is often poor. Provide supportive care including IV fluids for renal support, NSAIDs (flunixin meglumine 1.1 mg/kg IV) for inflammation, and corticosteroids if severe granulomatous nephritis is present. Nephrectomy of the affected kidney may be considered in unilateral cases if medical therapy fails.
treatment_ja: フェンベンダゾール（10 mg/kg 経口、5日間連日投与）やイベルメクチン（0.2 mg/kg 経口）などの広域駆虫薬を投与するが、Halicephalobus gingivalisに対する効果は限定的である場合が多い。腎機能維持のための輸液療法、フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg 静注）による抗炎症治療、重度の肉芽腫性腎炎にはコルチコステロイドを併用する。片側性病変で内科的治療が奏効しない場合は、患側腎の腎摘出術を検討する。

name: Renal Viral Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Viral agents such as equine herpesvirus (EHV-1) or equine arteritis virus (EAV) can cause vasculitis and immune-mediated damage to renal vasculature and glomeruli, leading to impaired renal filtration and tubular necrosis. Immune complex deposition in the glomeruli and direct viral cytopathic effects result in progressive nephritis, proteinuria, and potential renal insufficiency.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬ヘルペスウイルス（EHV-1）や馬動脈炎ウイルス（EAV）などのウイルスが腎血管や糸球体に血管炎および免疫介在性障害を引き起こし、腎濾過機能の低下や尿細管壊死をもたらす。糸球体への免疫複合体沈着およびウイルスの直接的な細胞障害作用により、進行性の腎炎、蛋白尿、腎不全が生じる。
causes: Primary causes include equine herpesvirus type 1 (EHV-1), equine arteritis virus (EAV), and potentially other systemic viral infections that target or secondarily affect the kidneys. Secondary causes include immune complex-mediated glomerulonephritis, systemic vasculitis, and dehydration or hemodynamic compromise during severe viral illness.
treatment: No specific antiviral cure exists; treatment is supportive. Administer IV balanced crystalloid fluids (e.g., lactated Ringer's solution) to maintain renal perfusion, use flunixin meglumine (1.1 mg/kg IV) for anti-inflammatory support, and consider broad-spectrum antibiotics to prevent secondary infections. Monitor renal values (BUN, creatinine) closely and manage electrolyte imbalances.
treatment_ja: 特異的な抗ウイルス治療法は存在せず、支持療法が中心となる。乳酸リンゲル液などの等張晶質液を静脈内投与し腎灌流を維持する。フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg IV）を抗炎症目的で使用し、二次感染予防のため広域スペクトル抗菌薬を検討する。BUN・クレアチニンなどの腎機能指標を頻回にモニタリングし、電解質異常を適宜補正する。

name: Renal Bacterial Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Bacterial infection of the kidneys (pyelonephritis) in horses typically occurs via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract or, less commonly, through hematogenous spread. Bacteria colonize the renal pelvis and parenchyma, triggering an inflammatory response that leads to tissue destruction, abscess formation, and progressive impairment of renal function. Chronic infection may result in fibrosis, nephron loss, and ultimately renal failure if bilateral involvement occurs.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎臓細菌感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、通常下部尿路からの上行性感染、またはまれに血行性播種により発生します。細菌が腎盂および腎実質に定着し、炎症反応を引き起こして組織破壊、膿瘍形成、腎機能の進行性障害をもたらします。慢性感染は線維化、ネフロンの喪失を引き起こし、両側性の場合は最終的に腎不全に至る可能性があります。
causes: Common causative organisms include Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Staphylococcus spp., Enterobacter spp., and Corynebacterium renale. Predisposing factors include urolithiasis, urinary tract obstruction, bladder paralysis, catheterization, immunosuppression, and conditions causing urinary stasis. Ascending infection from cystitis is the most frequent route of infection in horses.
treatment: Initiate aggressive systemic antimicrobial therapy based on urine culture and sensitivity; commonly start with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (30 mg/kg PO BID) or enrofloxacin (5 mg/kg IV/PO SID) pending results. Provide IV fluid therapy to maintain hydration and promote renal perfusion. Address underlying predisposing factors such as urolithiasis or urinary obstruction surgically if needed, and continue antibiotics for 4-6 weeks with serial urinalysis monitoring.
treatment_ja: 尿培養・感受性試験に基づき、積極的な全身性抗菌薬療法を開始する。結果判明までトリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾール（30 mg/kg PO BID）またはエンロフロキサシン（5 mg/kg IV/PO SID）を第一選択とする。輸液療法により水和を維持し腎灌流を確保する。尿石症や尿路閉塞などの素因がある場合は外科的に対処し、抗菌薬投与を4〜6週間継続しながら連続的な尿検査でモニタリングを行う。

name: Renal Fungal Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Fungal organisms, most commonly Aspergillus spp. or Candida spp., colonize the renal parenchyma and/or renal pelvis, leading to granulomatous or necrotizing inflammation. This results in progressive destruction of renal tissue, impaired renal function, and potential formation of fungal granulomas or mycetomas. Hematogenous dissemination from a primary site or ascending infection from the lower urinary tract can lead to renal involvement, often exacerbated by immunosuppression or prolonged antibiotic use.
pathophysiology_ja: Aspergillus属やCandida属などの真菌が腎実質や腎盂に定着し、肉芽腫性または壊死性の炎症を引き起こします。これにより腎組織の進行性破壊、腎機能障害、真菌性肉芽腫や菌腫の形成が生じます。血行性播種や下部尿路からの上行性感染が原因となり、免疫抑制や長期抗菌薬使用により悪化することがあります。
causes: Primary causes include opportunistic fungal infections by Aspergillus spp., Candida spp., or less commonly other environmental fungi. Secondary predisposing factors include prolonged broad-spectrum antibiotic therapy, immunosuppression (from corticosteroid use, systemic illness, or stress), indwelling urinary catheters, and pre-existing renal damage or urinary tract obstruction.
treatment: Systemic antifungal therapy with fluconazole (5 mg/kg PO q24h) or amphotericin B (0.3-0.5 mg/kg IV slowly, with careful renal monitoring) for prolonged courses. Discontinue predisposing antibiotics and immunosuppressants. Nephrectomy may be indicated for unilateral renal involvement with extensive fungal granulomas unresponsive to medical therapy; supportive IV fluid therapy to maintain renal perfusion.
treatment_ja: フルコナゾール（5 mg/kg 経口 1日1回）またはアムホテリシンB（0.3〜0.5 mg/kg 緩徐静注、腎機能の慎重なモニタリング下）による長期全身抗真菌療法を実施する。誘因となる広域抗菌薬や免疫抑制剤は中止する。片側性で真菌性肉芽腫が広範かつ内科療法に反応しない場合は腎摘出術を検討し、腎灌流維持のため補液療法を併用する。

name: Renal Infection (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infection (pyelonephritis) in horses typically occurs via ascending bacterial infection from the lower urinary tract through the ureters to the renal pelvis and parenchyma. Bacteria colonize the renal medulla and pelvis, causing inflammation, abscessation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue. In severe or chronic cases, fibrosis and impaired renal function may develop, potentially leading to renal failure if bilateral.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路から尿管を通じて腎盂および腎実質へ細菌が上行性に感染することで発生します。細菌が腎髄質および腎盂に定着し、炎症、膿瘍形成、腎組織の進行性破壊を引き起こします。重度または慢性の場合、線維化と腎機能障害が進行し、両側性であれば腎不全に至る可能性があります。
causes: The most common causative agents are Escherichia coli, Corynebacterium renale, Streptococcus spp., and other gram-negative bacteria ascending from the lower urinary tract. Predisposing factors include urolithiasis, urinary stasis, bladder paralysis, catheterization, immunosuppression, and anatomical abnormalities. Hematogenous spread from systemic infections is less common but possible.
treatment: Initiate aggressive, prolonged antimicrobial therapy based on urine culture and sensitivity; commonly trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (30 mg/kg PO BID) or enrofloxacin (5 mg/kg IV/PO SID) for 4-6 weeks minimum. Provide IV fluid therapy to promote diuresis, correct electrolyte imbalances, and manage pain with flunixin meglumine (1.1 mg/kg IV). Address underlying predisposing factors such as urolithiasis or urinary obstruction surgically if needed.
treatment_ja: 尿培養・感受性試験に基づき、トリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾール（30 mg/kg 経口 BID）またはエンロフロキサシン（5 mg/kg 静注/経口 SID）を最低4〜6週間投与する長期抗菌療法を開始する。静脈内輸液により利尿を促進し、電解質異常を補正し、フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg 静注）で疼痛管理を行う。尿路結石や尿路閉塞などの基礎疾患がある場合は外科的介入も検討する。

name: Renal Inflammation (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal inflammation (nephritis) in horses involves immune-mediated or infectious injury to the glomeruli, tubules, or interstitium of the kidneys. This leads to impaired filtration, tubular dysfunction, proteinuria, and accumulation of metabolic waste products (azotemia). Prolonged inflammation can result in fibrosis, chronic renal failure, and loss of functional nephrons.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎炎は、免疫介在性または感染性の障害により糸球体、尿細管、または間質に炎症が生じる疾患です。これにより濾過機能の低下、尿細管機能障害、蛋白尿、および代謝老廃物の蓄積（高窒素血症）が起こります。炎症が長期化すると線維化、慢性腎不全、機能的ネフロンの喪失に至ることがあります。
causes: Primary causes include bacterial infections (e.g., Leptospira, Streptococcus), viral infections (e.g., equine infectious anemia), and immune-mediated glomerulonephritis. Secondary causes include nephrotoxic drugs (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides), toxin exposure (heavy metals, oxalate-containing plants), systemic sepsis, and hemodynamic insults such as severe dehydration or endotoxemia.
treatment: Discontinue nephrotoxic agents (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides) immediately. Provide aggressive IV fluid therapy (balanced crystalloids such as lactated Ringer's solution) to restore renal perfusion and correct electrolyte imbalances. Administer appropriate antimicrobials (e.g., penicillin for Leptospira or Streptococcus) based on culture results, and consider corticosteroids (dexamethasone 0.05-0.1 mg/kg IV) for immune-mediated nephritis. Monitor serum creatinine, BUN, and urine output closely.
treatment_ja: 腎毒性薬剤（NSAIDs、アミノグリコシド系）を直ちに中止する。乳酸リンゲル液などの平衡晶質液による積極的な静脈内輸液療法を実施し、腎灌流の回復と電解質異常の是正を図る。培養結果に基づき適切な抗菌薬（レプトスピラやレンサ球菌にはペニシリン系）を投与し、免疫介在性腎炎にはデキサメタゾン（0.05〜0.1 mg/kg IV）の使用を検討する。血清クレアチニン、BUN、尿量を継続的にモニタリングする。

name: Renal Neoplasia (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal neoplasia in horses involves the uncontrolled proliferation of cells within the kidney, most commonly renal cell carcinoma, lymphoma, or nephroblastoma. The tumor mass disrupts normal renal architecture and function, potentially causing obstruction, hemorrhage, and progressive renal insufficiency. Metastasis may occur via hematogenous or lymphatic routes to lungs, liver, and other organs, leading to systemic disease.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎腫瘍は腎臓内の細胞の無制御な増殖を伴い、最も一般的なものは腎細胞癌、リンパ腫、または腎芽腫である。腫瘍塊は正常な腎構造と機能を破壊し、閉塞、出血、および進行性の腎機能不全を引き起こす可能性がある。血行性またはリンパ行性に肺、肝臓、その他の臓器へ転移し、全身性疾患を引き起こすことがある。
causes: The exact etiology of renal neoplasia in horses is largely unknown, with no consistently identified risk factors. Possible contributing factors include genetic predisposition, chronic inflammation, and exposure to environmental carcinogens. Renal cell carcinoma is the most frequently reported primary renal tumor, while lymphoma may represent systemic neoplastic involvement of the kidney.
treatment: Unilateral nephrectomy is the primary treatment for localized renal tumors when the contralateral kidney is functional. For lymphoma, systemic chemotherapy with corticosteroids (dexamethasone) and cyclophosphamide may be considered. Supportive care includes IV fluid therapy, analgesics (flunixin meglumine), and monitoring renal parameters.
treatment_ja: 対側腎の機能が正常であれば、限局性腎腫瘍に対しては片側腎摘出術が第一選択となる。リンパ腫の場合、デキサメタゾンやシクロホスファミドによる全身化学療法を検討する。支持療法として静脈内輸液、鎮痛剤（フルニキシンメグルミン）の投与、および腎機能パラメータの継続的モニタリングを行う。

name: Renal Metabolic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal metabolic disease in horses involves impaired kidney function leading to disrupted electrolyte balance, acid-base homeostasis, and waste product excretion. The kidneys fail to adequately regulate calcium, phosphorus, and other mineral metabolism, potentially resulting in hypercalcemia or hyperphosphatemia, metabolic acidosis, and azotemia. Progressive nephron loss leads to inability to concentrate urine and maintain fluid-electrolyte equilibrium, contributing to secondary metabolic derangements including renal secondary hyperparathyroidism.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎代謝疾患は、腎機能障害により電解質バランス、酸塩基平衡、および老廃物排泄が障害される病態である。腎臓がカルシウム、リン、その他のミネラル代謝を適切に調節できなくなり、高カルシウム血症または高リン血症、代謝性アシドーシス、高窒素血症を引き起こす。進行性のネフロン喪失により尿濃縮能と体液電解質平衡の維持が不能となり、腎性二次性上皮小体機能亢進症などの二次的代謝異常を招く。
causes: Primary causes include chronic kidney disease from nephrotoxin exposure (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals), nephrolithiasis, pyelonephritis, and glomerulonephritis. Secondary causes include dehydration, prolonged hemodynamic compromise, systemic infections, and dietary imbalances such as excessive calcium or oxalate-containing plant ingestion. Age-related degenerative changes and congenital renal anomalies may also predispose horses to renal metabolic dysfunction.
treatment: Administer IV fluid therapy (balanced polyionic solutions) to correct dehydration and restore renal perfusion. Discontinue nephrotoxic drugs (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs). Correct electrolyte imbalances with calcium gluconate or phosphate binders as needed. Manage acidosis with sodium bicarbonate and provide dietary modification with reduced protein and calcium intake.
treatment_ja: 脱水の補正と腎灌流の回復のため、バランス電解質輸液の静脈内投与を行う。腎毒性薬剤（アミノグリコシド系、NSAIDs）を直ちに中止する。必要に応じてグルコン酸カルシウムやリン吸着剤で電解質異常を補正し、重炭酸ナトリウムでアシドーシスを管理する。タンパク質およびカルシウム摂取量を制限した食事療法を併用する。

name: Renal Nutritional Deficiency (Horse)
pathophysiology: Nutritional deficiencies, particularly of vitamin A, vitamin D, calcium, phosphorus, or oxalate-containing plant ingestion, lead to renal tubular damage, nephrocalcinosis, or impaired renal function in horses. Chronic imbalances disrupt calcium-phosphorus homeostasis, causing mineralization of renal tissues, tubular degeneration, and progressive loss of nephron function. Secondary hyperparathyroidism may develop, further exacerbating renal mineral deposition and structural damage.
pathophysiology_ja: ビタミンA、ビタミンD、カルシウム、リンなどの栄養素の欠乏やシュウ酸含有植物の摂取により、腎尿細管の損傷、腎石灰化症、または腎機能障害が馬に生じます。慢性的なミネラル不均衡はカルシウム・リンの恒常性を乱し、腎組織の石灰化、尿細管変性、およびネフロン機能の進行性喪失を引き起こします。二次性副甲状腺機能亢進症が発症し、腎臓へのミネラル沈着と構造的損傷をさらに悪化させることがあります。
causes: Primary causes include dietary deficiencies or imbalances of calcium, phosphorus, vitamin A, and vitamin D, as well as excessive ingestion of oxalate-rich plants (e.g., Setaria, Cenchrus, Oxalis species) that bind calcium and cause renal oxalate deposition. Secondary causes include prolonged feeding of high-grain/low-forage diets leading to inverted calcium-phosphorus ratios, and chronic exposure to nephrotoxic plants or mycotoxins.
treatment: Correct dietary imbalances by providing balanced calcium-phosphorus ratios (approximately 2:1), and supplement with vitamin A and vitamin D as needed. Remove oxalate-containing plants from pasture or diet. Provide IV fluid therapy (lactated Ringer's solution) for dehydrated or azotemic horses, and administer calcium gluconate cautiously if hypocalcemia is confirmed. Monitor renal values (BUN, creatinine) serially and adjust diet long-term.
treatment_ja: カルシウムとリンの比率（約2:1）を適正化し、必要に応じてビタミンAおよびビタミンDを補給する。シュウ酸含有植物を牧草地や飼料から除去する。脱水や高窒素血症がある場合は乳酸リンゲル液による輸液療法を行い、低カルシウム血症が確認された場合はグルコン酸カルシウムを慎重に投与する。BUN・クレアチニンを定期的にモニタリングし、長期的な飼料管理を行う。

name: Renal Genetic Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal genetic disorders in horses involve inherited mutations affecting renal tubular or glomerular structure and function, leading to progressive nephron loss, impaired filtration, and concentrating ability. Examples include renal dysplasia and polycystic kidney disease, where abnormal renal development or cyst formation disrupts normal renal architecture. Progressive fibrosis and inflammation result in chronic kidney disease and eventual renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎遺伝性疾患は、腎尿細管や糸球体の構造・機能に影響を及ぼす遺伝子変異に起因し、進行性のネフロン喪失、濾過機能および濃縮能の低下を引き起こします。腎異形成や多発性嚢胞腎などが含まれ、異常な腎発達や嚢胞形成により正常な腎構造が破壊されます。進行性の線維化と炎症により慢性腎臓病および最終的に腎不全に至ります。
causes: The primary cause is inherited genetic mutations (autosomal recessive or dominant depending on the specific disorder) affecting renal development or structural proteins. Specific examples include renal dysplasia reported in certain horse breeds and polycystic kidney disease. Consanguineous breeding and limited gene pools within certain breeds increase the prevalence of these disorders.
causes_ja: 主な原因は、腎臓の発達や構造タンパク質に影響を与える遺伝子変異（特定の疾患により常染色体劣性または優性）です。特定の馬品種で報告されている腎異形成や多発性嚢胞腎が含まれます。近親交配や特定品種における限られた遺伝子プールがこれらの疾患の発生率を高めます。
treatment: No curative therapy exists; management is supportive. Administer IV fluid therapy (balanced polyionic solutions) to maintain hydration and electrolyte balance. Use ACE inhibitors (e.g., enalapril 0.5 mg/kg PO q24h) to reduce glomerular hypertension, phosphate binders for hyperphosphatemia, and dietary protein restriction. Monitor renal values (BUN, creatinine, SDMA) serially. Breeding animals should be removed from programs to prevent propagation of the defective allele.
treatment_ja: 根治療法は存在せず、対症療法が中心となる。静脈内輸液療法（バランス型電解質液）で水和と電解質バランスを維持する。ACE阻害薬（エナラプリル0.5 mg/kg 経口 1日1回）で糸球体内高血圧を軽減し、高リン血症にはリン吸着剤を使用、食事中のタンパク質制限を行う。BUN・クレアチニン・SDMAを定期的にモニタリングする。遺伝的拡散防止のため、罹患馬は繁殖から除外すべきである。

name: Renal Autoimmune Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: The immune system produces autoantibodies or autoreactive T cells directed against renal antigens, leading to immune complex deposition in glomeruli and/or tubulointerstitial inflammation. This results in progressive glomerulonephritis or tubulointerstitial nephritis, impairing glomerular filtration, causing proteinuria, and eventually leading to chronic renal failure. Complement activation and inflammatory cell infiltration further exacerbate tissue damage and fibrosis.
pathophysiology_ja: 免疫系が腎臓の抗原に対する自己抗体または自己反応性T細胞を産生し、糸球体への免疫複合体の沈着および/または尿細管間質の炎症を引き起こします。これにより進行性の糸球体腎炎または尿細管間質性腎炎が生じ、糸球体濾過の障害、蛋白尿、最終的には慢性腎不全に至ります。補体の活性化と炎症細胞の浸潤が組織障害と線維化をさらに悪化させます。
causes: The primary cause is a dysregulation of immune tolerance leading to autoimmune targeting of renal tissue, potentially triggered by preceding infections (e.g., Streptococcus equi), drug reactions, or systemic autoimmune conditions such as systemic lupus erythematosus. Secondary causes include chronic antigenic stimulation from persistent infections, equine infectious anemia, or other immune-mediated diseases that result in circulating immune complex deposition in the kidneys.
treatment: Initiate immunosuppressive therapy with corticosteroids (dexamethasone 0.05-0.1 mg/kg IV daily, tapering over weeks) combined with azathioprine (3 mg/kg PO daily) to suppress autoantibody production and reduce renal inflammation. Provide supportive care including IV fluid therapy to maintain renal perfusion, ACE inhibitors (benazepril 0.5 mg/kg PO daily) to reduce proteinuria, and monitor renal values and urine protein-to-creatinine ratio regularly.
treatment_ja: 副腎皮質ステロイド（デキサメタゾン0.05〜0.1 mg/kg 静脈内投与、数週間かけて漸減）とアザチオプリン（3 mg/kg 経口投与）による免疫抑制療法を開始し、自己抗体産生と腎炎症を抑制する。腎灌流維持のための輸液療法、蛋白尿軽減のためのACE阻害薬（ベナゼプリル0.5 mg/kg 経口投与）を併用し、腎機能値および尿蛋白クレアチニン比を定期的にモニタリングする。

name: Renal Degenerative Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal degenerative disease in horses involves progressive deterioration of renal parenchyma, including tubular degeneration, interstitial fibrosis, and glomerulosclerosis, leading to impaired filtration, concentration, and excretion functions. Chronic nephron loss triggers compensatory hyperfiltration in remaining nephrons, which ultimately accelerates further damage. This progressive loss of functional renal tissue results in azotemia, electrolyte imbalances, and eventual renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎変性疾患は、尿細管変性、間質線維化、糸球体硬化症を含む腎実質の進行性劣化を伴い、濾過・濃縮・排泄機能の障害を引き起こす。慢性的なネフロン喪失により残存ネフロンの代償性過剰濾過が生じ、さらなる損傷が加速される。機能的腎組織の進行性喪失により、高窒素血症、電解質異常、最終的には腎不全に至る。
causes: Primary causes include chronic exposure to nephrotoxins such as aminoglycoside antibiotics, NSAIDs, heavy metals, and certain plants (e.g., red maple, oak). Secondary causes include chronic dehydration, prolonged hemodynamic compromise, age-related degenerative changes, and sequelae of acute kidney injury or chronic pyelonephritis. Vitamin D toxicosis and oxalate-containing plants can also contribute to renal calcification and degeneration.
treatment: Discontinue all nephrotoxic agents (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides). Provide IV fluid therapy (balanced polyionic solutions) to correct dehydration and support renal perfusion. Manage electrolyte imbalances (calcium, phosphorus) with dietary modification, phosphate binders, and ACE inhibitors (benazepril 0.5 mg/kg PO q24h) to reduce glomerular hyperfiltration.
treatment_ja: 全ての腎毒性薬剤（NSAIDs、アミノグリコシド系）を直ちに中止する。脱水補正と腎灌流維持のため等張電解質輸液を静脈内投与する。電解質異常（カルシウム・リン）は食事管理およびリン吸着剤で対応し、糸球体過剰濾過を軽減するためACE阻害薬（ベナゼプリル0.5 mg/kg 経口 1日1回）を投与する。

name: Renal Traumatic Injury (Horse)
pathophysiology: Blunt or penetrating trauma to the lumbar region causes direct damage to the renal parenchyma, capsule, or renal vasculature. This leads to hemorrhage (subcapsular or perirenal hematoma), disruption of the collecting system with possible urine leakage (uroperitoneum or retroperitoneal urine accumulation), and subsequent inflammation. Severe cases may result in renal ischemia, nephron loss, and systemic complications such as hemorrhagic shock or secondary infection.
pathophysiology_ja: 腰部への鈍的または穿通性外傷により、腎実質、腎被膜、または腎血管に直接的な損傷が生じる。これにより出血（被膜下または腎周囲血腫）、集合系の破裂による尿漏出（尿腹症または後腹膜尿貯留）、およびそれに続く炎症が引き起こされる。重症例では腎虚血、ネフロンの喪失、出血性ショックや二次感染などの全身性合併症に至ることがある。
causes: Primary causes include blunt abdominal or lumbar trauma from kicks by other horses, falls, collisions with fixed objects, or casting injuries during anesthesia. Secondary causes include penetrating injuries from sharp objects, fractures of lumbar transverse processes lacerating the kidney, and iatrogenic damage during percutaneous renal biopsy or surgical procedures.
treatment: Stabilize with IV crystalloid fluids (LRS or 0.9% NaCl) and control hemorrhage; administer flunixin meglumine (1.1 mg/kg IV q12h) for pain and anti-endotoxic effects. Monitor hematocrit, creatinine, and ultrasound serially. Severe cases (renal pedicle avulsion, uncontrolled hemorrhage) require nephrectomy via flank laparotomy. Broad-spectrum antibiotics (e.g., gentamicin 6.6 mg/kg IV q24h with penicillin) prevent secondary infection.
treatment_ja: 乳酸リンゲル液または生理食塩水の静脈内投与で循環を安定させ、フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg IV 12時間毎）で疼痛管理および抗エンドトキシン作用を図る。ヘマトクリット、クレアチニン、超音波検査で経時的にモニタリングを行う。腎茎断裂や止血困難な重症例では側腹部開腹術による腎摘出術を実施する。ゲンタマイシン（6.6 mg/kg IV 24時間毎）とペニシリン併用で二次感染を予防する。

name: Renal Behavioral Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal behavioral disorder in horses involves abnormal behaviors (such as frequent posturing to urinate, flank watching, or stretching) that arise secondary to renal pain or dysfunction. Chronic or acute renal inflammation, calculi, or nephritis can stimulate visceral pain receptors, leading to behavioral changes that mimic colic or musculoskeletal pain. Altered electrolyte balance and uremic toxin accumulation may also contribute to central nervous system effects and abnormal behavior.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎行動障害は、腎臓の疼痛や機能障害に起因する異常行動（頻繁な排尿姿勢、腹部を見る仕草、伸展姿勢など）を伴います。慢性または急性の腎炎症、結石、腎炎が内臓痛受容体を刺激し、疝痛や筋骨格系の痛みに類似した行動変化を引き起こします。電解質バランスの乱れや尿毒素の蓄積も中枢神経系に影響を与え、異常行動に寄与する可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include renal calculi (nephrolithiasis or ureterolithiasis), pyelonephritis, renal neoplasia, and chronic renal failure causing visceral pain. Secondary causes may involve urinary tract infections ascending to the kidneys, nephrotoxic drug exposure (e.g., NSAIDs, aminoglycosides), or renal ischemia following dehydration or hemodynamic compromise.
treatment: Address the underlying renal pathology: administer appropriate antimicrobials (trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole or enrofloxacin) for pyelonephritis, and provide analgesics such as flunixin meglumine (1.1 mg/kg IV) or butorphanol (0.01-0.04 mg/kg IV) for visceral pain management. Surgical intervention (nephrectomy or lithotripsy) may be required for renal calculi or neoplasia. Supportive care includes IV fluid therapy to maintain renal perfusion and correct electrolyte imbalances, and discontinuation of any nephrotoxic agents.
treatment_ja: 基礎にある腎疾患の治療を行う。腎盂腎炎にはトリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾールまたはエンロフロキサシン等の抗菌薬を投与し、内臓痛管理としてフルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg IV）やブトルファノール（0.01～0.04 mg/kg IV）を使用する。腎結石や腫瘍には外科的介入（腎摘出術や砕石術）が必要となる場合がある。補助療法として静脈内輸液による腎灌流維持と電解質補正を行い、腎毒性薬剤は直ちに中止する。

name: Renal Infectious Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infectious disease in horses involves bacterial colonization of the renal parenchyma, typically ascending from the lower urinary tract or via hematogenous spread. Infection leads to inflammation (pyelonephritis), tubular damage, abscess formation, and progressive impairment of renal function. Common pathogens include Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Actinobacillus equuli, and Corynebacterium spp., which cause neutrophilic infiltration, tissue necrosis, and fibrosis if untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症は、下部尿路からの上行性感染または血行性播種により細菌が腎実質に定着することで発症する。感染により炎症（腎盂腎炎）、尿細管障害、膿瘍形成が起こり、腎機能が進行性に低下する。一般的な病原体には大腸菌、連鎖球菌、アクチノバチルス・エクーリ、コリネバクテリウム属などがあり、好中球浸潤、組織壊死、線維化を引き起こす。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infection from the lower urinary tract (commonly E. coli, Streptococcus spp., Actinobacillus equuli), hematogenous spread from systemic infections, and nephrolithiasis causing obstruction and secondary infection. Predisposing factors include urinary stasis, immunosuppression, urolithiasis, bladder dysfunction, and catheterization or urinary tract trauma.
treatment: Initiate aggressive parenteral antibiotic therapy based on urine culture and sensitivity, commonly trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (30 mg/kg PO BID) or enrofloxacin (5 mg/kg IV/PO SID) for 4-6 weeks. Provide IV fluid therapy to maintain hydration and renal perfusion. Address underlying causes such as nephrolithiasis via surgical removal or lithotripsy, and manage pain with flunixin meglumine (1.1 mg/kg IV).
treatment_ja: 尿培養・感受性試験に基づき、トリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾール（30 mg/kg 経口 BID）またはエンロフロキサシン（5 mg/kg 静注/経口 SID）による積極的な抗菌薬治療を4〜6週間実施する。静脈内輸液療法により水分補給と腎灌流を維持する。腎結石症などの基礎疾患に対しては外科的除去または砕石術を検討し、フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg 静注）で疼痛管理を行う。

name: Renal Parasitic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal parasitic disease in horses occurs when parasitic organisms such as Halicephalobus gingivalis (Halicephalobus deletrix), Strongylus vulgaris larvae, or Dioctophyme renale migrate to or establish within the renal parenchyma. The parasites cause direct tissue destruction, granulomatous inflammation, and fibrosis of the kidney, leading to impaired renal function. Larval migration through renal vasculature can also result in thrombosis, infarction, and secondary bacterial infection of the affected kidney.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎寄生虫症は、Halicephalobus gingivalis、Strongylus vulgarisの幼虫、またはDioctophyme renaleなどの寄生虫が腎実質に移行・寄生することで発生する。寄生虫は直接的な組織破壊、肉芽腫性炎症、および腎臓の線維化を引き起こし、腎機能障害をもたらす。幼虫の腎血管内移行は血栓症、梗塞、および二次的な細菌感染を引き起こすこともある。
causes: Primary causes include infection by parasites such as Halicephalobus gingivalis (a free-living nematode with opportunistic pathogenicity), migrating Strongylus vulgaris larvae, and rarely Dioctophyme renale (giant kidney worm). Infection may occur through ingestion of contaminated feed or water, or through wound contamination. Secondary causes include immunosuppression and concurrent debilitating conditions that predispose to opportunistic parasitic invasion.
treatment: Administer high-dose anthelmintics such as fenbendazole (10 mg/kg PO daily for 5 days) or ivermectin (0.2 mg/kg PO); however, efficacy against Halicephalobus gingivalis is often poor. Supportive care includes NSAIDs (flunixin meglumine 1.1 mg/kg IV) for inflammation and renal support with IV fluid therapy. Nephrectomy of the affected kidney may be considered in unilateral cases if medical therapy fails.
treatment_ja: フェンベンダゾール（10 mg/kg 経口、5日間連続投与）やイベルメクチン（0.2 mg/kg 経口）などの高用量駆虫薬を投与するが、Halicephalobus gingivalisに対する効果は限定的である場合が多い。フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg 静脈内投与）による抗炎症療法および輸液療法による腎臓の支持療法を併用する。片側性病変で内科的治療が奏効しない場合は、患側腎の腎摘出術を検討する。

name: Renal Viral Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Viral agents such as equine herpesvirus (EHV) or equine arteritis virus (EAV) can cause systemic vasculitis and immune-mediated damage to renal vasculature and glomeruli. This leads to glomerulonephritis, tubular necrosis, and impaired renal filtration due to immune complex deposition and direct viral cytopathic effects on renal endothelial and epithelial cells. Progressive inflammation may result in acute kidney injury or chronic renal insufficiency.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬ヘルペスウイルス（EHV）や馬動脈炎ウイルス（EAV）などのウイルスが全身性血管炎を引き起こし、腎血管および糸球体に免疫介在性の損傷をもたらす。免疫複合体の沈着やウイルスの直接的な細胞傷害効果により糸球体腎炎や尿細管壊死が生じ、腎濾過機能が障害される。進行性の炎症により急性腎障害または慢性腎不全に至ることがある。
causes: Primary causes include viral infections such as equine herpesvirus (EHV-1, EHV-4), equine arteritis virus (EAV), and occasionally equine infectious anemia virus (EIAV) that target or secondarily affect renal tissues. Secondary causes include immune complex deposition, systemic vasculitis, and dehydration or hemodynamic compromise associated with the primary viral illness.
treatment: No specific antiviral cure exists; treatment is primarily supportive. Administer IV crystalloid fluids (lactated Ringer's or 0.9% NaCl) to maintain renal perfusion and correct dehydration. Use flunixin meglumine (1.1 mg/kg IV BID) to control inflammation, along with broad-spectrum antibiotics to prevent secondary infection. Monitor electrolytes, BUN, and creatinine closely; consider corticosteroids cautiously if immune-complex glomerulonephritis is confirmed.
treatment_ja: 特異的な抗ウイルス治療は存在せず、主に支持療法が中心となる。乳酸リンゲル液または生理食塩水の静脈内輸液により腎灌流を維持し脱水を補正する。フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg IV BID）で炎症を制御し、二次感染予防に広域スペクトル抗菌薬を併用する。電解質・BUN・クレアチニンを継続的にモニタリングし、免疫複合体性糸球体腎炎が確認された場合はコルチコステロイドの慎重な投与を検討する。

name: Renal Bacterial Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Bacterial infection of the kidneys (pyelonephritis) in horses typically occurs via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract, or less commonly through hematogenous spread. Bacteria colonize the renal pelvis and parenchyma, causing inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue. Common causative organisms include Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Staphylococcus spp., and Corynebacterium spp., leading to impaired renal function if left untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎臓における細菌感染（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路からの上行性感染、またはまれに血行性播種によって生じます。細菌が腎盂および腎実質に定着し、炎症、膿瘍形成、腎組織の進行性破壊を引き起こします。一般的な原因菌には大腸菌、連鎖球菌、ブドウ球菌、コリネバクテリウム属などが含まれ、未治療の場合は腎機能障害に至ります。
causes: Primary causes include ascending urinary tract infections (most common), hematogenous bacterial spread from distant infection sites, and urolithiasis causing urinary stasis. Secondary contributing factors include urinary tract obstruction, bladder paralysis, immunosuppression, indwelling urinary catheters, and anatomical abnormalities that predispose to urine retention and bacterial colonization.
treatment: Initiate prolonged systemic antibiotic therapy (4-6 weeks minimum) based on urine culture and sensitivity, commonly trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole or enrofloxacin. Provide IV fluid therapy to maintain renal perfusion and promote diuresis. Address underlying causes such as urolithiasis removal or catheter management, and monitor renal function via serial bloodwork and urinalysis.
treatment_ja: 尿培養・感受性試験に基づき、トリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾールやエンロフロキサシンなどの全身性抗菌薬を最低4〜6週間投与する。腎灌流維持と利尿促進のため静脈輸液療法を実施する。尿路結石の除去やカテーテル管理など基礎疾患への対処を行い、血液検査および尿検査で腎機能を継続的にモニタリングする。

name: Renal Fungal Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Fungal organisms, most commonly Aspergillus spp. or Candida spp., colonize the renal parenchyma and/or renal pelvis, leading to granulomatous or necrotizing inflammation. The infection disrupts normal renal architecture, potentially causing obstruction, abscess formation, and progressive loss of renal function. Hematogenous dissemination or ascending infection from the lower urinary tract can facilitate fungal invasion, particularly in immunocompromised horses.
pathophysiology_ja: 主にAspergillus属やCandida属などの真菌が腎実質や腎盂に定着し、肉芽腫性または壊死性の炎症を引き起こします。感染により正常な腎構造が破壊され、閉塞、膿瘍形成、進行性の腎機能低下を招く可能性があります。血行性播種や下部尿路からの上行性感染により、特に免疫機能が低下した馬で真菌の侵入が促進されます。
causes: Primary causes include opportunistic fungal infections by Aspergillus spp., Candida spp., or other environmental fungi that invade renal tissue. Secondary factors include prolonged antibiotic therapy, immunosuppression (corticosteroid use, debilitating illness), indwelling urinary catheters, and pre-existing renal damage that predisposes to fungal colonization.
causes_ja: 主な原因はAspergillus属、Candida属などの環境中の日和見真菌による腎組織への感染です。二次的要因として、長期間の抗菌薬投与、免疫抑制（コルチコステロイド使用、衰弱性疾患）、留置尿道カテーテル、および真菌の定着を促進する既存の腎障害が挙げられます。
treatment: Systemic antifungal therapy with fluconazole (5 mg/kg PO q24h) or voriconazole (3 mg/kg PO q12h initially, then q24h) for prolonged courses (weeks to months). Discontinue immunosuppressive agents and unnecessary antibiotics. Nephrectomy of the affected kidney may be indicated if unilateral disease with abscessation or obstruction is confirmed, combined with supportive fluid therapy to maintain renal perfusion.
treatment_ja: フルコナゾール（5 mg/kg 経口 1日1回）またはボリコナゾール（3 mg/kg 経口 初期は1日2回、その後1日1回）による全身性抗真菌療法を数週間から数ヶ月間実施する。免疫抑制剤や不要な抗菌薬は中止する。片側性の膿瘍形成や閉塞が確認された場合は患側腎の腎摘出術を検討し、腎灌流維持のための輸液療法を併用する。

name: Renal Infection (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infection (pyelonephritis) in horses typically results from ascending bacterial infection via the ureters from the lower urinary tract, or less commonly from hematogenous spread. Bacteria colonize the renal pelvis and parenchyma, causing inflammation, abscessation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue. Chronic infection can lead to fibrosis, hydronephrosis, and eventual loss of renal function in the affected kidney.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路から尿管を経由した上行性細菌感染、またはまれに血行性播種によって発生します。細菌が腎盂および腎実質に定着し、炎症、膿瘍形成、腎組織の進行性破壊を引き起こします。慢性感染は線維化、水腎症、罹患腎の機能喪失につながる可能性があります。
causes: The most common causative agents include Escherichia coli, Corynebacterium renale, Proteus spp., Streptococcus spp., and Staphylococcus spp. Predisposing factors include urolithiasis, urinary stasis, bladder paralysis, catheterization, immunosuppression, and anatomical abnormalities. Mares may be more predisposed due to their shorter urethra facilitating ascending infections.
treatment: Initiate prolonged systemic antibiotic therapy (4-6 weeks) based on urine culture and sensitivity, commonly trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole or enrofloxacin. Provide IV fluid therapy to maintain renal perfusion and urine flow. Address predisposing factors such as urolithiasis or bladder dysfunction, and monitor renal function via serial bloodwork and urinalysis.
treatment_ja: 尿培養および感受性試験に基づき、トリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾールやエンロフロキサシンなどの全身性抗菌薬を4〜6週間長期投与する。腎灌流と尿流量を維持するために輸液療法を実施する。尿路結石や膀胱機能障害などの素因を是正し、血液検査および尿検査により腎機能を継続的にモニタリングする。

name: Renal Inflammation (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal inflammation (nephritis) in horses involves immune-mediated or infectious injury to the glomeruli, tubules, or interstitium, leading to impaired filtration, tubular dysfunction, and progressive loss of nephron function. Inflammatory cell infiltration, edema, and fibrosis disrupt normal renal architecture, resulting in azotemia, electrolyte imbalances, and potentially renal failure. Immune complex deposition, direct bacterial infection, or toxic insults can trigger the inflammatory cascade.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎炎（腎臓の炎症）は、免疫介在性または感染性の障害により糸球体、尿細管、または間質に炎症が生じ、濾過機能の低下、尿細管機能障害、ネフロンの進行性喪失を引き起こします。炎症細胞の浸潤、浮腫、線維化が正常な腎構造を破壊し、高窒素血症、電解質異常、さらには腎不全に至ることがあります。免疫複合体の沈着、細菌の直接感染、または毒性物質が炎症カスケードを引き起こします。
causes: Primary causes include bacterial infections (e.g., leptospirosis, streptococcal infections), viral infections (e.g., equine infectious anemia), and immune-mediated glomerulonephritis. Secondary causes include nephrotoxic drugs (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides), exposure to toxic plants, systemic sepsis, and chronic dehydration or hemodynamic compromise leading to ischemic renal injury.
treatment: Treat underlying cause with appropriate antimicrobials (e.g., penicillin for streptococcal infections, oxytetracycline for leptospirosis). Discontinue nephrotoxic drugs (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides) immediately. Provide aggressive IV fluid therapy (balanced electrolyte solutions) to restore renal perfusion, correct electrolyte imbalances, and support diuresis. Corticosteroids (dexamethasone 0.05-0.1 mg/kg IV) may be indicated for immune-mediated nephritis.
treatment_ja: 原因に応じた適切な抗菌薬投与（連鎖球菌感染にはペニシリン、レプトスピラ症にはオキシテトラサイクリン）を行う。腎毒性薬剤（NSAIDs、アミノグリコシド系）は直ちに中止する。積極的な静脈内輸液療法（平衡電解質液）により腎灌流の回復、電解質補正、利尿を促進する。免疫介在性腎炎にはデキサメタゾン（0.05〜0.1 mg/kg IV）の投与を検討する。

name: Renal Neoplasia (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal neoplasia in horses involves the uncontrolled proliferation of cells within the kidney, most commonly renal cell carcinoma, lymphoma, or nephroblastoma. The tumor mass progressively disrupts normal renal parenchyma, impairing filtration and excretory functions, and may metastasize to regional lymph nodes, lungs, and other organs. Paraneoplastic syndromes such as polycythemia or hypercalcemia may occur due to aberrant hormone or cytokine production by tumor cells.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎腫瘍は、腎臓内の細胞が制御不能に増殖する疾患であり、腎細胞癌、リンパ腫、腎芽腫が最も一般的です。腫瘍塊は正常な腎実質を進行性に破壊し、濾過・排泄機能を障害するとともに、所属リンパ節や肺などへ転移する可能性があります。腫瘍細胞による異常なホルモンやサイトカインの産生により、多血症や高カルシウム血症などの腫瘍随伴症候群が生じることがあります。
causes: The exact etiology of renal neoplasia in horses is largely unknown. Potential contributing factors include genetic predisposition, chronic renal inflammation or injury, and age-related cellular mutations. No specific infectious, toxic, or environmental agents have been definitively identified as causative factors in equine renal tumors.
treatment: Primary treatment is unilateral nephrectomy when the tumor is confined to one kidney and no metastasis is detected. Chemotherapy options are limited in horses but may include doxorubicin or cyclophosphamide for lymphoma cases. Supportive care includes IV fluid therapy, NSAIDs for pain management (flunixin meglumine 1.1 mg/kg IV), and monitoring renal function via serial bloodwork.
treatment_ja: 腫瘍が片側腎に限局し転移がない場合、片側腎摘出術が第一選択となる。馬における化学療法の選択肢は限られるが、リンパ腫にはドキソルビシンやシクロホスファミドが検討される。支持療法として輸液療法、フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg 静脈投与）による疼痛管理、および連続的な血液検査による腎機能モニタリングを実施する。

name: Renal Metabolic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal metabolic disease in horses involves impaired kidney function leading to disrupted electrolyte balance, acid-base homeostasis, and waste product excretion. The kidneys fail to adequately regulate calcium, phosphorus, and other mineral metabolism, potentially resulting in hypercalcemia or hyperphosphatemia, metabolic acidosis, and azotemia. Chronic cases may lead to renal tubular dysfunction, impaired concentration ability, and secondary hyperparathyroidism with subsequent soft tissue mineralization and osteodystrophy.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎代謝疾患は、腎機能の低下により電解質バランス、酸塩基平衡、および老廃物の排泄が障害される病態である。腎臓がカルシウム、リン、その他のミネラル代謝を十分に調節できなくなり、高カルシウム血症や高リン血症、代謝性アシドーシス、高窒素血症を引き起こす。慢性例では腎尿細管機能障害、濃縮能の低下、および二次性上皮小体機能亢進症による軟部組織の石灰化や骨異栄養症に至る場合がある。
causes: Primary causes include chronic renal failure, nephrotoxin exposure (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals, vitamin D toxicosis), and excessive dietary calcium or oxalate-containing plants. Secondary causes include dehydration, prolonged hemodynamic compromise, systemic infections, and age-related renal degeneration. Nutritional imbalances such as high-phosphorus or high-calcium diets can also contribute to metabolic derangements affecting renal function.
treatment: Administer IV fluid therapy (balanced polyionic solutions) to correct dehydration and promote renal perfusion. Discontinue nephrotoxic agents (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides) immediately. Correct electrolyte imbalances with calcium gluconate or phosphate binders as needed; provide dietary modification with low-calcium, low-protein feed and monitor acid-base status with sodium bicarbonate supplementation for metabolic acidosis.
treatment_ja: 脱水補正と腎灌流促進のため、バランス電解質輸液（ポリイオン溶液）を静脈内投与する。腎毒性薬剤（NSAIDs、アミノグリコシド系）は直ちに中止する。グルコン酸カルシウムやリン吸着剤で電解質異常を補正し、低カルシウム・低タンパク飼料への変更を行う。代謝性アシドーシスには重炭酸ナトリウムの補充を検討し、酸塩基平衡を継続的にモニタリングする。

name: Renal Nutritional Deficiency (Horse)
pathophysiology: Nutritional deficiencies, particularly of vitamins (such as vitamin A, D, or E) and minerals (such as calcium, phosphorus, or magnesium), can impair renal tubular function, alter renal hemodynamics, and lead to nephrocalcinosis or tubular degeneration. Imbalanced calcium-phosphorus ratios may promote mineralization of renal tissues, while chronic deficiency states can compromise the kidney's ability to concentrate urine and maintain electrolyte homeostasis. Prolonged deficiency leads to progressive renal parenchymal damage and potential secondary renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: ビタミン（A、D、Eなど）やミネラル（カルシウム、リン、マグネシウムなど）の栄養欠乏は、腎尿細管機能の障害、腎血行動態の変化、腎石灰化症や尿細管変性を引き起こす。カルシウム・リン比の不均衡は腎組織の石灰化を促進し、慢性的な欠乏状態は腎臓の尿濃縮能力および電解質恒常性維持能力を損なう。長期的な欠乏は進行性の腎実質障害および二次性腎不全につながる。
causes: Primary causes include dietary deficiencies of essential vitamins (A, D, E) and minerals (calcium, phosphorus, magnesium), or severe imbalances in the calcium-to-phosphorus ratio from poor-quality forage or unbalanced concentrate feeds. Secondary causes include chronic malabsorption syndromes, excessive oxalate-containing plants (such as tropical grasses) binding calcium, and prolonged feeding of high-grain/low-forage diets leading to mineral imbalances affecting renal function.
treatment: Correct dietary imbalances by adjusting the calcium-to-phosphorus ratio (ideally 1.5–2:1) and supplementing deficient vitamins (A, D, E) and minerals (calcium, magnesium, phosphorus) as indicated by serum biochemistry. Provide IV fluid therapy with balanced electrolyte solutions to support renal perfusion and tubular recovery. Address underlying malabsorption or concurrent conditions and monitor renal parameters (BUN, creatinine, electrolytes) serially.
treatment_ja: 血清生化学検査に基づき、カルシウム・リン比（理想は1.5〜2:1）を是正し、不足しているビタミン（A、D、E）およびミネラル（カルシウム、マグネシウム、リン）を補給する。バランス電解質輸液を静脈内投与し、腎灌流および尿細管機能の回復を支援する。吸収不良など基礎疾患を治療し、BUN・クレアチニン・電解質を定期的にモニタリングする。

name: Renal Genetic Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal genetic disorders in horses involve inherited mutations affecting renal tubular or glomerular function, leading to progressive nephron loss, impaired filtration, and accumulation of metabolic waste products. Examples include renal dysplasia and polycystic kidney disease, where abnormal renal development or cyst formation disrupts normal kidney architecture. Progressive fibrosis and loss of functional renal parenchyma ultimately result in chronic renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎臓遺伝性疾患は、腎尿細管や糸球体機能に影響を及ぼす遺伝子変異を伴い、ネフロンの進行性喪失、濾過機能の低下、および代謝老廃物の蓄積を引き起こします。腎異形成や多発性嚢胞腎などが含まれ、異常な腎発育や嚢胞形成が正常な腎構造を破壊します。進行性の線維化と機能的腎実質の喪失により、最終的に慢性腎不全に至ります。
causes: The primary cause is inherited genetic mutations transmitted in autosomal recessive or dominant patterns, leading to abnormal renal development or function. Specific conditions include renal dysplasia, polycystic kidney disease, and renal tubular acidosis associated with breed predispositions. Secondary factors such as dehydration, concurrent infections, or nephrotoxic agents may accelerate progression of the underlying genetic defect.
treatment: No curative treatment exists for renal genetic disorders in horses; management is supportive. Intravenous fluid therapy (balanced polyionic solutions) to maintain hydration and renal perfusion, dietary protein and phosphorus restriction, and oral phosphate binders (aluminum hydroxide 30-90 mg/kg PO BID) are recommended. ACE inhibitors (benazepril 0.5 mg/kg PO SID) may slow glomerular damage progression. Sodium bicarbonate supplementation addresses metabolic acidosis in renal tubular acidosis cases.
treatment_ja: 馬の腎遺伝性疾患に根治療法は存在せず、管理は対症療法が中心となる。等張性輸液による水分補給と腎灌流の維持、食事中のタンパク質およびリン制限、経口リン吸着剤（水酸化アルミニウム30-90 mg/kg 1日2回経口投与）が推奨される。ACE阻害薬（ベナゼプリル0.5 mg/kg 1日1回経口投与）は糸球体障害の進行を遅延させる可能性がある。腎尿細管性アシドーシスの場合は重炭酸ナトリウムの補充で代謝性アシドーシスを補正する。

name: Renal Autoimmune Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: The immune system produces autoantibodies or autoreactive lymphocytes directed against renal antigens, including glomerular basement membrane components and tubular epithelial cells. Immune complex deposition or direct antibody-mediated attack leads to glomerulonephritis or tubulointerstitial nephritis, resulting in progressive inflammation, fibrosis, and loss of renal function. Complement activation and infiltration of inflammatory cells further exacerbate tissue damage and impair glomerular filtration.
pathophysiology_ja: 免疫系が糸球体基底膜成分や尿細管上皮細胞などの腎抗原に対する自己抗体や自己反応性リンパ球を産生します。免疫複合体の沈着や直接的な抗体介在性攻撃により糸球体腎炎や尿細管間質性腎炎が生じ、進行性の炎症、線維化、腎機能低下を引き起こします。補体活性化や炎症細胞の浸潤がさらに組織障害を悪化させ、糸球体濾過を障害します。
causes: The primary cause involves dysregulation of immune tolerance leading to autoimmune targeting of renal tissues, potentially triggered by chronic infections (e.g., Streptococcus equi), viral infections, or drug reactions. Secondary causes include immune complex deposition from systemic autoimmune conditions such as systemic lupus erythematosus-like syndrome, and chronic antigenic stimulation from persistent infections or neoplasia. Genetic predisposition and environmental factors may also contribute to disease development.
treatment: Immunosuppressive therapy with corticosteroids (dexamethasone 0.05-0.1 mg/kg IV/IM daily, tapering over weeks) is the cornerstone, often combined with azathioprine (3 mg/kg PO daily) for steroid-sparing effect. Supportive care includes IV fluid therapy to maintain renal perfusion, ACE inhibitors (enalapril 0.5 mg/kg PO BID) to reduce proteinuria, and treatment of any underlying infections such as Streptococcus equi.
treatment_ja: 免疫抑制療法として副腎皮質ステロイド（デキサメタゾン0.05〜0.1 mg/kg IV/IM、1日1回、数週間かけて漸減）を基本とし、アザチオプリン（3 mg/kg PO、1日1回）をステロイド節約目的で併用する。支持療法として腎灌流維持のための輸液療法、蛋白尿軽減のためのACE阻害薬（エナラプリル0.5 mg/kg PO BID）、およびStreptococcus equiなどの基礎感染症の治療を実施する。

name: Renal Degenerative Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal degenerative disease in horses involves progressive deterioration of renal parenchyma, including tubular degeneration, interstitial fibrosis, and glomerulosclerosis, leading to impaired filtration, concentration, and excretion functions. Chronic loss of functional nephrons results in azotemia, electrolyte imbalances, and eventual renal failure. The disease may be initiated by toxic insults (e.g., aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals), chronic ischemia, or immune-mediated mechanisms that trigger irreversible structural damage.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎変性疾患は、尿細管変性、間質性線維化、糸球体硬化症を含む腎実質の進行性劣化を伴い、濾過・濃縮・排泄機能の障害を引き起こす。機能的ネフロンの慢性的な喪失により高窒素血症、電解質異常、最終的には腎不全に至る。毒性物質（アミノグリコシド系抗菌薬、NSAIDs、重金属など）、慢性虚血、または免疫介在性機序が不可逆的な構造的損傷を引き起こすことがある。
causes: Primary causes include nephrotoxic drug exposure (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, vitamin D toxicosis), ingestion of toxic plants (e.g., oak, red maple, oxalate-containing plants), and heavy metal poisoning. Secondary causes include chronic dehydration, hemodynamic compromise, chronic urinary obstruction, systemic infections, and age-related degenerative changes. Immune-mediated glomerulonephritis and chronic pyelonephritis may also contribute to progressive renal degeneration.
treatment: Discontinue all nephrotoxic agents (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs). Provide aggressive IV fluid therapy (polyionic isotonic crystalloids) to correct dehydration and support renal perfusion. Manage electrolyte imbalances (calcium, phosphorus) and azotemia with dietary protein restriction, phosphate binders, and supportive care including gastroprotectants (omeprazole, sucralfate) for secondary uremic gastritis.
treatment_ja: すべての腎毒性薬剤（アミノグリコシド系、NSAIDs）を直ちに中止する。脱水補正と腎灌流維持のため、等張晶質液による積極的な静脈内輸液療法を実施する。電解質異常（カルシウム・リン）の是正、食事中のタンパク質制限、リン吸着剤の投与、および尿毒症性胃炎に対する胃粘膜保護剤（オメプラゾール、スクラルファート）の投与など、包括的な支持療法を行う。

name: Renal Traumatic Injury (Horse)
pathophysiology: Blunt or penetrating trauma to the lumbar or flank region causes direct damage to the renal parenchyma, capsule, or renal vasculature. This leads to hemorrhage (subcapsular or perirenal hematoma), parenchymal contusion or laceration, and potential disruption of the collecting system resulting in urine leakage (uroperitoneum or retroperitoneal urine accumulation). Secondary inflammation, ischemia, and possible infection can further compromise renal function.
pathophysiology_ja: 腰部または脇腹への鈍的または穿通性外傷により、腎実質、腎被膜、または腎血管系に直接的な損傷が生じる。これにより出血（被膜下または腎周囲血腫）、実質の挫傷や裂傷、集合系の破綻による尿漏出（尿腹膜炎や後腹膜尿貯留）が引き起こされる。二次的な炎症、虚血、感染がさらに腎機能を障害する可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include blunt trauma from kicks by other horses, falls, collisions with fixed objects, or vehicular accidents. Secondary causes include penetrating injuries from stakes, fencing materials, or surgical complications, as well as severe crush injuries during casting or prolonged recumbency.
causes_ja: 主な原因は他馬からの蹴り、転倒、固定物への衝突、交通事故などによる鈍的外傷である。二次的原因には杭やフェンス資材による穿通性外傷、手術合併症、キャスティング中や長期臥位時の重度圧挫傷が含まれる。
treatment: Stabilize with IV crystalloid fluids (LRS or 0.9% NaCl) and control hemorrhage; administer flunixin meglumine (1.1 mg/kg IV q12h) for analgesia and anti-inflammatory effect. Broad-spectrum antibiotics (gentamicin 6.6 mg/kg IV q24h plus penicillin) prevent secondary infection. Strict stall rest, serial ultrasonographic monitoring of hematoma resolution, and nephrectomy if uncontrolled hemorrhage or urine leakage persists.
treatment_ja: 乳酸リンゲル液または生理食塩水による輸液で循環を安定させ、出血を管理する。フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg IV 12時間毎）で鎮痛・抗炎症を図り、ゲンタマイシン（6.6 mg/kg IV 24時間毎）とペニシリンの併用で二次感染を予防する。厳格な馬房内安静とし、超音波検査で血腫の経過を定期的に観察し、止血困難や尿漏が持続する場合は腎摘出術を検討する。

name: Renal Behavioral Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal behavioral disorder in horses involves abnormal behaviors associated with underlying renal pain or dysfunction. Chronic renal disease, nephrolithiasis, or renal inflammation can cause visceral pain that manifests as behavioral changes such as flank biting, stretching, restlessness, and reluctance to work. The pain signals originating from the kidneys are referred to somatic structures, leading to observable behavioral abnormalities that may be misinterpreted as primary behavioral issues.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎行動障害は、腎臓の痛みや機能障害に関連した異常行動を伴います。慢性腎疾患、腎結石、または腎炎症が内臓痛を引き起こし、脇腹を噛む、伸展姿勢、不穏、運動拒否などの行動変化として現れます。腎臓由来の疼痛シグナルが体性構造に関連痛として伝達され、原発性の行動問題と誤認される可能性のある行動異常を引き起こします。
causes: Primary causes include nephrolithiasis, pyelonephritis, renal neoplasia, and chronic renal failure causing persistent discomfort. Secondary causes may involve ureterolithiasis, renal cysts, renal vascular disorders, or toxic nephropathy from ingestion of nephrotoxic plants (e.g., oak, red maple) or medications (e.g., NSAIDs, aminoglycosides).
treatment: Address underlying renal pathology: surgical removal of nephroliths or ureteroliths if present; treat pyelonephritis with prolonged systemic antibiotics (trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole or enrofloxacin). Manage visceral pain with flunixin meglumine (1.1 mg/kg IV) or phenylbutazone. Provide IV fluid therapy to support renal perfusion and correct azotemia.
treatment_ja: 基礎的な腎疾患の治療として、腎結石・尿管結石がある場合は外科的除去を行い、腎盂腎炎にはトリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾールまたはエンロフロキサシンによる長期全身抗菌療法を実施する。内臓痛にはフルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg IV）またはフェニルブタゾンで疼痛管理を行う。静脈輸液療法により腎灌流を維持し高窒素血症を是正する。

name: Renal Infectious Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infectious disease in horses involves bacterial colonization of the renal parenchyma, typically via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract or hematogenous spread. Bacteria such as Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., and Actinobacillus spp. cause inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue (pyelonephritis). Chronic infection may lead to renal fibrosis, impaired glomerular filtration, and eventual renal insufficiency.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症は、下部尿路からの上行性感染や血行性播種により細菌が腎実質に定着することで発症する。大腸菌、レンサ球菌、アクチノバチルス属などの細菌が炎症、膿瘍形成、腎組織の進行性破壊（腎盂腎炎）を引き起こす。慢性感染は腎線維化、糸球体濾過率の低下、最終的に腎不全に至る可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infections (most commonly E. coli, Streptococcus spp., Corynebacterium spp., and Actinobacillus equuli), often facilitated by urolithiasis, bladder dysfunction, or urethral obstruction. Secondary causes include hematogenous spread from distant infection sites, immunosuppression, chronic catheterization, and anatomical abnormalities predisposing to urinary stasis.
treatment: Initiate broad-spectrum antimicrobial therapy based on urine culture and sensitivity, commonly trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (30 mg/kg PO BID) or enrofloxacin (5 mg/kg IV/PO SID) for 2-4 weeks. Provide IV fluid therapy to maintain renal perfusion and correct dehydration. Address underlying causes such as urolithiasis or urethral obstruction surgically if indicated, and administer NSAIDs (flunixin meglumine 1.1 mg/kg IV) for pain and inflammation control.
treatment_ja: 尿培養および感受性試験に基づき、トリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾール（30 mg/kg 経口 BID）またはエンロフロキサシン（5 mg/kg 静注/経口 SID）を2〜4週間投与する広域抗菌療法を開始する。輸液療法により腎灌流を維持し脱水を補正する。尿路結石や尿道閉塞などの基礎疾患がある場合は外科的に対処し、フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg 静注）を用いて疼痛および炎症を管理する。

name: Renal Parasitic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal parasitic disease in horses occurs when parasitic organisms such as Halicephalobus gingivalis (formerly Halicephalobus deletrix), Strongylus vulgaris larvae, or Dioctophyme renale migrate to and colonize the kidneys. The parasites cause direct mechanical damage to renal parenchyma, provoke granulomatous inflammation, and can lead to progressive nephritis, tubular destruction, and impaired renal function. Larval migration through renal vasculature may also cause thrombosis, infarction, and secondary bacterial infection.
