Bacteria such as Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., and Actinobacillus equuli cause inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue, leading to impaired glomerular filtration and tubular function. Chronic infection may result in pyelonephritis, interstitial nephritis, perirenal abscessation, and eventual renal failure if left untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症は、下部尿路からの上行性感染または血行性播種により細菌が腎実質に定着することで発生します。大腸菌、連鎖球菌、Actinobacillus equuliなどの細菌が炎症、膿瘍形成、腎組織の進行性破壊を引き起こし、糸球体濾過および尿細管機能の障害をもたらします。慢性感染は腎盂腎炎、間質性腎炎、腎周囲膿瘍、さらには腎不全に進行する可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infections (most commonly E. coli, Streptococcus spp., Corynebacterium spp.) from the lower urinary tract, and hematogenous spread from distant infection sites. Secondary causes include urolithiasis causing urinary stasis, immunosuppression, urinary tract obstruction, bladder dysfunction, and catheterization-associated contamination. Predisposing factors include dehydration, concurrent systemic illness, and nephrolithiasis.
treatment: Initiate aggressive systemic antibiotic therapy based on urine culture and sensitivity, commonly trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (30 mg/kg PO BID) or enrofloxacin (5 mg/kg IV/PO SID). Provide IV fluid therapy to maintain renal perfusion and promote diuresis. Address underlying causes such as urolithiasis surgically if present, and administer NSAIDs (flunixin meglumine 1.1 mg/kg IV) for pain and inflammation control.
treatment_ja: 尿培養・感受性試験に基づき、トリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾール（30 mg/kg 経口 BID）またはエンロフロキサシン（5 mg/kg 静注/経口 SID）などの全身性抗菌薬を積極的に投与する。静脈内輸液療法により腎灌流を維持し利尿を促進する。尿路結石などの基礎疾患がある場合は外科的に対処し、フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg 静注）を用いて疼痛および炎症を管理する。

name: Renal Parasitic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal parasitic disease in horses involves migration and colonization of parasites such as Halicephalobus gingivalis (Halicephalobus deletrix), Strongylus vulgaris larvae, or Dioctophyme renale within the renal parenchyma or vasculature. Parasitic invasion leads to granulomatous nephritis, tubular destruction, interstitial fibrosis, and impaired renal function. Larval migration through renal arteries can also cause thrombosis, ischemia, and infarction of renal tissue.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎寄生虫症は、Halicephalobus gingivalis、普通円虫（Strongylus vulgaris）の幼虫、または腎虫（Dioctophyme renale）などの寄生虫が腎実質や血管系に移行・定着することで発症する。寄生虫の侵入により肉芽腫性腎炎、尿細管の破壊、間質の線維化、腎機能障害が引き起こされる。幼虫の腎動脈への移行は血栓形成、虚血、腎組織の梗塞を引き起こすこともある。
causes: Primary causes include parasitic infections by Halicephalobus gingivalis (a free-living nematode with opportunistic pathogenicity), aberrant migration of Strongylus vulgaris larvae through the renal vasculature, and rarely Dioctophyme renale infection. Secondary causes include immunosuppression or concurrent illness that facilitates opportunistic parasitic invasion, as well as environmental exposure to contaminated soil or water containing infective larvae.
treatment: Administer high-dose anthelmintics such as fenbendazole (10 mg/kg PO daily for 5 days) or ivermectin (0.2 mg/kg PO); however, efficacy against Halicephalobus gingivalis is often poor. Supportive care includes NSAIDs (flunixin meglumine 1.1 mg/kg IV) for inflammation and IV fluid therapy for renal support. Unilateral nephrectomy may be considered for severe, localized granulomatous nephritis unresponsive to medical management.
treatment_ja: 高用量の駆虫薬（フェンベンダゾール10 mg/kg 経口1日1回5日間、またはイベルメクチン0.2 mg/kg 経口）を投与するが、Halicephalobus gingivalisに対する有効性は限定的である。フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg 静注）による抗炎症療法および輸液療法で腎機能を補助する。内科的治療に反応しない片側性の重度肉芽腫性腎炎には片側腎摘出術を検討する。

name: Renal Viral Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Viral agents such as equine herpesvirus (EHV) or equine arteritis virus (EAV) can cause direct cytopathic damage to renal tubular epithelial cells and glomerular endothelium, leading to acute interstitial nephritis and impaired renal function. Immune-mediated mechanisms including immune complex deposition in glomeruli may contribute to progressive renal injury. Vasculitis induced by viral infection can compromise renal blood flow, exacerbating tubular necrosis and nephron loss.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬ヘルペスウイルス（EHV）や馬動脈炎ウイルス（EAV）などのウイルスが腎尿細管上皮細胞や糸球体内皮に直接的な細胞障害を引き起こし、急性間質性腎炎や腎機能障害をもたらす。免疫複合体の糸球体への沈着など免疫介在性機序も腎障害の進行に寄与する。ウイルス感染による血管炎が腎血流を障害し、尿細管壊死やネフロン喪失を悪化させる。
causes: Primary causes include equine herpesvirus (EHV-1, EHV-4), equine arteritis virus (EAV), and potentially other systemic viral infections that exhibit renal tropism. Secondary causes include immune complex-mediated glomerulonephritis triggered by chronic viral antigenemia, as well as secondary bacterial infections in immunocompromised horses. Pre-existing renal compromise, stress, and concurrent illness may predispose horses to viral renal involvement.
treatment: No specific antiviral therapy is curative; supportive care includes aggressive IV fluid therapy (balanced polyionic solutions) to maintain renal perfusion, along with NSAIDs (flunixin meglumine 1.1 mg/kg IV BID) for inflammation control. Administer broad-spectrum antibiotics (trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole) to prevent secondary bacterial infection. Monitor serum creatinine, BUN, and electrolytes closely, adjusting fluid rates accordingly.
treatment_ja: 特異的な抗ウイルス療法はなく、支持療法が中心となる。腎灌流維持のため積極的な輸液療法（バランス電解質液の静脈内投与）を行い、フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg IV BID）で炎症を制御する。二次細菌感染予防にトリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾールを投与する。血清クレアチニン、BUN、電解質を継続的にモニタリングし、輸液速度を適宜調整する。

name: Renal Bacterial Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Bacterial infection of the kidneys (pyelonephritis) in horses typically occurs via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract or, less commonly, through hematogenous spread. Bacteria colonize the renal pelvis and parenchyma, causing inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue. This can lead to impaired renal function, septicemia, and in severe or bilateral cases, renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎臓細菌感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路からの上行性感染、またはまれに血行性伝播によって発生します。細菌が腎盂および腎実質に定着し、炎症、膿瘍形成、腎組織の進行性破壊を引き起こします。重症例や両側性の場合、腎機能障害、敗血症、腎不全に至ることがあります。
causes: Common causative organisms include Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Staphylococcus spp., Corynebacterium spp., and Actinobacillus equuli. Predisposing factors include urolithiasis, urinary tract obstruction, bladder paralysis, catheterization, immunosuppression, and pre-existing lower urinary tract infections. Nephrolithiasis and anatomical abnormalities may also facilitate bacterial colonization.
treatment: Administer prolonged systemic antibiotic therapy (4-6 weeks) based on urine culture and sensitivity, commonly trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, enrofloxacin, or penicillin-gentamicin combinations. Provide IV fluid therapy to maintain renal perfusion and correct electrolyte imbalances. Address predisposing factors such as urolithiasis or urinary obstruction surgically if indicated, and monitor renal function via serial bloodwork and urinalysis.
treatment_ja: 尿培養および感受性試験に基づき、トリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾール、エンロフロキサシン、またはペニシリン・ゲンタマイシン併用などの全身性抗菌薬を4〜6週間の長期投与する。輸液療法により腎灌流を維持し電解質異常を補正する。尿路結石や尿路閉塞などの素因がある場合は必要に応じて外科的に対処し、血液検査および尿検査で腎機能を継続的にモニタリングする。

name: Renal Fungal Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Fungal organisms, most commonly Aspergillus spp. or Candida spp., colonize the renal parenchyma or renal pelvis, causing granulomatous or necrotizing inflammation. The infection disrupts normal renal architecture, leading to progressive nephritis, fibrosis, and potential obstruction of the urinary tract. Hematogenous dissemination or ascending infection from the lower urinary tract can facilitate fungal colonization, particularly in immunocompromised horses.
pathophysiology_ja: Aspergillus属やCandida属などの真菌が腎実質や腎盂に定着し、肉芽腫性または壊死性炎症を引き起こします。感染により正常な腎組織構造が破壊され、進行性の腎炎、線維化、および尿路閉塞を生じる可能性があります。血行性播種または下部尿路からの上行性感染により、特に免疫低下状態の馬において真菌の定着が促進されます。
causes: Primary causes include opportunistic fungal infections by Aspergillus spp., Candida spp., or other environmental fungi that invade renal tissue. Secondary causes include prolonged antibiotic therapy causing fungal overgrowth, immunosuppression (e.g., from corticosteroid use or concurrent illness such as Cushing's disease), indwelling urinary catheters, and debilitation or chronic stress.
treatment: Systemic antifungal therapy with fluconazole (5 mg/kg PO q24h) or itraconazole (3-5 mg/kg PO q12-24h) for prolonged courses (weeks to months). Amphotericin B (0.3-0.5 mg/kg IV slowly, with careful renal monitoring) may be used in severe cases. Discontinue unnecessary antibiotics/corticosteroids, provide IV fluid support to maintain renal perfusion, and consider nephrectomy for unilateral end-stage renal involvement.
treatment_ja: フルコナゾール（5 mg/kg 経口 1日1回）またはイトラコナゾール（3-5 mg/kg 経口 1日1-2回）による長期全身性抗真菌療法を実施する。重症例ではアムホテリシンB（0.3-0.5 mg/kg 緩徐静注、腎機能を慎重にモニタリング）を使用する。不要な抗菌薬やコルチコステロイドを中止し、腎灌流維持のため輸液療法を行い、片側性の末期腎障害には腎摘出術を検討する。

name: Renal Infection (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infection (pyelonephritis) in horses typically occurs via ascending bacterial infection from the lower urinary tract through the ureters to the renal pelvis and parenchyma. Bacteria colonize the renal medulla, triggering an inflammatory response that leads to tissue destruction, abscess formation, and progressive loss of renal function. Common causative organisms include Escherichia coli, Corynebacterium renale, Streptococcus spp., and Actinobaculum suis, which damage the tubular epithelium and impair urine concentration ability.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路から尿管を経由して腎盂および腎実質へ細菌が上行性に感染することで発生します。細菌が腎髄質に定着し、炎症反応を引き起こして組織破壊、膿瘍形成、および進行性の腎機能低下をもたらします。主な原因菌には大腸菌、Corynebacterium renale、Streptococcus属、Actinobaculum suisなどがあり、尿細管上皮を障害し尿濃縮能を低下させます。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infections from the lower urinary tract, often secondary to cystitis, urolithiasis, or urethral obstruction that causes urine stasis. Predisposing factors include immunosuppression, urinary catheterization, anatomical abnormalities, pregnancy, and conditions causing incomplete bladder emptying. Hematogenous spread from distant infection sites is less common but possible.
treatment: Initiate prolonged systemic antibiotic therapy (4-6 weeks) based on urine culture and sensitivity, commonly trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole or enrofloxacin. Provide IV fluid therapy to maintain renal perfusion and promote diuresis. Address underlying causes such as urolithiasis or obstruction, and perform nephrectomy if unilateral infection is refractory to medical management.
treatment_ja: 尿培養・感受性試験に基づき、トリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾールやエンロフロキサシン等の全身性抗菌薬を4〜6週間長期投与する。腎灌流維持と利尿促進のため輸液療法を実施する。尿路結石や閉塞などの基礎疾患を治療し、片側性感染で内科療法に抵抗性の場合は腎摘出術を検討する。

name: Renal Inflammation (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal inflammation (nephritis) in horses involves immune-mediated or infectious damage to the glomeruli, tubules, or interstitium of the kidneys, leading to impaired filtration, proteinuria, and azotemia. Inflammatory cell infiltration and edema disrupt normal renal architecture, potentially progressing to fibrosis and chronic renal failure. Glomerulonephritis may result from immune complex deposition, while tubulointerstitial nephritis often follows toxic or infectious insults.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎炎（ネフライティス）は、免疫介在性または感染性の障害により糸球体、尿細管、または間質が損傷を受け、濾過機能の低下、蛋白尿、高窒素血症を引き起こす。炎症細胞の浸潤と浮腫が正常な腎構造を破壊し、線維化や慢性腎不全に進行する可能性がある。糸球体腎炎は免疫複合体の沈着により生じ、尿細管間質性腎炎は毒性物質や感染に続発することが多い。
causes: Primary causes include bacterial infections (e.g., Leptospira, Streptococcus equi), viral infections (e.g., equine infectious anemia), and nephrotoxic agents such as NSAIDs, aminoglycosides, heavy metals, and toxic plants (e.g., red maple, oak). Secondary causes include immune-complex deposition from chronic infections (e.g., Streptococcus equi-associated purpura hemorrhagica), severe dehydration, septicemia, and hemolytic conditions leading to pigment nephropathy.
treatment: Remove the inciting cause (discontinue nephrotoxic drugs, treat underlying infection with appropriate antibiotics such as penicillin for Streptococcus or oxytetracycline for Leptospira). Provide aggressive IV fluid therapy (balanced polyionic solutions) to maintain renal perfusion and correct electrolyte imbalances. Administer corticosteroids (dexamethasone 0.05-0.1 mg/kg IV) for immune-mediated cases, and use diuretics (furosemide 1-2 mg/kg IV) if oliguria persists.
treatment_ja: 原因の除去（腎毒性薬剤の中止、レプトスピラにはオキシテトラサイクリン、連鎖球菌にはペニシリンなど適切な抗菌薬による感染治療）を最優先とする。腎灌流維持と電解質補正のため、バランス電解質輸液による積極的な静脈内輸液療法を実施する。免疫介在性の場合はデキサメタゾン（0.05〜0.1 mg/kg IV）を投与し、乏尿が持続する場合はフロセミド（1〜2 mg/kg IV）を使用する。

name: Renal Neoplasia (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal neoplasia in horses involves abnormal, uncontrolled cellular proliferation within the kidney parenchyma or surrounding structures. The most commonly reported primary renal tumors include renal cell carcinoma, nephroblastoma, and lymphoma, which can disrupt normal renal architecture, impair kidney function, and potentially metastasize to other organs including the lungs, liver, and lymph nodes. Tumor growth may cause progressive renal insufficiency, hematuria, and space-occupying effects leading to abdominal discomfort.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎腫瘍は、腎実質または周囲の構造における異常かつ制御不能な細胞増殖を伴う。最も一般的に報告される原発性腎腫瘍には腎細胞癌、腎芽腫（ネフロブラストーマ）、リンパ腫があり、正常な腎構造を破壊し、腎機能を障害し、肺・肝臓・リンパ節などへ転移する可能性がある。腫瘍の増大により進行性の腎不全、血尿、腹部不快感を伴う占拠性病変が生じる。
causes: The exact etiology of renal neoplasia in horses is largely unknown, though genetic predisposition, chronic inflammation, and environmental carcinogen exposure may play a role. Nephroblastoma is more commonly seen in younger horses, suggesting a congenital or developmental origin, while renal cell carcinoma tends to occur in older horses. Secondary renal involvement can occur via metastasis from other primary tumors or through multicentric lymphoma.
treatment: Primary treatment is unilateral nephrectomy when the tumor is confined to one kidney and no metastasis is detected. Supportive care includes IV fluid therapy, NSAIDs (flunixin meglumine 1.1 mg/kg IV) for pain management, and broad-spectrum antibiotics perioperatively. Chemotherapy options are limited in horses; prognosis is guarded to poor, especially with renal cell carcinoma or metastatic disease.
treatment_ja: 腫瘍が片側腎に限局し転移がない場合、片側腎摘出術が第一選択です。術後はフルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg IV）による疼痛管理、輸液療法、周術期の広域抗菌薬投与を含む支持療法を行います。馬における化学療法の選択肢は限られており、腎細胞癌や転移性疾患では予後は慎重から不良です。

name: Renal Metabolic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal metabolic disease in horses involves impaired kidney function leading to disrupted electrolyte balance, acid-base homeostasis, and waste product excretion. The kidneys fail to adequately regulate calcium, phosphorus, and other mineral metabolism, potentially resulting in hypercalcemia or hyperphosphatemia, metabolic acidosis, and azotemia. Chronic dysfunction can lead to renal secondary hyperparathyroidism, soft tissue mineralization, and progressive nephron loss.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎代謝性疾患は、腎機能障害により電解質バランス、酸塩基平衡、および老廃物排泄が障害される疾患である。腎臓がカルシウム、リン、その他のミネラル代謝を適切に調節できなくなり、高カルシウム血症または高リン血症、代謝性アシドーシス、高窒素血症を引き起こす。慢性的な機能障害は腎性二次性上皮小体機能亢進症、軟部組織の石灰化、進行性ネフロン喪失につながる。
causes: Primary causes include chronic kidney disease from nephrotoxic agents (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals), nephrolithiasis, and pyelonephritis. Secondary causes include dehydration, hemodynamic compromise, excessive dietary calcium or oxalate-containing plants, and systemic diseases such as leptospirosis or immune-mediated glomerulonephritis. Age-related degenerative changes and congenital renal abnormalities may also contribute.
treatment: Administer IV crystalloid fluids (0.9% NaCl or lactated Ringer's) to restore renal perfusion and correct dehydration. Discontinue nephrotoxic agents (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs) and correct electrolyte imbalances—use furosemide (1 mg/kg IV) for hypercalcemia. Manage dietary calcium/phosphorus ratios and treat underlying infections (e.g., trimethoprim-sulfa for pyelonephritis).
treatment_ja: 腎灌流回復と脱水補正のため、生理食塩水または乳酸リンゲル液の静脈内輸液を実施する。腎毒性薬剤（アミノグリコシド系、NSAIDs）を中止し、高カルシウム血症にはフロセミド（1 mg/kg IV）で電解質補正を行う。食餌中のカルシウム・リン比を管理し、腎盂腎炎などの基礎疾患にはトリメトプリム・サルファ剤で治療する。

name: Renal Nutritional Deficiency (Horse)
pathophysiology: Nutritional deficiencies, particularly of vitamin A, vitamin D, calcium, phosphorus, or oxalate-rich diets, can impair renal tubular function and lead to nephrocalcinosis or renal tubular degeneration in horses. Chronic imbalances in calcium-phosphorus ratios or excessive oxalate intake damage renal parenchyma by promoting mineral deposition within renal tissue, leading to progressive nephron loss and decreased glomerular filtration rate. Secondary hyperparathyroidism may develop, further exacerbating renal calcium handling abnormalities.
pathophysiology_ja: ビタミンA、ビタミンD、カルシウム、リンなどの栄養素の欠乏やシュウ酸塩の過剰摂取は、腎尿細管機能を障害し、馬において腎石灰化症や腎尿細管変性を引き起こす。カルシウム・リン比の慢性的な不均衡やシュウ酸塩の過剰摂取は、腎実質内へのミネラル沈着を促進し、進行性のネフロン喪失と糸球体濾過率の低下をもたらす。二次性副甲状腺機能亢進症が発生し、腎臓のカルシウム処理異常をさらに悪化させることがある。
causes: Primary causes include dietary imbalances such as excessive phosphorus relative to calcium, vitamin A or D deficiency, and chronic ingestion of oxalate-rich plants (e.g., Oxalis, Halogeton, or tropical grasses high in oxalates). Secondary causes include prolonged feeding of grain-heavy diets without adequate forage, poor-quality hay, and lack of mineral supplementation leading to chronic metabolic derangements affecting renal function.
treatment: Correct dietary imbalances by adjusting the calcium-to-phosphorus ratio to approximately 2:1, discontinue oxalate-rich forages, and supplement with vitamin A and vitamin D as needed. Provide IV fluid therapy (balanced polyionic solutions) to support renal perfusion and tubular recovery. Administer calcium gluconate IV if hypocalcemia is present, and transition to a balanced grass hay and appropriate mineral supplementation long-term.
treatment_ja: カルシウムとリンの比率を約2:1に調整し、シュウ酸塩を多く含む飼料を中止し、必要に応じてビタミンAおよびビタミンDを補給します。腎灌流と尿細管の回復を支援するため、バランスの取れた多電解質輸液による静脈内輸液療法を実施します。低カルシウム血症がある場合はグルコン酸カルシウムを静脈内投与し、長期的にはバランスの良い乾草と適切なミネラル補給への移行を行います。

name: Renal Genetic Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal genetic disorders in horses involve inherited mutations affecting renal tubular or glomerular structure and function, leading to progressive nephron loss, impaired filtration, and compromised electrolyte and fluid homeostasis. Examples include renal dysplasia and polycystic kidney disease, where abnormal embryonic development or cyst formation disrupts normal renal architecture. Progressive fibrosis and nephron destruction ultimately result in chronic renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎臓遺伝性疾患は、腎尿細管または糸球体の構造と機能に影響を与える遺伝子変異に起因し、進行性のネフロン喪失、濾過機能の低下、電解質および水分バランスの障害を引き起こします。腎異形成や多発性嚢胞腎などが含まれ、異常な胎生期発育や嚢胞形成により正常な腎構造が破壊されます。進行性の線維化とネフロン破壊により最終的に慢性腎不全に至ります。
causes: The primary cause is inherited genetic mutations (autosomal recessive or dominant) affecting renal development or function, such as those seen in renal dysplasia or polycystic kidney disease in certain horse breeds. Secondary contributing factors include consanguineous breeding practices that increase the prevalence of homozygous deleterious alleles. Environmental stressors and concurrent infections may accelerate the progression of underlying genetic renal disease.
treatment: No curative treatment exists; management is supportive. ACE inhibitors (enalapril 0.5 mg/kg PO q24h) may slow proteinuria progression. IV fluid therapy corrects dehydration and electrolyte imbalances. Phosphate binders and dietary protein restriction help manage azotemia. Breeding animals should be screened and affected individuals removed from breeding programs.
treatment_ja: 根治療法は存在せず、対症療法が主体となる。ACE阻害薬（エナラプリル0.5 mg/kg 経口 1日1回）により蛋白尿の進行を抑制する。輸液療法で脱水および電解質異常を補正し、リン吸着剤や食事中タンパク質制限により高窒素血症を管理する。繁殖個体の遺伝子スクリーニングを行い、罹患馬は繁殖から除外すべきである。

name: Renal Autoimmune Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: The immune system produces autoantibodies or autoreactive T-cells directed against renal antigens, leading to immune complex deposition in the glomeruli and/or tubulointerstitial tissues. This triggers complement activation, inflammatory cell infiltration, and progressive destruction of renal parenchyma, resulting in glomerulonephritis or tubulointerstitial nephritis. Over time, chronic inflammation leads to fibrosis, nephron loss, and progressive renal insufficiency.
pathophysiology_ja: 免疫系が腎臓の抗原に対する自己抗体または自己反応性T細胞を産生し、糸球体および/または尿細管間質組織に免疫複合体が沈着します。これにより補体活性化、炎症細胞浸潤、および腎実質の進行性破壊が引き起こされ、糸球体腎炎または尿細管間質性腎炎が生じます。慢性炎症により線維化、ネフロンの喪失、進行性腎不全に至ります。
causes: Primary causes include aberrant immune responses generating autoantibodies against glomerular basement membrane or other renal antigens, potentially triggered by genetic predisposition. Secondary causes include chronic infections (such as equine infectious anemia or streptococcal infections), drug reactions, or systemic autoimmune conditions that result in immune complex formation and subsequent renal deposition.
treatment: Immunosuppressive therapy with corticosteroids (dexamethasone 0.05-0.1 mg/kg IV/IM initially, tapering to oral prednisolone) is the cornerstone. Azathioprine (3 mg/kg PO q24h) may be added for steroid-sparing effect. Supportive care includes IV fluid therapy, ACE inhibitors (benazepril 0.5 mg/kg PO) for proteinuria management, and treatment of underlying infections.
treatment_ja: 副腎皮質ステロイド（デキサメタゾン0.05-0.1 mg/kg IV/IM初期投与後、経口プレドニゾロンへ漸減）による免疫抑制療法が治療の中心となる。アザチオプリン（3 mg/kg PO q24h）をステロイド節約目的で併用する場合がある。補助療法として輸液療法、蛋白尿管理のためのACE阻害薬（ベナゼプリル0.5 mg/kg PO）、および基礎感染症の治療を行う。

name: Renal Degenerative Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal degenerative disease in horses involves progressive deterioration of renal parenchyma, including tubular degeneration, interstitial fibrosis, and glomerulosclerosis, leading to impaired filtration, reabsorption, and concentrating ability. Chronic insult results in nephron loss, azotemia, electrolyte imbalances, and eventual renal failure. The remaining nephrons undergo compensatory hypertrophy but ultimately fail as the disease progresses beyond a critical threshold.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎変性疾患は、尿細管変性、間質線維化、糸球体硬化症を含む腎実質の進行性劣化を伴い、濾過能、再吸収能および濃縮能の障害を引き起こす。慢性的な障害によりネフロンが喪失し、高窒素血症、電解質異常、最終的には腎不全に至る。残存ネフロンは代償性肥大を起こすが、疾患が臨界閾値を超えると最終的に機能不全に陥る。
causes: Primary causes include chronic nephrotoxin exposure (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals, vitamin D toxicosis), chronic ischemia, and age-related degenerative changes. Secondary causes include chronic pyelonephritis, nephrolithiasis, systemic diseases such as equine infectious anemia, and prolonged hemodynamic compromise. Ingestion of toxic plants (e.g., oak, red maple, oxalate-containing plants) can also contribute to renal degeneration.
treatment: Remove nephrotoxic agents (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides) immediately. Provide aggressive IV fluid therapy (balanced polyionic solutions) to correct azotemia and electrolyte imbalances. Supportive care includes dietary protein restriction, phosphate binders (aluminum hydroxide 30-90 mg/kg PO BID), ACE inhibitors (benazepril 0.5 mg/kg PO SID) to reduce glomerular hyperfiltration, and management of secondary complications such as gastric ulceration (omeprazole 4 mg/kg PO SID).
treatment_ja: 腎毒性薬剤（NSAIDs、アミノグリコシド系）を直ちに中止する。積極的な静脈内輸液療法（バランス電解質液）で高窒素血症および電解質異常を是正する。支持療法として食事中タンパク質制限、リン吸着剤（水酸化アルミニウム30-90 mg/kg 経口BID）、ACE阻害薬（ベナゼプリル0.5 mg/kg 経口SID）による糸球体過剰濾過の抑制、胃潰瘍などの二次合併症管理（オメプラゾール4 mg/kg 経口SID）を実施する。

name: Renal Traumatic Injury (Horse)
pathophysiology: Blunt or penetrating trauma to the lumbar or flank region causes disruption of the renal parenchyma, capsule, or vascular pedicle. This leads to hemorrhage (perirenal, subcapsular, or intra-abdominal), potential urine leakage (uroperitoneum), inflammation, and if severe, compromised renal perfusion resulting in ischemic necrosis. Secondary complications include hematuria, retroperitoneal abscessation, adhesion formation, and in bilateral or severe unilateral cases, acute renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 腰部または脇腹への鈍的または穿通性外傷により、腎実質、腎被膜、または血管茎の損傷が生じる。これにより出血（腎周囲、被膜下、または腹腔内）、尿漏出（尿腹症）、炎症が引き起こされ、重度の場合は腎灌流障害による虚血性壊死が生じる。二次的合併症として血尿、後腹膜膿瘍、癒着形成、および両側性または重度片側性の場合には急性腎不全が起こりうる。
causes: Primary causes include blunt abdominal trauma from kicks by other horses, falls, collision with fixed objects, or traffic accidents. Penetrating injuries from fence posts, stakes, or other sharp objects can also directly damage the kidney. Iatrogenic injury during percutaneous renal biopsy or surgical procedures is a less common cause.
treatment: Stabilize with IV crystalloid fluids (LRS or 0.9% NaCl) and control hemorrhage; administer flunixin meglumine (1.1 mg/kg IV) for pain and anti-endotoxic effects. Monitor hematocrit and renal values serially. Severe cases with uncontrolled hemorrhage or renal pedicle avulsion may require nephrectomy; uroperitoneum requires abdominal drainage and surgical repair.
treatment_ja: 乳酸リンゲル液または生理食塩水による輸液で循環を安定させ、出血を管理する。フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg IV）を鎮痛・抗エンドトキシン目的で投与し、ヘマトクリットおよび腎機能値を経時的にモニタリングする。制御不能な出血や腎血管茎離断の重症例では腎摘出術を検討し、尿腹症には腹腔ドレナージおよび外科的修復を行う。

name: Renal Behavioral Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal behavioral disorder in horses involves abnormal behaviors (such as frequent posturing to urinate, flank watching, or stretching) that arise secondary to renal pain or discomfort caused by underlying kidney pathology such as nephrolithiasis, pyelonephritis, or renal neoplasia. Chronic renal irritation or inflammation stimulates visceral afferent nerves, leading to pain-associated behavioral changes that may be misinterpreted as colic or musculoskeletal issues. The disorder reflects the horse's behavioral response to ongoing renal dysfunction or discomfort rather than a primary behavioral condition.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎行動障害は、腎結石症、腎盂腎炎、腎腫瘍などの基礎的な腎臓疾患に起因する腎臓の痛みや不快感に伴う異常行動（頻繁な排尿姿勢、腹部を見る行動、伸展姿勢など）を含みます。慢性的な腎臓の刺激や炎症が内臓求心性神経を刺激し、疝痛や筋骨格系の問題と誤認される可能性のある疼痛関連行動変化を引き起こします。本疾患は原発性行動障害ではなく、持続的な腎機能障害や不快感に対する馬の行動反応を反映しています。
causes: Primary causes include nephrolithiasis (kidney stones), pyelonephritis, renal cysts, renal neoplasia, and chronic interstitial nephritis that produce persistent renal pain. Secondary causes may include ureterolithiasis, hydronephrosis, perirenal abscessation, or referred pain from adjacent structures. Predisposing factors include chronic dehydration, high-calcium diets, recurrent urinary tract infections, and age-related renal degeneration.
treatment: Address the underlying renal pathology: surgical removal of nephroliths or nephrotomy for kidney stones, antimicrobial therapy (trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole or enrofloxacin) for pyelonephritis, and nephrectomy for unilateral neoplasia or non-functional kidneys. Manage renal pain with flunixin meglumine (1.1 mg/kg IV q12-24h) or phenylbutazone, and provide IV fluid therapy to support renal perfusion.
treatment_ja: 基礎疾患の治療が重要である。腎結石には外科的除去（腎切石術）、腎盂腎炎にはトリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾールまたはエンロフロキサシンによる抗菌療法、片側性腫瘍や機能喪失腎には腎摘出術を実施する。腎性疼痛にはフルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg IV 12-24時間毎）またはフェニルブタゾンを投与し、輸液療法で腎灌流を維持する。

name: Renal Infectious Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infectious disease in horses involves bacterial colonization of the renal parenchyma, typically ascending from the lower urinary tract or via hematogenous spread. Bacterial infection leads to inflammation (pyelonephritis), abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue, impairing glomerular filtration and tubular function. Chronic infection may result in fibrosis, renal insufficiency, and potentially septicemia if left untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症は、下部尿路からの上行感染または血行性播種により細菌が腎実質に定着することで発症します。細菌感染により腎盂腎炎、膿瘍形成、腎組織の進行性破壊が生じ、糸球体濾過および尿細管機能が障害されます。慢性感染は線維化、腎不全、さらに未治療の場合は敗血症に至る可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infections (commonly Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Corynebacterium spp., and Actinobacillus equuli) from the lower urinary tract, and hematogenous spread from distant infection sites. Secondary causes include urolithiasis causing urinary stasis, immunosuppression, urinary catheterization, anatomical abnormalities, and pre-existing bladder dysfunction that predispose to bacterial colonization.
treatment: Administer prolonged systemic antibiotics based on urine culture and sensitivity, commonly trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (30 mg/kg PO BID) or enrofloxacin (5 mg/kg IV/PO SID) for 4-6 weeks. Provide IV fluid therapy to maintain renal perfusion and correct dehydration. Address underlying causes such as urolithiasis surgically if present, and monitor renal function via serial bloodwork and urinalysis.
treatment_ja: 尿培養・感受性試験に基づき、トリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾール（30 mg/kg 経口 BID）またはエンロフロキサシン（5 mg/kg 静注/経口 SID）を4～6週間長期全身投与する。静脈内輸液療法により腎灌流を維持し脱水を補正する。尿路結石などの基礎疾患がある場合は外科的に対処し、血液検査および尿検査で腎機能を定期的にモニタリングする。

name: Renal Parasitic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal parasitic disease in horses involves migration and colonization of parasites such as Halicephalobus gingivalis (Halicephalobus deletrix), Strongylus vulgaris larvae, or Dioctophyme renale within the renal parenchyma or vasculature. Parasitic invasion causes granulomatous inflammation, tubular destruction, interstitial nephritis, and potentially vascular thrombosis, leading to progressive renal dysfunction. Aberrant larval migration from the gastrointestinal tract via the mesenteric vasculature or direct hematogenous spread can result in both unilateral and bilateral kidney damage.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎寄生虫症は、Halicephalobus gingivalis、普通円虫（Strongylus vulgaris）の幼虫、または腎虫（Dioctophyme renale）などの寄生虫が腎実質や腎血管系に移行・定着することで発症する。寄生虫の侵入により肉芽腫性炎症、尿細管破壊、間質性腎炎、および血管血栓症が引き起こされ、進行性の腎機能障害に至る。消化管からの異所性幼虫移行や血行性播種により片側または両側の腎臓が障害される。
causes: Primary causes include aberrant migration of Strongylus vulgaris larvae through the renal vasculature, infection with Halicephalobus gingivalis (a free-living nematode that can invade the kidneys), and rarely Dioctophyme renale (giant kidney worm). Secondary factors include immunosuppression, heavy parasitic burden due to inadequate deworming, and environmental exposure to contaminated soil or water sources harboring free-living nematodes.
treatment: Administer high-dose anthelmintics such as fenbendazole (10 mg/kg PO daily for 5 days) or ivermectin (0.2 mg/kg PO); however, efficacy against Halicephalobus gingivalis is often poor. Nephrectomy of the affected kidney may be indicated for unilateral severe granulomatous disease. Supportive care includes NSAIDs (flunixin meglumine 1.1 mg/kg IV) for inflammation, IV fluids, and antimicrobials for secondary infections.
treatment_ja: フェンベンダゾール（10 mg/kg 経口、5日間連続投与）やイベルメクチン（0.2 mg/kg 経口）などの高用量駆虫薬を投与するが、Halicephalobus gingivalisに対する効果は限定的である場合が多い。片側性の重度肉芽腫性病変には罹患腎の腎摘出術が適応となる。フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg 静注）による抗炎症療法、輸液療法、二次感染に対する抗菌薬投与などの支持療法を併用する。

name: Renal Viral Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Viral agents such as equine herpesvirus (EHV) or equine arteritis virus (EAV) can cause direct cytopathic damage to renal tubular epithelial cells and glomeruli, leading to immune-complex deposition, vasculitis, interstitial nephritis, and progressive renal dysfunction. Viremia results in endothelial damage within renal vasculature, causing ischemia and secondary tubular necrosis. Inflammatory infiltrates and edema compromise renal filtration and concentrating ability.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬ヘルペスウイルス（EHV）や馬動脈炎ウイルス（EAV）などのウイルスが腎尿細管上皮細胞や糸球体に直接的な細胞障害を引き起こし、免疫複合体の沈着、血管炎、間質性腎炎、進行性腎機能障害をもたらす。ウイルス血症により腎血管内皮が障害され、虚血および続発性尿細管壊死が生じる。炎症性浸潤と浮腫が腎濾過機能および濃縮能を低下させる。
causes: Primary causes include equine herpesvirus (EHV-1, EHV-4), equine arteritis virus (EAV), and potentially other systemic viral infections that target or secondarily affect the kidneys. Secondary causes include immune-mediated glomerulonephritis triggered by viral antigen-antibody complex deposition, dehydration, and concurrent bacterial infections that exacerbate renal damage.
treatment: No specific antiviral cure exists; treatment is primarily supportive. Administer IV crystalloid fluids (lactated Ringer's or 0.9% NaCl) to maintain renal perfusion, correct electrolyte imbalances, and support diuresis. Valacyclovir (30 mg/kg PO q8h) may be considered for EHV cases. NSAIDs should be avoided; use flunixin meglumine cautiously only if needed. Broad-spectrum antibiotics (e.g., trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole) for secondary infections, and corticosteroids (dexamethasone 0.05-0.1 mg/kg IV) if immune-complex nephritis is confirmed.
treatment_ja: 特異的な抗ウイルス薬は存在せず、治療は主に支持療法となる。乳酸リンゲル液または生理食塩水の静脈内輸液により腎灌流を維持し、電解質補正および利尿を促進する。EHV症例にはバラシクロビル（30 mg/kg PO 8時間毎）の投与を検討する。NSAIDsの使用は避け、フルニキシンメグルミンは必要時のみ慎重に使用する。二次感染にはトリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾール等の広域抗菌薬を投与し、免疫複合体性腎炎が確認された場合はデキサメタゾン（0.05〜0.1 mg/kg IV）を使用する。

name: Renal Bacterial Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Bacterial infection of the renal parenchyma (pyelonephritis) typically occurs via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract, or less commonly through hematogenous spread. Bacteria colonize the renal pelvis and parenchyma, causing inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue. This leads to impaired renal function, including decreased concentrating ability, azotemia, and potential septicemia if left untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 腎実質の細菌感染（腎盂腎炎）は、通常下部尿路からの上行性感染、まれに血行性播種により発生します。細菌が腎盂および腎実質に定着し、炎症、膿瘍形成、および腎組織の進行性破壊を引き起こします。これにより濃縮能低下、高窒素血症、未治療の場合は敗血症に至る腎機能障害が生じます。
causes: Common causative organisms include Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Staphylococcus spp., Proteus spp., and Klebsiella spp., often ascending from the lower urinary tract. Predisposing factors include urolithiasis, urinary tract obstruction, bladder paralysis, catheterization, immunosuppression, and anatomical abnormalities. Mares may be more susceptible due to their shorter urethra and proximity to fecal contamination.
treatment: Initiate aggressive systemic antibiotic therapy based on urine culture and sensitivity; common empirical choices include trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (30 mg/kg PO BID) or enrofloxacin (5 mg/kg IV/PO SID). Continue antibiotics for 4-6 weeks minimum. Provide IV fluid therapy to maintain hydration and renal perfusion, correct electrolyte imbalances, and address any underlying predisposing factors such as urolithiasis or obstruction.
treatment_ja: 尿培養および感受性試験に基づき、積極的な全身性抗菌薬療法を開始する。経験的治療としてトリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾール（30 mg/kg 経口 BID）またはエンロフロキサシン（5 mg/kg 静注/経口 SID）が一般的に選択される。抗菌薬は最低4～6週間継続する。輸液療法により水分補給と腎灌流を維持し、電解質異常を補正するとともに、尿路結石や閉塞などの基礎疾患に対処する。

name: Renal Fungal Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Fungal organisms, most commonly Aspergillus spp. or Candida spp., colonize the renal parenchyma and/or renal pelvis, leading to granulomatous or necrotizing inflammation. The infection disrupts normal renal architecture, potentially causing obstruction, abscess formation, and progressive loss of renal function. Hematogenous dissemination or ascending infection from the lower urinary tract can lead to fungal nephritis and pyelonephritis.
pathophysiology_ja: 主にAspergillus属やCandida属などの真菌が腎実質や腎盂に定着し、肉芽腫性または壊死性の炎症を引き起こす。感染により正常な腎構造が破壊され、閉塞、膿瘍形成、進行性の腎機能低下を招く可能性がある。血行性播種または下部尿路からの上行性感染により真菌性腎炎および腎盂腎炎が発生する。
causes: Primary causes include opportunistic fungal infections by Aspergillus spp., Candida spp., or other environmental fungi that invade the kidneys. Predisposing factors include prolonged antibiotic therapy, immunosuppression, indwelling urinary catheters, debilitation, and concurrent systemic illness that compromises immune defenses. Secondary bacterial infections may complicate the condition.
causes_ja: 主な原因はAspergillus属、Candida属、その他の環境中の真菌による日和見感染である。長期間の抗菌薬投与、免疫抑制状態、尿道カテーテルの留置、衰弱、免疫機能を低下させる併発疾患が素因となる。二次的な細菌感染が病態を複雑化させることがある。
treatment: Systemic antifungal therapy with fluconazole (5 mg/kg PO q24h) or itraconazole (3 mg/kg PO q12h) for prolonged courses (weeks to months). Discontinue predisposing antibiotics and address immunosuppression. Nephrectomy may be considered for unilateral disease with abscessation or obstruction unresponsive to medical therapy. Supportive care includes IV fluid therapy and monitoring renal parameters.
treatment_ja: フルコナゾール（5 mg/kg PO 1日1回）またはイトラコナゾール（3 mg/kg PO 1日2回）による全身性抗真菌療法を数週間から数ヶ月間実施する。誘因となる抗菌薬の中止および免疫抑制状態の改善を図る。片側性の膿瘍形成や閉塞で内科的治療に反応しない場合は腎摘出術を検討する。輸液療法と腎機能モニタリングによる支持療法も併せて行う。

name: Renal Infection (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infection (pyelonephritis) in horses typically occurs via ascending bacterial infection from the lower urinary tract through the ureters to the renal pelvis and parenchyma. Bacterial colonization triggers an inflammatory response leading to neutrophilic infiltration, tubular damage, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue. If untreated, chronic infection can result in fibrosis, impaired renal function, and potentially septicemia.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路から尿管を経由して腎盂および腎実質へ細菌が上行性に感染することで発生します。細菌の定着により炎症反応が誘発され、好中球浸潤、尿細管障害、膿瘍形成、腎組織の進行性破壊が生じます。未治療の場合、慢性感染により線維化、腎機能障害、さらには敗血症に至る可能性があります。
causes: The most common causative organisms include Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Staphylococcus spp., Corynebacterium renale, and Actinobacillus equuli, typically ascending from the lower urinary tract. Predisposing factors include urolithiasis, bladder paralysis, urinary catheterization, immunosuppression, and anatomical abnormalities that promote urinary stasis. Hematogenous spread from distant infection sites is a less common but recognized route.
treatment: Initiate aggressive parenteral antimicrobial therapy based on urine culture and sensitivity; commonly trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (30 mg/kg PO BID) or enrofloxacin (5 mg/kg IV/PO SID) for 4-6 weeks. Provide IV fluid therapy to maintain hydration and promote renal perfusion. Address predisposing factors such as urolithiasis or bladder dysfunction.
treatment_ja: 尿培養・感受性試験に基づき、トリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾール（30 mg/kg PO BID）またはエンロフロキサシン（5 mg/kg IV/PO SID）などの抗菌薬を4〜6週間積極的に投与する。静脈内輸液により水和を維持し腎灌流を促進する。尿路結石や膀胱機能障害など素因となる疾患の治療も並行して行う。

name: Renal Inflammation (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal inflammation (nephritis) in horses involves immune-mediated or infectious damage to the glomeruli, tubules, or interstitium of the kidneys, leading to impaired filtration, reabsorption, and secretion functions. Inflammatory cell infiltration and edema disrupt normal renal architecture, potentially progressing to fibrosis and chronic renal insufficiency. This results in azotemia, electrolyte imbalances, and impaired waste elimination.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎炎は、免疫介在性または感染性の障害により糸球体、尿細管、または間質に炎症が生じ、濾過・再吸収・分泌機能が障害される疾患です。炎症細胞の浸潤と浮腫が正常な腎構造を破壊し、線維化や慢性腎不全へ進行する可能性があります。その結果、高窒素血症、電解質異常、老廃物排泄障害が生じます。
causes: Primary causes include bacterial infections (e.g., Leptospira spp., Streptococcus equi), viral infections (e.g., equine infectious anemia), and immune-mediated glomerulonephritis. Secondary causes include nephrotoxic drugs (e.g., NSAIDs, aminoglycosides), toxin exposure (e.g., heavy metals, toxic plants such as oak or red maple), and systemic diseases such as septicemia or endotoxemia.
treatment: Treat underlying cause with appropriate antimicrobials (e.g., penicillin for Streptococcus, oxytetracycline for Leptospira). Discontinue nephrotoxic drugs (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides) immediately. Provide aggressive IV fluid therapy (isotonic crystalloids) to maintain renal perfusion, correct electrolyte imbalances, and consider corticosteroids (dexamethasone) for immune-mediated nephritis.
treatment_ja: 原因に応じた抗菌薬投与（例：連鎖球菌にはペニシリン、レプトスピラにはオキシテトラサイクリン）を実施する。腎毒性薬物（NSAIDs、アミノグリコシド系）は直ちに中止する。等張晶質液の積極的な静脈内輸液により腎灌流を維持し、電解質異常を補正する。免疫介在性腎炎にはデキサメタゾン等のコルチコステロイドの使用を検討する。

name: Renal Neoplasia (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal neoplasia in horses involves abnormal, uncontrolled cellular proliferation within the kidney parenchyma or renal pelvis. The most commonly reported types include renal cell carcinoma, nephroblastoma, and lymphoma, which can disrupt normal renal architecture, impair glomerular filtration and tubular function, and potentially metastasize to regional lymph nodes, lungs, and other organs. As the tumor expands, it may cause compression of adjacent renal tissue leading to progressive renal insufficiency and hematuria.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎腫瘍は、腎実質または腎盂における異常かつ無制御な細胞増殖を伴う。最も一般的に報告される種類には腎細胞癌、腎芽腫、リンパ腫があり、正常な腎構造を破壊し、糸球体濾過および尿細管機能を障害し、所属リンパ節や肺などへ転移する可能性がある。腫瘍の拡大に伴い、隣接する腎組織が圧迫され、進行性の腎機能不全や血尿を引き起こす。
causes: The exact etiology of renal neoplasia in horses is largely unknown, with no clearly identified genetic, infectious, or environmental risk factors consistently documented. Renal cell carcinoma is the most frequently reported primary renal tumor in adult horses, while nephroblastoma tends to occur in younger animals. Chronic inflammation or unknown carcinogenic exposures may play a contributing role, but definitive causative agents have not been established.
treatment: Unilateral nephrectomy is the primary treatment for localized renal tumors when the contralateral kidney is functional. For lymphoma, systemic chemotherapy (e.g., corticosteroids such as dexamethasone, with or without cyclophosphamide) may be attempted. Supportive care includes IV fluid therapy, analgesics (flunixin meglumine), and monitoring renal function via serial bloodwork.
treatment_ja: 対側腎の機能が正常であれば、限局性腎腫瘍に対しては片側腎摘出術が第一選択となる。リンパ腫の場合、デキサメタゾン等のコルチコステロイドやシクロホスファミドを用いた全身化学療法が試みられる。支持療法として静脈輸液、フルニキシンメグルミンによる鎮痛、および血液検査による腎機能の継続的モニタリングを行う。

name: Renal Metabolic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal metabolic disease in horses involves impaired kidney function leading to disrupted electrolyte balance, acid-base homeostasis, and waste product excretion. The kidneys fail to adequately regulate calcium, phosphorus, and other mineral metabolism, potentially resulting in hypercalcemia or hyperphosphatemia, metabolic acidosis, and azotemia. Chronic dysfunction can lead to secondary hyperparathyroidism, renal osteodystrophy, and progressive nephron loss.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎代謝疾患は、腎機能の障害により電解質バランス、酸塩基平衡、および老廃物の排泄が乱れる疾患である。腎臓がカルシウム、リン、その他のミネラル代謝を適切に調節できなくなり、高カルシウム血症や高リン血症、代謝性アシドーシス、高窒素血症を引き起こす。慢性的な機能障害は二次性上皮小体機能亢進症、腎性骨異栄養症、進行性のネフロン喪失につながる可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include chronic kidney disease, nephrotoxin exposure (such as aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals, or vitamin D toxicosis), and nephrolithiasis. Secondary causes include dehydration, systemic infections, hemodynamic compromise, oxalate-containing plant ingestion, and age-related renal degeneration. Dietary imbalances with excessive calcium or phosphorus intake can also contribute to renal metabolic dysfunction.
treatment: Administer IV fluid therapy (balanced polyionic solutions) to correct dehydration and promote renal perfusion. Discontinue nephrotoxic agents (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides). Manage electrolyte imbalances with calcium gluconate or phosphate binders as needed; correct acid-base disturbances with sodium bicarbonate. Provide dietary modification with reduced protein and calcium intake.
treatment_ja: 脱水補正と腎灌流促進のため、バランス電解質輸液による静脈内補液療法を実施する。腎毒性薬剤（NSAIDs、アミノグリコシド系抗菌薬）を直ちに中止する。電解質異常にはグルコン酸カルシウムやリン吸着剤を必要に応じて投与し、酸塩基平衡異常には重炭酸ナトリウムで補正する。低タンパク質・低カルシウム食への食事管理を行う。

name: Renal Nutritional Deficiency (Horse)
pathophysiology: Nutritional deficiencies, particularly of vitamin A, vitamin D, calcium, or phosphorus, can impair normal renal tubular function and structural integrity in horses. Chronic imbalances, especially excessive phosphorus relative to calcium (inverted Ca:P ratio), lead to calcium deposition in renal tissues (nephrocalcinosis), tubular degeneration, and progressive loss of renal function. Secondary hyperparathyroidism may also contribute to renal mineralization and fibrosis.
pathophysiology_ja: ビタミンA、ビタミンD、カルシウム、リンなどの栄養素の欠乏や不均衡は、馬の腎尿細管機能および構造的完全性を損なう。特にカルシウムに対するリンの過剰（Ca:P比の逆転）は腎組織へのカルシウム沈着（腎石灰化症）、尿細管変性、進行性の腎機能低下を引き起こす。二次性副甲状腺機能亢進症も腎臓の石灰化および線維化に寄与する。
causes: Primary causes include dietary calcium-phosphorus imbalance (especially excessive phosphorus from high-grain or bran-heavy diets), vitamin A deficiency, and vitamin D deficiency or excess. Secondary causes include oxalate-rich pastures (e.g., tropical grasses) that bind dietary calcium, leading to chronic calcium deficiency and compensatory renal mineral disturbances.
treatment: Correct dietary Ca:P ratio to approximately 2:1 by reducing grain/bran intake and supplementing calcium carbonate or limestone. Provide adequate vitamin A (retinyl palmitate) and balanced vitamin D supplementation. Administer IV fluid therapy with balanced electrolytes in acute cases to support renal perfusion, and monitor serum calcium, phosphorus, and renal parameters regularly.
treatment_ja: 食餌中のCa:P比を約2:1に是正するため、穀物・ふすまの給与量を削減し、�iteite calcium carbonateまたは石灰石を補給する。レチニルパルミテートによるビタミンA補給およびビタミンDの適正な補給を行う。急性例では電解質バランスの取れた輸液を静脈内投与し腎灌流を維持する。血清カルシウム、リン、腎機能パラメータを定期的にモニタリングする。

name: Renal Genetic Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal genetic disorders in horses involve inherited mutations affecting renal tubular or glomerular structure and function, leading to progressive nephron loss, impaired filtration, and concentrating ability. Examples include renal dysplasia and polycystic kidney disease, where abnormal kidney development or cyst formation results in progressive renal insufficiency. Over time, compensatory mechanisms fail, leading to azotemia, electrolyte imbalances, and eventual renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎遺伝性疾患は、腎尿細管や糸球体の構造・機能に影響を与える遺伝子変異に起因し、進行性のネフロン喪失、濾過機能および濃縮能の低下を引き起こします。腎形成不全や多発性嚢胞腎などが含まれ、腎臓の発育異常や嚢胞形成により進行性の腎機能不全が生じます。代償機構が破綻すると、高窒素血症、電解質異常、最終的に腎不全に至ります。
causes: The primary cause is inherited genetic mutations affecting kidney development or function, often transmitted in an autosomal recessive or dominant pattern depending on the specific disorder. Specific examples include renal dysplasia and polycystic kidney disease observed in certain horse breeds. Secondary factors such as dehydration, nephrotoxic agents, or concurrent infections may accelerate disease progression.
treatment: No curative treatment exists; management is supportive. Administer IV fluid therapy (balanced polyionic solutions) to maintain hydration and renal perfusion. Use ACE inhibitors (e.g., enalapril 0.5 mg/kg PO q24h) to reduce glomerular hypertension, phosphate binders for hyperphosphatemia, and dietary protein restriction to slow progression. Monitor renal values (BUN, creatinine, SDMA) regularly.
treatment_ja: 根治療法は存在せず、支持療法が中心となる。静脈内輸液療法（バランス電解質液）で水分補給と腎灌流を維持する。ACE阻害薬（エナラプリル0.5 mg/kg 経口 1日1回）で糸球体内圧を軽減し、高リン血症にはリン吸着剤を使用、食事中のタンパク質制限により進行を遅延させる。腎機能指標（BUN、クレアチニン、SDMA）を定期的にモニタリングする。

name: Renal Autoimmune Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: The immune system produces autoantibodies or autoreactive T-cells directed against renal antigens, leading to immune complex deposition in the glomeruli and/or tubulointerstitial tissue. This triggers complement activation, inflammatory cell infiltration, and progressive destruction of renal parenchyma, resulting in glomerulonephritis or tubulointerstitial nephritis. Chronic inflammation leads to fibrosis, loss of functional nephrons, and eventual renal insufficiency.
pathophysiology_ja: 免疫系が腎臓の抗原に対する自己抗体または自己反応性T細胞を産生し、糸球体および/または尿細管間質組織に免疫複合体が沈着します。これにより補体活性化、炎症細胞浸潤、腎実質の進行性破壊が引き起こされ、糸球体腎炎または尿細管間質性腎炎を発症します。慢性炎症は線維化、機能ネフロンの喪失、最終的な腎不全を引き起こします。
causes: Primary causes include idiopathic autoimmune dysregulation targeting renal glomerular or tubular basement membrane antigens. Secondary causes may involve chronic infections (e.g., Streptococcus equi, equine infectious anemia), drug reactions, or systemic immune-mediated diseases that result in immune complex deposition in the kidneys. Genetic predisposition and environmental triggers may also contribute to disease onset.
treatment: Initiate immunosuppressive therapy with corticosteroids (dexamethasone 0.05-0.1 mg/kg IV daily, tapering over weeks) combined with azathioprine (3 mg/kg PO daily) to suppress autoantibody production and inflammation. Provide supportive care including IV fluid therapy, ACE inhibitors (benazepril 0.5 mg/kg PO) for proteinuria management, and monitor renal values closely.
treatment_ja: 免疫抑制療法としてデキサメタゾン（0.05〜0.1 mg/kg IV、漸減投与）およびアザチオプリン（3 mg/kg PO 1日1回）を開始し、自己抗体産生と炎症を抑制する。補液療法、蛋白尿管理のためのACE阻害薬（ベナゼプリル0.5 mg/kg PO）による支持療法を併用し、腎機能値を定期的にモニタリングする。

name: Renal Degenerative Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal degenerative disease in horses involves progressive loss of functional nephrons due to chronic tubular degeneration, interstitial fibrosis, and glomerulosclerosis. This leads to impaired glomerular filtration, reduced concentrating ability, and accumulation of uremic toxins. Over time, compensatory mechanisms fail, resulting in chronic renal failure with azotemia, electrolyte imbalances, and metabolic derangements.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎変性疾患は、慢性的な尿細管変性、間質線維化、および糸球体硬化症による機能的ネフロンの進行性喪失を伴います。これにより糸球体濾過率の低下、濃縮能の低下、尿毒症性毒素の蓄積が生じます。やがて代償機構が破綻し、高窒素血症、電解質異常、代謝障害を伴う慢性腎不全に至ります。
causes: Primary causes include chronic nephrotoxin exposure (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals, vitamin D toxicosis), chronic pyelonephritis, and age-related degenerative changes. Secondary causes include chronic dehydration, hemodynamic compromise from prolonged hypotension, and immune-mediated glomerulonephritis. In some cases, the etiology remains idiopathic.
treatment: Treatment is primarily supportive: IV fluid therapy (balanced polyionic solutions) to correct dehydration and promote diuresis, dietary modification with reduced protein and calcium, and discontinuation of all nephrotoxic agents (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides). ACE inhibitors (enalapril 0.5 mg/kg PO q24h) may reduce proteinuria. Phosphate binders and gastric protectants (omeprazole 4 mg/kg PO q24h) address uremic complications.
treatment_ja: 治療は主に支持療法が中心となる。脱水補正と利尿促進のためバランス電解質輸液を静脈内投与し、低タンパク・低カルシウム食への変更、およびすべての腎毒性薬剤（NSAIDs、アミノグリコシド系）の中止を行う。ACE阻害薬（エナラプリル0.5 mg/kg 経口 1日1回）でタンパク尿を軽減し、リン吸着剤や胃粘膜保護剤（オメプラゾール4 mg/kg 経口 1日1回）で尿毒症性合併症に対処する。

name: Renal Traumatic Injury (Horse)
pathophysiology: Blunt or penetrating trauma to the lumbar region causes direct damage to the renal parenchyma, vasculature, or collecting system. This can result in subcapsular hematoma, parenchymal laceration, renal pedicle injury, or urine leakage into the retroperitoneal space. Subsequent hemorrhage, inflammation, and potential uroperitoneum can lead to systemic compromise including hypovolemia, azotemia, and sepsis.
pathophysiology_ja: 腰部への鈍的または穿通性外傷により、腎実質、血管系、または集合系に直接的な損傷が生じる。これにより被膜下血腫、実質裂傷、腎茎損傷、または後腹膜腔への尿漏出が起こりうる。続発する出血、炎症、および尿腹症は循環血液量減少、高窒素血症、敗血症などの全身的な障害を引き起こす可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include external blunt force trauma such as kicks from other horses, falls, collisions with fixed objects, or vehicular accidents. Secondary causes include penetrating injuries from sharp objects, fractured ribs lacerating the kidney, or iatrogenic injury during percutaneous procedures. Violent athletic activities such as racing or jumping may also predispose to renal trauma.
causes_ja: 主な原因は他馬からの蹴り、転倒、固定物への衝突、交通事故などの外部からの鈍的外力である。二次的原因として鋭利な物体による穿通性損傷、肋骨骨折による腎臓の裂傷、経皮的処置中の医原性損傷がある。競馬や障害飛越などの激しい運動活動も腎外傷の素因となりうる。
treatment: Stabilize with IV crystalloid fluids (LRS or 0.9% NaCl) and manage hemorrhage; administer flunixin meglumine (1.1 mg/kg IV) for pain and anti-inflammatory effect. Minor injuries are managed conservatively with stall rest, serial ultrasound monitoring, and broad-spectrum antibiotics (e.g., potassium penicillin 22,000 IU/kg IV q6h plus gentamicin 6.6 mg/kg IV q24h). Severe lacerations or pedicle injuries may require nephrectomy.
treatment_ja: 乳酸リンゲル液または生理食塩水による輸液で循環を安定させ、出血管理を行う。フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg IV）を鎮痛・抗炎症目的で投与する。軽度損傷には馬房安静、連続超音波モニタリング、広域抗菌薬（ペニシリンカリウム22,000 IU/kg IV q6h＋ゲンタマイシン6.6 mg/kg IV q24h）による保存療法を実施する。重度の裂傷や腎茎損傷には腎摘出術が必要となる場合がある。

name: Renal Behavioral Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal behavioral disorder in horses involves abnormal behaviors (such as excessive flank watching, stretching, posturing to urinate, or intermittent colic-like signs) that are associated with renal pain or dysfunction. Chronic renal inflammation, nephrolithiasis, or renal neoplasia can stimulate visceral afferent nerves, leading to referred pain and characteristic behavioral changes. The disorder may also involve altered electrolyte balance and uremic toxin accumulation affecting the central nervous system.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎行動障害は、腎臓の疼痛や機能障害に関連する異常行動（過度の腹部注視、伸展姿勢、排尿姿勢、間欠的な疝痛様症状など）を伴います。慢性腎炎症、腎結石、または腎腫瘍が内臓求心性神経を刺激し、関連痛や特徴的な行動変化を引き起こします。電解質バランスの異常や尿毒症性毒素の蓄積が中枢神経系に影響を与えることもあります。
causes: Primary causes include nephrolithiasis, renal neoplasia (such as renal cell carcinoma), chronic pyelonephritis, and renal cysts causing persistent renal pain. Secondary causes may include ureterolithiasis, chronic interstitial nephritis, renal abscessation, or toxic nephropathy from ingestion of nephrotoxic plants (e.g., oak, red maple) or medications (e.g., NSAIDs, aminoglycosides).
treatment: Address the underlying cause: surgical nephrectomy for renal neoplasia or large nephroliths; antimicrobial therapy (trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole or enrofloxacin) for pyelonephritis. Provide analgesia with flunixin meglumine (1.1 mg/kg IV q12h) or buscopan for visceral pain. Supportive IV fluid therapy to maintain renal perfusion and correct electrolyte imbalances.
treatment_ja: 原因疾患の治療を行う：腎腫瘍や大型腎結石には外科的腎摘出術を実施し、腎盂腎炎にはトリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾールまたはエンロフロキサシンによる抗菌療法を行う。フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg IV 12時間ごと）やブスコパンで内臓痛を管理する。静脈内輸液療法により腎灌流の維持および電解質バランスの補正を行う。

name: Renal Infectious Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infectious disease in horses involves bacterial colonization of the renal parenchyma, typically ascending from the lower urinary tract or via hematogenous spread. Infection leads to inflammation (pyelonephritis), tubular damage, interstitial edema, and abscess formation, which can progressively impair glomerular filtration and concentrating ability. Chronic infection may result in fibrosis, nephron loss, and eventual renal insufficiency or failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症は、下部尿路からの上行性感染または血行性播種により細菌が腎実質に定着することで発症する。感染により腎盂腎炎、尿細管障害、間質性浮腫および膿瘍形成が生じ、糸球体濾過率や濃縮能が進行性に低下する。慢性感染は線維化やネフロンの喪失を引き起こし、最終的に腎不全に至ることがある。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infections (commonly Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Corynebacterium spp., and Actinobacillus equuli) from the lower urinary tract, as well as hematogenous spread from distant infection sites. Secondary contributing factors include urolithiasis, urinary tract obstruction, immunosuppression, catheterization, and pre-existing lower urinary tract disease that predispose to bacterial colonization.
treatment: Initiate broad-spectrum antimicrobial therapy based on urine culture and sensitivity, commonly trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (30 mg/kg PO BID) or enrofloxacin (5 mg/kg IV/PO SID) for 2-4 weeks. Provide aggressive IV fluid therapy to maintain renal perfusion and correct dehydration. Address underlying causes such as urolithiasis surgically if present, and administer NSAIDs (flunixin meglumine 1.1 mg/kg IV) for pain and inflammation control.
treatment_ja: 尿培養および感受性試験に基づき、トリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾール（30 mg/kg 経口 1日2回）またはエンロフロキサシン（5 mg/kg 静注/経口 1日1回）などの広域抗菌薬を2〜4週間投与する。積極的な静脈内輸液療法により腎灌流の維持と脱水の補正を行う。尿路結石などの基礎疾患がある場合は外科的に対処し、フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg 静注）を用いて疼痛および炎症を管理する。

name: Renal Parasitic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal parasitic disease in horses involves migration and colonization of parasites such as Halicephalobus gingivalis (Halicephalobus deletrix), Strongylus vulgaris larvae, or Dioctophyme renale within the renal parenchyma and vasculature. Parasitic invasion causes granulomatous inflammation, tubular destruction, fibrosis, and impaired renal function. Larval migration through renal arteries can also lead to thrombosis, infarction, and secondary bacterial infection of the kidney.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎寄生虫症は、Halicephalobus gingivalis、大型円虫（Strongylus vulgaris）の幼虫、または腎虫（Dioctophyme renale）などの寄生虫が腎実質や腎血管系に移行・寄生することで発生する。寄生虫の侵入は肉芽腫性炎症、尿細管の破壊、線維化、腎機能障害を引き起こす。幼虫の腎動脈内移行は血栓症、梗塞、二次的な細菌感染を引き起こすことがある。
causes: Primary causes include parasitic infection by Halicephalobus gingivalis (a free-living nematode with opportunistic pathogenicity), migrating Strongylus vulgaris larvae (large strongyles), and rarely Dioctophyme renale (giant kidney worm). Secondary causes include immunosuppression, poor hygiene, and exposure to contaminated soil or water facilitating parasitic entry. Aberrant larval migration from intestinal parasites may also target the kidneys.
treatment: Administer high-dose anthelmintics such as fenbendazole (10 mg/kg PO daily for 5 days) or ivermectin (0.2 mg/kg PO); however, efficacy against Halicephalobus gingivalis is often poor. Supportive care includes NSAIDs (flunixin meglumine 1.1 mg/kg IV) for inflammation and IV fluid therapy for renal support. Nephrectomy of the affected kidney may be considered in unilateral cases with severe parenchymal destruction.
treatment_ja: 高用量の駆虫薬（フェンベンダゾール10 mg/kg 経口 1日1回5日間、またはイベルメクチン0.2 mg/kg 経口）を投与するが、Halicephalobus gingivalisに対する効果は限定的であることが多い。抗炎症薬（フルニキシンメグルミン1.1 mg/kg 静注）による炎症管理および輸液療法による腎支持療法を併用する。片側性で腎実質の重度破壊がある場合は、患側腎の摘出術（腎摘除術）を検討する。

name: Renal Viral Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Viral agents such as equine herpesvirus (EHV) or equine arteritis virus (EAV) can cause vasculitis and immune-mediated damage to renal glomeruli and tubules, leading to impaired filtration, proteinuria, and progressive renal dysfunction. Viral-induced endothelial injury and immune complex deposition in renal vasculature result in ischemia, tubular necrosis, and interstitial nephritis. In severe cases, widespread renal parenchymal damage leads to acute or chronic renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬ヘルペスウイルス（EHV）や馬動脈炎ウイルス（EAV）などのウイルスが血管炎や免疫介在性の糸球体・尿細管障害を引き起こし、濾過機能の低下、蛋白尿、進行性の腎機能障害をもたらす。ウイルスによる内皮損傷と免疫複合体の腎血管への沈着が虚血、尿細管壊死、間質性腎炎を引き起こす。重症例では広範な腎実質障害により急性または慢性腎不全に至る。
causes: Primary causes include equine herpesvirus (EHV-1, EHV-4), equine arteritis virus (EAV), and potentially other nephrotrophic viruses that target renal tissue. Secondary causes include immune complex deposition, systemic vasculitis, dehydration, and concurrent bacterial infections that exacerbate viral-induced renal damage.
treatment: No specific antiviral cure exists; treatment is supportive. Administer IV balanced crystalloid fluids (e.g., lactated Ringer's solution) to maintain renal perfusion and correct dehydration. Use flunixin meglumine (1.1 mg/kg IV q12-24h) for anti-inflammatory effects, broad-spectrum antibiotics to prevent secondary bacterial infection, and ACE inhibitors or renal-protective agents for proteinuria management. Monitor renal values (BUN, creatinine) closely.
treatment_ja: 特異的な抗ウイルス治療薬は存在せず、支持療法が中心となる。乳酸リンゲル液などの等張晶質液を静脈内投与し、腎灌流の維持と脱水の補正を行う。フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg IV 12-24時間毎）で抗炎症効果を得るとともに、二次的細菌感染予防のため広域スペクトル抗菌薬を使用する。蛋白尿管理にはACE阻害薬や腎保護薬を検討し、BUN・クレアチニン値を頻回にモニタリングする。

name: Renal Bacterial Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Bacterial infection of the kidneys (pyelonephritis) in horses typically occurs via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract, or less commonly through hematogenous spread. Bacteria colonize the renal pelvis and parenchyma, causing inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue. This can lead to impaired renal function, septicemia, and potentially chronic renal failure if left untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎臓の細菌感染（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路からの上行性感染、またはまれに血行性播種によって発生します。細菌が腎盂および腎実質に定着し、炎症、膿瘍形成、および腎組織の進行性破壊を引き起こします。未治療の場合、腎機能障害、敗血症、さらには慢性腎不全に至る可能性があります。
causes: Common causative organisms include Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Staphylococcus spp., Corynebacterium spp., and Actinobacillus equuli. Predisposing factors include urolithiasis, urinary tract obstruction, bladder paralysis, catheterization, immunosuppression, and pre-existing lower urinary tract infections. Nephrolithiasis and structural abnormalities of the urinary tract may also facilitate bacterial colonization.
treatment: Initiate prolonged systemic antibiotic therapy (4-6 weeks) based on urine culture and sensitivity, commonly trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole or enrofloxacin. Provide IV fluid therapy to maintain renal perfusion and correct electrolyte imbalances. Address underlying predisposing factors such as urolithiasis or urinary obstruction surgically if indicated.
treatment_ja: 尿培養および感受性試験に基づき、トリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾールまたはエンロフロキサシン等の全身性抗菌薬を長期間（4〜6週間）投与する。静脈内輸液療法により腎灌流を維持し、電解質異常を補正する。尿路結石や尿路閉塞などの基礎疾患がある場合は、必要に応じて外科的に対処する。

name: Renal Fungal Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Fungal organisms, most commonly Aspergillus spp. or Candida spp., colonize the renal parenchyma and/or renal pelvis, leading to granulomatous or necrotizing inflammation. The infection disrupts normal renal architecture, impairing glomerular filtration and tubular function, and may result in fungal ball (mycetoma) formation causing urinary obstruction. Hematogenous dissemination or ascending infection from the lower urinary tract can lead to progressive renal insufficiency and potential systemic mycosis.
pathophysiology_ja: 主にAspergillus属やCandida属などの真菌が腎実質や腎盂に定着し、肉芽腫性または壊死性の炎症を引き起こします。感染により正常な腎構造が破壊され、糸球体濾過や尿細管機能が障害され、真菌球（菌腫）の形成により尿路閉塞を引き起こすことがあります。血行性播種または下部尿路からの上行感染により、進行性の腎不全や全身性真菌症に至る可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include opportunistic fungal infections by Aspergillus spp., Candida spp., or less commonly Cryptococcus spp., often secondary to immunosuppression from prolonged antibiotic therapy, corticosteroid use, or debilitating systemic illness. Predisposing factors include indwelling urinary catheters, urinary stasis, diabetes mellitus, and chronic renal disease that compromises local immune defenses. Hematogenous spread from pulmonary or gastrointestinal fungal infections may also seed the kidneys.
treatment: Systemic antifungal therapy with fluconazole (5 mg/kg PO q24h) or itraconazole (3-5 mg/kg PO q12-24h) for prolonged courses (weeks to months). Discontinue immunosuppressive agents and predisposing antibiotics. Provide IV fluid therapy for renal support; consider nephrectomy if unilateral disease with extensive parenchymal destruction.
treatment_ja: フルコナゾール（5 mg/kg 経口 1日1回）またはイトラコナゾール（3-5 mg/kg 経口 1日1-2回）による全身性抗真菌療法を数週間から数ヶ月間実施する。免疫抑制剤や誘因となる抗菌薬は中止する。腎機能維持のため輸液療法を行い、片側性で実質の広範な破壊がある場合は腎摘出術を検討する。

name: Renal Infection (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infection (pyelonephritis) in horses typically occurs via ascending bacterial infection from the lower urinary tract through the ureters to the renal pelvis and parenchyma. Bacteria colonize the renal medulla, triggering an inflammatory response that leads to tissue destruction, abscess formation, and progressive impairment of renal function. Hematogenous spread from distant infection sites is a less common route. Predisposing factors include urinary stasis, urolithiasis, and immunosuppression.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路から尿管を経由して腎盂および腎実質へ細菌が上行性に感染することで発生します。細菌が腎髄質に定着し、炎症反応を引き起こして組織破壊、膿瘍形成、および腎機能の進行性障害をもたらします。血行性の感染経路はまれですが起こり得ます。尿停滞、尿路結石、免疫抑制が素因となります。
causes: The most common causative organisms include Escherichia coli, Proteus spp., Klebsiella spp., Streptococcus spp., and Corynebacterium renale. Predisposing factors include urolithiasis, bladder paralysis, urethral obstruction, catheterization, and conditions causing urinary stasis. Secondary causes include hematogenous spread from systemic infections, immunosuppression, and anatomical abnormalities of the urinary tract.
treatment: Initiate aggressive, prolonged antibiotic therapy (4-6 weeks minimum) based on urine culture and sensitivity; commonly used agents include trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, enrofloxacin, or penicillin-gentamicin combinations. Correct predisposing factors such as urolithiasis or urinary obstruction. Provide IV fluid therapy to maintain renal perfusion and promote diuresis, along with NSAIDs (flunixin meglumine) for pain and inflammation control.
treatment_ja: 尿培養・感受性試験に基づき、トリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾール、エンロフロキサシン、またはペニシリン・ゲンタマイシン併用などの抗菌薬を最低4〜6週間長期投与する。尿路結石や尿路閉塞などの素因を外科的・内科的に是正する。腎灌流維持と利尿促進のため積極的な輸液療法を行い、フルニキシンメグルミン等のNSAIDsで疼痛・炎症管理を実施する。

name: Renal Inflammation (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal inflammation (nephritis) in horses involves immune-mediated or infectious insult to the glomeruli, tubules, or interstitium, leading to impaired filtration, proteinuria, and progressive loss of renal function. Inflammatory cell infiltration and edema damage the nephron architecture, potentially resulting in fibrosis and chronic kidney disease if unresolved. Immune complex deposition, direct bacterial infection, or toxin-mediated injury can trigger the inflammatory cascade affecting one or both kidneys.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎炎（腎臓の炎症）は、免疫介在性または感染性の障害により糸球体、尿細管、または間質に炎症が生じ、濾過機能の低下、蛋白尿、進行性の腎機能障害を引き起こします。炎症細胞の浸潤と浮腫がネフロン構造を損傷し、未解決の場合は線維化や慢性腎臓病に進行する可能性があります。免疫複合体の沈着、細菌の直接感染、または毒素性障害が炎症カスケードを誘発します。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infections (e.g., Streptococcus, E. coli), immune-mediated glomerulonephritis, and nephrotoxic agents such as NSAIDs, aminoglycosides, or heavy metals. Secondary causes include systemic infections (e.g., equine infectious anemia, leptospirosis), dehydration, septicemia, and endotoxemia. Ingestion of nephrotoxic plants (e.g., oak, red maple) and pigment nephropathy from myoglobinuria or hemoglobinuria can also contribute.
treatment: Treat underlying cause: administer appropriate antibiotics (e.g., trimethoprim-sulfonamide or penicillin) for bacterial nephritis; discontinue nephrotoxic drugs immediately. Provide aggressive IV fluid therapy (lactated Ringer's or 0.9% NaCl) to restore renal perfusion. Supportive care includes corticosteroids (dexamethasone) for immune-mediated cases, electrolyte correction, and monitoring of serum creatinine and BUN.
treatment_ja: 原因に応じた治療を行う：細菌性腎炎にはトリメトプリム・スルホンアミドやペニシリンなどの適切な抗菌薬を投与し、腎毒性薬物は直ちに中止する。乳酸リンゲル液や生理食塩水による積極的な輸液療法で腎灌流を回復させる。免疫介在性の場合はデキサメタゾンなどの副腎皮質ステロイドを使用し、電解質補正、血清クレアチニンおよびBUNのモニタリングを含む支持療法を実施する。

name: Renal Neoplasia (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal neoplasia in horses involves the uncontrolled proliferation of abnormal cells within the kidney parenchyma or renal pelvis. The most commonly reported types include renal cell carcinoma, nephroblastoma, and lymphoma, which can disrupt normal renal architecture, impair filtration and excretory functions, and potentially metastasize to other organs such as the lungs, liver, and lymph nodes. Progressive tumor growth leads to renal insufficiency, compression of adjacent structures, and systemic paraneoplastic effects.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎腫瘍は、腎実質または腎盂における異常細胞の無制御な増殖を伴う。最も多く報告される腫瘍は腎細胞癌、腎芽腫（ネフロブラストーマ）、リンパ腫であり、正常な腎構造を破壊し、濾過・排泄機能を障害し、肺、肝臓、リンパ節などへ転移する可能性がある。腫瘍の進行により腎不全、隣接臓器の圧迫、全身性の腫瘍随伴症候群が生じる。
causes: The exact etiology of renal neoplasia in horses is largely unknown, though genetic mutations, chronic inflammation, and possible environmental carcinogen exposure may contribute. Nephroblastoma tends to occur more frequently in younger horses, suggesting a congenital or developmental origin, while renal cell carcinoma is more common in older horses.
treatment: Primary treatment is unilateral nephrectomy when the tumor is confined to one kidney and no metastasis is detected. Supportive care includes IV fluid therapy, NSAIDs such as flunixin meglumine (1.1 mg/kg IV) for pain management, and antimicrobials post-surgery. Chemotherapy options are limited in equine practice; palliative care with analgesics is recommended for inoperable or metastatic cases.
treatment_ja: 腫瘍が片側腎に限局し転移がない場合、片側腎摘出術が第一選択となる。術後は輸液療法、フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg 静脈投与）による疼痛管理、および抗菌薬投与を含む支持療法を実施する。馬における化学療法の選択肢は限られており、手術不能例や転移例には鎮痛薬を用いた緩和的治療が推奨される。

name: Renal Metabolic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal metabolic disease in horses involves disruption of the kidney's ability to regulate electrolyte balance, acid-base homeostasis, and waste product excretion. Impaired renal tubular function leads to abnormal handling of calcium, phosphorus, and bicarbonate, potentially resulting in hypercalcemia, hyperphosphatemia, or metabolic acidosis. Chronic dysfunction can lead to renal tubular acidosis, nephrocalcinosis, and progressive nephron loss with subsequent azotemia.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎代謝性疾患は、電解質バランス、酸塩基平衡、および老廃物排泄を調節する腎臓の機能障害を伴う。腎尿細管機能の低下により、カルシウム、リン、重炭酸塩の異常な処理が生じ、高カルシウム血症、高リン血症、または代謝性アシドーシスを引き起こす可能性がある。慢性的な機能障害は腎尿細管性アシドーシス、腎石灰化症、進行性のネフロン喪失および高窒素血症につながる。
causes: Primary causes include excessive dietary calcium or oxalate-containing plants (such as tropical grasses), chronic vitamin D toxicosis, and inherited or acquired renal tubular defects. Secondary causes include chronic kidney disease from nephrotoxins (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals), prolonged dehydration, septicemia, and conditions causing chronic hypercalcemia such as hyperparathyroidism. Nutritional imbalances with high calcium-to-phosphorus ratios or excessive protein intake can also contribute.
treatment: Correct dietary imbalances by removing high-calcium or oxalate-rich feeds and adjusting calcium-to-phosphorus ratios. Provide IV fluid therapy (balanced polyionic solutions) to support renal perfusion and correct electrolyte and acid-base disturbances. Discontinue nephrotoxic agents (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides) and administer supportive care including phosphate binders if hyperphosphatemia is present.
treatment_ja: 高カルシウムまたはシュウ酸塩含有飼料を除去し、カルシウム・リン比を適正化して食事性不均衡を是正する。静脈内輸液療法（バランス型電解質液）により腎灌流を維持し、電解質および酸塩基異常を補正する。腎毒性薬剤（NSAIDs、アミノグリコシド系）を中止し、高リン血症にはリン吸着剤を投与するなど対症療法を実施する。

name: Renal Nutritional Deficiency (Horse)
pathophysiology: Nutritional deficiencies, particularly of vitamins (such as vitamin A, D, or E) and minerals (such as calcium, phosphorus, or magnesium), can impair normal renal tubular function, glomerular integrity, and electrolyte homeostasis in horses. Imbalances in the calcium-to-phosphorus ratio or excessive oxalate-containing forages can lead to calcium deposition in renal tissues (nephrocalcinosis), tubular degeneration, and progressive renal dysfunction. Chronic deficiency states may result in secondary hyperparathyroidism, soft tissue mineralization, and eventual renal fibrosis.
pathophysiology_ja: ビタミン（A、D、Eなど）やミネラル（カルシウム、リン、マグネシウムなど）の栄養欠乏は、馬の腎尿細管機能、糸球体の完全性、および電解質恒常性を障害する。カルシウムとリンの比率の不均衡やシュウ酸を多く含む飼料の過剰摂取は、腎組織へのカルシウム沈着（腎石灰化症）、尿細管変性、進行性腎機能障害を引き起こす。慢性的な欠乏状態は二次性副甲状腺機能亢進症、軟部組織の石灰化、最終的には腎線維症に至ることがある。
causes: Primary causes include dietary imbalances such as excessive phosphorus relative to calcium (inverted Ca:P ratio), feeding of high-oxalate grasses (e.g., tropical pastures such as buffel grass or setaria), and deficiencies in vitamin A or D. Secondary causes include prolonged grazing on nutrient-poor pastures, inadequate mineral supplementation, and chronic ingestion of nephrotoxic plants that exacerbate underlying nutritional imbalances.
treatment: Correct dietary Ca:P ratio to 2:1 by supplementing calcium carbonate (50-100 g/day orally) and removing high-oxalate forages. Administer parenteral vitamin A (100,000-250,000 IU IM) and vitamin D as needed. Provide IV fluid therapy with balanced electrolytes to support renal perfusion and correct dehydration.
treatment_ja: カルシウムとリンの比率を2:1に是正するため、炭酸カルシウム（50～100 g/日、経口投与）を補給し、高シュウ酸牧草を除去する。必要に応じてビタミンA（100,000～250,000 IU 筋注）およびビタミンDを非経口投与する。バランス電解質輸液を静脈内投与し、腎灌流の維持と脱水の補正を行う。

name: Renal Genetic Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal genetic disorders in horses involve inherited mutations affecting renal tubular or glomerular structure and function, leading to progressive nephron loss, impaired filtration, and concentrating ability. Examples include renal dysplasia and polycystic kidney disease, where abnormal renal development or cyst formation results in progressive destruction of functional renal parenchyma. Over time, compensatory mechanisms fail, leading to azotemia, electrolyte imbalances, and chronic renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎遺伝性疾患は、腎尿細管や糸球体の構造・機能に影響を与える遺伝子変異に起因し、進行性のネフロン喪失、濾過能力および濃縮能力の低下を引き起こします。腎異形成や多発性嚢胞腎などが含まれ、腎臓の異常発達や嚢胞形成により機能的な腎実質が進行性に破壊されます。やがて代償機構が破綻し、高窒素血症、電解質異常、慢性腎不全に至ります。
causes: The primary cause is inherited genetic mutations, often autosomal recessive or dominant, affecting genes responsible for normal renal development and function. Specific conditions include renal dysplasia (commonly reported in certain horse breeds) and polycystic kidney disease. Consanguinity or inbreeding within certain bloodlines increases the prevalence of these disorders.
causes_ja: 主な原因は、正常な腎発達および機能に関与する遺伝子の常染色体劣性または優性の遺伝子変異です。腎異形成（特定の馬品種で報告が多い）や多発性嚢胞腎などが含まれます。特定の血統内での近親交配が、これらの疾患の発生率を高めます。
treatment: No curative treatment exists; management is supportive. ACE inhibitors (benazepril 0.5 mg/kg PO q24h) may slow proteinuria progression. IV fluid therapy corrects dehydration and electrolyte imbalances. Phosphate binders and dietary protein restriction help manage azotemia. Monitor renal values regularly and manage secondary complications such as anemia with erythropoietin if needed.
treatment_ja: 根治療法は存在せず、対症療法が中心となる。ACE阻害薬（ベナゼプリル0.5 mg/kg 経口 1日1回）で蛋白尿の進行を遅延させる。輸液療法により脱水・電解質異常を補正し、リン吸着剤や食事中の蛋白質制限で高窒素血症を管理する。腎数値を定期的にモニタリングし、貧血などの二次的合併症にはエリスロポエチン投与を検討する。

name: Renal Autoimmune Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: The immune system produces autoantibodies or autoreactive lymphocytes directed against renal antigens, including glomerular basement membrane components or tubular epithelial cells. Immune complex deposition or direct antibody-mediated injury leads to glomerulonephritis or tubulointerstitial nephritis, resulting in progressive inflammation, fibrosis, and loss of renal function. Complement activation and inflammatory cell infiltration further exacerbate tissue damage and impair glomerular filtration.
pathophysiology_ja: 免疫系が糸球体基底膜成分や尿細管上皮細胞などの腎臓抗原に対する自己抗体または自己反応性リンパ球を産生します。免疫複合体の沈着や直接的な抗体介在性障害により糸球体腎炎や尿細管間質性腎炎が引き起こされ、進行性の炎症・線維化・腎機能低下をもたらします。補体活性化や炎症細胞浸潤がさらに組織損傷を悪化させ、糸球体濾過機能を障害します。
causes: Primary causes include dysregulation of immune tolerance leading to autoantibody production against renal self-antigens, possibly triggered by molecular mimicry following infectious diseases (e.g., Streptococcus equi, EIA virus). Secondary causes may include chronic infections, drug reactions, neoplasia, or systemic autoimmune conditions such as systemic lupus erythematosus-like syndromes that result in immune complex-mediated renal injury.
treatment: Immunosuppressive therapy with corticosteroids (dexamethasone 0.05-0.1 mg/kg IV/IM daily, tapering over weeks) is first-line. Azathioprine (3 mg/kg PO daily) may be added for steroid-sparing effect. Supportive care includes IV fluid therapy to maintain renal perfusion, ACE inhibitors (benazepril 0.5 mg/kg PO) to reduce proteinuria, and treatment of underlying infections such as Streptococcus equi.
treatment_ja: 免疫抑制療法として副腎皮質ステロイド（デキサメタゾン0.05〜0.1 mg/kg IV/IM、数週間かけて漸減）が第一選択である。アザチオプリン（3 mg/kg PO）をステロイド節約目的で併用可能。補助療法として腎灌流維持のための輸液療法、蛋白尿軽減のためACE阻害薬（ベナゼプリル0.5 mg/kg PO）、およびStreptococcus equi等の基礎感染症の治療を行う。

name: Renal Degenerative Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal degenerative disease in horses involves progressive deterioration of renal parenchyma, including tubular degeneration, interstitial fibrosis, and glomerulosclerosis, leading to a gradual decline in glomerular filtration rate and impaired renal function. Chronic nephrotoxic insults, ischemia, or immune-mediated damage result in irreversible nephron loss, eventually progressing to chronic renal failure with azotemia, electrolyte imbalances, and impaired waste excretion.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎変性疾患は、尿細管変性、間質線維化、糸球体硬化症を含む腎実質の進行性劣化を伴い、糸球体濾過率の低下と腎機能障害を引き起こす。慢性的な腎毒性障害、虚血、または免疫介在性損傷により不可逆的なネフロン喪失が生じ、最終的に高窒素血症、電解質異常、老廃物排泄障害を伴う慢性腎不全に進行する。
causes: Primary causes include chronic exposure to nephrotoxins (such as aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals, and oxalate-containing plants), chronic ischemia, and age-related degeneration. Secondary causes include systemic diseases such as leptospirosis, equine infectious anemia, immune-mediated glomerulonephritis, and chronic urinary obstruction or recurrent pyelonephritis.
treatment: Discontinue all nephrotoxic agents (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs). Provide IV fluid therapy with balanced polyionic solutions to maintain hydration and support renal perfusion. Manage electrolyte imbalances (calcium, phosphorus) and implement dietary protein restriction. Administer ACE inhibitors (benazepril) to reduce glomerular hyperfiltration, and treat underlying infections or systemic diseases as indicated.
treatment_ja: 全ての腎毒性薬剤（アミノグリコシド系、NSAIDs）を中止する。バランス電解質輸液による静脈内輸液療法を実施し、水分補給と腎灌流の維持を図る。電解質異常（カルシウム、リン）を是正し、食事中のタンパク質制限を行う。ACE阻害薬（ベナゼプリル）を投与して糸球体過剰濾過を軽減し、基礎疾患となる感染症や全身性疾患があれば併せて治療する。

name: Renal Traumatic Injury (Horse)
pathophysiology: Blunt or penetrating trauma to the lumbar region causes direct damage to the renal parenchyma, capsule, or renal vasculature, leading to hemorrhage, hematoma formation, and potential urine leakage into the retroperitoneal space. The resulting inflammation, ischemia, and possible secondary infection can compromise renal function. In severe cases, vascular pedicle injury may cause life-threatening hemorrhage or complete renal infarction.
pathophysiology_ja: 腰部への鈍的または穿通性外傷により、腎実質、腎被膜、または腎血管系に直接的な損傷が生じ、出血、血腫形成、および後腹膜腔への尿漏出が起こる。続発する炎症、虚血、および二次感染の可能性により腎機能が障害される。重症例では血管茎損傷により致命的な出血や完全な腎梗塞を引き起こすことがある。
causes: Primary causes include blunt abdominal or lumbar trauma from kicks by other horses, falls, collisions with fixed objects, or vehicular accidents. Secondary causes include penetrating injuries from sharp objects, fractured ribs lacerating renal tissue, or iatrogenic injury during percutaneous procedures such as renal biopsy. Extreme physical exertion or violent struggling during recumbency may also contribute.
causes_ja: 主な原因は、他馬からの蹴り、転倒、固定物への衝突、または交通事故による腹部・腰部への鈍的外傷である。二次的原因として、鋭利な物体による穿通性損傷、肋骨骨折による腎組織の裂傷、腎生検などの経皮的処置中の医原性損傷がある。過度の運動や横臥時の激しい暴れも原因となりうる。
treatment: Stabilize with IV crystalloid fluids (LRS or 0.9% NaCl) and control hemorrhage. Administer flunixin meglumine (1.1 mg/kg IV q12h) for pain/inflammation and broad-spectrum antibiotics (e.g., gentamicin 6.6 mg/kg IV q24h plus penicillin 22,000 IU/kg IV q6h). Monitor hematocrit, creatinine, and perform serial ultrasound. Severe cases with uncontrolled hemorrhage or urine leakage may require nephrectomy.
treatment_ja: 乳酸リンゲル液または生理食塩水による輸液で循環を安定させ、出血を管理する。フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg IV 12時間毎）で疼痛・炎症を制御し、ゲンタマイシン（6.6 mg/kg IV 24時間毎）およびペニシリン（22,000 IU/kg IV 6時間毎）で広域抗菌療法を行う。ヘマトクリット、クレアチニンの継続的監視と連続超音波検査を実施し、止血不能や尿漏出が持続する重症例では腎摘出術を検討する。

name: Renal Behavioral Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal behavioral disorder in horses involves chronic renal pain or discomfort arising from kidney pathology (such as nephrolithiasis, pyelonephritis, or chronic renal failure) that manifests as abnormal behavioral patterns. The persistent nociceptive input from the renal system leads to altered posture, reluctance to move, flank guarding, and changes in urination behavior. Secondary hormonal and metabolic imbalances from impaired renal function may further contribute to neurological and behavioral changes.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎行動障害は、腎結石症、腎盂腎炎、慢性腎不全などの腎臓病変に起因する慢性的な腎臓の疼痛や不快感が異常な行動パターンとして発現するものです。腎臓からの持続的な侵害受容入力により、姿勢の変化、運動拒否、側腹部の防御反応、排尿行動の変化が生じます。腎機能低下に伴うホルモンおよび代謝異常が、神経学的・行動学的変化をさらに悪化させる可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include nephrolithiasis, renal neoplasia, pyelonephritis, chronic interstitial nephritis, and renal cysts causing persistent renal pain. Secondary causes may include ureterolithiasis, hydronephrosis, toxic nephropathy (from NSAIDs, aminoglycosides, or heavy metals), and ischemic renal injury leading to chronic discomfort and behavioral manifestations.
treatment: Address underlying renal pathology: surgical removal of nephroliths or nephrotomy if indicated; antimicrobial therapy (trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 30 mg/kg PO BID) for pyelonephritis. Manage pain with flunixin meglumine (1.1 mg/kg IV SID) short-term, transitioning to gabapentin (5-10 mg/kg PO BID) for chronic neuropathic pain. Provide IV fluid therapy for renal support and behavioral modification through environmental enrichment.
treatment_ja: 基礎疾患である腎病変への対応として、腎結石の外科的除去や腎切開術を検討する。腎盂腎炎にはトリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾール（30 mg/kg PO BID）を投与する。疼痛管理としてフルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg IV SID）を短期使用し、慢性神経障害性疼痛にはガバペンチン（5-10 mg/kg PO BID）へ移行する。腎機能維持のための輸液療法および環境エンリッチメントによる行動修正を併用する。

name: Renal Infectious Disease (Horse)
