Secondary causes may involve ureterolithiasis, renal neoplasia, renal trauma, or referred pain from adjacent structures. Predisposing factors include chronic dehydration, high-calcium diets, and recurrent urinary tract infections.
treatment: Address underlying cause: surgical removal of nephroliths or renal cysts via nephrotomy or nephrectomy if indicated; treat pyelonephritis with prolonged antimicrobials (trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 30 mg/kg PO BID). Manage visceral pain with flunixin meglumine (1.1 mg/kg IV SID) or buscopan (0.3 mg/kg IV) for acute episodes. Ensure adequate hydration with IV fluid therapy and correct electrolyte imbalances.
treatment_ja: 原因疾患の治療として、腎結石や腎嚢胞には腎切開術や腎摘出術を検討し、腎盂腎炎にはトリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾール（30 mg/kg 経口 1日2回）の長期抗菌薬療法を実施する。内臓痛管理にはフルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg 静注 1日1回）やブスコパン（0.3 mg/kg 静注）を急性期に使用する。十分な輸液療法で水和を維持し、電解質異常を補正する。

name: Renal Infectious Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infectious disease in horses involves bacterial colonization of the renal parenchyma, typically ascending from the lower urinary tract or via hematogenous spread. Bacterial infection triggers an inflammatory response leading to pyelonephritis, abscess formation, or interstitial nephritis, resulting in progressive damage to nephrons, impaired renal function, and potential sepsis. Chronic cases may lead to renal fibrosis, hydronephrosis, and eventual renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎臓感染症は、主に下部尿路からの上行性感染または血行性播種により細菌が腎実質に定着することで発症する。細菌感染により炎症反応が誘発され、腎盂腎炎、膿瘍形成、または間質性腎炎を引き起こし、ネフロンの進行性障害、腎機能低下、敗血症の可能性がある。慢性例では腎線維化、水腎症、最終的に腎不全に至ることがある。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infections (commonly Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Actinobacillus equuli, and Corynebacterium spp.) from the lower urinary tract, as well as hematogenous spread from distant infection sites. Secondary causes include urolithiasis, urinary tract obstruction, immunosuppression, indwelling urinary catheters, and conditions predisposing to urinary stasis such as recumbency or neurological disorders.
treatment: Initiate aggressive parenteral antibiotic therapy based on urine culture and sensitivity, commonly trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (30 mg/kg PO BID) or enrofloxacin (5 mg/kg IV/PO SID) for 4-6 weeks. Provide IV fluid therapy to maintain renal perfusion and correct electrolyte imbalances. Address underlying causes such as urolithiasis surgically if present, and monitor renal function via serial bloodwork and urinalysis.
treatment_ja: 尿培養・感受性試験に基づき、トリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾール（30 mg/kg PO BID）またはエンロフロキサシン（5 mg/kg IV/PO SID）を4〜6週間積極的に全身投与する。腎灌流維持と電解質補正のため静脈輸液を実施する。尿路結石など基礎疾患が存在する場合は外科的処置を行い、連続的な血液検査および尿検査で腎機能を継続的にモニタリングする。

name: Renal Parasitic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal parasitic disease in horses occurs when parasitic organisms such as Halicephalobus gingivalis (Halicephalobus deletrix), Strongylus vulgaris larvae, or Dioctophyme renale migrate to or lodge within the renal parenchyma, renal pelvis, or perirenal tissues. The parasites cause direct mechanical damage, granulomatous inflammation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue, potentially leading to nephritis, abscess formation, hydronephrosis, and impaired renal function. Larval migration through renal vasculature can also induce thrombosis and ischemic necrosis of kidney tissue.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎寄生虫症は、Halicephalobus gingivalis、普通円虫（Strongylus vulgaris）の幼虫、または腎虫（Dioctophyme renale）などの寄生虫が腎実質、腎盂、または腎周囲組織に移行・寄生することで発生する。寄生虫は直接的な機械的損傷、肉芽腫性炎症、腎組織の進行性破壊を引き起こし、腎炎、膿瘍形成、水腎症、および腎機能障害を招く可能性がある。幼虫が腎血管を移行することで血栓症や虚血性壊死を引き起こすこともある。
causes: Primary causes include aberrant migration of parasites such as Halicephalobus gingivalis (a free-living nematode that can become an opportunistic parasite), migrating larvae of Strongylus vulgaris, and rarely Dioctophyme renale (giant kidney worm). Secondary causes include immunosuppression, heavy parasite burdens due to inadequate deworming, and environmental exposure to contaminated soil or water harboring infective larvae or parasitic stages.
treatment: Administer high-dose anthelmintics such as fenbendazole (10 mg/kg PO daily for 5 days) or ivermectin (0.2 mg/kg PO); however, efficacy against Halicephalobus gingivalis is often poor. Supportive care includes NSAIDs (flunixin meglumine 1.1 mg/kg IV) for inflammation and nephroprotective IV fluid therapy. Nephrectomy of the affected kidney may be considered in unilateral cases with severe parenchymal destruction.
treatment_ja: フェンベンダゾール（10 mg/kg 経口、5日間連続投与）やイベルメクチン（0.2 mg/kg 経口）などの高用量駆虫薬を投与するが、Halicephalobus gingivalisに対する有効性は低いことが多い。フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg 静注）による抗炎症療法および腎保護目的の輸液療法を実施する。片側性で腎実質の破壊が重度な場合は、患側腎の腎摘出術を検討する。

name: Renal Viral Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Viral agents such as equine herpesvirus (EHV) or equine arteritis virus (EAV) can cause immune-mediated or direct cytopathic damage to renal tubular and glomerular structures. Viral replication in endothelial cells leads to vasculitis, thrombosis, and ischemic injury to the kidneys, resulting in impaired glomerular filtration and tubular necrosis. Immune complex deposition in glomeruli may further contribute to progressive renal dysfunction.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬ヘルペスウイルス（EHV）や馬動脈炎ウイルス（EAV）などのウイルスが腎尿細管および糸球体構造に免疫介在性または直接的な細胞障害を引き起こします。血管内皮細胞でのウイルス増殖により血管炎、血栓症、腎虚血性障害が生じ、糸球体濾過機能の低下と尿細管壊死をもたらします。糸球体への免疫複合体の沈着がさらに進行性の腎機能障害に寄与する場合があります。
causes: Primary causes include systemic viral infections such as equine herpesvirus type 1 (EHV-1), equine arteritis virus (EAV), and potentially other nephrotrophic viruses that secondarily affect the kidneys. Secondary causes include immune-mediated glomerulonephritis triggered by viral antigen-antibody complex deposition, as well as hemodynamic compromise from systemic viral illness leading to renal hypoperfusion.
treatment: No specific antiviral cure exists; treatment is primarily supportive. Administer IV balanced crystalloid fluids (e.g., lactated Ringer's solution) to maintain renal perfusion and correct electrolyte imbalances. Use valacyclovir (30 mg/kg PO q8h) for EHV-1 cases, NSAIDs (flunixin meglumine 1.1 mg/kg IV) cautiously for inflammation, and consider corticosteroids if immune-mediated glomerulonephritis is confirmed. Monitor renal values closely and provide nutritional support.
treatment_ja: 特異的な抗ウイルス治療は存在せず、主に支持療法が中心となる。乳酸リンゲル液などの等張晶質液を静脈内投与し、腎灌流の維持と電解質補正を行う。EHV-1症例にはバラシクロビル（30 mg/kg 経口 8時間毎）を使用し、フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg 静注）を慎重に投与して炎症を抑制する。免疫介在性糸球体腎炎が確認された場合はコルチコステロイドを検討する。腎機能値を綿密にモニタリングし、栄養管理を併行する。

name: Renal Bacterial Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Bacterial pathogens, commonly Escherichia coli, Actinobacillus spp., Streptococcus spp., or Corynebacterium spp., ascend from the lower urinary tract or spread hematogenously to the kidneys, causing inflammation, abscessation, and progressive destruction of renal parenchyma. The resulting pyelonephritis impairs tubular and glomerular function, leading to impaired urine concentration, electrolyte imbalances, and potentially renal failure if left untreated. Chronic infection may lead to fibrosis, nephrolithiasis, and irreversible loss of functional nephrons.
pathophysiology_ja: 大腸菌、アクチノバチルス属、連鎖球菌属、コリネバクテリウム属などの細菌が下部尿路からの上行感染または血行性に腎臓に到達し、炎症、膿瘍形成、腎実質の進行性破壊を引き起こす。結果として生じる腎盂腎炎は尿細管および糸球体機能を障害し、尿濃縮能の低下、電解質異常、未治療の場合は腎不全に至る。慢性感染は線維化、腎結石、不可逆的なネフロン喪失を引き起こす可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include ascending urinary tract infections (most commonly E. coli), hematogenous spread from distant infection sites, and urolithiasis causing urinary stasis and secondary infection. Predisposing factors include bladder paralysis, urethral obstruction, immunosuppression, catheterization, and anatomical abnormalities that impair normal urine flow.
treatment: Initiate broad-spectrum antimicrobial therapy (trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 30 mg/kg PO BID or enrofloxacin 5 mg/kg IV/PO SID), adjusting based on urine culture and sensitivity results; continue for 4-6 weeks minimum. Provide IV fluid therapy to maintain renal perfusion and correct azotemia. Address underlying causes such as urolithiasis removal or bladder catheterization, and monitor renal values and urinalysis serially.
treatment_ja: 尿培養・感受性試験の結果に基づき、広域スペクトル抗菌薬（トリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾール 30 mg/kg 経口 1日2回、またはエンロフロキサシン 5 mg/kg 静注/経口 1日1回）を最低4〜6週間投与する。静脈輸液療法により腎灌流を維持し高窒素血症を是正する。尿路結石の除去や膀胱カテーテル管理など基礎疾患への対処を行い、腎数値および尿検査を定期的にモニタリングする。

name: Renal Fungal Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Fungal organisms, most commonly Aspergillus spp. or Candida spp., colonize the renal parenchyma and/or renal pelvis, causing granulomatous or necrotizing inflammation. The infection disrupts normal renal architecture, leading to progressive nephritis, fungal ball (mycetoma) formation, and impaired renal function. Hematogenous dissemination or ascending infection from the lower urinary tract can occur, particularly in immunocompromised horses.
pathophysiology_ja: 主にAspergillus属やCandida属などの真菌が腎実質や腎盂に定着し、肉芽腫性または壊死性の炎症を引き起こす。感染により正常な腎構造が破壊され、真菌球（菌腫）の形成や腎機能障害が進行する。血行性播種または下部尿路からの上行性感染が、特に免疫機能が低下した馬で生じることがある。
causes: Primary causes include opportunistic fungal infections by Aspergillus spp., Candida spp., or other environmental fungi. Predisposing factors include prolonged antibiotic therapy, immunosuppression (e.g., corticosteroid use, debilitating illness), indwelling urinary catheters, and pre-existing renal damage or urinary tract obstruction.
causes_ja: 主な原因はAspergillus属、Candida属、その他の環境真菌による日和見感染である。長期間の抗菌薬投与、免疫抑制（副腎皮質ステロイドの使用や衰弱性疾患）、留置尿道カテーテル、既存の腎障害や尿路閉塞が素因となる。
treatment: Systemic antifungal therapy with amphotericin B (0.3–0.5 mg/kg IV slowly, every 48 hrs) combined with fluconazole (2–5 mg/kg PO q24h) for extended duration. Surgical nephrectomy is indicated for unilateral mycetoma or refractory infection. Discontinue predisposing antibiotics/corticosteroids and provide IV fluid support to maintain renal perfusion.
treatment_ja: アムホテリシンB（0.3～0.5 mg/kg、48時間ごとに緩徐に静注）とフルコナゾール（2～5 mg/kg、1日1回経口投与）による長期全身性抗真菌療法を実施する。片側性の真菌腫や難治性感染には外科的腎摘出術が適応となる。誘因となる抗菌薬やコルチコステロイドを中止し、腎灌流維持のため輸液療法を行う。

name: Renal Infection (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infection (pyelonephritis) in horses occurs when pathogenic bacteria ascend from the lower urinary tract or, less commonly, spread hematogenously to the renal parenchyma and collecting system. Bacterial colonization triggers an inflammatory response leading to neutrophilic infiltration, tubular damage, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue. Chronic infection can result in fibrosis, hydronephrosis, and eventual loss of renal function in the affected kidney.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、病原性細菌が下部尿路から上行性に、またはまれに血行性に腎実質および集合系に到達することで発生します。細菌の定着により好中球浸潤を伴う炎症反応が引き起こされ、尿細管の損傷、膿瘍形成、および腎組織の進行性破壊が生じます。慢性感染は線維化、水腎症、および罹患腎の機能喪失につながる可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infection from the lower urinary tract, most commonly by organisms such as Escherichia coli, Proteus spp., Klebsiella spp., and Streptococcus spp. Secondary contributing factors include urolithiasis, urinary tract obstruction, bladder paralysis or dysfunction (e.g., from equine herpesvirus-1 myeloencephalopathy), catheterization, and immunosuppression. Nephroliths and anatomical abnormalities may predispose to chronic or recurrent infection.
treatment: Initiate prolonged systemic antimicrobial therapy (4-6 weeks) based on urine culture and sensitivity, commonly trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole or enrofloxacin. Provide IV fluid therapy to maintain renal perfusion and urine flow. Address underlying causes such as urolithiasis or obstruction surgically if indicated, and monitor renal function via serial blood work and urinalysis.
treatment_ja: 尿培養および感受性試験に基づき、トリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾールやエンロフロキサシンなどの全身性抗菌薬を4～6週間長期投与する。腎灌流と尿流を維持するため静脈内輸液療法を実施する。尿路結石や閉塞などの基礎疾患がある場合は外科的に対処し、連続的な血液検査および尿検査により腎機能を継続的にモニタリングする。

name: Renal Inflammation (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal inflammation (nephritis) in horses involves immune-mediated or infectious processes that damage the glomeruli, tubules, or interstitium of the kidneys. Inflammatory infiltrates and edema compromise renal filtration, tubular reabsorption, and secretion, leading to progressive loss of renal function. Prolonged inflammation can result in fibrosis, nephron loss, and ultimately chronic renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎炎は、免疫介在性または感染性の過程により糸球体、尿細管、または間質が損傷される疾患です。炎症性浸潤や浮腫により腎濾過機能、尿細管の再吸収・分泌機能が低下し、腎機能が進行性に障害されます。長期の炎症は線維化やネフロンの喪失を引き起こし、最終的に慢性腎不全に至る可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include bacterial infections (e.g., Leptospira, Streptococcus), viral infections (e.g., equine infectious anemia), and immune-mediated glomerulonephritis. Secondary causes include nephrotoxic drugs (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides), systemic sepsis, endotoxemia, heavy metal exposure, and complications from conditions such as equine purpura hemorrhagica or chronic infectious diseases.
treatment: Aggressive IV fluid therapy (balanced polyionic solutions) to restore renal perfusion and promote diuresis. Discontinue all nephrotoxic agents (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides). Administer broad-spectrum antibiotics (penicillin, ceftiofur) for bacterial causes, and corticosteroids (dexamethasone) for immune-mediated nephritis. Electrolyte and acid-base imbalances should be corrected; supportive care includes dietary protein restriction and monitoring of serum creatinine and BUN.
treatment_ja: 腎灌流の回復と利尿促進のため、バランス電解質輸液による積極的な静脈内輸液療法を実施する。全ての腎毒性薬剤（NSAIDs、アミノグリコシド系）を中止する。細菌性原因にはペニシリンやセフチオフルなどの広域抗菌薬を、免疫介在性腎炎にはデキサメタゾンなどの副腎皮質ステロイドを投与する。電解質および酸塩基平衡の補正、食事中のタンパク質制限、血清クレアチニン・BUNのモニタリングを含む支持療法を行う。

name: Renal Neoplasia (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal neoplasia in horses involves abnormal proliferation of cells within the kidney parenchyma, collecting system, or surrounding tissues. The most common primary renal tumors include renal cell carcinoma, nephroblastoma, and lymphoma, which can cause progressive destruction of normal renal architecture, leading to impaired renal function, hematuria, and potential metastasis to lungs, liver, and lymph nodes. Space-occupying lesions may obstruct urine flow, compress adjacent structures, and induce paraneoplastic syndromes.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎腫瘍は、腎実質、集合系、または周囲組織における細胞の異常増殖を伴う。最も一般的な原発性腎腫瘍には腎細胞癌、腎芽腫、リンパ腫があり、正常な腎構造の進行性破壊を引き起こし、腎機能障害、血尿、および肺・肝臓・リンパ節への転移の可能性がある。腫瘤性病変は尿路を閉塞し、隣接構造を圧迫し、傍腫瘍症候群を誘発することがある。
causes: The exact etiology of renal neoplasia in horses is largely unknown, though genetic predisposition, chronic inflammation, and environmental carcinogen exposure may play a role. Renal cell carcinoma is the most frequently reported primary renal tumor in adult horses, while nephroblastoma is more common in younger horses. Secondary renal involvement can occur through metastasis from other primary tumors or multicentric lymphoma.
treatment: Unilateral nephrectomy is the primary treatment for localized renal tumors if the contralateral kidney is functional. Supportive care includes IV fluids, NSAIDs (flunixin meglumine 1.1 mg/kg IV) for pain, and monitoring renal parameters. Chemotherapy options are limited in horses; palliative care is indicated for metastatic disease.
treatment_ja: 対側腎が正常に機能している場合、限局性腎腫瘍に対しては片側腎摘出術が第一選択となる。支持療法として輸液療法、疼痛管理にフルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg 静脈内投与）などのNSAIDs投与、および腎機能パラメータのモニタリングを行う。馬における化学療法の選択肢は限られており、転移性疾患には緩和療法が適応となる。

name: Renal Metabolic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal metabolic disease in horses involves impaired kidney function leading to disrupted electrolyte balance, acid-base homeostasis, and waste product excretion. The kidneys fail to adequately regulate calcium, phosphorus, and bicarbonate metabolism, potentially resulting in hypercalcemia or hypocalcemia, metabolic acidosis or alkalosis, and azotemia. Chronic cases may lead to renal tubular dysfunction, nephrocalcinosis, and progressive nephron loss with secondary metabolic derangements including renal secondary hyperparathyroidism.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎代謝疾患は、腎機能の障害により電解質バランス、酸塩基平衡、および老廃物の排泄が乱れる疾患である。腎臓がカルシウム、リン、重炭酸塩の代謝を適切に調節できなくなり、高カルシウム血症または低カルシウム血症、代謝性アシドーシスまたはアルカローシス、高窒素血症を引き起こす可能性がある。慢性例では腎尿細管機能障害、腎石灰化症、進行性ネフロン喪失が生じ、二次性腎性上皮小体機能亢進症などの続発性代謝異常を伴う。
causes: Primary causes include chronic kidney disease, toxic nephropathy (from NSAIDs, aminoglycosides, heavy metals, or nephrotoxic plants such as oak or red maple), and hypercalcemic nephropathy. Secondary causes include dehydration, systemic infections, urolithiasis, obstructive uropathy, and prolonged electrolyte imbalances due to dietary excess or deficiency of calcium and phosphorus.
treatment: Administer IV crystalloid fluids (0.9% NaCl or lactated Ringer's) to correct dehydration and restore renal perfusion. Discontinue nephrotoxic agents (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides). Correct electrolyte imbalances with calcium gluconate or phosphate binders as needed, and manage acidosis with sodium bicarbonate supplementation. Monitor urine output and serum creatinine closely.
treatment_ja: 脱水補正と腎灌流回復のため、生理食塩水または乳酸リンゲル液の静脈内輸液を実施する。NSAIDsやアミノグリコシドなどの腎毒性薬剤を直ちに中止する。グルコン酸カルシウムやリン吸着剤で電解質異常を補正し、代謝性アシドーシスには重炭酸ナトリウムを投与する。尿量および血清クレアチニン値を継続的にモニタリングする。

name: Renal Nutritional Deficiency (Horse)
pathophysiology: Nutritional deficiencies, particularly of vitamin A, vitamin D, calcium, phosphorus, or oxalate-rich diets, can impair renal tubular function and lead to nephrocalcinosis or renal tubular degeneration in horses. Chronic imbalances in calcium-phosphorus ratio or excessive oxalate intake can cause calcium oxalate crystal deposition in renal tissue, resulting in progressive renal parenchymal damage. Vitamin A deficiency may lead to squamous metaplasia of renal tubular epithelium, while vitamin D excess or deficiency disrupts calcium homeostasis and contributes to renal mineralization.
pathophysiology_ja: ビタミンA、ビタミンD、カルシウム、リンなどの栄養欠乏やシュウ酸を多く含む飼料の摂取は、腎尿細管機能を障害し、腎石灰化症や腎尿細管変性を引き起こします。カルシウム・リン比の慢性的な不均衡やシュウ酸の過剰摂取は、腎組織にシュウ酸カルシウム結晶の沈着を引き起こし、進行性の腎実質障害をもたらします。ビタミンA欠乏は腎尿細管上皮の扁平上皮化生を引き起こし、ビタミンDの過不足はカルシウム恒常性を乱し腎石灰化に寄与します。
treatment: Correct dietary imbalances by adjusting calcium-phosphorus ratio to 2:1, supplement vitamin A (50,000-100,000 IU/day) and vitamin D as needed, and eliminate oxalate-rich forages. Provide IV fluid therapy with balanced electrolytes to support renal perfusion. Monitor serum calcium, phosphorus, and renal parameters; administer nephroprotective supportive care as indicated.
treatment_ja: カルシウムとリンの比率を2:1に調整し、ビタミンA（50,000〜100,000 IU/日）およびビタミンDを必要に応じて補給し、シュウ酸含有量の高い飼料を除去する。バランス電解質液による静脈内輸液療法で腎灌流を維持する。血清カルシウム・リン・腎機能パラメータを定期的にモニタリングし、腎保護的な支持療法を実施する。

name: Renal Genetic Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal genetic disorders in horses involve inherited mutations affecting renal tubular or glomerular structure and function, leading to progressive nephron loss, impaired filtration, and concentrating ability. Examples include renal dysplasia and polycystic kidney disease, where abnormal kidney development or cyst formation results in gradual replacement of functional parenchyma with fibrotic or cystic tissue. This leads to chronic renal failure with azotemia, electrolyte imbalances, and eventual end-stage kidney disease.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎遺伝性疾患は、腎尿細管や糸球体の構造・機能に影響を及ぼす遺伝子変異により、進行性のネフロン喪失、濾過機能障害、濃縮能低下を引き起こします。腎異形成や多発性嚢胞腎などがあり、腎臓の発達異常や嚢胞形成により機能的な実質が線維性または嚢胞性組織に置換されます。最終的に高窒素血症、電解質異常を伴う慢性腎不全へと進行します。
causes: The primary cause is inherited genetic mutations affecting renal development or function, which may follow autosomal recessive or dominant inheritance patterns depending on the specific disorder. Breed predispositions have been noted, and consanguineous breeding increases the risk of expression. Secondary factors such as infection, dehydration, or nephrotoxin exposure may accelerate progression of the underlying genetic defect.
treatment: No curative treatment exists for renal genetic disorders in horses. Management is supportive: IV fluid therapy to maintain hydration, dietary modification with reduced protein and phosphorus, ACE inhibitors (e.g., benazepril 0.5 mg/kg PO q24h) to manage proteinuria and glomerular hypertension, and phosphate binders (aluminum hydroxide) for hyperphosphatemia. Serial monitoring of BUN, creatinine, and electrolytes guides therapy adjustments.
treatment_ja: 馬の腎遺伝性疾患に根治療法は存在しません。治療は対症療法が中心で、輸液療法による水和維持、低タンパク・低リン食への食事管理、ACE阻害薬（例：ベナゼプリル0.5 mg/kg 経口 1日1回）による蛋白尿・糸球体高血圧の管理、高リン血症に対する水酸化アルミニウム等のリン吸着剤投与を行います。BUN、クレアチニン、電解質の定期的モニタリングにより治療を調整します。

name: Renal Autoimmune Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: The immune system produces autoantibodies or autoreactive T cells directed against renal antigens, leading to immune complex deposition in the glomeruli and/or tubulointerstitial tissues. This triggers complement activation, inflammatory cell infiltration, and progressive damage to the glomerular basement membrane and tubular structures, resulting in glomerulonephritis or tubulointerstitial nephritis. Chronic inflammation leads to fibrosis, impaired renal filtration, proteinuria, and eventual renal insufficiency.
pathophysiology_ja: 免疫系が腎臓の自己抗原に対する自己抗体または自己反応性T細胞を産生し、糸球体や尿細管間質組織に免疫複合体が沈着します。これにより補体の活性化、炎症細胞の浸潤、糸球体基底膜および尿細管構造の進行性損傷が引き起こされ、糸球体腎炎または尿細管間質性腎炎を生じます。慢性炎症は線維化、腎濾過機能の低下、蛋白尿、最終的には腎不全に至ります。
causes: The primary cause is immune dysregulation leading to loss of self-tolerance against renal antigens, potentially triggered by chronic infections (e.g., Streptococcus equi, equine infectious anemia), drug reactions, or systemic autoimmune conditions. Secondary causes include immune complex deposition from persistent antigenic stimulation, molecular mimicry between infectious agents and renal epitopes, and genetic predisposition to autoimmune responses.
treatment: Initiate immunosuppressive therapy with corticosteroids (dexamethasone 0.05-0.1 mg/kg IV daily, tapering over weeks) combined with azathioprine (3 mg/kg PO daily) to suppress autoantibody production and inflammatory cascades. Provide supportive care including IV fluid therapy to maintain renal perfusion, ACE inhibitors (benazepril 0.5 mg/kg PO daily) to reduce proteinuria, and manage secondary complications such as edema and hypertension. Monitor renal function via serial serum creatinine, BUN, and urine protein-to-creatinine ratio.
treatment_ja: 副腎皮質ステロイド（デキサメタゾン0.05〜0.1 mg/kg IV、漸減投与）とアザチオプリン（3 mg/kg PO 1日1回）による免疫抑制療法を開始し、自己抗体産生および炎症カスケードを抑制する。腎灌流維持のための輸液療法、蛋白尿軽減のためのACE阻害薬（ベナゼプリル0.5 mg/kg PO 1日1回）を含む支持療法を実施し、浮腫や高血圧などの二次的合併症を管理する。血清クレアチニン、BUN、尿蛋白/クレアチニン比を定期的にモニタリングし腎機能を評価する。

name: Renal Degenerative Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal degenerative disease in horses involves progressive deterioration of nephron structure and function, including tubular degeneration, interstitial fibrosis, and glomerulosclerosis. This leads to impaired glomerular filtration, loss of concentrating ability, and accumulation of metabolic waste products (azotemia). Chronic progressive nephropathy ultimately results in end-stage renal failure with irreversible loss of functional renal tissue.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎変性疾患は、尿細管変性、間質線維化、糸球体硬化症を含むネフロン構造と機能の進行性劣化を伴います。これにより糸球体濾過率の低下、濃縮能の喪失、代謝老廃物の蓄積（高窒素血症）が生じます。慢性進行性腎症は最終的に機能的腎組織の不可逆的喪失を伴う末期腎不全に至ります。
causes: Primary causes include chronic exposure to nephrotoxins (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals, vitamin D toxicosis), oxalate-containing plants, and pigment nephropathy from myoglobinuria or hemoglobinuria. Secondary causes include chronic renal ischemia, recurrent pyelonephritis, immune-mediated glomerulonephritis, and age-related degenerative changes. Hypercalcemia and prolonged dehydration can also contribute to progressive renal degeneration.
treatment: Remove nephrotoxic agents immediately. Provide IV fluid therapy (polyionic isotonic solutions) to correct dehydration and support renal perfusion. Manage azotemia with dietary protein restriction, correct electrolyte imbalances (calcium, phosphorus), and administer ACE inhibitors (benazepril) to reduce glomerular hypertension. Treat secondary complications such as gastric ulceration with omeprazole and anemia with erythropoietin if indicated.
treatment_ja: 腎毒性物質を直ちに除去する。脱水補正と腎灌流維持のために等張性電解質輸液を静脈内投与する。高窒素血症には食事中タンパク質制限を行い、電解質異常（カルシウム・リン）を是正し、糸球体内高血圧軽減のためACE阻害薬（ベナゼプリル）を投与する。続発する胃潰瘍にはオメプラゾール、貧血にはエリスロポエチンの投与を必要に応じて検討する。

name: Renal Traumatic Injury (Horse)
pathophysiology: Blunt or penetrating trauma to the lumbar region causes direct damage to the renal parenchyma, capsule, or vasculature. This leads to hemorrhage (subcapsular or perirenal hematoma), disruption of renal tubules and collecting system, and potential urine leakage (uroperitoneum or retroperitoneal urine accumulation). Secondary inflammation, ischemia, and possible infection may further compromise renal function.
pathophysiology_ja: 腰部への鈍的または穿通性外傷により、腎実質・被膜・血管系に直接的な損傷が生じる。これにより出血（被膜下血腫または腎周囲血腫）、腎尿細管や集合系の断裂、尿漏出（尿腹症または後腹膜腔への尿貯留）が起こる。二次的な炎症、虚血、感染がさらに腎機能を悪化させる可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include blunt abdominal or lumbar trauma from kicks by other horses, falls, collisions with fixed objects, or crush injuries. Secondary causes include penetrating wounds (e.g., impalement, surgical complications) and iatrogenic injury during percutaneous renal biopsy. Severe exertion or violent casting for procedures may also rarely contribute to renal trauma.
causes_ja: 主な原因は、他馬からの蹴り、転倒、固定物への衝突、圧挫傷による腹部・腰部への鈍的外傷である。二次的原因として穿通創（杭刺創、手術合併症）や経皮的腎生検時の医原性損傷がある。激しい運動や保定時の暴れも稀に腎外傷の原因となりうる。
treatment: Initial stabilization with IV crystalloid fluids (LRS or 0.9% NaCl) and blood transfusion if severe hemorrhage occurs. Administer flunixin meglumine (1.1 mg/kg IV q12h) for analgesia and anti-inflammatory effect, and broad-spectrum antimicrobials (e.g., gentamicin 6.6 mg/kg IV q24h plus penicillin 22,000 IU/kg IV q6h) to prevent secondary infection. Mild cases are managed conservatively with stall rest and serial ultrasonographic monitoring; severe renal pedicle avulsion or uncontrollable hemorrhage may require nephrectomy.
treatment_ja: 初期安定化として乳酸リンゲル液や生理食塩水の静脈内輸液を行い、重度出血時には輸血を実施する。フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg 静注 12時間毎）で鎮痛・抗炎症を図り、ゲンタマイシン（6.6 mg/kg 静注 24時間毎）およびペニシリン（22,000 IU/kg 静注 6時間毎）等の広域抗菌薬で二次感染を予防する。軽度例は馬房安静と超音波検査による経過観察で保存的に管理し、腎茎断裂や止血困難な重度例では腎摘出術を検討する。

name: Renal Behavioral Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal behavioral disorder in horses involves abnormal behaviors (such as excessive flank watching, stretching, frequent posturing to urinate, or irritability) associated with renal pain or dysfunction. Chronic renal inflammation, nephrolithiasis, or subclinical renal disease can stimulate visceral pain pathways, leading to altered behavior patterns. The discomfort originating from the kidneys or ureters manifests as behavioral changes rather than overt clinical signs of renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎行動障害は、腎臓の痛みや機能障害に関連した異常行動（過度な脇腹注視、伸展姿勢、頻繁な排尿姿勢、易刺激性など）を伴います。慢性腎炎症、腎結石症、または無症候性の腎疾患が内臓痛経路を刺激し、行動パターンの変化を引き起こします。腎臓や尿管からの不快感が、明確な腎不全の臨床症状ではなく行動変化として現れます。
causes: Primary causes include nephrolithiasis, pyelonephritis, renal cysts, or renal neoplasia causing visceral discomfort. Secondary causes may involve chronic urinary tract infections, ureteral obstruction, or referred pain from adjacent structures. Toxic nephropathy from NSAID overuse or ingestion of nephrotoxic plants can also contribute to renal discomfort and associated behavioral changes.
treatment: Address underlying cause: surgical removal of nephroliths if present, antibiotics (trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 30 mg/kg PO BID) for pyelonephritis, and discontinue nephrotoxic drugs. Manage renal pain with flunixin meglumine (1.1 mg/kg IV) short-term and butorphanol (0.02-0.04 mg/kg IV) for visceral analgesia. Provide IV fluid therapy to support renal perfusion and correct electrolyte imbalances.
treatment_ja: 原因疾患の治療を優先し、腎結石があれば外科的除去、腎盂腎炎にはトリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾール（30 mg/kg 経口 1日2回）を投与し、腎毒性薬剤を中止する。疼痛管理としてフルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg 静注）を短期使用し、ブトルファノール（0.02-0.04 mg/kg 静注）で内臓痛を緩和する。輸液療法で腎灌流を維持し電解質異常を補正する。

name: Renal Infectious Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infectious disease in horses involves bacterial colonization of the renal parenchyma, typically via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract or hematogenous spread. Bacteria such as Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., and Actinobacillus spp. cause inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue, leading to impaired glomerular filtration and tubular function. If untreated, this can progress to pyelonephritis, septicemia, or chronic renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症は、下部尿路からの上行感染または血行性播種により細菌が腎実質に定着することで発生する。大腸菌、連鎖球菌、アクチノバチルス属などの細菌が炎症、膿瘍形成、腎組織の進行性破壊を引き起こし、糸球体濾過および尿細管機能の障害をもたらす。未治療の場合、腎盂腎炎、敗血症、または慢性腎不全に進行する可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infections (most commonly E. coli, Streptococcus spp., Corynebacterium spp.) from the lower urinary tract, and hematogenous spread from distant infection sites. Secondary causes include urolithiasis, urinary tract obstruction, immunosuppression, bladder dysfunction, and catheterization-related contamination that predispose to bacterial colonization of the kidneys.
treatment: Initiate aggressive antimicrobial therapy based on urine culture and sensitivity; empirical treatment with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (30 mg/kg PO BID) or enrofloxacin (5 mg/kg IV/PO SID) pending results. Provide IV fluid therapy to maintain renal perfusion and correct dehydration. Address underlying causes such as urolithiasis or obstruction surgically if indicated, and provide NSAIDs (flunixin meglumine 1.1 mg/kg IV) for analgesia and anti-inflammatory support.
treatment_ja: 尿培養・感受性試験に基づき積極的な抗菌薬療法を開始する。結果判明までトリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾール（30 mg/kg 経口 BID）またはエンロフロキサシン（5 mg/kg 静注/経口 SID）を経験的に投与する。輸液療法により腎灌流の維持と脱水の補正を行う。尿路結石や閉塞などの基礎疾患がある場合は外科的に対処し、フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg 静注）で鎮痛および抗炎症療法を実施する。

name: Renal Parasitic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal parasitic disease in horses involves migration and colonization of parasites such as Halicephalobus gingivalis (Halicephalobus deletrix), Strongylus vulgaris larvae, or Dioctophyme renale within the renal parenchyma or vasculature. Parasitic invasion leads to granulomatous nephritis, tubular destruction, interstitial fibrosis, and compromised renal function. Larval migration through renal arteries can also cause thrombosis, ischemic damage, and secondary bacterial infection of renal tissue.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎寄生虫症は、Halicephalobus gingivalis、普通円虫（Strongylus vulgaris）の幼虫、または腎虫（Dioctophyme renale）などの寄生虫が腎実質や血管系に移行・寄生することで生じます。寄生虫の侵入により肉芽腫性腎炎、尿細管の破壊、間質性線維化が起こり、腎機能が障害されます。幼虫の腎動脈内移行は血栓症、虚血性障害、および二次的な細菌感染を引き起こすこともあります。
causes: Primary causes include parasitic infection by Halicephalobus gingivalis (a free-living nematode with opportunistic tissue invasion), migrating Strongylus vulgaris larvae through mesenteric and renal vasculature, and rarely Dioctophyme renale (giant kidney worm). Secondary causes include immunosuppression, poor sanitation, and exposure to contaminated soil or water facilitating parasitic entry.
treatment: Administer high-dose fenbendazole (10 mg/kg PO daily for 5 days) or ivermectin (0.2 mg/kg PO) targeting migrating larvae; combine with anti-inflammatory therapy (flunixin meglumine 1.1 mg/kg IV) for granulomatous nephritis. Nephrectomy may be indicated for unilateral severe destruction by Dioctophyme renale. Supportive care includes IV fluid therapy and monitoring renal function.
treatment_ja: 移行幼虫を標的としてフェンベンダゾール（10 mg/kg 経口、5日間連日投与）またはイベルメクチン（0.2 mg/kg 経口）を投与し、肉芽腫性腎炎に対しフルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg 静注）による抗炎症療法を併用する。Dioctophyme renaleによる片側性の重度腎破壊には腎摘出術が適応となる。補液療法および腎機能モニタリングによる支持療法を実施する。

name: Renal Viral Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Viral agents such as equine herpesvirus (EHV) or equine arteritis virus (EAV) can cause systemic infection with secondary renal involvement, leading to immune-mediated glomerulonephritis, vasculitis of renal vessels, and tubular necrosis. Viral replication within renal endothelial cells and immune complex deposition in glomeruli impair filtration and tubular function, resulting in progressive renal dysfunction. Inflammatory infiltrates and edema further compromise renal blood flow and parenchymal integrity.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬ヘルペスウイルス（EHV）や馬動脈炎ウイルス（EAV）などのウイルスが全身感染を引き起こし、免疫介在性糸球体腎炎、腎血管の血管炎、尿細管壊死を通じて二次的に腎臓を障害する。腎内皮細胞でのウイルス増殖と糸球体への免疫複合体沈着により、濾過機能および尿細管機能が低下し、進行性の腎機能障害を引き起こす。炎症性浸潤と浮腫がさらに腎血流と実質の健全性を損なう。
causes: Primary causes include equine herpesvirus (EHV-1, EHV-4), equine arteritis virus (EAV), and potentially other systemic viral infections that have tropism for renal vasculature and parenchyma. Secondary causes include immune complex deposition, systemic vasculitis, and hemodynamic compromise associated with viral septicemia. Predisposing factors include immunosuppression, stress, and concurrent infections.
treatment: No specific antiviral cure exists; supportive care includes IV fluid therapy to maintain renal perfusion, NSAIDs (flunixin meglumine 1.1 mg/kg IV) for inflammation control, and corticosteroids if immune-mediated glomerulonephritis is confirmed. Antiviral agents such as valacyclovir (30 mg/kg PO BID) may be considered for EHV-1 cases. Monitor renal values and electrolytes closely.
treatment_ja: 特異的な抗ウイルス療法は存在せず、支持療法が中心となる。腎灌流維持のための輸液療法、フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg IV）による抗炎症治療、免疫介在性糸球体腎炎が確認された場合はコルチコステロイドを使用する。EHV-1症例にはバラシクロビル（30 mg/kg 経口 BID）の投与を検討する。腎機能値および電解質を厳密にモニタリングする。

name: Renal Bacterial Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Bacterial infection of the kidneys (pyelonephritis) in horses typically occurs via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract, or less commonly through hematogenous spread. Bacteria colonize the renal pelvis and parenchyma, causing inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue. Common causative organisms include Escherichia coli, Actinobacillus equuli, Streptococcus spp., and Corynebacterium spp., leading to impaired renal function if left untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎臓細菌感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路からの上行性感染、またはまれに血行性播種によって発生します。細菌が腎盂および腎実質に定着し、炎症、膿瘍形成、腎組織の進行性破壊を引き起こします。主な原因菌には大腸菌、Actinobacillus equuli、レンサ球菌、コリネバクテリウムなどがあり、未治療の場合は腎機能障害に至ります。
causes: Primary causes include ascending urinary tract infections, urolithiasis causing urinary stasis, and hematogenous bacterial spread from distant infection sites. Secondary causes and predisposing factors include immunosuppression, urinary catheterization, bladder paralysis, anatomical abnormalities, and conditions causing urine retention or reflux.
treatment: Initiate prolonged systemic antibiotic therapy (4-6 weeks minimum) based on urine culture and sensitivity, commonly trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole or enrofloxacin. Provide IV fluid therapy to maintain renal perfusion and correct electrolyte imbalances. Address underlying causes such as urolithiasis removal or catheter management, and monitor renal function via serial bloodwork and urinalysis.
treatment_ja: 尿培養および感受性試験に基づき、トリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾールやエンロフロキサシン等の全身性抗菌薬を最低4〜6週間投与する。腎灌流維持と電解質補正のため輸液療法を実施する。尿路結石の除去やカテーテル管理など根本原因に対処し、血液検査および尿検査で腎機能を定期的にモニタリングする。

name: Renal Fungal Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Fungal organisms, most commonly Aspergillus spp. or Candida spp., colonize the renal parenchyma and/or renal pelvis, leading to granulomatous or necrotizing inflammation. The infection disrupts normal renal architecture, potentially causing tubular obstruction, progressive nephritis, and impaired renal function. Hematogenous spread or ascending urinary tract infection allows fungal invasion, particularly in immunocompromised or chronically debilitated horses.
pathophysiology_ja: 主にAspergillus属やCandida属などの真菌が腎実質や腎盂に定着し、肉芽腫性または壊死性の炎症を引き起こします。感染により正常な腎構造が破壊され、尿細管閉塞、進行性腎炎、腎機能障害を生じる可能性があります。血行性播種または上行性尿路感染により、特に免疫抑制状態や慢性衰弱馬において真菌の侵入が起こります。
causes: Primary causes include opportunistic fungal infection by Aspergillus spp., Candida spp., or other fungi colonizing the urinary tract or reaching the kidneys hematogenously. Secondary causes and predisposing factors include prolonged antibiotic therapy, immunosuppression, chronic illness, indwelling urinary catheters, and concurrent systemic disease that compromise host defenses.
causes_ja: 主な原因はAspergillus属、Candida属などの日和見真菌による尿路または血行性の腎感染です。二次的原因および素因として、長期抗菌薬投与、免疫抑制、慢性疾患、留置尿道カテーテル、宿主防御能を低下させる併発全身疾患などが挙げられます。
treatment: Administer systemic antifungal therapy such as fluconazole (5 mg/kg PO q24h) or voriconazole for Aspergillus spp., or fluconazole/amphotericin B for Candida spp. infections. Discontinue predisposing antibiotics and immunosuppressants where possible. Provide IV fluid support to maintain renal perfusion; consider nephrectomy if unilateral disease is severe and unresponsive to medical therapy.
treatment_ja: アスペルギルス属にはフルコナゾール（5 mg/kg 経口 1日1回）またはボリコナゾール、カンジダ属にはフルコナゾールまたはアムホテリシンBによる全身性抗真菌療法を実施する。誘因となる抗菌薬や免疫抑制剤は可能な限り中止する。腎灌流維持のため輸液療法を行い、片側性で内科治療に反応しない重症例では腎摘出術を検討する。

name: Renal Infection (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infection (pyelonephritis) in horses typically results from ascending bacterial infection via the ureters from the lower urinary tract, or less commonly from hematogenous spread. Bacteria colonize the renal pelvis and parenchyma, causing inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue. Chronic infection can lead to fibrosis, impaired renal function, and potentially septicemia if left untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路から尿管を介した上行性細菌感染、またはまれに血行性播種によって生じます。細菌が腎盂および腎実質に定着し、炎症、膿瘍形成、腎組織の進行性破壊を引き起こします。慢性感染は線維化、腎機能障害、さらに未治療の場合は敗血症に至る可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infections, most commonly by Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Corynebacterium renale, and Actinobacillus equuli. Secondary causes include urolithiasis, urinary tract obstruction, catheterization, immunosuppression, and pre-existing lower urinary tract infections. Mares may be more predisposed due to their shorter urethra facilitating bacterial ascent.
treatment: Initiate prolonged systemic antibiotic therapy (4-6 weeks) based on urine culture and sensitivity, commonly trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole or enrofloxacin. Provide IV fluid therapy to maintain renal perfusion and promote diuresis. Address underlying causes such as urolithiasis or obstruction surgically if present, and monitor renal function via serial bloodwork and urinalysis.
treatment_ja: 尿培養・感受性試験に基づき、トリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾールやエンロフロキサシン等の全身性抗菌薬を4〜6週間長期投与する。静脈内輸液療法で腎灌流を維持し利尿を促進する。尿路結石や閉塞などの基礎疾患がある場合は外科的に対処し、血液検査および尿検査で腎機能を継続的にモニタリングする。

name: Renal Inflammation (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal inflammation (nephritis) in horses involves immune-mediated or infectious damage to the glomeruli, tubules, or interstitium of the kidneys, leading to impaired filtration, tubular dysfunction, and potential progression to fibrosis. Inflammatory cell infiltration and edema compromise renal blood flow and glomerular filtration rate, resulting in azotemia, electrolyte imbalances, and impaired waste excretion. Chronic inflammation may lead to irreversible nephron loss and progressive renal insufficiency.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎炎（腎臓の炎症）は、免疫介在性または感染性の障害により糸球体、尿細管、または間質が損傷を受け、濾過機能障害や尿細管機能不全を引き起こし、線維化へ進行する可能性がある。炎症細胞の浸潤や浮腫により腎血流量や糸球体濾過率が低下し、高窒素血症、電解質異常、老廃物排泄障害が生じる。慢性炎症はネフロンの不可逆的喪失と進行性腎不全につながることがある。
causes: Primary causes include bacterial infections (e.g., Leptospira spp., Streptococcus equi), viral infections (e.g., equine infectious anemia), and immune-mediated glomerulonephritis. Secondary causes include nephrotoxic drugs (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides), prolonged dehydration, systemic sepsis, heavy metal exposure, and extension of lower urinary tract infections. Immune complex deposition from chronic infections such as Streptococcus equi (purpura hemorrhagica) can also trigger renal inflammation.
treatment: Treat underlying cause with appropriate antibiotics (e.g., penicillin for Streptococcus equi, oxytetracycline for Leptospira). Discontinue nephrotoxic drugs (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides) immediately. Provide aggressive IV fluid therapy (lactated Ringer's solution) to restore renal perfusion, and administer corticosteroids (dexamethasone) for immune-mediated nephritis.
treatment_ja: 原因に応じた抗菌薬投与（例：Streptococcus equiにはペニシリン、レプトスピラにはオキシテトラサイクリン）を実施する。腎毒性薬剤（NSAIDs、アミノグリコシド系）は直ちに中止する。乳酸リンゲル液による積極的な静脈内輸液療法で腎灌流を回復させ、免疫介在性腎炎にはデキサメタゾン等の副腎皮質ステロイドを投与する。

name: Renal Neoplasia (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal neoplasia in horses involves the abnormal proliferation of cells within the kidney, most commonly renal cell carcinoma, lymphoma, or nephroblastoma. The tumor mass disrupts normal renal architecture, impairing filtration, concentrating ability, and endocrine functions of the kidney. Locally invasive tumors may compress adjacent structures, obstruct the ureter, and metastasize to the lungs, liver, lymph nodes, and other organs via hematogenous or lymphatic routes.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎臓腫瘍は、腎細胞癌、リンパ腫、腎芽腫などが最も多く、腎臓内の細胞が異常に増殖する疾患である。腫瘍塊は正常な腎構造を破壊し、濾過能力、濃縮能力、および内分泌機能を障害する。局所浸潤性の腫瘍は隣接臓器を圧迫し、尿管を閉塞させ、血行性またはリンパ行性に肺、肝臓、リンパ節などへ転移する可能性がある。
causes: The exact etiology of renal neoplasia in horses is largely unknown; no specific genetic, environmental, or infectious causes have been consistently identified. Renal cell carcinoma is the most commonly reported primary renal tumor, while lymphoma may affect the kidneys as part of multicentric disease. Nephroblastoma is occasionally seen in younger horses and may have a developmental or embryonal origin.
treatment: Unilateral nephrectomy is the primary treatment for localized renal tumors such as renal cell carcinoma or nephroblastoma, provided the contralateral kidney is functional. For renal lymphoma, systemic chemotherapy (e.g., corticosteroids, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin) may be attempted. Supportive care includes IV fluid therapy, analgesics (flunixin meglumine), and monitoring renal function.
treatment_ja: 腎細胞癌や腎芽腫などの限局性腎腫瘍には、対側腎の機能が正常であることを確認した上で患側腎摘出術が第一選択となる。腎リンパ腫に対しては、副腎皮質ステロイド、シクロホスファミド、ドキソルビシン等による全身化学療法が試みられる。支持療法として輸液療法、鎮痛薬（フルニキシンメグルミン）の投与、および腎機能のモニタリングを行う。

name: Renal Metabolic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal metabolic disease in horses involves disruption of the kidney's ability to regulate electrolyte balance, acid-base homeostasis, and waste product excretion. Impaired renal tubular function leads to abnormal handling of calcium, phosphorus, and bicarbonate, potentially resulting in metabolic acidosis or alkalosis, hypercalcemia or hypocalcemia, and azotemia. Chronic dysfunction can lead to renal tubular acidosis, nephrocalcinosis, and progressive renal insufficiency.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎代謝疾患は、腎臓の電解質バランス、酸塩基平衡、老廃物排泄の調節機能が障害される疾患である。腎尿細管機能の障害により、カルシウム、リン、重炭酸塩の異常な処理が生じ、代謝性アシドーシスまたはアルカローシス、高カルシウム血症または低カルシウム血症、高窒素血症を引き起こす。慢性的な機能障害は腎尿細管性アシドーシス、腎石灰化症、進行性腎不全に至ることがある。
causes: Primary causes include excessive dietary calcium or oxalate-containing plants (such as tropical grasses), vitamin D toxicosis, and primary hyperparathyroidism. Secondary causes include chronic kidney disease, prolonged NSAID use, aminoglycoside nephrotoxicity, dehydration, and nutritional secondary hyperparathyroidism due to high phosphorus/low calcium diets. Heavy metal exposure and systemic conditions such as sepsis can also contribute to renal metabolic dysfunction.
treatment: Correct underlying cause by removing offending dietary sources (oxalate-rich plants, excess calcium) and discontinuing nephrotoxic drugs (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides). Administer IV balanced crystalloid fluids to restore hydration and electrolyte balance; correct metabolic acidosis with sodium bicarbonate as needed. Provide phosphate binders if hyperphosphatemia is present and supplement vitamin D or calcium cautiously based on bloodwork.
treatment_ja: 原因の除去として、シュウ酸含有植物や過剰カルシウムの摂取を中止し、腎毒性薬剤（NSAIDs、アミノグリコシド系）を中断する。バランス晶質液の静脈内投与により脱水・電解質異常を補正し、代謝性アシドーシスには必要に応じて重炭酸ナトリウムを投与する。高リン血症にはリン吸着剤を使用し、血液検査結果に基づきビタミンDやカルシウムを慎重に補充する。

name: Renal Nutritional Deficiency (Horse)
pathophysiology: Nutritional deficiencies, particularly of vitamin A, vitamin D, calcium, or phosphorus, lead to impaired renal tubular function and structural damage in horses. Chronic imbalances in calcium-phosphorus ratios or oxalate-rich diets can cause calcium deposition in renal tissues (nephrocalcinosis), tubular degeneration, and progressive loss of renal function. Secondary hyperparathyroidism may develop, further exacerbating mineral imbalances and contributing to renal parenchymal damage.
pathophysiology_ja: ビタミンA、ビタミンD、カルシウム、リンなどの栄養素の欠乏により、馬の腎尿細管機能障害および構造的損傷が生じる。カルシウム・リン比の慢性的な不均衡やシュウ酸含有量の多い飼料は、腎組織へのカルシウム沈着（腎石灰化症）、尿細管変性、進行性の腎機能低下を引き起こす。二次性副甲状腺機能亢進症が発症し、ミネラル不均衡と腎実質障害をさらに悪化させることがある。
causes: Primary causes include prolonged dietary deficiency of vitamin A, vitamin D, calcium, or phosphorus, as well as excessive intake of oxalate-containing plants (e.g., tropical grasses) that bind calcium. Secondary causes include imbalanced calcium-to-phosphorus ratios in feed, chronic high-grain/low-forage diets, and inadequate access to mineral supplements or clean water.
treatment: Correct dietary imbalances by adjusting calcium-to-phosphorus ratio (ideally 1.5-2:1), supplementing vitamin A (50,000-100,000 IU/day) and vitamin D (6,000-10,000 IU/day) as needed. Remove oxalate-rich forages and provide quality grass hay and balanced mineral supplementation. Administer IV fluid therapy with calcium gluconate for acute hypocalcemia; monitor renal function via serum creatinine and urinalysis.
treatment_ja: カルシウムとリンの比率を適正値（1.5〜2:1）に調整し、必要に応じてビタミンA（50,000〜100,000 IU/日）およびビタミンD（6,000〜10,000 IU/日）を補給する。シュウ酸を多く含む飼料を除去し、良質な乾草とバランスの取れたミネラル補給を行う。急性低カルシウム血症にはグルコン酸カルシウムの静脈内輸液を実施し、血清クレアチニンおよび尿検査で腎機能を継続的にモニタリングする。

name: Renal Genetic Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal genetic disorders in horses involve inherited mutations affecting renal tubular or glomerular structure and function, leading to progressive nephron loss, impaired filtration, and compromised electrolyte and fluid homeostasis. Specific conditions include renal dysplasia, polycystic kidney disease, and renal tubular acidosis, where abnormal kidney development or cystic degeneration results in progressive renal insufficiency. Accumulation of metabolic waste products and disruption of acid-base balance ultimately lead to chronic kidney failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎遺伝性疾患は、腎尿細管または糸球体の構造と機能に影響を与える遺伝子変異に起因し、進行性のネフロン喪失、濾過障害、電解質および体液恒常性の破綻を引き起こす。腎異形成、多発性嚢胞腎、腎尿細管性アシドーシスなどの特定の疾患では、異常な腎発達または嚢胞性変性が進行性腎不全をもたらす。代謝老廃物の蓄積と酸塩基平衡の乱れが最終的に慢性腎不全に至る。
causes: Primary causes are inherited genetic mutations, often autosomal recessive or dominant, affecting genes responsible for normal renal development, tubular transport proteins, or structural components of the nephron. Secondary factors such as dehydration, nephrotoxic exposure, or concurrent infections can accelerate the progression of underlying genetic renal dysfunction. Breed predisposition has been noted in certain horse breeds, suggesting a heritable component.
treatment: No curative therapy exists; management is supportive. Provide IV fluid therapy (balanced polyionic solutions) to maintain hydration, correct electrolyte imbalances (calcium, phosphorus, potassium supplementation as needed), and manage azotemia with dietary protein restriction. Administer ACE inhibitors (e.g., enalapril 0.5 mg/kg PO q24h) to reduce glomerular hypertension, phosphate binders (aluminum hydroxide) for hyperphosphatemia, and erythropoietin if anemia develops. Monitor renal values serially and manage secondary infections promptly.
treatment_ja: 根治療法は存在せず、支持療法が中心となる。静脈内輸液療法（バランス電解質液）で水和を維持し、電解質異常（カルシウム、リン、カリウム）を補正し、低タンパク食で高窒素血症を管理する。ACE阻害薬（エナラプリル0.5 mg/kg 経口 1日1回）で糸球体高血圧を軽減し、高リン血症には水酸化アルミニウムを、貧血にはエリスロポエチンを投与する。腎機能値を定期的にモニタリングし、二次感染には迅速に対処する。

name: Renal Autoimmune Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: The immune system produces autoantibodies or autoreactive lymphocytes directed against renal antigens, leading to immune complex deposition in the glomeruli and/or tubulointerstitial regions. This triggers complement activation, inflammatory cell infiltration, and progressive glomerulonephritis or tubulointerstitial nephritis, resulting in impaired renal function. Chronic immune-mediated damage leads to fibrosis, nephron loss, and eventual renal insufficiency.
pathophysiology_ja: 免疫系が腎臓の抗原に対する自己抗体または自己反応性リンパ球を産生し、糸球体や尿細管間質領域に免疫複合体が沈着します。これにより補体活性化、炎症細胞浸潤、進行性の糸球体腎炎または尿細管間質性腎炎が引き起こされ、腎機能障害に至ります。慢性的な免疫介在性損傷は線維化、ネフロン喪失、最終的な腎不全へと進行します。
causes: Primary causes include idiopathic autoimmune responses against glomerular basement membrane or tubular antigens, possibly triggered by molecular mimicry following infectious diseases such as Streptococcus equi or equine infectious anemia. Secondary causes may include chronic infections, drug reactions, neoplasia, or systemic autoimmune conditions that lead to immune complex formation and renal deposition. Genetic predisposition and environmental factors may also play a role.
treatment: Initiate immunosuppressive therapy with corticosteroids (dexamethasone 0.05-0.1 mg/kg IV initially, then oral prednisolone tapering over weeks) combined with azathioprine (3 mg/kg PO q24h) to suppress autoantibody production. Provide supportive care including IV fluid therapy, ACE inhibitors (benazepril 0.5 mg/kg PO q24h) to reduce proteinuria, and dietary protein management. Monitor renal values and adjust therapy based on response.
treatment_ja: 副腎皮質ステロイド（デキサメタゾン0.05-0.1 mg/kg IV、その後経口プレドニゾロンを漸減）とアザチオプリン（3 mg/kg PO 1日1回）による免疫抑制療法を開始し、自己抗体産生を抑制する。輸液療法、ACE阻害薬（ベナゼプリル0.5 mg/kg PO 1日1回）による蛋白尿軽減、食事中の蛋白質管理などの支持療法を実施する。腎機能値を定期的にモニタリングし、治療反応に応じて投薬を調整する。

name: Renal Degenerative Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal degenerative disease in horses involves progressive deterioration of renal parenchyma, including tubular degeneration, interstitial fibrosis, and glomerulosclerosis, leading to impaired filtration, reabsorption, and excretion functions. Chronic nephron loss results in compensatory hyperfiltration of remaining nephrons, which eventually accelerates further damage. End-stage disease manifests as chronic renal failure with azotemia, electrolyte imbalances, and uremia.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎変性疾患は、尿細管変性、間質線維化、糸球体硬化症を含む腎実質の進行性劣化を伴い、濾過・再吸収・排泄機能の障害を引き起こす。慢性的なネフロン喪失により残存ネフロンの代償性過剰濾過が生じ、さらなる損傷が加速される。末期には高窒素血症、電解質異常、尿毒症を伴う慢性腎不全として発現する。
causes: Primary causes include chronic exposure to nephrotoxins such as aminoglycoside antibiotics, NSAIDs, heavy metals, and toxic plants (e.g., oak, red maple). Secondary causes include chronic dehydration, recurrent episodes of acute kidney injury, systemic infections, immune-mediated glomerulonephritis, and age-related degenerative changes. Hemodynamic insults from prolonged hypotension or severe colic episodes may also contribute.
treatment: Discontinue all nephrotoxic agents (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides). Provide aggressive IV fluid therapy (polyionic isotonic solutions) to maintain hydration and support renal perfusion. Manage electrolyte imbalances (calcium, phosphorus) and azotemia with dietary protein restriction; administer ACE inhibitors (e.g., benazepril) to reduce glomerular hyperfiltration and slow disease progression.
treatment_ja: 全ての腎毒性薬剤（NSAIDs、アミノグリコシド系抗菌薬）を直ちに中止する。積極的な静脈内輸液療法（等張多電解質液）により水和を維持し腎灌流を支持する。電解質異常（カルシウム、リン）および高窒素血症に対しては食事中の蛋白質制限を行い、ACE阻害薬（例：ベナゼプリル）を投与して糸球体過剰濾過を軽減し、疾患の進行を遅延させる。

name: Renal Traumatic Injury (Horse)
pathophysiology: Blunt or penetrating trauma to the flank or dorsal abdomen causes direct injury to the renal parenchyma, capsule, or vascular pedicle. This leads to hemorrhage (subcapsular, perirenal, or intra-abdominal), potential urine leakage (uroperitoneum), parenchymal contusion or laceration, and subsequent inflammation. Severe cases may result in renal ischemia, nephron loss, and secondary complications such as peritonitis or hemorrhagic shock.
pathophysiology_ja: 側腹部や背側腹部への鈍的または穿通性外傷により、腎実質、腎被膜、または腎血管茎に直接的な損傷が生じる。これにより出血（被膜下、腎周囲、または腹腔内）、尿漏出（尿腹症）、実質の挫傷や裂傷、および続発する炎症が引き起こされる。重症例では腎虚血、ネフロンの喪失、腹膜炎や出血性ショックなどの二次合併症に至ることがある。
causes: Primary causes include blunt abdominal trauma from kicks by other horses, falls (especially during jumping or racing), collisions with fixed objects, or crush injuries. Secondary causes include penetrating wounds from sharp objects, iatrogenic injury during percutaneous procedures (e.g., renal biopsy), and rarely, fractures of the last ribs causing direct renal laceration.
treatment: Stabilize with IV crystalloid fluids (LRS or 0.9% NaCl) and control hemorrhage; administer flunixin meglumine (1.1 mg/kg IV q12h) for pain and anti-endotoxic effects. Monitor PCV/TP and urine output; transfuse whole blood if PCV drops below 20%. Surgical nephrectomy via flank laparotomy is indicated for severe lacerations, persistent hemorrhage, or urine leakage unresponsive to conservative management. Broad-spectrum antimicrobials (e.g., gentamicin 6.6 mg/kg IV q24h plus penicillin) are given prophylactically.
treatment_ja: 乳酸リンゲル液または生理食塩水による積極的な輸液で循環を安定させ、フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg IV 12時間毎）で鎮痛および抗エンドトキシン効果を得る。PCV/TPおよび尿量をモニタリングし、PCVが20%以下に低下した場合は全血輸血を行う。重度の腎裂傷、持続的な出血、または保存療法に反応しない尿漏れがある場合は、側腹部開腹による腎摘出術が適応となる。ゲンタマイシン（6.6 mg/kg IV 24時間毎）とペニシリンの併用による広域抗菌薬を予防的に投与する。

name: Renal Behavioral Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal behavioral disorder in horses involves chronic renal pain or discomfort arising from kidney pathology (such as nephrolithiasis, pyelonephritis, or chronic renal failure) that manifests as abnormal behavioral signs. The persistent nociceptive input from the kidneys and surrounding structures leads to changes in posture, gait, appetite, and temperament. Compensatory mechanisms and referred pain to the flank and lumbar regions further contribute to behavioral alterations including irritability, reluctance to work, and postural abnormalities.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎行動障害は、腎結石症、腎盂腎炎、慢性腎不全などの腎臓病変に起因する慢性的な腎臓の痛みや不快感が異常な行動徴候として現れるものである。腎臓および周囲組織からの持続的な侵害刺激が姿勢、歩様、食欲、気性の変化をもたらす。側腹部や腰部への関連痛や代償機構により、易刺激性、運動拒否、姿勢異常などの行動変化がさらに助長される。
causes: Primary causes include nephrolithiasis, pyelonephritis, renal neoplasia, chronic renal failure, and renal cysts that generate persistent pain or discomfort. Secondary causes involve ureterolithiasis, perirenal abscessation, toxic nephropathy (e.g., from NSAID overuse or aminoglycoside toxicity), and dehydration-related renal compromise. Metabolic imbalances such as hypercalcemia and electrolyte disturbances may also contribute to behavioral changes.
treatment: Treat the underlying renal pathology (e.g., antimicrobials such as trimethoprim-sulfonamide for pyelonephritis, surgical removal of nephroliths). Manage pain with flunixin meglumine (1.1 mg/kg IV q12h) or butorphanol (0.01-0.04 mg/kg IV), and provide IV fluid therapy to support renal perfusion and correct electrolyte imbalances.
treatment_ja: 基礎にある腎疾患を治療する（例：腎盂腎炎にはトリメトプリム・スルホンアミド等の抗菌薬投与、腎結石には外科的摘出）。疼痛管理としてフルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg IV 12時間毎）やブトルファノール（0.01〜0.04 mg/kg IV）を使用し、輸液療法で腎灌流の維持と電解質補正を行う。

name: Renal Infectious Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infectious disease in horses involves bacterial colonization of the renal parenchyma, typically ascending from the lower urinary tract or via hematogenous spread. Infection leads to inflammation (pyelonephritis), abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue, impairing glomerular filtration and tubular function. Chronic cases may result in fibrosis, renal insufficiency, and potentially septicemia if left untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症は、下部尿路からの上行感染または血行性播種により細菌が腎実質に定着することで発生します。感染により炎症（腎盂腎炎）、膿瘍形成、腎組織の進行性破壊が起こり、糸球体濾過機能および尿細管機能が障害されます。慢性例では線維化、腎不全、さらに未治療の場合は敗血症に至る可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infections (commonly Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Corynebacterium spp., and Actinobacillus equuli) from the lower urinary tract, or hematogenous spread from distant infection sites. Secondary causes include urolithiasis causing urinary stasis, immunosuppression, urinary catheterization, and structural abnormalities that predispose to bacterial colonization.
treatment: Initiate aggressive antimicrobial therapy based on urine culture and sensitivity; commonly trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (30 mg/kg PO BID) or enrofloxacin (5 mg/kg IV/PO SID) for 4-6 weeks. Provide IV fluid therapy to maintain renal perfusion and correct dehydration. Address underlying causes such as urolithiasis surgically if present, and provide NSAIDs (flunixin meglumine 1.1 mg/kg IV) for pain and inflammation control.
treatment_ja: 尿培養および感受性試験に基づき、トリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾール（30 mg/kg PO BID）またはエンロフロキサシン（5 mg/kg IV/PO SID）を4〜6週間投与する積極的な抗菌療法を開始する。静脈内輸液療法で腎灌流を維持し脱水を補正する。尿路結石などの基礎疾患がある場合は外科的に対処し、フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg IV）で疼痛・炎症管理を行う。

name: Renal Parasitic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal parasitic disease in horses involves migration and colonization of parasites such as Halicephalobus gingivalis (Halicephalobus deletrix), Strongylus vulgaris larvae, or Dioctophyme renale within the renal parenchyma and vasculature. Parasitic invasion causes granulomatous inflammation, tubular destruction, interstitial nephritis, and potential vascular thrombosis, leading to progressive renal dysfunction. Larval migration through renal tissue disrupts normal filtration and concentrating ability, potentially resulting in hematuria, proteinuria, and eventual renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎寄生虫症は、Halicephalobus gingivalis（ハリセファロブス）やStrongylus vulgarisの幼虫、Dioctophyme renaleなどの寄生虫が腎実質や血管系に移行・定着することで発症します。寄生虫の侵入により肉芽腫性炎症、尿細管破壊、間質性腎炎、血管血栓症が引き起こされ、進行性の腎機能障害に至ります。幼虫の腎組織内移行により正常な濾過・濃縮機能が障害され、血尿、蛋白尿、最終的に腎不全を引き起こす可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include parasitic infection by Halicephalobus gingivalis (most significant), migrating Strongylus vulgaris larvae, and rarely Dioctophyme renale. Infection occurs through ingestion of larvae from contaminated soil or water, or through wound contamination, with subsequent hematogenous or direct migration to the kidneys. Immunosuppression, poor pasture management, and inadequate deworming programs are predisposing factors.
treatment: Treatment is often unrewarding, especially for Halicephalobus gingivalis infections, which are typically diagnosed postmortem. High-dose anthelmintics such as fenbendazole (10 mg/kg PO daily for 5 days) or ivermectin (0.2 mg/kg PO) may be attempted for Strongylus vulgaris larval migration. Supportive care includes NSAIDs for inflammation, IV fluid therapy for renal support, and nephrectomy may be considered for unilateral Dioctophyme renale infection.
treatment_ja: 治療は困難な場合が多く、特にHalicephalobus gingivalis感染症は死後診断されることが大半である。Strongylus vulgaris幼虫移行に対してはフェンベンダゾール（10 mg/kg 経口 1日1回 5日間）やイベルメクチン（0.2 mg/kg 経口）などの高用量駆虫薬投与を試みる。補助療法として抗炎症薬（NSAIDs）、腎機能維持のための輸液療法を行い、Dioctophyme renaleの片側性感染では腎摘出術も検討される。

name: Renal Viral Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Viral agents such as equine herpesvirus (EHV) or equine arteritis virus (EAV) can cause direct cytopathic damage to renal tubular epithelial cells and glomerular endothelium. Immune-mediated mechanisms, including immune complex deposition in the glomeruli and interstitial inflammation, contribute to progressive renal dysfunction. Vascular damage and thrombosis within renal vasculature may further compromise renal perfusion, leading to acute or chronic renal insufficiency.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬ヘルペスウイルス（EHV）や馬動脈炎ウイルス（EAV）などのウイルスが腎尿細管上皮細胞や糸球体内皮に直接的な細胞障害を引き起こす。免疫複合体の糸球体沈着や間質性炎症などの免疫介在性機序が腎機能障害の進行に寄与する。腎血管内の血管障害や血栓形成が腎灌流をさらに低下させ、急性または慢性腎不全に至る場合がある。
causes: Primary causes include equine herpesvirus (particularly EHV-1), equine arteritis virus (EAV), and potentially other systemic viral infections that have tropism for renal tissue. Secondary causes include immune-complex mediated glomerulonephritis triggered by persistent viremia, as well as hemodynamic compromise from viral-induced systemic vasculitis or disseminated intravascular coagulation.
treatment: No specific antiviral therapy is established; supportive care includes IV fluid therapy (balanced polyionic solutions) to maintain renal perfusion, NSAIDs (flunixin meglumine 1.1 mg/kg IV) for inflammation control, and ACE inhibitors if proteinuria is significant. Antiviral agents such as valacyclovir (30 mg/kg PO q8h) may be considered for EHV-1 cases. Monitor serum creatinine and urine output closely.
treatment_ja: 特異的な抗ウイルス療法は確立されていないため、腎灌流維持のための静脈輸液（バランス電解質液）、フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg IV）による抗炎症療法、蛋白尿が顕著な場合はACE阻害薬を用いた支持療法が中心となる。EHV-1症例にはバラシクロビル（30 mg/kg PO 8時間毎）の投与を検討する。血清クレアチニンおよび尿量を厳密にモニタリングする。

name: Renal Bacterial Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Bacterial infection of the kidneys (pyelonephritis) in horses typically occurs via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract, or less commonly through hematogenous spread. Bacteria colonize the renal pelvis and parenchyma, causing inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue. Common causative organisms include Escherichia coli, Actinobacillus equuli, Streptococcus spp., and Corynebacterium spp., leading to impaired renal function if left untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎臓細菌感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路からの上行性感染、またはまれに血行性播種により発生します。細菌が腎盂および腎実質に定着し、炎症、膿瘍形成、腎組織の進行性破壊を引き起こします。一般的な原因菌には大腸菌、Actinobacillus equuli、連鎖球菌属、コリネバクテリウム属があり、未治療では腎機能障害に至ります。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infection from the lower urinary tract (cystitis, urethritis), often associated with urolithiasis, urinary stasis, or catheterization. Secondary causes include hematogenous spread from distant infection sites (e.g., endocarditis, respiratory infections), immunosuppression, and structural abnormalities of the urinary tract that predispose to bacterial colonization.
treatment: Initiate prolonged antimicrobial therapy (4-6 weeks) based on urine culture and sensitivity; commonly trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (30 mg/kg PO BID) or enrofloxacin (7.5 mg/kg PO SID). Provide IV fluid therapy to maintain hydration and promote renal perfusion. Address underlying causes such as urolithiasis removal or urinary obstruction relief; NSAIDs (flunixin meglumine 1.1 mg/kg IV) for pain and inflammation management.
treatment_ja: 尿培養・感受性試験に基づき、長期間（4〜6週間）の抗菌薬治療を開始する。一般的にトリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾール（30 mg/kg 経口 1日2回）またはエンロフロキサシン（7.5 mg/kg 経口 1日1回）を使用する。静脈内輸液により水分補給と腎灌流を維持する。尿路結石の除去や尿路閉塞の解除など根本原因に対処し、フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg 静注）で疼痛・炎症を管理する。

name: Renal Fungal Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Fungal organisms, most commonly Aspergillus spp. or Candida spp., colonize the renal parenchyma and/or renal pelvis, leading to granulomatous or necrotizing inflammation. This results in progressive destruction of renal tissue, impaired renal function, and potential formation of fungal masses (fungal balls) that may obstruct urine flow. Hematogenous dissemination from a primary site or ascending infection from the lower urinary tract can initiate renal involvement.
pathophysiology_ja: 主にAspergillus属やCandida属などの真菌が腎実質や腎盂に定着し、肉芽腫性または壊死性の炎症を引き起こします。これにより腎組織の進行性破壊、腎機能障害、さらには尿路を閉塞する真菌塊（ファンガスボール）の形成が生じます。血行性播種または下部尿路からの上行性感染により腎への感染が開始されます。
causes: Primary causes include opportunistic fungal infections by Aspergillus spp., Candida spp., or other environmental fungi. Predisposing factors include prolonged antibiotic therapy, immunosuppression, indwelling urinary catheters, debilitation, and concurrent systemic illness that compromises immune defenses.
causes_ja: 主な原因はAspergillus属、Candida属、その他の環境中真菌による日和見感染です。長期間の抗菌薬投与、免疫抑制状態、留置尿道カテーテル、衰弱、および免疫機能を低下させる併発全身疾患が素因として挙げられます。
treatment: Systemic antifungal therapy with fluconazole (5 mg/kg PO q24h) or voriconazole (3 mg/kg PO q12h) for prolonged courses (weeks to months). Amphotericin B (0.3-0.5 mg/kg IV slowly) may be used in severe cases with careful renal monitoring. Nephrectomy is indicated for unilateral fungal masses unresponsive to medical therapy; concurrent supportive care includes IV fluids and discontinuation of predisposing antibiotics.
treatment_ja: フルコナゾール（5 mg/kg 経口 1日1回）またはボリコナゾール（3 mg/kg 経口 1日2回）による長期全身抗真菌療法を実施する。重症例ではアムホテリシンB（0.3〜0.5 mg/kg 緩徐静注）を腎機能を慎重にモニタリングしながら使用する。内科療法に反応しない片側性真菌塊には腎摘出術を検討し、輸液療法や誘因となる抗菌薬の中止などの支持療法を併用する。

name: Renal Infection (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infection (pyelonephritis) in horses typically occurs via ascending bacterial infection from the lower urinary tract through the ureters to the renal pelvis and parenchyma. Bacteria colonize the renal medulla, triggering an inflammatory response that leads to tissue destruction, abscess formation, and progressive impairment of renal function. In severe or chronic cases, fibrosis and nephron loss can result in renal insufficiency, and infection may spread hematogenously or extend to perirenal tissues.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路から尿管を経由して腎盂および腎実質へ細菌が上行性に感染することで発生します。細菌が腎髄質に定着し、炎症反応を引き起こして組織破壊、膿瘍形成、および腎機能の進行性障害をもたらします。重症例や慢性例では、線維化やネフロンの喪失により腎不全に至る場合があり、血行性播種や腎周囲組織への波及も起こり得ます。
causes: The most common causative agents are gram-negative bacteria such as Escherichia coli, Proteus spp., Klebsiella spp., and Actinobacillus equuli, often ascending from the lower urinary tract. Predisposing factors include urolithiasis, urinary tract obstruction, bladder paralysis, catheterization, immunosuppression, and conditions causing urinary stasis. Hematogenous spread from distant infection sites is a less common but possible route.
treatment: Initiate prolonged systemic antibiotic therapy (4-6 weeks) based on urine culture and sensitivity, commonly trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole or enrofloxacin for gram-negative coverage. Correct predisposing factors such as urolithiasis or obstruction. Provide IV fluid therapy to maintain hydration and renal perfusion, along with NSAIDs (flunixin meglumine) for pain and inflammation control.
treatment_ja: 尿培養・感受性試験に基づき、トリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾールやエンロフロキサシンなどの全身性抗菌薬を4〜6週間長期投与する。尿路結石や閉塞などの素因を外科的・内科的に是正する。輸液療法で水和と腎灌流を維持し、フルニキシンメグルミン等のNSAIDsで疼痛・炎症管理を行う。

name: Renal Inflammation (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal inflammation (nephritis) in horses involves immune-mediated or infectious processes that damage the glomeruli, tubules, or interstitium of the kidneys. Inflammatory cell infiltration and immune complex deposition lead to impaired glomerular filtration, tubular dysfunction, and progressive loss of renal function. Prolonged inflammation can result in fibrosis, chronic renal failure, and systemic azotemia.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎炎は、免疫介在性または感染性の過程により糸球体、尿細管、または間質が損傷される疾患です。炎症細胞の浸潤や免疫複合体の沈着により糸球体濾過率の低下、尿細管機能障害、腎機能の進行性喪失が生じます。慢性化すると線維化、慢性腎不全、全身性高窒素血症に至ることがあります。
causes: Primary causes include bacterial infections (e.g., Leptospira spp., Streptococcus equi), viral infections (e.g., equine infectious anemia), and immune-mediated glomerulonephritis. Secondary causes include nephrotoxic drugs (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides), systemic sepsis, heavy metal toxicity, and prolonged dehydration or hemodynamic compromise.
causes_ja: 主な原因として、細菌感染（レプトスピラ、腺疫菌など）、ウイルス感染（馬伝染性貧血など）、および免疫介在性糸球体腎炎が挙げられます。二次的原因には、腎毒性薬物（NSAIDs、アミノグリコシド系抗生物質）、全身性敗血症、重金属中毒、長期脱水や血行動態障害が含まれます。
treatment: Treat underlying cause with appropriate antibiotics (e.g., penicillin for Streptococcus equi, oxytetracycline for Leptospira). Discontinue nephrotoxic drugs (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides) immediately. Provide aggressive IV fluid therapy (balanced electrolyte solutions) to maintain renal perfusion, correct electrolyte imbalances, and consider corticosteroids (dexamethasone 0.05-0.1 mg/kg IV) for immune-mediated nephritis.
treatment_ja: 原因疾患に応じた抗菌薬投与（Streptococcus equiにはペニシリン、レプトスピラにはオキシテトラサイクリン）を実施する。腎毒性薬剤（NSAIDs、アミノグリコシド系）は直ちに中止する。積極的な静脈内輸液療法（バランス電解質液）で腎灌流を維持し、電解質異常を補正する。免疫介在性腎炎にはデキサメタゾン（0.05～0.1 mg/kg IV）の投与を検討する。

name: Renal Neoplasia (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal neoplasia in horses involves the uncontrolled proliferation of cells within the kidney parenchyma or renal pelvis. The most commonly reported types include renal cell carcinoma, nephroblastoma, and lymphoma, which can disrupt normal renal architecture, impair kidney function, and potentially metastasize to lungs, liver, and other organs. Progressive tumor growth leads to compression of normal renal tissue, hematuria, and eventually renal insufficiency if bilateral or if the contralateral kidney is compromised.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎腫瘍は、腎実質または腎盂内の細胞が無秩序に増殖することで発生します。最も多く報告される腫瘍は腎細胞癌、腎芽腫（ネフロブラストーマ）、およびリンパ腫であり、正常な腎構造を破壊し、腎機能を障害し、肺や肝臓など他臓器へ転移する可能性があります。腫瘍の進行により正常腎組織が圧迫され、血尿や最終的には腎不全に至ることがあります。
causes: The exact etiology of renal neoplasia in horses is largely unknown, and no specific genetic, viral, or environmental risk factors have been definitively established. Nephroblastoma (embryonal nephroma) is considered a congenital tumor arising from persistent embryonic renal tissue and is more commonly seen in young horses. Renal cell carcinoma occurs more frequently in older horses and may arise from spontaneous somatic mutations in tubular epithelial cells.
treatment: Unilateral nephrectomy is the primary treatment for localized renal tumors when the contralateral kidney is functional. For renal lymphoma, systemic chemotherapy with corticosteroids (dexamethasone) and cyclophosphamide may be attempted. Supportive care includes IV fluid therapy, analgesics (flunixin meglumine), and monitoring renal parameters.
treatment_ja: 対側腎の機能が正常であれば、限局性腎腫瘍に対しては患側腎の摘出術（片側腎摘出術）が第一選択となる。腎リンパ腫の場合、デキサメタゾンやシクロホスファミドによる全身化学療法が試みられることがある。支持療法として静脈内輸液、フルニキシンメグルミン等の鎮痛剤投与、および腎機能パラメータの継続的モニタリングを行う。

name: Renal Metabolic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal metabolic disease in horses involves disruption of the kidney's ability to maintain electrolyte balance, acid-base homeostasis, and waste product excretion. Impaired renal tubular function leads to abnormal handling of calcium, phosphorus, and bicarbonate, potentially resulting in metabolic acidosis or alkalosis, hypercalcemia, or hyperphosphatemia. Chronic dysfunction can lead to renal secondary hyperparathyroidism, soft tissue mineralization, and progressive nephron loss.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎代謝疾患は、電解質バランス、酸塩基平衡、および老廃物排泄を維持する腎臓の機能障害を伴う。腎尿細管機能の低下により、カルシウム、リン、重炭酸塩の異常な処理が生じ、代謝性アシドーシスまたはアルカローシス、高カルシウム血症、高リン血症を引き起こす可能性がある。慢性的な機能不全は腎性二次性副甲状腺機能亢進症、軟部組織の石灰化、進行性のネフロン喪失につながる。
causes: Primary causes include chronic kidney disease, nephrolithiasis, and toxic nephropathy from ingestion of nephrotoxic plants (e.g., oak, red maple) or drugs (e.g., NSAIDs, aminoglycosides). Secondary causes include dehydration, systemic infections, hemodynamic compromise, and dietary imbalances such as excessive calcium or oxalate intake. Age-related degenerative changes and congenital renal anomalies may also contribute.
treatment: Aggressive IV fluid therapy (isotonic crystalloids such as lactated Ringer's solution) to restore renal perfusion and correct dehydration. Discontinue all nephrotoxic agents (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides). Correct electrolyte imbalances (calcium gluconate for hypocalcemia, sodium bicarbonate for metabolic acidosis) and manage hyperphosphatemia with dietary phosphorus restriction and aluminum hydroxide binders. Supportive care includes monitoring urine output and serial renal biochemistry.
treatment_ja: 腎灌流回復および脱水補正のため、乳酸リンゲル液などの等張晶質液による積極的な静脈内輸液療法を実施する。NSAIDsやアミノグリコシド系薬剤など全ての腎毒性薬剤を中止する。電解質異常の補正（低カルシウム血症にはグルコン酸カルシウム、代謝性アシドーシスには重炭酸ナトリウム）を行い、高リン血症にはリン制限食と水酸化アルミニウム系リン吸着剤で管理する。尿量および腎機能の連続的なモニタリングによる支持療法を継続する。

name: Renal Nutritional Deficiency (Horse)
pathophysiology: Nutritional deficiencies, particularly of vitamin A, vitamin D, calcium, phosphorus, or oxalate-rich diets, can impair renal tubular function and lead to nephrocalcinosis or renal tubular degeneration in horses. Chronic imbalances in calcium-phosphorus ratios (especially excess phosphorus or oxalate ingestion) promote calcium deposition in renal parenchyma, disrupting normal glomerular and tubular function. Progressive renal damage leads to impaired waste excretion, electrolyte imbalance, and eventual renal insufficiency.
pathophysiology_ja: ビタミンA、ビタミンD、カルシウム、リンなどの栄養素の欠乏やシュウ酸塩の過剰摂取により、腎尿細管機能の障害や腎石灰化症が引き起こされます。カルシウム・リン比の慢性的な不均衡は腎実質へのカルシウム沈着を促進し、糸球体および尿細管機能を障害します。進行性の腎障害により、老廃物排泄の低下、電解質異常、最終的に腎不全に至ります。
causes: Primary causes include chronic dietary calcium-phosphorus imbalance (high phosphorus, low calcium diets), excessive oxalate ingestion from plants such as Setaria or Oxalis species, and deficiencies in vitamin A or vitamin D. Secondary causes include prolonged feeding of bran-heavy or grain-heavy diets without adequate forage, and chronic ingestion of nephrotoxic plants that compound nutritional stress on the kidneys.
treatment: Correct dietary calcium-phosphorus ratio to approximately 2:1 by supplementing calcium carbonate or limestone and reducing bran/grain-heavy feeds. Remove oxalate-rich forages (Setaria, Oxalis). Supplement vitamin A and vitamin D as needed, provide IV fluid therapy for renal support, and monitor serum electrolytes and renal parameters regularly.
treatment_ja: 食事中のカルシウム・リン比を約2:1に是正するため、�ite calcium carbonate（炭酸カルシウム）や石灰石を補給し、ふすまや穀物過多の飼料を削減する。シュウ酸含有量の高い牧草（セタリア、カタバミ属）を除去する。必要に応じてビタミンAおよびビタミンDを補充し、腎機能維持のため輸液療法を実施し、血清電解質および腎機能パラメータを定期的にモニタリングする。

name: Renal Genetic Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal genetic disorders in horses involve inherited mutations affecting renal tubular or glomerular structure and function, leading to progressive nephron loss, impaired filtration, and eventual chronic kidney disease. Examples include renal dysplasia and polycystic kidney disease, where abnormal renal development or cyst formation disrupts normal renal architecture. Progressive fibrosis and loss of functional nephrons result in azotemia, electrolyte imbalances, and renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎遺伝性疾患は、腎尿細管や糸球体の構造・機能に影響を及ぼす遺伝子変異に起因し、ネフロンの進行性喪失、濾過機能障害、最終的には慢性腎臓病に至ります。腎異形成や多発性嚢胞腎などが含まれ、異常な腎発育や嚢胞形成により正常な腎構造が破壊されます。進行性の線維化と機能的ネフロンの喪失により、高窒素血症、電解質異常、腎不全が生じます。
causes: The primary cause is inherited genetic mutations affecting renal development or function, often transmitted in an autosomal recessive or dominant pattern depending on the specific disorder. Specific gene defects may affect proteins essential for nephron differentiation, tubular transport, or basement membrane integrity. Secondary factors such as dehydration, nephrotoxic agents, or concurrent infections may accelerate disease progression.
treatment: No curative therapy exists; management is supportive. Administer IV fluid therapy to correct dehydration and electrolyte imbalances. Use ACE inhibitors (enalapril 0.5 mg/kg PO q24h) to reduce glomerular hypertension, phosphate binders for hyperphosphatemia, and dietary protein restriction to slow progression of chronic kidney disease.
treatment_ja: 根治療法は存在せず、治療は対症療法が中心となる。脱水および電解質異常の補正に静脈内輸液療法を実施する。糸球体内高血圧の軽減にACE阻害薬（エナラプリル0.5 mg/kg 経口 1日1回）を投与し、高リン血症にはリン吸着剤を使用、慢性腎臓病の進行を遅延させるため食事中のタンパク質制限を行う。

name: Renal Autoimmune Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: The immune system produces autoantibodies or autoreactive lymphocytes directed against renal antigens, leading to immune complex deposition in the glomeruli and/or tubulointerstitial tissue. This triggers complement activation, inflammatory cell infiltration, and progressive destruction of renal parenchyma, resulting in glomerulonephritis or tubulointerstitial nephritis. Over time, chronic inflammation leads to fibrosis, nephron loss, and progressive renal insufficiency.
pathophysiology_ja: 免疫系が腎抗原に対する自己抗体または自己反応性リンパ球を産生し、糸球体や尿細管間質組織に免疫複合体が沈着する。これにより補体活性化、炎症細胞浸潤、腎実質の進行性破壊が引き起こされ、糸球体腎炎や尿細管間質性腎炎を生じる。慢性炎症は線維化、ネフロン喪失、進行性腎不全へと進展する。
causes: The primary cause is dysregulation of immune tolerance leading to autoimmune attack against renal structures, potentially triggered by preceding infections (e.g., Streptococcus equi), drug reactions, or systemic immune-mediated diseases such as systemic lupus erythematosus. Secondary causes include chronic antigenic stimulation from persistent infections (e.g., equine infectious anemia) and immune complex formation from other systemic diseases that deposit in the kidneys.
treatment: Initiate immunosuppressive therapy with dexamethasone (0.05-0.2 mg/kg IV/IM daily, tapering over weeks) combined with azathioprine (3 mg/kg PO daily) to suppress autoantibody production and inflammatory response. Provide supportive care including IV fluid therapy to maintain renal perfusion, ACE inhibitors such as enalapril (0.5 mg/kg PO BID) to reduce proteinuria, and dietary protein management.
treatment_ja: デキサメタゾン（0.05〜0.2 mg/kg IV/IM、1日1回、段階的に減量）とアザチオプリン（3 mg/kg PO、1日1回）による免疫抑制療法を開始し、自己抗体産生と炎症反応を抑制する。腎灌流維持のための輸液療法、蛋白尿軽減のためのエナラプリル（0.5 mg/kg PO BID）などのACE阻害薬投与、食事中のタンパク質管理を含む支持療法を併用する。

name: Renal Degenerative Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal degenerative disease in horses involves progressive deterioration of renal parenchyma, including tubular degeneration, interstitial fibrosis, and glomerulosclerosis, leading to impaired glomerular filtration and tubular reabsorption. Chronic nephron loss results in azotemia, electrolyte imbalances, and eventual renal failure. The disease may progress insidiously, with clinical signs appearing only after significant loss of functional renal mass (>70-75%).
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎変性疾患は、尿細管変性、間質線維化、糸球体硬化症を含む腎実質の進行性劣化を伴い、糸球体濾過および尿細管再吸収の障害を引き起こす。慢性的なネフロン喪失により高窒素血症、電解質異常、最終的には腎不全に至る。機能的腎量の大部分（70〜75%以上）が失われるまで臨床症状が現れないことが多く、潜行性に進行する。
causes: Primary causes include chronic exposure to nephrotoxins such as aminoglycoside antibiotics, NSAIDs, heavy metals, and oxalate-containing plants. Secondary causes include chronic dehydration, recurrent episodes of acute kidney injury, age-related degenerative changes, and systemic diseases such as leptospirosis or equine infectious anemia that cause chronic renal inflammation.
treatment: Treatment is primarily supportive: intravenous fluid therapy (balanced polyionic solutions) to correct dehydration and electrolyte imbalances, discontinuation of all nephrotoxic agents (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides), and dietary management with reduced protein intake. Administer phosphate binders (aluminum hydroxide) if hyperphosphatemia is present, and manage hypertension with ACE inhibitors (benazepril 0.5 mg/kg PO q24h). Monitor BUN, creatinine, and electrolytes serially.
treatment_ja: 治療は主に対症療法であり、脱水および電解質異常の補正のための静脈内輸液療法（バランス電解質液）、すべての腎毒性薬剤（NSAIDs、アミノグリコシド系抗菌薬）の中止、低タンパク食への食事管理を行う。高リン血症にはリン吸着剤（水酸化アルミニウム）を投与し、高血圧にはACE阻害薬（ベナゼプリル0.5 mg/kg 経口 1日1回）で管理する。BUN、クレアチニン、電解質を定期的にモニタリングする。

name: Renal Traumatic Injury (Horse)
pathophysiology: Blunt or penetrating trauma to the kidney causes disruption of the renal parenchyma, capsule, or vascular pedicle, leading to hemorrhage, hematoma formation, and potential urine leakage into the retroperitoneal space. Subsequent inflammation, ischemia, and possible secondary infection can result in progressive renal dysfunction. In severe cases, vascular compromise may lead to renal infarction or life-threatening hemorrhage into the peritoneal or retroperitoneal cavities.
pathophysiology_ja: 鈍的外傷または穿通性外傷により腎実質、腎被膜、または血管茎が損傷を受け、出血、血腫形成、および後腹膜腔への尿漏出が生じる。続発する炎症、虚血、二次感染により腎機能が進行性に低下する可能性がある。重症例では血管損傷により腎梗塞や腹腔・後腹膜腔への致命的な出血を引き起こすことがある。
causes: Primary causes include blunt abdominal trauma from kicks by other horses, falls during exercise or competition, collisions with fixed objects, and vehicular accidents. Secondary causes include penetrating injuries from foreign bodies, fractured ribs lacerating the kidney, and iatrogenic injury during percutaneous renal biopsy or surgical procedures. Foals may sustain renal trauma during dystocia or rough handling.
treatment: Initial stabilization with IV crystalloid fluids (LRS or 0.9% NaCl) and colloids for hemorrhagic shock. Administer flunixin meglumine (1.1 mg/kg IV) for analgesia and anti-inflammatory effect, broad-spectrum antibiotics (gentamicin 6.6 mg/kg IV q24h plus penicillin 22,000 IU/kg IV q6h) to prevent secondary infection. Monitor hematocrit, renal values, and urine output; perform serial ultrasonography. Surgical intervention (nephrectomy) is indicated for uncontrolled hemorrhage, shattered kidney, or renal pedicle avulsion.
treatment_ja: 出血性ショックに対し乳酸リンゲル液または生理食塩水の静脈内輸液およびコロイド製剤で初期安定化を行う。フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg IV）で鎮痛・抗炎症を図り、二次感染予防にゲンタマイシン（6.6 mg/kg IV q24h）とペニシリン（22,000 IU/kg IV q6h）を投与する。ヘマトクリット、腎機能値、尿量を継続的に監視し、超音波検査を反復実施する。制御不能な出血、腎臓の粉砕損傷、または腎茎断裂の場合は腎摘出術を適応とする。

name: Renal Behavioral Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal behavioral disorder in horses involves abnormal behaviors arising from chronic renal pain or discomfort due to underlying kidney pathology such as nephrolithiasis, nephritis, or renal neoplasia. Persistent nociceptive input from the renal capsule or parenchyma leads to changes in behavior including flank guarding, stretching postures, decreased performance, and irritability.
