The resulting inflammation, ischemia, and possible secondary infection can compromise renal function. In severe cases, vascular disruption may lead to life-threatening hemorrhage or subsequent renal infarction and fibrosis.
pathophysiology_ja: 腰部への鈍的または穿通性外傷により、腎実質、腎被膜、または腎血管系に直接的な損傷が生じ、出血、血腫形成、および後腹膜腔への尿漏出が起こる。結果として生じる炎症、虚血、二次感染により腎機能が障害される可能性がある。重症例では血管損傷により致命的な出血や、その後の腎梗塞および線維化を引き起こすことがある。
causes: Primary causes include blunt trauma from kicks by other horses, falls during exercise or competition, collision with fixed objects, and vehicular accidents. Secondary causes include penetrating injuries from sharp objects, fractured ribs lacerating the kidney, and iatrogenic injury during percutaneous renal biopsy or surgical procedures.
causes_ja: 主な原因として、他馬からの蹴り、運動中や競技中の転倒、固定物への衝突、車両事故による鈍的外傷が挙げられる。二次的原因には鋭利な物体による穿通性外傷、肋骨骨折による腎臓の裂傷、経皮的腎生検や外科的処置中の医原性損傷がある。
treatment: Initial stabilization with IV crystalloid fluids (LRS or 0.9% NaCl) and blood transfusion if severe hemorrhage occurs. Administer flunixin meglumine (1.1 mg/kg IV q12h) for pain and inflammation, broad-spectrum antibiotics (gentamicin 6.6 mg/kg IV q24h plus penicillin 22,000 IU/kg IV q6h) to prevent secondary infection. Monitor with serial ultrasound; surgical nephrectomy is indicated for uncontrolled hemorrhage or extensive parenchymal disruption.
treatment_ja: 初期安定化として乳酸リンゲル液または生理食塩水の静脈内輸液を行い、重度出血時には輸血を実施する。フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg IV 12時間毎）で疼痛・炎症を管理し、ゲンタマイシン（6.6 mg/kg IV 24時間毎）およびペニシリン（22,000 IU/kg IV 6時間毎）の広域抗菌薬で二次感染を予防する。連続超音波検査でモニタリングを行い、止血困難や広範な腎実質損傷がある場合は腎摘出術を適応とする。

name: Renal Behavioral Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal behavioral disorder in horses involves abnormal behaviors arising from chronic renal pain or discomfort due to underlying kidney pathology such as nephrolithiasis, pyelonephritis, or renal neoplasia. Persistent nociceptive input from the renal capsule or ureters can manifest as flank guarding, stretching postures, reluctance to move, and altered urination patterns. Chronic pain may lead to secondary behavioral changes including irritability, reduced performance, and changes in appetite.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎行動障害は、腎結石症、腎盂腎炎、腎腫瘍などの腎臓病変に起因する慢性的な腎臓の痛みや不快感から生じる異常行動を伴います。腎被膜や尿管からの持続的な侵害受容入力が、側腹部の防御姿勢、伸展姿勢、運動嫌忌、排尿パターンの変化として現れます。慢性疼痛は、易刺激性、パフォーマンス低下、食欲変化などの二次的な行動変化を引き起こすことがあります。
causes: Primary causes include nephrolithiasis, renal calculi, pyelonephritis, renal cysts, and renal neoplasia causing chronic kidney pain. Secondary causes include ureterolithiasis causing ureteral obstruction, chronic interstitial nephritis, and referred pain from adjacent organ pathology. Predisposing factors include high-calcium diets, inadequate water intake, and chronic urinary tract infections.
treatment: Address underlying renal pathology: surgical removal of nephroliths or calculi via nephrotomy or lithotripsy; treat pyelonephritis with prolonged antimicrobials (trimethoprim-sulfadiazine 30 mg/kg PO BID or enrofloxacin 5 mg/kg IV SID). Manage pain with flunixin meglumine (1.1 mg/kg IV BID) or phenylbutazone (2.2 mg/kg PO BID), and gabapentin (5-10 mg/kg PO BID) for neuropathic components. Provide supportive IV fluid therapy to maintain renal perfusion and monitor renal values serially.
treatment_ja: 基礎となる腎疾患の治療として、腎結石に対しては腎切開術や砕石術を実施し、腎盂腎炎にはトリメトプリム・スルファジアジン（30 mg/kg PO BID）やエンロフロキサシン（5 mg/kg IV SID）の長期抗菌薬療法を行う。疼痛管理にはフルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg IV BID）またはフェニルブタゾン（2.2 mg/kg PO BID）を使用し、神経因性疼痛にはガバペンチン（5-10 mg/kg PO BID）を併用する。腎灌流維持のため静脈内輸液療法を行い、腎機能値を継続的にモニタリングする。

name: Renal Infectious Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infectious disease in horses involves bacterial colonization of the renal parenchyma, typically via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract or hematogenous spread. Bacterial invasion triggers an inflammatory response leading to nephritis or pyelonephritis, causing tubular damage, interstitial inflammation, and potential abscess formation. Progressive infection can impair glomerular filtration and tubular function, leading to renal insufficiency or failure if untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症は、下部尿路からの上行感染または血行性播種により細菌が腎実質に定着することで発生します。細菌の侵入により炎症反応が惹起され、腎炎や腎盂腎炎を引き起こし、尿細管障害、間質性炎症、膿瘍形成を生じます。感染が進行すると糸球体濾過および尿細管機能が障害され、未治療の場合は腎不全に至る可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infections (commonly Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Actinobacillus equuli, and Corynebacterium spp.) from the lower urinary tract, as well as hematogenous spread from distant infection sites. Secondary causes include urolithiasis causing urinary stasis, immunosuppression, indwelling urinary catheters, and structural abnormalities of the urinary tract that predispose to bacterial colonization.
treatment: Initiate broad-spectrum antimicrobial therapy based on urine culture and sensitivity, commonly trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (30 mg/kg PO BID) or enrofloxacin (5 mg/kg IV/PO SID) for 2-4 weeks. Provide aggressive IV fluid therapy (lactated Ringer's solution) to maintain hydration and renal perfusion. Address underlying causes such as urolithiasis surgically if present, and administer NSAIDs (flunixin meglumine 1.1 mg/kg IV) for pain and inflammation control.
treatment_ja: 尿培養および感受性試験に基づき、トリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾール（30 mg/kg 経口 BID）またはエンロフロキサシン（5 mg/kg 静注/経口 SID）による広域抗菌薬療法を2〜4週間実施する。乳酸リンゲル液による積極的な輸液療法で水分補給と腎灌流を維持する。尿路結石などの基礎疾患が存在する場合は外科的に対処し、フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg 静注）を用いて疼痛および炎症の管理を行う。

name: Renal Parasitic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal parasitic disease in horses occurs when parasitic organisms such as Halicephalobus gingivalis (Halicephalobus deletrix), Strongylus vulgaris larvae, or Dioctophyme renale migrate to or establish within the renal parenchyma. The parasites cause granulomatous inflammation, tissue destruction, tubular necrosis, and fibrosis of the kidney, leading to impaired renal function. Larval migration through renal vasculature can also cause thrombosis, infarction, and secondary bacterial infection.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎寄生虫症は、Halicephalobus gingivalis、普通円虫（Strongylus vulgaris）の幼虫、または腎虫（Dioctophyme renale）などの寄生虫が腎実質に移行・寄生することで発生する。寄生虫は肉芽腫性炎症、組織破壊、尿細管壊死、線維化を引き起こし、腎機能障害をもたらす。幼虫の腎血管内移行は血栓症、梗塞、および二次的細菌感染を引き起こすこともある。
causes: Primary causes include migration of parasitic larvae such as Strongylus vulgaris through mesenteric and renal vasculature, infection by Halicephalobus gingivalis (a free-living nematode with opportunistic parasitic potential), and rarely Dioctophyme renale. Secondary causes include immunosuppression, poor deworming management, and environmental contamination with infective larvae or eggs.
treatment: Administer broad-spectrum anthelmintics such as ivermectin (0.2 mg/kg PO) or fenbendazole (10 mg/kg PO daily for 5 days) to target migrating larvae. For Halicephalobus gingivalis, prognosis is grave; high-dose fenbendazole or moxidectin may be attempted but efficacy is limited. Supportive care includes NSAIDs (flunixin meglumine 1.1 mg/kg IV) for pain, IV fluid therapy for renal support, and nephrectomy of the affected kidney if disease is unilateral.
treatment_ja: 移行性幼虫に対し、イベルメクチン（0.2 mg/kg 経口）やフェンベンダゾール（10 mg/kg 経口、5日間連日投与）などの広域駆虫薬を投与する。Halicephalobus gingivalis感染では予後は極めて不良であり、高用量フェンベンダゾールやモキシデクチンの投与を試みるが効果は限定的である。疼痛管理にはフルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg 静注）、腎機能維持のための輸液療法を実施し、片側性病変の場合は患側腎の腎摘出術を検討する。

name: Renal Viral Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Viral agents such as equine herpesvirus (EHV) or equine arteritis virus (EAV) can infect renal vascular endothelium and tubular epithelial cells, leading to immune-mediated glomerulonephritis, vasculitis, and tubular necrosis. Immune complex deposition in glomeruli and direct viral cytopathic effects result in progressive renal dysfunction, proteinuria, and impaired glomerular filtration. Chronic infection may lead to interstitial nephritis and fibrosis with progressive loss of renal function.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬ヘルペスウイルス（EHV）や馬動脈炎ウイルス（EAV）などのウイルスが腎血管内皮や尿細管上皮細胞に感染し、免疫介在性糸球体腎炎、血管炎、尿細管壊死を引き起こす。糸球体への免疫複合体の沈着やウイルスの直接的な細胞障害作用により、腎機能障害、蛋白尿、糸球体濾過率の低下が生じる。慢性感染では間質性腎炎や線維化が進行し、腎機能が漸進的に喪失する。
causes: Primary causes include equine herpesvirus (EHV-1, EHV-4), equine arteritis virus (EAV), and potentially other systemic viral infections that target or secondarily affect the kidneys. Secondary causes include immune complex deposition from persistent viremia, systemic vasculitis, and hemodynamic compromise due to viral-induced sepsis or endotoxemia. Predisposing factors include immunosuppression, stress, and concurrent infections.
treatment: No specific antiviral therapy exists; supportive care includes IV fluid therapy (balanced polyionic solutions) to maintain renal perfusion, NSAIDs (flunixin meglumine 1.1 mg/kg IV) for inflammation control, and corticosteroids (dexamethasone 0.05-0.1 mg/kg IV) for immune-mediated glomerulonephritis. Antiviral agents such as valacyclovir (30 mg/kg PO q8h) may be considered for EHV cases. Monitor renal values and urine output closely.
treatment_ja: 特異的な抗ウイルス療法は存在せず、支持療法が中心となる。腎灌流維持のための静脈内輸液（バランス電解質液）、抗炎症目的でフルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg IV）、免疫介在性糸球体腎炎に対しデキサメタゾン（0.05～0.1 mg/kg IV）を投与する。EHV症例にはバラシクロビル（30 mg/kg PO 8時間毎）を検討する。腎機能値と尿量を厳密にモニタリングする。

name: Renal Bacterial Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Bacterial infection of the kidneys (pyelonephritis) in horses typically occurs via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract, or less commonly through hematogenous spread. Bacteria colonize the renal pelvis and parenchyma, triggering an inflammatory response that leads to tissue destruction, abscess formation, and progressive impairment of renal function. Common causative organisms include Escherichia coli, Actinobacillus equuli, Streptococcus spp., and Corynebacterium spp.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎細菌感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路からの上行性感染、またはまれに血行性播種によって発生します。細菌が腎盂および腎実質に定着し、炎症反応を引き起こして組織破壊、膿瘍形成、および進行性の腎機能障害をもたらします。一般的な起因菌には大腸菌、Actinobacillus equuli、レンサ球菌属、コリネバクテリウム属などがあります。
causes: Primary causes include ascending urinary tract infections (most common), hematogenous bacterial spread from distant infection sites, and urolithiasis or urinary obstruction predisposing to bacterial colonization. Secondary causes include immunosuppression, urinary catheterization, anatomical abnormalities, nephrolithiasis, and conditions causing urinary stasis.
treatment: Initiate aggressive systemic antibiotic therapy based on urine culture and sensitivity; commonly trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (30 mg/kg PO BID) or enrofloxacin (5 mg/kg IV/PO SID) for 4-6 weeks. Provide IV fluid therapy to maintain renal perfusion and correct dehydration. Address underlying causes such as urolithiasis or obstruction surgically if indicated, and monitor renal function via serial bloodwork and urinalysis.
treatment_ja: 尿培養・感受性試験に基づき、トリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾール（30 mg/kg 経口 BID）またはエンロフロキサシン（5 mg/kg 静注/経口 SID）を4〜6週間投与する積極的な全身抗菌療法を開始する。静脈輸液療法により腎灌流の維持と脱水の補正を行う。尿路結石や閉塞などの基礎疾患がある場合は外科的に対処し、血液検査および尿検査を定期的に実施して腎機能をモニタリングする。

name: Renal Fungal Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Fungal organisms, most commonly Aspergillus spp. or Candida spp., colonize the renal parenchyma and/or renal pelvis, leading to granulomatous or necrotizing inflammation. This results in progressive destruction of renal tissue, impaired renal function, and potential formation of fungal masses (fungal balls) that may obstruct urine flow. Hematogenous dissemination or ascending infection from the lower urinary tract can contribute to renal involvement.
pathophysiology_ja: 主にAspergillus属やCandida属などの真菌が腎実質や腎盂に定着し、肉芽腫性または壊死性炎症を引き起こす。これにより腎組織の進行性破壊、腎機能障害、および尿流を閉塞し得る真菌塊（ファンガスボール）の形成が生じる。血行性播種または下部尿路からの上行性感染が腎への波及に関与する。
causes: Primary causes include opportunistic fungal infections by Aspergillus spp., Candida spp., or other environmental fungi. Predisposing factors include prolonged antibiotic therapy, immunosuppression (e.g., from corticosteroid use or systemic illness), indwelling urinary catheters, and pre-existing renal disease. Secondary bacterial infections may complicate the condition.
causes_ja: 主な原因はAspergillus属、Candida属、その他の環境真菌による日和見感染である。素因として長期抗菌薬投与、免疫抑制（コルチコステロイド使用や全身性疾患）、留置尿道カテーテル、既存の腎疾患が挙げられる。二次的な細菌感染が病態を複雑化することがある。
treatment: Systemic antifungal therapy with fluconazole (5 mg/kg PO q24h) or amphotericin B (0.3-0.5 mg/kg IV slowly, with careful renal monitoring) is the primary approach. Discontinue predisposing antibiotics and immunosuppressive agents. Nephrectomy may be indicated for unilateral fungal masses unresponsive to medical therapy, combined with IV fluid support to maintain renal perfusion.
treatment_ja: フルコナゾール（5 mg/kg 経口 1日1回）またはアムホテリシンB（0.3〜0.5 mg/kg 緩徐静注、腎機能を慎重にモニタリング）による全身性抗真菌療法が主な治療法である。誘因となる抗菌薬や免疫抑制剤は中止する。内科治療に反応しない片側性の真菌塊には腎摘出術が適応となり、腎灌流維持のための輸液療法を併用する。

name: Renal Infection (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infection (pyelonephritis) in horses typically occurs via ascending bacterial infection from the lower urinary tract through the ureters to the renal pelvis and parenchyma. Bacteria colonize the renal medulla, triggering an inflammatory response that leads to tissue destruction, abscess formation, and progressive impairment of renal function. Chronic infection can result in fibrosis, hydronephrosis, and eventual loss of functional nephrons, potentially leading to renal failure if bilateral.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路から尿管を経由して腎盂および腎実質に細菌が上行性に感染することで発生する。細菌が腎髄質に定着し、炎症反応を引き起こして組織破壊、膿瘍形成、腎機能の進行性障害をもたらす。慢性感染は線維化、水腎症を引き起こし、両側性の場合は最終的に腎不全に至る可能性がある。
causes: The most common causative agents include Escherichia coli, Corynebacterium renale, Proteus spp., and Streptococcus spp., which ascend from the lower urinary tract. Predisposing factors include urolithiasis, urinary tract obstruction, bladder paralysis, catheterization, immunosuppression, and anatomical abnormalities. Hematogenous spread from distant infection sites is less common but possible.
treatment: Initiate prolonged antimicrobial therapy (4-6 weeks) based on urine culture and sensitivity, commonly trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (30 mg/kg PO BID) or enrofloxacin (5 mg/kg PO SID). Provide IV fluid therapy to maintain renal perfusion and correct dehydration. Address predisposing factors such as urolithiasis or obstruction surgically if needed, and monitor renal function via serial bloodwork and urinalysis.
treatment_ja: 尿培養および感受性試験に基づき、トリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾール（30 mg/kg 経口 BID）またはエンロフロキサシン（5 mg/kg 経口 SID）などの抗菌薬を4〜6週間長期投与する。静脈内輸液療法により腎灌流を維持し脱水を補正する。尿路結石や閉塞などの素因がある場合は外科的に対処し、血液検査および尿検査で腎機能を継続的にモニタリングする。

name: Renal Inflammation (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal inflammation (nephritis) in horses involves immune-mediated or infectious damage to the glomeruli, tubules, or interstitium of the kidneys. Inflammatory infiltration and edema compromise renal blood flow, glomerular filtration, and tubular function, leading to impaired waste excretion, electrolyte imbalances, and potentially azotemia. Chronic inflammation may progress to fibrosis and irreversible loss of nephron function.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎炎は、免疫介在性または感染性の障害により糸球体、尿細管、または間質に炎症が生じる疾患です。炎症性細胞浸潤や浮腫により腎血流や糸球体濾過率、尿細管機能が低下し、老廃物の排泄障害や電解質異常、高窒素血症を引き起こします。慢性炎症は線維化に進行し、不可逆的なネフロン機能喪失に至ることがあります。
causes: Primary causes include bacterial infections (e.g., Leptospira, Streptococcus), viral infections (e.g., equine infectious anemia), and immune-mediated glomerulonephritis. Secondary causes include nephrotoxic drugs (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides), systemic infections, toxin ingestion (heavy metals, plants such as oak or red maple), and dehydration or hemodynamic compromise leading to ischemic renal injury.
treatment: Treat underlying cause with appropriate antimicrobials (e.g., penicillin for Streptococcus, oxytetracycline for Leptospira). Discontinue nephrotoxic drugs (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides) immediately. Provide aggressive IV fluid therapy (balanced polyionic solutions) to restore renal perfusion, correct electrolyte imbalances, and support diuresis. Corticosteroids (dexamethasone) may be indicated for immune-mediated nephritis.
treatment_ja: 原因に応じた適切な抗菌薬（レンサ球菌にはペニシリン、レプトスピラにはオキシテトラサイクリン等）を投与する。腎毒性薬剤（NSAIDs、アミノグリコシド系）は直ちに中止する。積極的な静脈内輸液療法（バランス電解質液）により腎灌流の回復、電解質異常の補正、利尿を促進する。免疫介在性腎炎にはデキサメタゾン等の副腎皮質ステロイドの投与を検討する。

name: Renal Neoplasia (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal neoplasia in horses involves the abnormal proliferation of cells within the kidney, most commonly renal cell carcinoma, lymphoma, or nephroblastoma. The tumor mass disrupts normal renal parenchyma, impairing filtration and excretory functions, and may invade the renal vein or metastasize to lungs, liver, and other organs. Local expansion can cause compression of adjacent structures, hematuria, and progressive renal insufficiency.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎腫瘍は腎臓内の細胞の異常増殖であり、腎細胞癌、リンパ腫、腎芽腫が最も多く見られます。腫瘍塊は正常な腎実質を破壊し、濾過機能や排泄機能を障害し、腎静脈への浸潤や肺・肝臓など他臓器への転移を起こすことがあります。局所的な腫瘍の拡大により隣接組織の圧迫、血尿、進行性の腎機能不全が引き起こされます。
causes: The exact etiology of renal neoplasia in horses is largely unknown. Potential contributing factors include genetic predisposition, chronic inflammation or irritation of renal tissue, and possible environmental carcinogen exposure. Renal cell carcinoma is the most commonly reported primary renal tumor, while lymphoma may involve the kidney as part of multicentric disease.
treatment: Unilateral nephrectomy is the primary treatment for localized renal tumors when the contralateral kidney is functional. For lymphoma, systemic chemotherapy (e.g., corticosteroids such as dexamethasone, with or without cyclophosphamide) may be attempted. Supportive care includes IV fluid therapy, NSAIDs for pain management, and monitoring renal parameters.
treatment_ja: 対側腎が機能している場合、限局性腎腫瘍に対しては片側腎摘出術が第一選択となる。リンパ腫の場合、デキサメタゾン等の副腎皮質ステロイドにシクロホスファミドを併用する全身化学療法が試みられる。支持療法として静脈内輸液、NSAIDsによる疼痛管理、および腎機能パラメータの継続的モニタリングを実施する。

name: Renal Metabolic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal metabolic disease in horses involves dysfunction of the kidneys' ability to properly regulate electrolyte balance, acid-base homeostasis, and waste product excretion. Impaired tubular reabsorption and secretion lead to accumulation of metabolic byproducts such as urea, creatinine, and phosphorus, while causing imbalances in calcium, potassium, and bicarbonate. Progressive nephron loss results in azotemia, metabolic acidosis, and secondary mineral imbalances including renal secondary hyperparathyroidism.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎代謝疾患は、電解質バランス、酸塩基平衡、および老廃物排泄を適切に調節する腎臓の機能不全を伴う。尿細管の再吸収・分泌機能の障害により、尿素・クレアチニン・リンなどの代謝副産物が蓄積し、カルシウム・カリウム・重炭酸塩の不均衡が生じる。進行性のネフロン喪失により、高窒素血症、代謝性アシドーシス、および腎性二次性上皮小体機能亢進症が引き起こされる。
causes: Primary causes include chronic kidney disease from nephrotoxic agents (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals), nephrolithiasis, and chronic pyelonephritis. Secondary causes include dehydration, systemic infections, hemodynamic compromise, oxalate-containing plant ingestion, and hypercalcemia from excessive vitamin D or calcium supplementation.
treatment: Aggressive IV fluid therapy (isotonic crystalloids such as lactated Ringer's solution) to restore renal perfusion and correct dehydration. Discontinue nephrotoxic agents (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs). Correct electrolyte imbalances (calcium, phosphorus, potassium) and manage metabolic acidosis with sodium bicarbonate as needed. Dietary modification with reduced protein and phosphorus intake. Treat underlying causes such as pyelonephritis with appropriate antibiotics (trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole) and manage nephrolithiasis surgically if indicated.
treatment_ja: 積極的な静脈内輸液療法（乳酸リンゲル液などの等張晶質液）により腎灌流を回復し脱水を補正する。腎毒性薬剤（アミノグリコシド系抗菌薬、NSAIDs）を直ちに中止する。電解質異常（カルシウム、リン、カリウム）を是正し、代謝性アシドーシスには必要に応じて炭酸水素ナトリウムを投与する。低タンパク質・低リン食への食事管理を行う。腎盂腎炎にはトリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾール等の抗菌薬を使用し、腎結石症は必要に応じて外科的に対処する。

name: Renal Nutritional Deficiency (Horse)
pathophysiology: Nutritional deficiencies, particularly of vitamin A, vitamin D, calcium, phosphorus, or oxalate-rich diets, can lead to renal tubular damage, nephrocalcinosis, or impaired renal function in horses. Chronic imbalances in calcium-phosphorus ratios or excessive oxalate intake can cause calcium oxalate crystal deposition in renal tubules, leading to tubular necrosis and progressive renal insufficiency. Vitamin A deficiency may result in squamous metaplasia of renal epithelium, while vitamin D excess or deficiency disrupts calcium homeostasis and contributes to renal mineralization.
pathophysiology_ja: ビタミンA、ビタミンD、カルシウム、リンなどの栄養素の欠乏、またはシュウ酸を多く含む飼料の摂取により、腎尿細管の損傷、腎石灰化、または腎機能障害が馬に生じます。カルシウム・リン比の慢性的な不均衡やシュウ酸の過剰摂取は、腎尿細管にシュウ酸カルシウム結晶を沈着させ、尿細管壊死と進行性の腎不全を引き起こします。ビタミンA欠乏は腎上皮の扁平上皮化生を引き起こし、ビタミンDの過不足はカルシウム恒常性を乱し腎石灰化に寄与します。
treatment: Correct dietary imbalances by adjusting calcium-phosphorus ratio (ideally 2:1), supplement vitamin A and D as needed, and remove oxalate-rich forages. Provide IV fluid therapy with balanced electrolytes for acute renal compromise. Administer activated charcoal if recent oxalate ingestion is suspected, and monitor renal values (BUN, creatinine) serially.
treatment_ja: カルシウムとリンの比率を理想的な2:1に調整し、必要に応じてビタミンAおよびDを補給し、シュウ酸塩を多く含む飼料を除去して食事の不均衡を是正する。急性腎障害にはバランス電解質液による静脈内輸液療法を実施する。シュウ酸塩の最近の摂取が疑われる場合は活性炭を投与し、BUNおよびクレアチニンなどの腎機能値を継続的にモニタリングする。

name: Renal Genetic Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal genetic disorders in horses involve inherited mutations affecting renal tubular or glomerular structure and function, leading to progressive nephron loss, impaired filtration, and concentrating ability. Depending on the specific mutation, pathology may include renal dysplasia, polycystic kidney disease, or tubular dysfunction, resulting in progressive chronic kidney disease. Accumulation of uremic toxins and electrolyte imbalances ensue as functional renal mass declines.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎臓遺伝性疾患は、腎尿細管や糸球体の構造・機能に影響を及ぼす遺伝子変異に起因し、進行性のネフロン喪失、濾過能力および濃縮能力の低下を引き起こします。特定の変異により腎異形成、多発性嚢胞腎、尿細管機能障害などの病態が生じ、慢性腎臓病へと進行します。機能的腎組織の減少に伴い、尿毒症性毒素の蓄積や電解質異常が発生します。
causes: The primary cause is inherited genetic mutations, often autosomal recessive, affecting renal development or function. Specific examples include renal dysplasia reported in certain horse breeds and familial renal disease. Secondary factors such as dehydration, nephrotoxic drugs, or concurrent infections may accelerate disease progression in genetically predisposed individuals.
treatment: No curative therapy exists for renal genetic disorders in horses. Treatment is supportive: IV fluid therapy (balanced polyionic solutions) to maintain hydration, dietary protein and phosphorus restriction, and phosphate binders (aluminum hydroxide 30-90 mg/kg PO BID). ACE inhibitors (benazepril 0.5 mg/kg PO SID) may slow glomerular damage. Manage secondary complications including anemia (erythropoietin if needed) and electrolyte imbalances. Monitor BUN, creatinine, and urinalysis regularly.
treatment_ja: 馬の腎遺伝性疾患に根治療法は存在しません。治療は対症療法が中心で、補液療法（バランス電解質輸液）による水分維持、食餌中のタンパク質およびリン制限、リン吸着剤（水酸化アルミニウム30～90 mg/kg 経口 1日2回）を実施します。ACE阻害薬（ベナゼプリル0.5 mg/kg 経口 1日1回）は糸球体障害の進行を遅らせる可能性があります。貧血（必要に応じてエリスロポエチン投与）や電解質異常などの二次的合併症を管理し、BUN・クレアチニン・尿検査を定期的にモニタリングします。

name: Renal Autoimmune Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: The immune system produces autoantibodies or autoreactive T cells directed against renal antigens, leading to immune complex deposition in the glomeruli and/or tubulointerstitial tissue. This triggers complement activation, inflammatory cell infiltration, and progressive destruction of nephrons, resulting in glomerulonephritis or tubulointerstitial nephritis. Over time, chronic inflammation leads to fibrosis, impaired renal filtration, and progressive loss of kidney function.
pathophysiology_ja: 免疫系が腎臓の抗原に対する自己抗体または自己反応性T細胞を産生し、糸球体および/または尿細管間質組織に免疫複合体が沈着します。これにより補体活性化、炎症細胞浸潤、およびネフロンの進行性破壊が引き起こされ、糸球体腎炎または尿細管間質性腎炎が生じます。慢性的な炎症は線維化、腎濾過機能の障害、および進行性の腎機能低下をもたらします。
causes: The primary cause is immune dysregulation leading to loss of self-tolerance against renal antigens, potentially triggered by chronic infections (e.g., Streptococcus equi, equine infectious anemia virus), drug reactions, or systemic autoimmune conditions. Secondary causes include immune complex deposition from other systemic diseases, chronic antigenic stimulation, and genetic predisposition to autoimmune responses.
treatment: Initiate immunosuppressive therapy with corticosteroids (dexamethasone 0.05-0.1 mg/kg IV/IM daily, tapering over weeks) combined with azathioprine (3 mg/kg PO daily) to suppress autoantibody production and inflammation. Provide supportive care including IV fluid therapy to maintain renal perfusion, ACE inhibitors (benazepril 0.5 mg/kg PO daily) to reduce proteinuria, and dietary protein management. Monitor renal values, urine protein-to-creatinine ratio, and adjust immunosuppression accordingly.
treatment_ja: 副腎皮質ステロイド（デキサメタゾン0.05〜0.1 mg/kg IV/IM、1日1回、数週間かけて漸減）とアザチオプリン（3 mg/kg PO、1日1回）による免疫抑制療法を開始し、自己抗体産生と炎症を抑制する。腎灌流維持のための輸液療法、蛋白尿軽減のためのACE阻害薬（ベナゼプリル0.5 mg/kg PO、1日1回）、および食事中のタンパク質管理を含む支持療法を実施する。腎機能値および尿蛋白/クレアチニン比を定期的にモニタリングし、免疫抑制療法を適宜調整する。

name: Renal Degenerative Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal degenerative disease in horses involves progressive deterioration of renal parenchyma, including tubular degeneration, interstitial fibrosis, and glomerulosclerosis, leading to impaired glomerular filtration and tubular function. Chronic nephron loss results in azotemia, electrolyte imbalances, and inability to concentrate urine. The condition may progress to end-stage renal failure with irreversible loss of functional nephrons.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎変性疾患は、尿細管変性、間質線維化、糸球体硬化症を含む腎実質の進行性劣化を伴い、糸球体濾過および尿細管機能の障害を引き起こす。慢性的なネフロン喪失により高窒素血症、電解質異常、尿濃縮能の低下が生じる。病態は進行し、機能的ネフロンの不可逆的喪失を伴う末期腎不全に至る可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include chronic exposure to nephrotoxins (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals, vitamin D toxicosis), pigment nephropathy from myoglobinuria or hemoglobinuria, and chronic ischemic injury. Secondary causes include systemic infections, immune-mediated glomerulonephritis, amyloidosis, and age-related degenerative changes. Oxalate-containing plants and prolonged dehydration may also contribute.
treatment: Treatment is primarily supportive: intravenous fluid therapy (balanced polyionic solutions) to correct dehydration and electrolyte imbalances, discontinuation of all nephrotoxic agents (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides), and dietary management with reduced protein and phosphorus intake. Phosphate binders (aluminum hydroxide 30-90 mg/kg PO BID) and ACE inhibitors (benazepril 0.5 mg/kg PO SID) may slow progression. Manage secondary complications including gastric ulceration with omeprazole (4 mg/kg PO SID) and anemia with erythropoietin if indicated.
treatment_ja: 治療は主に支持療法が中心となる。バランス電解質輸液による脱水・電解質異常の補正、全ての腎毒性薬剤（NSAIDs、アミノグリコシド系）の中止、低タンパク・低リン食への変更を行う。リン吸着剤（水酸化アルミニウム30-90 mg/kg 経口 1日2回）やACE阻害薬（ベナゼプリル0.5 mg/kg 経口 1日1回）により進行を遅延させる。続発する胃潰瘍にはオメプラゾール（4 mg/kg 経口 1日1回）、貧血にはエリスロポエチンの投与を検討する。

name: Renal Traumatic Injury (Horse)
pathophysiology: Blunt or penetrating trauma to the kidney results in disruption of the renal parenchyma, capsule, or vascular pedicle, leading to hemorrhage, urine leakage, and potential retroperitoneal or peritoneal contamination. The resulting inflammation, hematoma formation, and possible ischemia can progress to renal dysfunction, abscess formation, or peritonitis. In horses, the kidneys are partially protected by the last ribs and lumbar musculature, but severe external force (kicks, falls, crushing injuries) can still cause significant renal damage.
pathophysiology_ja: 鈍的または穿通性の外傷により腎実質、腎被膜、または血管茎が損傷を受け、出血、尿漏出、後腹膜腔または腹腔内への汚染が生じる。続発する炎症、血腫形成、虚血により腎機能障害、膿瘍形成、腹膜炎に進行する可能性がある。馬の腎臓は最後肋骨と腰部筋肉により部分的に保護されているが、蹴り、転倒、圧挫損傷などの強い外力により重大な腎損傷が発生しうる。
causes: Primary causes include blunt abdominal trauma from kicks by other horses, falls during exercise or competition, collision with fixed objects, and crush injuries. Secondary causes include penetrating wounds from sharp objects, iatrogenic injury during percutaneous procedures (such as renal biopsy), and rarely rib fractures with fragment displacement impacting the kidney.
treatment: Initial stabilization with IV crystalloid fluids (LRS or 0.9% NaCl) and colloids for hemorrhagic shock; administer flunixin meglumine (1.1 mg/kg IV) for pain and anti-inflammatory effect. Minor injuries are managed conservatively with stall rest, serial ultrasound monitoring, and broad-spectrum antimicrobials (e.g., gentamicin 6.6 mg/kg IV q24h plus penicillin). Severe cases with uncontrolled hemorrhage, vascular pedicle avulsion, or extensive urine leakage require nephrectomy via flank or ventral midline celiotomy.
treatment_ja: 初期安定化として乳酸リンゲル液または生理食塩水の静脈内輸液およびコロイド液による出血性ショックの治療を行い、フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg IV）を鎮痛・抗炎症目的で投与する。軽度損傷には馬房安静、連続超音波モニタリング、広域抗菌薬（ゲンタマイシン6.6 mg/kg IV q24hおよびペニシリン）による保存療法を実施する。制御不能な出血、腎血管茎断裂、広範な尿漏出を伴う重症例では、側腹部または腹部正中切開による腎摘出術が必要となる。

name: Renal Behavioral Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal behavioral disorder in horses involves abnormal behaviors (such as posturing to urinate frequently, straining, or dribbling urine) that arise secondary to renal pain, inflammation, or dysfunction. Renal pathology including nephrolithiasis, pyelonephritis, or renal neoplasia can stimulate visceral pain pathways, leading to altered posture, frequent urination attempts, and behavioral changes such as restlessness, flank-watching, or reluctance to move. Chronic renal discomfort may also result in decreased performance, irritability, and changes in appetite due to ongoing nociceptive stimulation.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎行動障害は、腎臓の疼痛、炎症、または機能障害に続発して生じる異常行動（頻繁な排尿姿勢、いきみ、尿の滴下など）を伴います。腎結石症、腎盂腎炎、腎腫瘍などの腎病変が内臓痛経路を刺激し、排尿姿勢の変化、頻尿、落ち着きのなさや腹部を気にする行動などの行動変化を引き起こします。慢性的な腎臓の不快感は、持続的な侵害受容刺激により運動能力の低下、易刺激性、食欲変化をもたらすこともあります。
causes: Primary causes include nephrolithiasis (kidney stones), pyelonephritis, renal cysts, renal neoplasia, and ectopic ureters causing renal pain or irritation. Secondary causes may include chronic urinary tract infections, toxin-induced nephropathy (such as from aminoglycosides or NSAIDs), or systemic diseases affecting renal function. Psychogenic polydipsia or learned behavioral patterns following a resolved renal insult may also contribute.
treatment: Address the underlying renal pathology: surgical removal of nephroliths if present, antimicrobial therapy (trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole or enrofloxacin) for pyelonephritis, and IV fluid therapy to support renal perfusion. Manage pain with flunixin meglumine (1.1 mg/kg IV) or butorphanol (0.01-0.04 mg/kg IV). Discontinue nephrotoxic agents and monitor renal parameters (BUN, creatinine, GGT) serially.
treatment_ja: 基礎的な腎疾患を治療する：腎結石があれば外科的除去、腎盂腎炎にはトリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾールまたはエンロフロキサシンによる抗菌療法、腎灌流維持のための静脈内輸液療法を実施する。疼痛管理にはフルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg IV）またはブトルファノール（0.01-0.04 mg/kg IV）を用いる。腎毒性薬剤を中止し、BUN・クレアチニン・GGTなど腎機能指標を継続的にモニタリングする。

name: Renal Infectious Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infectious disease in horses involves bacterial invasion of the renal parenchyma, typically via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract or hematogenous spread. Bacteria such as Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., and Actinobacillus spp. colonize the renal pelvis and parenchyma, causing inflammation (pyelonephritis), abscess formation, and progressive destruction of nephrons. This leads to impaired renal filtration, tubular dysfunction, azotemia, and potentially sepsis if untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症は、主に下部尿路からの上行性感染または血行性播種により細菌が腎実質に侵入することで発生します。大腸菌、レンサ球菌、アクチノバチルス属などの細菌が腎盂および腎実質に定着し、炎症（腎盂腎炎）、膿瘍形成、ネフロンの進行性破壊を引き起こします。これにより腎濾過機能や尿細管機能が障害され、高窒素血症や敗血症に至る可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infections (most commonly E. coli, Streptococcus spp., Corynebacterium spp., and Actinobacillus equuli), often secondary to urolithiasis, bladder paralysis, or urethral obstruction. Secondary causes include hematogenous spread from distant infections, immunosuppression, catheterization-related contamination, and anatomical abnormalities predisposing to urinary stasis.
treatment: Administer systemic antibiotics based on culture and sensitivity, such as trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (30 mg/kg PO BID) or enrofloxacin (5 mg/kg IV/PO SID) for 2-4 weeks. Provide aggressive IV fluid therapy (balanced polyionic solutions) to maintain renal perfusion and promote diuresis. Address underlying causes such as urolithiasis or obstruction surgically if indicated, and monitor renal function via serial bloodwork and urinalysis.
treatment_ja: 培養・感受性試験に基づき、トリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾール（30 mg/kg PO BID）またはエンロフロキサシン（5 mg/kg IV/PO SID）を2〜4週間全身投与する。積極的な輸液療法（バランス電解質液の静脈内投与）により腎灌流を維持し利尿を促進する。尿路結石や閉塞などの基礎疾患がある場合は外科的に対処し、血液検査および尿検査を定期的に実施して腎機能をモニタリングする。

name: Renal Parasitic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal parasitic disease in horses involves migration and colonization of parasites such as Halicephalobus gingivalis (Halicephalobus deletrix), Strongylus vulgaris larvae, or Dioctophyme renale within the renal parenchyma or vasculature. Parasitic invasion causes granulomatous inflammation, tubular destruction, interstitial nephritis, and potentially abscess formation, leading to progressive renal dysfunction. Larval migration through renal vasculature can also cause thrombosis, infarction, and hemorrhage within the kidney.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎寄生虫症は、Halicephalobus gingivalis、普通円虫（Strongylus vulgaris）の幼虫、または腎虫（Dioctophyme renale）などの寄生虫が腎実質や血管系に移行・定着することで発症します。寄生虫の侵入により肉芽腫性炎症、尿細管破壊、間質性腎炎、膿瘍形成が生じ、進行性の腎機能障害を引き起こします。幼虫の腎血管内移行は血栓症、梗塞、腎内出血を引き起こすこともあります。
causes: Primary causes include parasitic infections by Halicephalobus gingivalis (a free-living nematode with opportunistic pathogenicity), migrating Strongylus vulgaris larvae through mesenteric and renal arteries, and rarely Dioctophyme renale (giant kidney worm). Secondary causes include immunosuppression, poor hygiene, and environmental exposure to contaminated soil or water facilitating parasitic entry.
treatment: Administer high-dose fenbendazole (10 mg/kg PO daily for 5 days) or ivermectin (0.2 mg/kg PO) targeting migrating larvae; for Halicephalobus gingivalis, prolonged anthelmintic therapy with fenbendazole or moxidectin is attempted though prognosis is guarded. Supportive care includes IV fluids for renal support, NSAIDs (flunixin meglumine 1.1 mg/kg IV) for inflammation, and nephrectomy of the affected kidney in unilateral severe cases.
treatment_ja: フェンベンダゾール高用量投与（10 mg/kg 経口、5日間連続）またはイベルメクチン（0.2 mg/kg 経口）で移行幼虫を駆除する。Halicephalobus gingivalis感染にはフェンベンダゾールまたはモキシデクチンの長期投与を試みるが予後は慎重である。補液による腎支持療法、フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg 静注）による抗炎症治療を行い、片側性の重症例では患側腎の腎摘出術を検討する。

name: Renal Viral Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Viral agents such as equine herpesvirus (EHV) or equine arteritis virus (EAV) can cause systemic vasculitis and immune-mediated damage to the renal vasculature and glomeruli, leading to impaired renal filtration, tubular necrosis, and progressive loss of kidney function. Immune complex deposition in glomerular capillaries and direct viral cytopathic effects on renal tubular epithelial cells contribute to interstitial nephritis and renal insufficiency.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬ヘルペスウイルス（EHV）や馬動脈炎ウイルス（EAV）などのウイルスが全身性血管炎や免疫介在性の腎血管・糸球体障害を引き起こし、腎濾過機能の低下、尿細管壊死、進行性の腎機能不全をもたらす。糸球体毛細血管への免疫複合体沈着やウイルスの直接的な細胞障害作用により、間質性腎炎および腎不全が生じる。
causes: Primary causes include equine herpesvirus (EHV-1, EHV-4), equine arteritis virus (EAV), and potentially other systemic viral infections that have tropism for renal tissue. Secondary causes include immune complex-mediated glomerulonephritis following chronic viral infection, dehydration, and concurrent bacterial superinfection exacerbating renal damage.
treatment: No specific antiviral cure exists; treatment is supportive. Administer IV balanced polyionic fluids to maintain renal perfusion and correct electrolyte imbalances. Use flunixin meglumine (1.1 mg/kg IV q12-24h) for anti-inflammatory support, broad-spectrum antibiotics to prevent secondary infections, and ACE inhibitors (e.g., benazepril) if proteinuria is significant. Monitor renal values closely and adjust fluid therapy accordingly.
treatment_ja: 特異的な抗ウイルス治療法はなく、支持療法が中心となる。腎灌流の維持と電解質補正のため、バランス型ポリイオン輸液を静脈内投与する。フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg IV 12-24時間毎）による抗炎症療法、二次感染予防のための広域抗菌薬投与、蛋白尿が顕著な場合はACE阻害薬（ベナゼプリル等）を使用する。腎機能値を綿密にモニタリングし、輸液療法を適宜調整する。

name: Renal Bacterial Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Bacterial pathogens, commonly Escherichia coli, Actinobacillus spp., Streptococcus spp., or Corynebacterium spp., ascend via the urinary tract or spread hematogenously to the renal parenchyma. This leads to inflammatory infiltration, abscess formation, tubular damage, and progressive nephritis that can impair glomerular filtration and concentrating ability. Chronic infection may result in pyelonephritis, fibrosis, and eventual renal failure if left untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 大腸菌、アクチノバチルス属、レンサ球菌属、コリネバクテリウム属などの細菌が尿路上行性感染または血行性に腎実質に到達し、炎症性浸潤、膿瘍形成、尿細管障害を引き起こします。慢性化すると腎盂腎炎、線維化が進行し、糸球体濾過率および濃縮能が低下し、最終的に腎不全に至る可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include ascending urinary tract infections (commonly E. coli, Streptococcus spp., Corynebacterium renale, Actinobacillus spp.) and hematogenous spread from distant infection sites. Secondary causes and predisposing factors include urolithiasis, urinary tract obstruction, bladder paralysis, immunosuppression, catheterization, and concurrent systemic infections such as strangles or endocarditis.
treatment: Initiate aggressive systemic antibiotic therapy based on urine culture and sensitivity; common first-line choices include trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (30 mg/kg PO BID) or enrofloxacin (5 mg/kg IV/PO SID). Provide IV fluid therapy to maintain renal perfusion and correct electrolyte imbalances. Address underlying predisposing factors such as urolithiasis or urinary obstruction surgically if indicated.
treatment_ja: 尿培養・感受性試験に基づき、トリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾール（30 mg/kg 経口 1日2回）またはエンロフロキサシン（5 mg/kg 静注/経口 1日1回）などの全身性抗菌薬療法を積極的に開始する。静脈輸液療法により腎灌流を維持し、電解質異常を補正する。尿路結石や尿路閉塞などの基礎疾患が存在する場合は、必要に応じて外科的処置を実施する。

name: Renal Fungal Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Fungal organisms, most commonly Aspergillus spp. or Candida spp., colonize the renal parenchyma and/or renal pelvis, causing granulomatous or necrotizing inflammation. This leads to progressive destruction of renal tissue, impaired renal function, and potential formation of fungal masses (fungal balls) obstructing the urinary tract. Hematogenous dissemination or ascending infection from the lower urinary tract may be involved in pathogenesis.
pathophysiology_ja: Aspergillus属やCandida属などの真菌が腎実質や腎盂に定着し、肉芽腫性または壊死性炎症を引き起こす。これにより腎組織の進行性破壊、腎機能障害、および尿路を閉塞する真菌塊（ファンガルボール）の形成が生じる。血行性播種または下部尿路からの上行感染が病態に関与する。
causes: Primary causes include opportunistic fungal infections by Aspergillus spp., Candida spp., or other fungi, often secondary to immunosuppression, prolonged antibiotic therapy, or corticosteroid use. Predisposing factors include chronic illness, indwelling urinary catheters, diabetes mellitus, and any condition causing immunocompromise. Secondary bacterial infections may complicate the fungal disease.
causes_ja: 主な原因はAspergillus属、Candida属などによる日和見真菌感染であり、免疫抑制、長期抗菌薬投与、コルチコステロイド使用に続発することが多い。慢性疾患、留置カテーテル、糖尿病、その他の免疫不全状態が素因となる。二次的な細菌感染が合併することがある。
treatment: Systemic antifungal therapy with amphotericin B (0.3–0.5 mg/kg IV slowly, every 48 hrs) combined with fluconazole (2–5 mg/kg PO q24h) for prolonged duration. Discontinue immunosuppressive drugs and antibiotics if possible. Nephrectomy may be indicated for unilateral fungal masses unresponsive to medical therapy; supportive IV fluid therapy to maintain renal perfusion.
treatment_ja: アムホテリシンB（0.3〜0.5 mg/kg、48時間ごとに緩徐に静注）とフルコナゾール（2〜5 mg/kg、1日1回経口投与）による長期的な全身性抗真菌療法を実施する。免疫抑制薬や抗菌薬は可能な限り中止する。片側性の真菌塊が内科療法に反応しない場合は腎摘出術を検討し、腎灌流維持のため補液療法を併用する。

name: Renal Infection (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infection (pyelonephritis) in horses typically results from ascending bacterial infection via the ureters from the lower urinary tract, or less commonly through hematogenous spread. Bacteria colonize the renal pelvis and parenchyma, causing inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue. Chronic infection can lead to fibrosis, impaired renal function, and potentially septicemia if left untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路から尿管を経由した上行性細菌感染、またはまれに血行性播種によって生じます。細菌が腎盂および腎実質に定着し、炎症、膿瘍形成、腎組織の進行性破壊を引き起こします。慢性感染は線維化、腎機能障害、未治療の場合は敗血症に至る可能性があります。
causes: The most common causative organisms include Escherichia coli, Proteus spp., Klebsiella spp., Streptococcus spp., and Corynebacterium renale. Predisposing factors include urolithiasis, urinary tract obstruction, bladder paralysis, catheterization, and immunosuppression. Mares may be more susceptible due to their shorter urethra facilitating ascending infection.
treatment: Initiate prolonged antibiotic therapy (4-6 weeks) based on urine culture and sensitivity, commonly trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (30 mg/kg PO BID) or enrofloxacin (5 mg/kg IV/PO SID). Provide IV fluid therapy to maintain hydration and promote diuresis. Address underlying predisposing factors such as urolithiasis or urinary obstruction surgically if needed.
treatment_ja: 尿培養・感受性試験に基づき、トリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾール（30 mg/kg 経口 BID）またはエンロフロキサシン（5 mg/kg 静注/経口 SID）などの抗菌薬を4〜6週間長期投与する。輸液療法により水分補給と利尿促進を図る。尿路結石や尿路閉塞などの基礎疾患がある場合は外科的処置を含め適切に対処する。

name: Renal Inflammation (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal inflammation (nephritis) in horses involves immune-mediated or infectious damage to the glomeruli, tubules, or interstitium of the kidneys, leading to impaired filtration, protein loss, electrolyte imbalances, and accumulation of metabolic waste products. Inflammatory cell infiltration and edema compromise renal blood flow and tubular function, potentially progressing to fibrosis and chronic renal insufficiency. Immune complex deposition, direct bacterial infection, or toxic insult can trigger the inflammatory cascade within the renal parenchyma.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎炎は、免疫介在性または感染性の障害により糸球体、尿細管、または間質に炎症が生じ、濾過機能の低下、タンパク質の喪失、電解質異常、代謝老廃物の蓄積を引き起こします。炎症細胞の浸潤と浮腫により腎血流と尿細管機能が障害され、線維化や慢性腎不全へ進行する可能性があります。免疫複合体の沈着、直接的な細菌感染、または毒性物質が腎実質内の炎症カスケードを引き起こします。
causes: Primary causes include bacterial infections (e.g., Leptospira spp., Streptococcus equi), viral infections (e.g., equine infectious anemia), and nephrotoxic agents such as aminoglycoside antibiotics, NSAIDs, or heavy metals. Secondary causes include immune complex deposition from systemic diseases, septicemia, endotoxemia, dehydration-induced ischemic injury, and pigment nephropathy from myoglobinuria or hemoglobinuria. Ingestion of nephrotoxic plants (e.g., oak, red maple) can also contribute to renal inflammation.
treatment: Discontinue nephrotoxic agents (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides) immediately. Administer aggressive IV fluid therapy (balanced crystalloids) to restore renal perfusion and correct electrolyte imbalances. Treat underlying infections with renal-safe antibiotics (e.g., penicillin); consider corticosteroids (dexamethasone 0.05-0.1 mg/kg IV) for immune-mediated nephritis, and provide supportive care including dietary protein restriction and monitoring of serum creatinine and BUN.
treatment_ja: 腎毒性薬剤（NSAIDs、アミノグリコシド系抗生物質）を直ちに中止する。積極的な静脈内輸液療法（バランス晶質液）を実施し、腎灌流の回復と電解質補正を図る。基礎感染症には腎安全性の高い抗生物質（ペニシリン等）を投与し、免疫介在性腎炎にはデキサメタゾン（0.05〜0.1 mg/kg IV）を検討する。食事中のタンパク質制限、血清クレアチニンおよびBUNのモニタリングなどの支持療法を継続する。

name: Renal Neoplasia (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal neoplasia in horses involves the uncontrolled proliferation of abnormal cells within the kidney parenchyma or renal pelvis. The most commonly reported types include renal cell carcinoma, nephroblastoma, and lymphoma, which may disrupt normal renal architecture, impair kidney function, and potentially metastasize to lungs, liver, and other organs. Progressive tumor growth can lead to hematuria, hydronephrosis, renal insufficiency, and paraneoplastic syndromes.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎腫瘍は、腎実質または腎盂における異常細胞の無制御な増殖を伴う。最も一般的に報告される種類には腎細胞癌、腎芽腫（ネフロブラストーマ）、リンパ腫があり、正常な腎構造を破壊し、腎機能を障害し、肺や肝臓など他の臓器に転移する可能性がある。腫瘍の進行により血尿、水腎症、腎不全、および腫瘍随伴症候群が生じることがある。
causes: The exact etiology of renal neoplasia in horses is largely unknown, with no consistently identified genetic or environmental risk factors. Renal cell carcinoma is the most common primary renal tumor in adult horses, while nephroblastoma is more frequently seen in young horses and foals, suggesting possible congenital or developmental origins. Lymphoma affecting the kidneys may occur as part of multicentric neoplastic disease.
treatment: Unilateral nephrectomy is the primary treatment for localized renal tumors such as renal cell carcinoma or nephroblastoma, provided the contralateral kidney is functional. Supportive care includes IV fluids, NSAIDs (flunixin meglumine 1.1 mg/kg IV) for pain, and monitoring renal parameters. Chemotherapy options are limited in horses; lymphoma cases may respond to corticosteroids (dexamethasone) or multi-agent protocols.
treatment_ja: 腎細胞癌や腎芽腫などの限局性腎腫瘍には、対側腎の機能が正常であることを確認した上で片側腎摘出術が第一選択となる。術後は輸液療法、フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg IV）による疼痛管理、および腎機能パラメータのモニタリングを行う。馬における化学療法の選択肢は限られるが、リンパ腫の場合はデキサメタゾンなどのコルチコステロイドや多剤併用プロトコルが有効な場合がある。

name: Renal Metabolic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal metabolic disease in horses involves impaired kidney function leading to disruption of electrolyte balance, acid-base homeostasis, and waste product excretion. The kidneys fail to adequately regulate calcium, phosphorus, and bicarbonate metabolism, potentially resulting in hypercalcemia or hyperphosphatemia, metabolic acidosis or alkalosis, and accumulation of uremic toxins. Chronic cases may lead to renal secondary hyperparathyroidism, soft tissue mineralization, and osteodystrophy.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎代謝性疾患は、腎機能の低下により電解質バランス、酸塩基平衡、老廃物排泄の障害が生じる疾患である。腎臓がカルシウム、リン、重炭酸塩の代謝を適切に調節できなくなり、高カルシウム血症や高リン血症、代謝性アシドーシスまたはアルカローシス、尿毒症毒素の蓄積を引き起こす。慢性例では腎性二次性副甲状腺機能亢進症、軟部組織の石灰化、骨異栄養症に進行することがある。
causes: Primary causes include chronic kidney disease, nephrotoxin exposure (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals, vitamin D toxicosis), and nephrolithiasis. Secondary causes include dehydration, systemic infections, hemodynamic compromise, oxalate-containing plant ingestion, and prolonged high-calcium or high-phosphorus diets that stress renal metabolic capacity.
treatment: Administer IV fluid therapy (balanced polyionic solutions) to correct dehydration and promote diuresis. Discontinue nephrotoxic agents (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides). Correct electrolyte imbalances with calcium gluconate or phosphate binders as needed, and manage acidosis with sodium bicarbonate supplementation. Provide dietary modification with reduced protein and calcium intake.
treatment_ja: 脱水補正と利尿促進のため、平衡電解質輸液による静脈内輸液療法を実施する。腎毒性薬剤（NSAIDs、アミノグリコシド系）を直ちに中止する。必要に応じてグルコン酸カルシウムやリン吸着剤で電解質異常を是正し、重炭酸ナトリウムによる代謝性アシドーシスの管理を行う。低タンパク質・低カルシウム食への食事療法も併用する。

name: Renal Nutritional Deficiency (Horse)
pathophysiology: Nutritional deficiencies, particularly of vitamin A, vitamin D, calcium, phosphorus, or oxalate-rich diets, can impair renal tubular function and lead to nephrocalcinosis or renal tubular degeneration in horses. Chronic imbalances in calcium-phosphorus ratios or excessive oxalate ingestion from certain plants interfere with mineral metabolism, leading to calcium deposition in renal parenchyma and progressive renal dysfunction. Vitamin A deficiency may cause squamous metaplasia of renal tubular epithelium, while excess vitamin D can cause dystrophic calcification of renal tissues.
pathophysiology_ja: ビタミンA、ビタミンD、カルシウム、リンなどの栄養素の欠乏や不均衡、またはシュウ酸を多く含む飼料の摂取により、腎尿細管機能が障害され、腎石灰化症や腎尿細管変性が生じる。カルシウム・リン比の慢性的な不均衡やシュウ酸塩の過剰摂取はミネラル代謝を阻害し、腎実質へのカルシウム沈着と進行性の腎機能障害を引き起こす。ビタミンA欠乏は腎尿細管上皮の扁平上皮化生を引き起こし、ビタミンD過剰は腎組織の異栄養性石灰化を引き起こす可能性がある。
treatment: Correct dietary imbalances by adjusting calcium-phosphorus ratio (ideally 1.5-2:1), remove oxalate-rich forages, and supplement vitamin A and D as needed. Provide IV fluid therapy (balanced polyionic solutions) to support renal perfusion. Administer phosphate binders if hyperphosphatemia is present and monitor renal values serially.
treatment_ja: カルシウム・リン比を適正値（理想的には1.5〜2:1）に調整し、シュウ酸含有量の多い飼料を除去、必要に応じてビタミンAおよびDを補給する。腎灌流を維持するためにバランス電解質輸液を静脈内投与する。高リン血症がある場合はリン吸着剤を投与し、腎機能値を定期的にモニタリングする。

name: Renal Genetic Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal genetic disorders in horses involve inherited mutations affecting renal tubular or glomerular structure and function, leading to progressive nephron loss, impaired filtration, and disrupted electrolyte and fluid homeostasis. Specific conditions include renal tubular acidosis, polycystic kidney disease, and renal dysplasia, where abnormal kidney development or degeneration results in chronic renal insufficiency. Progressive fibrosis and loss of functional renal parenchyma ultimately lead to end-stage renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎遺伝性疾患は、腎尿細管や糸球体の構造・機能に影響を与える遺伝子変異に起因し、進行性のネフロン喪失、濾過機能障害、電解質・水分バランスの乱れを引き起こす。腎尿細管性アシドーシス、多発性嚢胞腎、腎異形成などが含まれ、腎臓の異常発達や変性により慢性腎不全に至る。進行性の線維化と機能的腎実質の喪失が最終的に末期腎不全をもたらす。
causes: The primary cause is inherited genetic mutations, often autosomal recessive or dominant, affecting genes responsible for normal renal development, tubular transport, or structural protein synthesis. Specific examples include mutations causing renal dysplasia in certain horse breeds and polycystic kidney disease. Secondary factors such as dehydration, concurrent infections, or nephrotoxic drug exposure may accelerate disease progression.
treatment: No curative treatment exists for renal genetic disorders in horses; management is supportive. Administer IV balanced crystalloid fluids (e.g., lactated Ringer's solution) to maintain hydration and electrolyte balance. Provide oral sodium bicarbonate (50-100 g/day) for renal tubular acidosis, dietary phosphorus restriction, ACE inhibitors such as benazepril (0.5 mg/kg PO q24h) for proteinuria, and monitor renal values regularly to slow disease progression.
treatment_ja: 馬の腎遺伝性疾患に根治的治療法は存在せず、管理は対症療法が中心となる。乳酸リンゲル液などの等張晶質液を静脈内投与し、水分・電解質バランスを維持する。腎尿細管性アシドーシスには重炭酸ナトリウム（50～100 g/日、経口）を投与し、食事中のリン制限、蛋白尿に対してはベナゼプリル（0.5 mg/kg、経口、1日1回）などのACE阻害薬を使用する。腎機能指標を定期的にモニタリングし、疾患進行の抑制に努める。

name: Renal Autoimmune Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: The immune system produces autoantibodies or autoreactive lymphocytes directed against renal antigens, including glomerular basement membrane components and tubular epithelial cells. Immune complex deposition in the glomeruli and tubulointerstitial regions triggers complement activation, inflammatory cell infiltration, and progressive renal tissue damage. This leads to glomerulonephritis, tubular necrosis, interstitial fibrosis, and progressive loss of renal function.
pathophysiology_ja: 免疫系が糸球体基底膜成分や尿細管上皮細胞などの腎抗原に対する自己抗体または自己反応性リンパ球を産生します。糸球体および尿細管間質領域への免疫複合体の沈着が補体活性化、炎症細胞浸潤、進行性の腎組織障害を引き起こします。これにより糸球体腎炎、尿細管壊死、間質線維化、腎機能の進行性低下が生じます。
causes: Primary causes include idiopathic autoimmune dysregulation targeting renal antigens, potentially triggered by molecular mimicry following infectious diseases such as Streptococcus equi or viral infections. Secondary causes include chronic immune complex disease associated with equine infectious anemia, systemic lupus-like syndromes, drug-induced immune responses, and chronic inflammatory conditions that lead to persistent immune complex deposition in the kidneys.
treatment: Immunosuppressive therapy with corticosteroids (dexamethasone 0.05-0.1 mg/kg IV initially, transitioning to oral prednisolone) is the cornerstone. Add azathioprine (3 mg/kg PO q24h) for steroid-sparing effect in refractory cases. Supportive care includes IV fluid therapy, ACE inhibitors (benazepril 0.5 mg/kg PO) for proteinuria management, and monitoring renal parameters closely.
treatment_ja: 免疫抑制療法として副腎皮質ステロイド（デキサメタゾン0.05-0.1 mg/kg IV、その後経口プレドニゾロンへ移行）を基本とする。難治例にはアザチオプリン（3 mg/kg PO q24h）をステロイド減量目的で併用する。支持療法として輸液療法、蛋白尿管理のためACE阻害薬（ベナゼプリル0.5 mg/kg PO）を投与し、腎機能パラメータを綿密にモニタリングする。

name: Renal Degenerative Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal degenerative disease in horses involves progressive deterioration of nephron structure and function, including tubular degeneration, interstitial fibrosis, and glomerulosclerosis. This leads to impaired glomerular filtration, loss of concentrating ability, and eventual accumulation of uremic toxins. Chronic ischemia, oxidative stress, and inflammatory mediators contribute to irreversible parenchymal damage and progressive loss of functional renal mass.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎変性疾患は、尿細管変性、間質線維化、糸球体硬化症を含むネフロン構造と機能の進行性悪化を伴います。これにより糸球体濾過率の低下、濃縮能の喪失、尿毒症性毒素の蓄積が生じます。慢性虚血、酸化ストレス、炎症性メディエーターが不可逆的な実質障害と機能的腎量の進行性喪失に寄与します。
causes: Primary causes include chronic nephrotoxin exposure (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals, vitamin D toxicosis), chronic renal ischemia, and age-related degeneration. Secondary causes include systemic diseases such as leptospirosis, equine infectious anemia, immune-mediated glomerulonephritis, nephrolithiasis, and prolonged dehydration or hemodynamic compromise leading to chronic renal hypoperfusion.
treatment: No curative treatment exists; management focuses on supportive care. Discontinue nephrotoxins immediately. Provide IV fluid therapy (balanced polyionic solutions) to correct dehydration and electrolyte imbalances. Manage uremia with dietary protein restriction, phosphate binders (aluminum hydroxide), and gastroprotectants (omeprazole 1-4 mg/kg PO SID). ACE inhibitors (benazepril) may reduce proteinuria.
treatment_ja: 根治療法は存在せず、対症療法が中心となる。腎毒性物質の投与を直ちに中止し、脱水・電解質異常の補正のためバランス電解質輸液を静脈内投与する。尿毒症管理として食事中タンパク質制限、リン吸着剤（水酸化アルミニウム）、胃粘膜保護薬（オメプラゾール1-4 mg/kg 経口1日1回）を使用する。ACE阻害薬（ベナゼプリル）はタンパク尿軽減に有用である。

name: Renal Traumatic Injury (Horse)
pathophysiology: Blunt or penetrating trauma to the flank or lumbar region causes direct damage to the renal parenchyma, capsule, or renal vasculature. This leads to hemorrhage (subcapsular or perirenal hematoma), possible urine leakage (uroperitoneum or uroretroperitoneum), inflammation, and potentially ischemic necrosis of renal tissue. Secondary complications include infection, adhesion formation, and progressive loss of renal function if damage is extensive or bilateral.
pathophysiology_ja: 腰部や側腹部への鈍的または穿通性外傷により、腎実質、腎被膜、または腎血管系に直接的な損傷が生じる。これにより出血（被膜下または腎周囲血腫）、尿漏出（尿腹症または後腹膜尿浸潤）、炎症、および腎組織の虚血性壊死が起こり得る。二次的合併症として感染、癒着形成、および広範囲または両側性損傷の場合は進行性の腎機能低下が生じる可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include blunt abdominal trauma from kicks by other horses, falls, collisions with fixed objects, or vehicular accidents. Penetrating injuries from fence posts, sharp objects, or surgical complications can also cause renal damage. Less commonly, severe exercise-related trauma or fractured ribs impinging on the kidney may be responsible.
treatment: Stabilize with IV crystalloid fluids (LRS or 0.9% NaCl) and control hemorrhage; administer flunixin meglumine (1.1 mg/kg IV q12h) for pain and anti-endotoxic effects. Broad-spectrum antibiotics (gentamicin 6.6 mg/kg IV q24h plus penicillin 22,000 IU/kg IV q6h) prevent secondary infection. Severe cases with uncontrolled hemorrhage or shattered kidney require nephrectomy; subcapsular hematomas may be managed conservatively with stall rest and serial ultrasound monitoring.
treatment_ja: 乳酸リンゲル液または生理食塩水による積極的な輸液療法で循環を安定させ、フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg IV 12時間毎）で鎮痛・抗エンドトキシン効果を図る。ゲンタマイシン（6.6 mg/kg IV 24時間毎）およびペニシリン（22,000 IU/kg IV 6時間毎）の広域抗菌薬で二次感染を予防する。制御不能な出血や腎臓の高度破裂には腎摘出術を実施し、被膜下血腫は馬房安静と連続超音波モニタリングによる保存的管理が可能である。

name: Renal Behavioral Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal behavioral disorder in horses involves abnormal behaviors arising from chronic renal pain or discomfort due to underlying kidney pathology such as nephrolithiasis, nephritis, or renal neoplasia. Persistent nociceptive input from the renal capsule or parenchyma leads to altered behavior patterns including flank guarding, stretching postures, and changes in urination habits. The disorder may also involve referred pain to the lumbar and sublumbar regions, affecting gait and temperament.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎行動障害は、腎結石症、腎炎、腎腫瘍などの基礎的な腎臓病変による慢性的な腎臓痛や不快感から生じる異常行動を伴います。腎被膜や実質からの持続的な侵害受容入力により、側腹部の防御姿勢、伸展姿勢、排尿習慣の変化などの行動パターンの変化が生じます。腰部および腰下部への関連痛が歩様や気質にも影響を及ぼす場合があります。
causes: Primary causes include nephrolithiasis, chronic interstitial nephritis, pyelonephritis, renal cysts, and renal neoplasia causing persistent renal discomfort. Secondary causes may include ureterolithiasis, chronic urinary tract infections, and toxin-induced nephropathy (e.g., from aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, or pigment nephropathy) that result in ongoing renal pain and associated behavioral changes.
treatment: Address underlying renal pathology: surgical removal of nephroliths or neoplasia if indicated; manage pyelonephritis with appropriate antibiotics (trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole or enrofloxacin). Provide analgesia with flunixin meglumine (1.1 mg/kg IV q12-24h) or firocoxib for chronic pain. Supportive care includes IV fluid therapy to maintain renal perfusion and behavioral modification through environmental enrichment.
treatment_ja: 原因となる腎病変への対処として、腎結石や腫瘍の外科的除去を検討し、腎盂腎炎にはトリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾールまたはエンロフロキサシン等の抗菌薬を投与する。疼痛管理としてフルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg IV q12-24h）またはフィロコキシブを使用する。補液療法による腎灌流維持と環境エンリッチメントによる行動改善を併せて行う。

name: Renal Infectious Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infectious disease in horses involves bacterial colonization of the renal parenchyma, typically ascending from the lower urinary tract or via hematogenous spread. Infection leads to inflammation (pyelonephritis), abscess formation, and progressive damage to renal tubules and glomeruli, potentially resulting in impaired renal function, septicemia, and renal failure if untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症は、下部尿路からの上行性感染または血行性播種により細菌が腎実質に定着することで発生します。感染により腎盂腎炎や膿瘍形成が起こり、腎尿細管および糸球体の進行性障害を引き起こし、未治療の場合は腎機能障害や敗血症、腎不全に至る可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include bacterial infections, most commonly Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Staphylococcus spp., and Corynebacterium spp., ascending from the lower urinary tract. Secondary causes include urolithiasis, urinary tract obstruction, immunosuppression, catheterization, and hematogenous spread from distant infection sites.
causes_ja: 主な原因は大腸菌、連鎖球菌、ブドウ球菌、コリネバクテリウムなどの細菌による下部尿路からの上行性感染です。二次的原因として尿路結石、尿路閉塞、免疫抑制、カテーテル留置、および遠隔感染巣からの血行性播種が挙げられます。
treatment: Initiate broad-spectrum antibiotic therapy based on urine culture and sensitivity, commonly trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (30 mg/kg PO BID) or enrofloxacin (5 mg/kg IV/PO SID). Provide aggressive IV fluid therapy (lactated Ringer's solution) to maintain renal perfusion and promote diuresis. Address underlying causes such as urolithiasis or obstruction surgically if needed, and monitor renal function via serial bloodwork and urinalysis.
treatment_ja: 尿培養および感受性試験に基づき、トリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾール（30 mg/kg 経口 BID）またはエンロフロキサシン（5 mg/kg 静注/経口 SID）などの広域抗菌薬療法を開始する。乳酸リンゲル液による積極的な輸液療法を行い、腎灌流の維持と利尿を促進する。尿石症や尿路閉塞などの基礎疾患がある場合は外科的に対処し、血液検査および尿検査で腎機能を継続的にモニタリングする。

name: Renal Parasitic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal parasitic disease in horses involves migration and colonization of parasites such as Halicephalobus gingivalis (Halicephalobus deletrix), Strongylus vulgaris larvae, or Dioctophyme renale within the renal parenchyma or vasculature. Parasitic invasion causes granulomatous inflammation, tissue destruction, fibrosis, and impaired renal function. Larval migration through renal arteries can also lead to thrombosis, infarction, and secondary bacterial infection of the kidneys.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎寄生虫病は、Halicephalobus gingivalis、普通円虫（Strongylus vulgaris）の幼虫、または腎虫（Dioctophyme renale）などの寄生虫が腎実質や血管系に移行・定着することで発症する。寄生虫の侵入は肉芽腫性炎症、組織破壊、線維化、腎機能障害を引き起こす。幼虫の腎動脈への移行は血栓症、梗塞、および二次的細菌感染を誘発することもある。
causes: Primary causes include parasitic infection by Halicephalobus gingivalis (rhabditid nematode), aberrant migration of Strongylus vulgaris larvae through the renal vasculature, and rarely Dioctophyme renale (giant kidney worm). Secondary causes include immunosuppression, heavy parasite burdens due to inadequate deworming, and environmental exposure to contaminated soil or water containing infective larvae.
treatment: Administer broad-spectrum anthelmintics such as ivermectin (0.2 mg/kg PO) or fenbendazole (10 mg/kg PO daily for 5 days) to target migrating larvae. For Halicephalobus gingivalis, prognosis is grave; high-dose moxidectin or ivermectin may be attempted alongside NSAIDs (flunixin meglumine 1.1 mg/kg IV) for inflammation. Nephrectomy may be considered for unilateral Dioctophyme renale infection with supportive fluid therapy.
treatment_ja: 駆虫薬としてイベルメクチン（0.2 mg/kg 経口）またはフェンベンダゾール（10 mg/kg 経口、5日間連続投与）を投与し、移行幼虫を標的とする。Halicephalobus gingivalis感染では予後は極めて不良であり、高用量モキシデクチンまたはイベルメクチンの投与を試みつつ、フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg 静注）で炎症を管理する。Dioctophyme renaleの片側性感染では腎摘出術を検討し、輸液療法による支持療法を併用する。

name: Renal Viral Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Viral agents such as equine herpesvirus (EHV) or equine arteritis virus (EAV) can cause systemic vasculitis and immune-mediated damage to renal glomeruli and tubules, leading to impaired renal filtration and function. Viral replication within renal endothelial and epithelial cells triggers inflammatory infiltration, tubular necrosis, and interstitial nephritis, resulting in progressive renal dysfunction.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬ヘルペスウイルス（EHV）や馬動脈炎ウイルス（EAV）などのウイルスが全身性血管炎および免疫介在性の糸球体・尿細管障害を引き起こし、腎濾過機能が低下します。腎臓の内皮細胞や上皮細胞内でのウイルス増殖により、炎症性細胞浸潤、尿細管壊死、間質性腎炎が生じ、進行性の腎機能障害をもたらします。
causes: Primary causes include viral infections such as equine herpesvirus (EHV-1, EHV-4), equine arteritis virus (EAV), and occasionally equine infectious anemia virus (EIAV) that target or secondarily affect renal tissues. Secondary causes include immune complex deposition, systemic vasculitis, and hemodynamic compromise associated with viremia.
treatment: No specific antiviral therapy is curative; treatment is primarily supportive. Administer IV crystalloid fluids (lactated Ringer's or 0.9% NaCl) to maintain renal perfusion and correct electrolyte imbalances. Use flunixin meglumine (1.1 mg/kg IV q12h) for anti-inflammatory support, and administer broad-spectrum antibiotics (e.g., trimethoprim-sulfa) to prevent secondary infections. Monitor renal values (BUN, creatinine) closely and adjust fluid therapy accordingly.
treatment_ja: 特異的な抗ウイルス療法は存在せず、治療は主に支持療法となる。乳酸リンゲル液または生理食塩水の静脈内輸液により腎灌流を維持し、電解質異常を補正する。フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg IV 12時間ごと）で抗炎症療法を行い、トリメトプリム・スルファなどの広域抗菌薬で二次感染を予防する。BUN・クレアチニンなどの腎機能指標を頻回にモニタリングし、輸液療法を適宜調整する。

name: Renal Bacterial Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Bacterial infection of the kidneys (pyelonephritis) in horses typically occurs via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract, or less commonly through hematogenous spread. Bacteria colonize the renal pelvis and parenchyma, causing inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue. Common causative organisms include Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Staphylococcus spp., Corynebacterium renale, and Actinobacillus equuli, leading to impaired renal function if left untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎臓細菌感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、主に下部尿路からの上行性感染、またはまれに血行性播種によって発生します。細菌が腎盂および腎実質に定着し、炎症、膿瘍形成、および腎組織の進行性破壊を引き起こします。主な原因菌には大腸菌、レンサ球菌、ブドウ球菌、Corynebacterium renale、Actinobacillus equuliなどがあり、未治療の場合は腎機能障害に至ります。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infection from the lower urinary tract (cystitis, urethritis), often associated with urolithiasis, urinary stasis, or catheterization. Secondary causes include hematogenous spread from distant infections (e.g., endocarditis, omphalitis in foals), immunosuppression, and anatomical abnormalities that predispose to urinary stasis or reflux.
treatment: Initiate prolonged systemic antibiotic therapy (4-6 weeks) based on urine culture and sensitivity, commonly trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole or enrofloxacin. Provide IV fluid therapy to maintain renal perfusion and correct electrolyte imbalances. Address underlying causes such as urolithiasis removal or urinary catheter management, and consider nephrectomy for unilateral renal abscessation unresponsive to medical therapy.
treatment_ja: 尿培養・感受性試験に基づき、トリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾールやエンロフロキサシン等の全身性抗菌薬を4〜6週間長期投与する。輸液療法により腎灌流を維持し電解質異常を補正する。尿路結石の除去やカテーテル管理など原因疾患の治療を行い、片側性腎膿瘍で内科療法に反応しない場合は腎摘出術を検討する。

name: Renal Fungal Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Fungal organisms (commonly Aspergillus spp., Candida spp., or Mucor spp.) colonize the renal parenchyma, leading to granulomatous or necrotizing inflammation. The infection may cause progressive destruction of renal tissue, formation of fungal granulomas or fungal balls within the renal pelvis, and impaired renal function. Hematogenous dissemination or ascending infection from the lower urinary tract can result in unilateral or bilateral renal involvement.
pathophysiology_ja: 真菌（主にAspergillus属、Candida属、Mucor属など）が腎実質に定着し、肉芽腫性または壊死性の炎症を引き起こす。感染は腎組織の進行性破壊、腎盂内の真菌肉芽腫または真菌塊の形成、および腎機能障害をもたらす。血行性播種または下部尿路からの上行性感染により、片側性または両側性の腎障害が生じうる。
causes: Primary causes include opportunistic fungal infections (Aspergillus spp., Candida spp., Cryptococcus spp.) that invade the kidneys, often following immunosuppression, prolonged antibiotic therapy, or corticosteroid use. Secondary causes include pre-existing renal damage, urinary tract obstruction, indwelling urinary catheters, and systemic debilitation that predispose the horse to fungal colonization.
treatment: Administer systemic antifungal therapy with fluconazole (5 mg/kg PO q24h) or amphotericin B (0.3-0.5 mg/kg IV slowly, with careful nephrotoxicity monitoring). Discontinue immunosuppressive agents and prolonged antibiotics. Provide IV fluid therapy for renal support; consider nephrectomy if unilateral disease with extensive parenchymal destruction or obstructive fungal balls are present.
treatment_ja: フルコナゾール（5 mg/kg 経口 1日1回）またはアムホテリシンB（0.3〜0.5 mg/kg 緩徐静注、腎毒性を慎重にモニタリング）による全身性抗真菌療法を実施する。免疫抑制剤および長期抗菌薬は中止する。輸液療法で腎機能を補助し、片側性の広範な腎実質破壊や閉塞性真菌塊が認められる場合は腎摘出術を検討する。

name: Renal Infection (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infection (pyelonephritis) in horses typically occurs via ascending bacterial infection from the lower urinary tract through the ureters to the renal pelvis and parenchyma. Bacteria colonize the renal medulla, inciting an inflammatory response that leads to tissue destruction, abscess formation, and progressive loss of renal function. Hematogenous spread from distant infection sites is less common but can also seed the kidneys, particularly in immunocompromised or debilitated horses.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路から尿管を経由して腎盂および腎実質へ細菌が上行性に感染することで発生します。細菌が腎髄質に定着し、炎症反応を引き起こすことで組織破壊、膿瘍形成、および腎機能の進行性低下をもたらします。遠隔感染巣からの血行性播種はまれですが、免疫力が低下した馬では発生する可能性があります。
causes: The most common causative agents include Escherichia coli, Proteus spp., Klebsiella spp., Streptococcus spp., and Corynebacterium renale, typically ascending from lower urinary tract infections, cystitis, or urolithiasis. Predisposing factors include urinary stasis, bladder paralysis (e.g., from cauda equina syndrome or equine herpesvirus-1 myelopathy), urethral obstruction, catheterization, and immunosuppression. Nephrolithiasis can also serve as a nidus for chronic renal infection.
treatment: Initiate prolonged systemic antibiotic therapy (4-6 weeks) based on urine culture and sensitivity, commonly trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole or enrofloxacin. Provide IV fluid therapy to promote diuresis and correct dehydration. Address underlying predisposing factors such as urolithiasis or bladder dysfunction, and consider nephrectomy for unilateral severe cases unresponsive to medical management.
treatment_ja: 尿培養・感受性試験に基づき、トリメトプリム・スルファメトキサゾールやエンロフロキサシン等の全身性抗菌薬を4～6週間長期投与する。輸液療法により利尿を促進し脱水を補正する。尿路結石や膀胱機能障害など基礎疾患の治療を行い、片側性で内科療法に反応しない重症例では腎摘出術を検討する。

name: Renal Inflammation (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal inflammation (nephritis) in horses involves an immune-mediated or infectious inflammatory response affecting the glomeruli, tubules, or interstitium of the kidneys. This leads to impaired filtration, tubular dysfunction, proteinuria, and progressive loss of nephron function. Prolonged inflammation can result in fibrosis, chronic renal insufficiency, and eventual renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎炎（腎臓の炎症）は、糸球体、尿細管、または間質に影響を及ぼす免疫介在性または感染性の炎症反応を伴います。これにより濾過機能の障害、尿細管機能不全、蛋白尿、およびネフロン機能の進行性喪失が生じます。炎症が長期化すると線維化、慢性腎不全へと進行する可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include bacterial infections (e.g., Leptospira, Streptococcus), viral infections (e.g., equine infectious anemia), and immune-mediated glomerulonephritis. Secondary causes include nephrotoxic drugs (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides), systemic infections, toxin exposure (heavy metals, plants such as oak or red maple), and extension of lower urinary tract infections.
causes_ja: 主な原因には細菌感染（レプトスピラ、連鎖球菌など）、ウイルス感染（馬伝染性貧血など）、および免疫介在性糸球体腎炎が含まれます。二次的原因には腎毒性薬物（NSAIDs、アミノグリコシド系薬）、全身性感染症、毒素曝露（重金属、オーク・レッドメープルなどの植物）、および下部尿路感染の波及があります。
treatment: Treat underlying cause with targeted antimicrobials (e.g., penicillin for Streptococcus, oxytetracycline for Leptospira). Discontinue nephrotoxic drugs (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides) immediately. Provide aggressive IV fluid therapy (balanced polyionic solutions) to maintain renal perfusion, correct electrolyte imbalances, and support diuresis. Corticosteroids (dexamethasone) may be considered for immune-mediated nephritis under close monitoring.
treatment_ja: 原因に応じた抗菌薬投与（連鎖球菌にはペニシリン、レプトスピラにはオキシテトラサイクリン等）を実施する。腎毒性薬剤（NSAIDs、アミノグリコシド系）は直ちに中止する。積極的な静脈内輸液療法（バランス電解質液）により腎灌流を維持し、電解質異常を補正し利尿を促進する。免疫介在性腎炎にはデキサメタゾン等の副腎皮質ステロイドを慎重にモニタリングしながら検討する。

name: Renal Neoplasia (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal neoplasia in horses involves abnormal proliferation of renal parenchymal or stromal cells, leading to progressive destruction of normal kidney architecture and impaired renal function. The most commonly reported types include renal cell carcinoma, nephroblastoma, and lymphoma. Tumors may grow locally, obstruct urine flow, cause hematuria, and in malignant cases metastasize to lungs, liver, and other organs.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎腫瘍は、腎実質または間質細胞の異常増殖により正常な腎構造が進行性に破壊され、腎機能が障害される疾患である。最も多く報告される腫瘍型は腎細胞癌、腎芽腫（ネフロブラストーマ）、およびリンパ腫である。腫瘍は局所的に増大し、尿路閉塞や血尿を引き起こし、悪性の場合は肺や肝臓などへ転移することがある。
causes: The exact etiology of renal neoplasia in horses is largely unknown, though genetic predisposition, chronic inflammation, and environmental carcinogens may play a role. Renal cell carcinoma is the most common primary renal tumor in adult horses, while nephroblastoma (Wilms' tumor) is more frequently seen in younger horses and foals. Secondary renal involvement can occur with disseminated lymphoma.
treatment: Unilateral nephrectomy is the primary treatment for localized renal tumors such as renal cell carcinoma or nephroblastoma, provided the contralateral kidney is functional. Supportive care includes IV fluid therapy, NSAIDs (flunixin meglumine 1.1 mg/kg IV) for pain, and monitoring renal parameters. Chemotherapy options are limited in equine oncology; palliative care is indicated for metastatic or inoperable cases.
treatment_ja: 腎細胞癌や腎芽腫などの限局性腎腫瘍に対しては、対側腎の機能が正常であることを確認した上で片側腎摘出術が第一選択となる。術後は輸液療法、フルニキシンメグルミン（1.1 mg/kg IV）による疼痛管理、腎機能パラメータのモニタリングなどの支持療法を行う。馬における化学療法の選択肢は限られており、転移性または手術不能な症例には緩和ケアが適応となる。

name: Renal Metabolic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal metabolic disease in horses involves impaired kidney function leading to disrupted electrolyte balance, acid-base homeostasis, and waste product excretion. The kidneys fail to adequately regulate calcium, phosphorus, and bicarbonate metabolism, potentially resulting in hypercalcemia or hypocalcemia, hyperphosphatemia, azotemia, and metabolic acidosis. Chronic cases may lead to renal secondary hyperparathyroidism, soft tissue mineralization, and progressive nephron loss.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎代謝性疾患は、腎機能の障害により電解質バランス、酸塩基平衡、および老廃物の排泄が乱れる疾患である。腎臓がカルシウム、リン、重炭酸塩の代謝を十分に調節できなくなり、高カルシウム血症または低カルシウム血症、高リン血症、高窒素血症、代謝性アシドーシスを引き起こす。慢性例では腎性二次性上皮小体機能亢進症、軟部組織の石灰化、進行性のネフロン喪失に至ることがある。
causes: Primary causes include chronic kidney disease (CKD) from nephrotoxic agents (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals), nephrolithiasis, and pyelonephritis. Secondary causes include dehydration, excessive dietary calcium or oxalate-containing plants, systemic infections, and age-related renal degeneration. Hemodynamic insults such as prolonged hypotension or severe colic episodes can also contribute to renal metabolic dysfunction.
treatment: Administer IV fluid therapy (balanced polyionic solutions) to correct dehydration and support renal perfusion. Discontinue nephrotoxic agents (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs). Manage electrolyte imbalances with calcium gluconate or phosphate binders as needed, and correct acidosis with sodium bicarbonate. Provide dietary modification with reduced protein and calcium, and treat underlying infections (e.g., pyelonephritis) with renal-safe antimicrobials such as trimethoprim-sulfonamide.
treatment_ja: 脱水の補正と腎灌流維持のため、バランス電解質輸液（ポリイオン溶液）を静脈内投与する。腎毒性薬剤（アミノグリコシド系、NSAIDs）を直ちに中止する。グルコン酸カルシウムやリン吸着剤で電解質異常を補正し、代謝性アシドーシスには重炭酸ナトリウムを用いる。低タンパク質・低カルシウム食への食事変更を行い、腎盂腎炎などの基礎疾患にはトリメトプリム・スルホンアミドなど腎臓に安全な抗菌薬で治療する。

name: Renal Nutritional Deficiency (Horse)
pathophysiology: Nutritional deficiencies, particularly of vitamins (such as vitamin A, D, or E) and minerals (such as calcium, phosphorus, or magnesium imbalances), can lead to renal tubular dysfunction, nephrocalcinosis, or nephrotoxicity in horses. Imbalanced calcium-to-phosphorus ratios, especially excess dietary phosphorus relative to calcium, can result in calcium deposition in renal tissue, causing progressive renal damage and impaired glomerular and tubular function. Chronic deficiency states may also impair renal blood flow and cellular integrity, leading to fibrosis and reduced renal capacity.
pathophysiology_ja: ビタミン（A、D、Eなど）やミネラル（カルシウム、リン、マグネシウムなど）の栄養欠乏や不均衡は、馬において腎尿細管機能障害、腎石灰沈着症、または腎毒性を引き起こす可能性があります。特にカルシウムとリンの比率の不均衡（リン過剰）は腎組織へのカルシウム沈着を引き起こし、進行性の腎障害を招きます。慢性的な欠乏状態は腎血流や細胞の完全性を損ない、線維化や腎機能低下につながります。
causes: Primary causes include dietary imbalances such as excessive phosphorus intake relative to calcium (inverted Ca:P ratio), vitamin A or D deficiency or excess, and inadequate overall mineral supplementation. Secondary causes include prolonged feeding of high-grain, low-forage diets, oxalate-rich pastures (which bind calcium), and concurrent conditions that impair nutrient absorption such as gastrointestinal disease or parasitism.
treatment: Correct dietary imbalances by restoring the calcium-to-phosphorus ratio to approximately 2:1, supplementing with appropriate levels of vitamin A, D, and E, and ensuring adequate forage intake. Administer IV calcium gluconate or oral calcium carbonate as needed for acute hypocalcemia. Provide supportive care including fluid therapy to promote renal perfusion, and gradually transition to a balanced diet with proper mineral supplementation.
treatment_ja: カルシウムとリンの比率を約2:1に是正し、ビタミンA・D・Eを適切に補給し、十分な粗飼料摂取を確保することで食餌性不均衡を改善する。急性低カルシウム血症にはグルコン酸カルシウムの静脈内投与または炭酸カルシウムの経口投与を行う。腎灌流を促進するための輸液療法を含む支持療法を実施し、適切なミネラル補給を伴うバランスの取れた食餌へ段階的に移行させる。

name: Renal Genetic Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal genetic disorders in horses involve inherited mutations affecting renal tubular or glomerular structure and function, leading to progressive nephron loss, impaired filtration, and electrolyte imbalances. Examples include renal tubular dysplasia and polycystic kidney disease, where abnormal development or cyst formation disrupts normal renal architecture. Progressive fibrosis and loss of functional nephrons ultimately result in chronic renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎遺伝性疾患は、腎尿細管や糸球体の構造・機能に影響を及ぼす遺伝子変異により、進行性のネフロン喪失、濾過障害、電解質異常を引き起こす。腎尿細管異形成や多発性嚢胞腎などが含まれ、腎臓の正常な構造が破壊される。進行性の線維化と機能的ネフロンの喪失により、最終的に慢性腎不全に至る。
causes: The primary cause is inherited genetic mutations, often autosomal recessive, affecting genes responsible for normal renal development and function. Specific mutations may affect proteins involved in tubular transport, basement membrane integrity, or ciliary function. Inbreeding and certain breed predispositions increase the risk of expression of these recessive traits.
causes_ja: 主な原因は常染色体劣性遺伝が多い遺伝子変異であり、正常な腎発達および機能に関与する遺伝子に影響を与える。特定の変異は尿細管輸送、基底膜の完全性、または繊毛機能に関わるタンパク質に影響する。近親交配や特定の品種素因がこれら劣性形質の発現リスクを高める。
treatment: No curative therapy exists; management is supportive. Administer IV fluid therapy (balanced polyionic solutions) to maintain hydration and correct electrolyte imbalances. Use ACE inhibitors (e.g., enalapril 0.5 mg/kg PO q24h) to reduce glomerular hypertension, phosphate binders for hyperphosphatemia, and dietary protein restriction to slow progression. Monitor renal values (BUN, creatinine, SDMA) regularly.
treatment_ja: 根治療法は存在せず、対症療法が中心となる。静脈内輸液療法（バランス電解質液）で水和を維持し電解質異常を補正する。ACE阻害薬（エナラプリル0.5 mg/kg 経口 1日1回）で糸球体内圧を軽減し、高リン血症にはリン吸着剤を使用、食事中のタンパク質制限により進行を遅延させる。BUN、クレアチニン、SDMAを定期的にモニタリングする。

name: Renal Autoimmune Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: The immune system produces autoantibodies or autoreactive lymphocytes directed against renal antigens, including glomerular basement membrane components or tubular structures. Immune complex deposition or direct antibody-mediated injury leads to glomerulonephritis, tubulointerstitial nephritis, or both, resulting in progressive inflammation, fibrosis, and loss of renal function. Complement activation and inflammatory cell infiltration further amplify tissue damage within the kidney.
pathophysiology_ja: 免疫系が糸球体基底膜や尿細管構造などの腎抗原に対する自己抗体または自己反応性リンパ球を産生する。免疫複合体の沈着や抗体を介した直接的な損傷により、糸球体腎炎や尿細管間質性腎炎が生じ、進行性の炎症、線維化、腎機能の喪失を引き起こす。補体活性化と炎症細胞浸潤が腎臓内の組織障害をさらに増幅させる。
causes: The primary cause is dysregulation of immune tolerance leading to autoimmune attack against renal tissues, potentially triggered by chronic infections (e.g., Streptococcus equi), viral infections, or drug reactions. Secondary causes include immune complex deposition from systemic autoimmune conditions such as systemic lupus erythematosus-like syndromes, equine infectious anemia, or other chronic antigenic stimulation. Genetic predisposition and environmental factors may also contribute to disease development.
treatment: Immunosuppressive therapy with corticosteroids (dexamethasone 0.05-0.1 mg/kg IV/IM daily, tapering over weeks) is first-line. Azathioprine (3 mg/kg PO daily) may be added for steroid-sparing effect. Supportive care includes IV fluid therapy to maintain renal perfusion, ACE inhibitors (benazepril 0.5 mg/kg PO) to reduce proteinuria, and treatment of any underlying infections such as Streptococcus equi.
treatment_ja: 免疫抑制療法として副腎皮質ステロイド（デキサメタゾン0.05-0.1 mg/kg IV/IM、数週間かけて漸減）を第一選択とする。アザチオプリン（3 mg/kg PO）をステロイド節約目的で併用可能。支持療法として腎灌流維持のための輸液療法、蛋白尿軽減のためACE阻害薬（ベナゼプリル0.5 mg/kg PO）、およびStreptococcus equiなどの基礎感染症の治療を行う。

name: Renal Degenerative Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal degenerative disease in horses involves progressive deterioration of renal tubular and/or glomerular structures, leading to impaired filtration, reabsorption, and secretion functions. Chronic insults result in nephron loss, fibrosis, and eventual renal insufficiency or failure. Compensatory hypertrophy of remaining nephrons may temporarily maintain function, but progressive loss leads to azotemia, electrolyte imbalances, and uremia.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎変性疾患は、腎尿細管および/または糸球体構造の進行性変性を伴い、濾過・再吸収・分泌機能の障害を引き起こす。慢性的な障害によりネフロンの喪失、線維化が進行し、最終的に腎不全に至る。残存ネフロンの代償性肥大により一時的に機能は維持されるが、進行性の喪失により高窒素血症、電解質異常、尿毒症が生じる。
causes: Primary causes include chronic exposure to nephrotoxins (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals, vitamin D toxicosis), oxalate-containing plants, and pigment nephropathy from myoglobinuria or hemoglobinuria. Secondary causes include chronic renal ischemia, systemic infections, immune-mediated glomerulonephritis, and age-related degenerative changes. Hypercalcemia and chronic dehydration may also contribute to progressive renal degeneration.
treatment: Remove nephrotoxic agents immediately. Provide aggressive IV fluid therapy (polyionic isotonic crystalloids) to correct dehydration and support renal perfusion. Manage electrolyte imbalances (calcium, phosphorus, potassium) and administer gastroprotectants (omeprazole 4 mg/kg PO SID). Dietary protein restriction and phosphorus binders (aluminum hydroxide) help slow progression. ACE inhibitors (benazepril) may reduce proteinuria in glomerular disease.
treatment_ja: 腎毒性物質を直ちに除去する。積極的な静脈内輸液療法（等張晶質液）で脱水を補正し、腎灌流を維持する。電解質異常（カルシウム、リン、カリウム）を是正し、胃粘膜保護薬（オメプラゾール4 mg/kg 経口1日1回）を投与する。食事中のタンパク質制限およびリン吸着剤（水酸化アルミニウム）で進行を遅延させる。糸球体疾患にはACE阻害薬（ベナゼプリル）がタンパク尿軽減に有用である。

name: Renal Traumatic Injury (Horse)
